docs.title: lumnik — defrost the enterprise
docs.text:
Documentation

lumnik reads the data in your ERP, LIMS and exports — read-only — and lets people ask it questions in plain language. The answer cites its sources, or declines and says why.

Read-only first

Your source system is never written to. Ingest first, risk nothing.

Fuse, conflicts kept

Conflicts are preserved in a _conflicts ledger, never silently resolved away.

Ask with guards

Answers cite their sources — or decline. The guards refuse to invent.

Operate for real

Deploy, connect, scope, and run day-2 operations from one docs set.

See the WOW Deploy lumnik Follow the guided path

docs.title: Admin tasks — lm and the API behind it
docs.text:
Day-to-day administration of a running hub: webhooks, deliveries, runs, secrets, migrations, modules, hooks, tenants. Every task below starts from an lm command or a TUI screen (lm ui); raw HTTP appears only where no lm command exists.

No admin web console ships with lumnik.

docs.title: Who can call what
docs.text:
Roles are matched literally, with no hierarchy: lm_superadmin alone does not open an lm_admin door, and the reverse.

Task Gesture Roles needed Wire webhooks lm integration · :integrations lm_integrator + lm_admin, no scope:* role (or lm_admin alone over /api/tenants/{tid}/integrations) Read and replay deliveries lm outputs · :outputs lm_integrator + lm_admin (or lm_superadmin), no scope:* role Runs and dead letters lm run, lm dlq · :runs, :dlq lm_integrator Read secrets (metadata) lm secret list, describe lm_integrator Create, rotate, delete secrets lm secret set, rm lm_integrator + lm_admin Migrations, modules, hooks list, event catalog lm migration, lm module, lm hook list, GET /api/platform/events lm_integrator Declared workflows lm workflow lm_integrator Live event stream the TUI, or GET /api/platform/events/stream lm_integrator, no scope:* role Toggle a hook for a tenant, read one hook POST /api/platform/hooks/{id}/toggle, lm hook get lm_integrator + lm_admin Tenants /api/tenants lm_superadmin Orgs, users, tenant roles /api/tenants/{tid}/… lm_admin, own tenant only

A scope-bound integrator sees only the runs and dead letters of connectors whose scopes it holds (Scopes).

No lm command prints your roles. Ask the hub (needs lm_user):

$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/bff/v1/me -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '{tenant: .tenant.id, roles}'
{
  "tenant": 1,
  "roles": [
    "lm_integrator",
    "lm_admin",
    "lm_user"
  ]
}

tenant is the {tid} the /api/tenants/{tid}/… paths want. Getting a token for curl: Test the API.

docs.title: Send events out to another system
docs.text:
Register a webhook target (here a test receiver on port 18955). Always pass the signing secret with --secret-stdin:

$ printf '%s' "$WEBHOOK_SECRET" | lm integration add ops-hook \
    --url http://localhost:18955/hook --events 'connector.run.*' --secret-stdin
registered: ops-hook (id 1001) — forwards subscribed events from now on

$ lm integration list
ID    NAME      URL                     EVENTS           ENABLED
1001  ops-hook  http://localhost:18955  connector.run.*  true

$ lm integration test 1001
delivered in 11ms (HTTP 200)
  • --events takes exact types or a prefix ending in .*; the default is decision.*.
  • test fires a catalog event (--event, default org.created). decision.* types are not in the catalog and cannot be tested this way: verify them with a real decision.
  • Only events fired after registration are delivered.
  • Delivery is at-least-once: a hub stop mid-send can deliver an event twice. Deduplicate on X-Lumnik-Event-Id.
  • lm integration describe ID shows one registration; lm integration rm ID removes it (the delivery history is kept, pending retries stop).
  • In lm ui, :integrations: n registers, T tests, Del removes, d shows recent deliveries.

Without --secret-stdin, the hub refuses the registration and stores nothing:

$ lm integration add erp-out --url https://erp.example.com/hook --events org.created
Error: API error 400: HMAC mode needs a secret (lm integration add: --secret-stdin)

What the receiver gets (headers, the HMAC signature, retries, retention): Outputs.

docs.title: Settings lm does not expose
docs.text:
lm integration add always registers an enabled target in HMAC mode. For another mode, or to change a registration, use the HTTP door /api/platform/integrations:

Field Values Default name unique within the tenant required targetUrl the receiver's URL required eventTypes exact types or .* prefixes required authMode HMAC (X-Lumnik-Signature: sha256=…), BEARER (Authorization: Bearer <secret>), NONE HMAC secret the HMAC key or the bearer token; never returned (hasSecret: true) none platform generic, make, zapier, n8n — a label only (lm integration add --platform) generic enabled true / false true

Rotate a target's secret (a PUT applies only the fields present; a blank secret is ignored):

$ curl -s -X PUT http://localhost:8080/api/platform/integrations/1001 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"secret":"the-new-shared-secret"}' | jq
{
  "id": 1001,
  "name": "ops-hook",
  "targetUrl": "http://localhost:18955/hook",
  "platform": "generic",
  "authMode": "HMAC",
  "eventTypes": [
    "connector.run.*"
  ],
  "enabled": true,
  "hasSecret": true
}

Change the receiver's copy in the same window: the next delivery is signed with the new secret.

docs.title: Watch deliveries and replay a failure
docs.text:
$ lm outputs list
ID    INTEGRATION  EVENT                    STATUS       WHEN              ERROR
1006  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  no response  2026-10-19 01:46  connection failed (ConnectException)
1005  ops-hook     connector.run.started    no response  2026-10-19 01:46  connection failed (ConnectException)
1001  (deleted)    connector.run.completed  no response  2026-10-19 01:44  endpoint gone, unsubscribed, or entity_filter no longer matches — retries stopped
1000  (deleted)    connector.run.started    no response  2026-10-19 01:44  endpoint gone, unsubscribed, or entity_filter no longer matches — retries stopped
1003  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  ok           2026-10-19 01:45
1002  ops-hook     connector.run.started    ok           2026-10-19 01:45
1004  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  ok           2026-10-19 01:44

Failures come first. A failed delivery is retried automatically, 3 attempts in all, about 30 s apart. After the third, replay it once the receiver is back:

$ lm outputs replay 1006
replayed: delivery 1006 — a new attempt is on record

$ lm outputs list
ID    INTEGRATION  EVENT                    STATUS       WHEN              ERROR
1006  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  no response  2026-10-19 01:46  connection failed (ConnectException)
…
1007  ops-hook     connector.run.completed  ok           2026-10-19 01:46

The replay is a new row (1007); the original row stays as it was, still listed as failed. In lm ui, :outputs shows the same list; ^R replays the selected delivery.

ERROR column Meaning Gesture connection failed (ConnectException) the receiver did not answer bring it back, then lm outputs replay ID HMAC mode but no secret configured the target was registered without a secret, before the hub refused that (Bearer mode but no token configured: same, in BEARER mode) set a secret (PUT above) or re-register with --secret-stdin, then replay endpoint gone, unsubscribed, or entity_filter no longer matches — retries stopped the target was removed, disabled, or no longer subscribes to that event re-enable or re-subscribe, then replay; a removed target accepts no replay (404)

docs.title: Find the event types you can subscribe to
docs.text:
No lm command lists the catalog; the running hub serves it:

$ curl -s http://localhost:8080/api/platform/events -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq -r '.[].type'
org.created
org.updated
org.moved
org.archived
connector.run.started
connector.run.completed
connector.run.partial
connector.run.cancelled
connector.run.failed
platform.secret.created
platform.secret.updated
platform.secret.deleted
platform.secret.read
data.row.changed
annotation.decision.acked

Each entry also carries its module, a description and the payload fields. decision.* types are not in this list: each kind:Process and kind:Workflow names its own, and a decision.* subscription matches them when they fire. What each type means: the event registry.

docs.title: Watch ingestion: runs, dead letters, live events
docs.text:
Gesture What it does lm run list [--connector NAME] recent runs, newest first: IN, OUT, SKIPPED, DEAD-LETTERS lm run get ID one run, with its failure reason or quarantine warning lm run cancel ID asks an in-flight run to stop lm dlq list --run ID / --connector NAME the quarantined rows, with their reason and RESOLUTION (REPLAYED/DISCARDED, empty while open) lm dlq get ID one entry, with the row as the source sent it lm dlq replayed ID --new-run-id RUN · lm dlq discard ID mark an entry handled

--connector lists only the entries still pending; --run lists the run's full history, handled entries included. Every run id in these gestures (--run, --new-run-id) takes the 8 characters lm run list shows.

The full walk, with captures: Diagnosing a failed run.

In lm ui, :runs, :dlq, :sources and :endpoints update by themselves while runs happen. They follow the live event stream, which your own tooling can read too:

Door GET /api/platform/events/stream?topic=connector.run.* (Accept: text/event-stream) topic repeatable; * is a wildcard over the event type; none = every event Each element {"topic": "<type>", "payload": "<JSON as a string>", "capturedAt": "<ISO-8601>"} Scope-bound caller 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}; in lm ui the footer says live events: … and views refresh only when opened

docs.title: Keep a connector credential: the secret store
docs.text:
Connector manifests name a secret (*_env fields); lm secret stores its value, encrypted. No command returns a value.

$ lm secret set ERP_DB_PASSWORD --description "ERP read account"
Value for ERP_DB_PASSWORD:
Created secret "ERP_DB_PASSWORD"

$ lm secret list
NAME                           ROTATED_AT                     DESCRIPTION
ERP_DB_PASSWORD                -                              ERP read account

$ lm secret rm ERP_DB_PASSWORD
Type 'delete' to confirm removal of "ERP_DB_PASSWORD": delete
Deleted secret "ERP_DB_PASSWORD"
  • The value is typed at the prompt and not shown. From a script: lm secret set NAME - reads stdin.
  • set on an existing name rotates the value (Updated secret "…", ROTATED_AT filled). Without --description, the description stays; --description "" clears it.
  • lm secret describe NAME shows metadata only; lm secret rm --force skips the prompt.
  • Which connectors read the store, and which read the hub's environment instead: REST, CSV, JDBC.

docs.title: Trace a citation back to its source row
docs.text:
lm data row <HASH>

Takes the row_hash of a chat citation and prints the raw source row (all values as text). It answers 404 when the hash resolves to nothing in your tenant. A scope-bound caller reads the row only if every connector writing its table carries one of its scopes.

SCHEMA    VERSION  PENDING  LAST APPLIED
core      75       0        2026-10-19 01:36

docs.title: Turn a hook on or off, and read declared workflows
docs.text: Gesture What it does lm hook list · lm hook get NAME the hooks this hub loaded lm workflow list · lm workflow get NAME the tenant's declared kind:Workflow manifests (Workflows) POST /api/platform/hooks/{hookId}/toggle?tenantId=… turns one hook on or off for one tenant; other hub threads see it within 60 s

docs.title: Manage tenants, orgs and users
docs.text:
No lm command manages identity; use the HTTP doors. Deletes archive, never erase. The gestures in context (onboarding, offboarding): Identity administration.

Method Path Contract GET /api/tenants active tenants (lm_superadmin) POST /api/tenants create {code, name, description?}; 201, 409 on a duplicate code PUT · DELETE /api/tenants/{id} update name/description · deactivate (204) GET · POST /api/tenants/{tid}/orgs list · create (409 on a duplicate code) GET /api/tenants/{tid}/orgs/tree?root=&depth= the org tree (default depth 3) PUT · DELETE /api/tenants/{tid}/orgs/{id} update · deactivate GET · POST /api/tenants/{tid}/users list · create {login, name, email?, description?} (409 on a duplicate login) PUT · DELETE /api/tenants/{tid}/users/{id} update profile · deactivate (204) POST /api/tenants/{tid}/users/{id}/unlock unlock a locked account /api/tenants/{tid}/roles, …/users/{uid}/roles/{roleId}, …/roles/{roleId}/orgs/{orgId} tenant roles, their assignment, their org access

Org changes emit org.created, org.updated, org.moved, org.archived. lumnik stores no passwords: users sign in through Keycloak or your IdP. On Pro, a user's hub record is created at first login.

docs.title: Act on behalf of a tenant (impersonation)
docs.text:
• Impersonation is a JWT claim minted by your IdP: acting_as_tenant: <tid>, on a token that carries lm_superadmin. There is no hub endpoint that mints it.
  • It switches the tenant, never the roles: the roles in the token are the ones checked.
  • A token carrying the claim without lm_superadmin is refused: 403 {"error": "lm_superadmin required to impersonate a tenant"}.
  • The X-Impersonate-Tenant header works only with lumnik.security.dev-bypass=true.

docs.title: Harden the deployment
docs.text: Concern What the hub does What you do Secrets encrypted at rest, never returned by any door protect the .env that holds the keys; key rotation is not supported (RLS & credentials) Impersonation honoured only for lm_superadmin grant lm_superadmin to as few accounts as possible; an impersonated write is audited in the target tenant under the superadmin's user id, with nothing marking it as impersonation; the impersonation itself shows only in log lines Dev bypass grants every role to every caller never set lumnik.security.dev-bypass=true outside development Platform doors /api/platform/* requires lm_integrator restrict /api/platform/* and /q/* at your proxy if the hub faces the internet

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer on /api/platform/* the token expired or was not sent lm login again API error 403: missing role lm_integrator the token lacks lm_integrator read your roles (above), then have it granted API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server — your account may lack the required role (raw HTTP: 403, empty body) a role the door needs is missing — often lm_admin read your roles, then have it granted access refused (403): scope not granted on lm integration, lm outputs (raw HTTP on the event stream: 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}) your account holds a scope:* role; these doors are tenant-wide use an account with no scope:* role 403 on /api/tenants/{tid}/… while you hold lm_admin {tid} is not your token's tenant use tenant from /api/bff/v1/me 400 {"error": "Unknown event type: …"} on lm integration test --event … the type is not in the catalog — decision.* never is test with a catalog type; verify decision.* with a real decision API error 400: HMAC mode needs a secret … on lm integration add no --secret-stdin pass the secret on stdin — see Send events out A failed delivery is no longer retried it used its 3 attempts lm outputs replay ID lm outputs replay ID answers 404 for an id in your list the target was removed with lm integration rm register the target again; new events reach it X-Impersonate-Tenant changes nothing the header works only with dev-bypass use the acting_as_tenant claim

docs.title: If none of that is it
docs.text:
• Your hub serves its live API contract at /q/openapi and a try-it console at /q/swagger-ui/: Test the API.
  • Security reports: contact@lumnik.fr (acknowledged within 72 hours). It is not a support channel; for configuration questions, ask your integrator.

docs.title: Architecture — the why
docs.text: Every other page describes a what. This one lists the design commitments everything else hangs from — the page to read when evaluating lumnik.

docs.title: Read-only first
docs.text:
Ingestion is one-way: there is no write path back to your systems — not behind a flag, not for administrators. The hub lands data in its own PostgreSQL, and fusion, chat, apps and events work on that copy. Your system of record stays the sole owner of its data.

The same posture extends downstream: the SQL that answers a chat question executes on a separate, physically read-only database connection — see the next commitment.

docs.title: Isolation lives in the database
docs.text:
Multi-tenant isolation is not application code you have to trust; it is PostgreSQL Row-Level Security, enforced by the layer that cannot be bypassed by a bug in the layer above. Three database roles carry three trust levels:

  • the request path runs RLS-enforced, and owns nothing;
  • LLM-generated SQL runs on a role that can only read, with an empty search_path;
  • deliberate cross-tenant work (migrations, purges) runs on a separate role that every code path must use explicitly.

The full mechanics — policies, the tenant GUC, what RLS does and does not protect against — are on RLS & database roles.

docs.title: Refusal over guessing
docs.text:
The system prefers a refusal to a plausible guess:

  • on the way in, a run's arithmetic always closes — a row is written, benignly skipped, or quarantined with its reason (seeing what was ingested);
  • on the way out, deterministic guards stand between a question and its answer, and an empty result is never phrased as a confident "there are none" (the five guards);
  • disagreements between sources are preserved in a ledger instead of silently resolved (entities).

docs.title: Declared over inferred
docs.text: Where meaning enters the system, a human declares it: connectors, entities, views, processes and lifecycles are all manifests an integrator applies — validated, refusable, versionable in git. A workflow even records how its lifecycle is known (provenance: declared), so the day something is inferred instead, the difference will be citable — not retrofitted.

docs.title: One hub, optional extensions
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph core["the hub — runs on its own"]
    ing["connectors"] --> raw[("raw tables")]
    raw --> ent["entities"]
  end
  subgraph ext["extensions — discovered at boot"]
    rag["search · chat"]
    llm["LLM providers"]
  end
  ent -.->|"if present"| rag
  rag -.-> llm

A hub without the chat extension still ingests, fuses and serves. What needs a model says so:

$ lm view generate desk "les clients de Lyon" -o lyon.yaml
Error: API error 400: generation abstained: no chat model is available on this hub — view generation needs one

Ready to verify any of this against a running system? Deploy is one command, and the cheat sheet is the minimum you need to poke at it.

docs.title: Stand it up
docs.text:
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build   # first run writes .env with fresh secrets — BACK IT UP
curl -s http://localhost:8080/q/health   # UP, or DOWN with the failing check named
./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub     # follow the hub (see: Reading the logs)

Full walkthroughs: Deploy · Reading the logs.

docs.title: The ten commands
docs.text:
# Command What it does 1 lm login authenticate once; lm remembers the context 2 lm validate -f FILE dry-run a kind: Connector manifest — errors field by field. The other kinds have no dry-run: their apply checks first and refuses rather than half-writes 3 lm apply -f FILE apply a connector manifest (upsert) 4 lm connector run NAME run it now 5 lm run list --connector NAME the run ledger — records in/out/skip at a glance 6 lm dlq list --run ID exactly which rows fell out, and why 7 lm entity apply -f FILE fuse sources into one canonical entity (lm entity delete NAME removes it, and frees a connector it blocked) 8 lm workflow apply -f FILE declare a lifecycle — prints the data-truth report 9 lm ask --scope S "question" ask the data — prints the answer, the rows and the SQL that ran (-o json for the whole result). lumnik Pro 10 lm secret set NAME store a secret — prompted, not echoed (NAME - reads stdin instead, for a multi-line key or a script); values are never returned

The full surface (sources, endpoints, mappings, tags, observations…) is in the CLI & TUI reference.

Command 5 is the screen you will read most. On every row, IN = OUT + SKIPPED:

$ lm run list
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
30b078c6  customers     default   Completed  12  12   0        0             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
f0466804  orders        default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
3ccd21eb  products      default   Failed     0   0    0        0             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
852771fa  crm-contacts  default   Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-09-05 05:39  2026-09-05 05:39
  • Failed is the run itself (source unreachable, bad credentials): lm run get 3ccd21eb prints the reason.
  • DEAD-LETTERS are rows set aside with their reason: lm dlq list.
  • Stop a running run: lm run cancel ID — it ends after the chunk in flight. An ended run is refused:
$ lm run cancel 2af6db4c
Error: API error 409: run 2af6db4c-31a5-4615-8cf9-96f7924fdce4 already ended (Completed)

Every -f also takes -f - (stdin), and every listing takes -o json: Integration as code. Command 9 answers 404 on the open edition — see which edition you installed.

docs.title: The TUI in six keys
docs.text:
lm with no arguments opens the TUI:

Key Does : command palette — :sources :runs :dlq :ask :inbox :outputs … r refresh d describe the selected row y yank the row to the clipboard ? help q quit

:runs, :dlq and :inbox live-update — you can watch a run while it happens.

docs.text: File Why it matters .env every secret of the stack; losing LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY makes stored secrets unrecoverable — back it up docker-compose.selfhost.yml the stack definition up.sh drives ~/.lm/config.yaml lm's contexts (server, token, TLS trust)

docs.title: When it refuses
docs.text: You see It means Where to look 403 {"error":"scope not granted"} your user holds scope roles, and this resource is in none of them Scopes "I can't answer that…" from the chat a guard refused rather than guess; the message says what to do next The five guards a run with SKIPPED > 0 rows counted and not written. Duplicates and policy-excluded rows are skipped without reaching the DLQ; DEAD-LETTERS is the part that did Ingestion honesty

docs.title: Choosing what your hub offers
docs.text:
The same hub can show a warehouse team two tabs and a sales team four, run with the AI switched off for a client who forbids a model, or carry Search when it was built in. Four questions, asked in order, decide what a métier app shows — and each has one gesture.

Who the integrator installing or tuning a hub Gestures the image you deploy, one environment variable, one line in a kind: App manifest — and, for Recherche, a kind: SearchIndex See the result lm module list, then the app itself Edition both — what differs is which answers are possible (Open vs Pro)

docs.title: The four questions
docs.text:
Questions 1 to 3 decide whether a tab is on an app. Question 4 decides whether it is worth showing: Recherche checks it before it appears, while Fiches opens anyway and says what is missing. Read them top to bottom; the first no is your answer when something is missing.

flowchart LR
  a["1. Is it in the build?"] --> b["2. Is it switched on?"] --> c["3. Does the app ask for it?"] --> d["4. Is it ready to be used?"]
  d --> tab(["the tab is there"])
# Question Who decides Your gesture Where you look 1 Is it in the build? the image you deploy pick Open or Pro; add a Search provider when you build the hub lm module list 2 Is it switched on? the operator LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false turns the AI family off; absent means on lm module list 3 Does the app ask for it? the métier's kind: App spec.tabs: [...]; leave it out to take everything the hub offers lm app apply 4 Is it ready to be used? the feature itself for Recherche, declare a search index the user may read the tab, and lm search status

The tabs and who brings them:

Tab Shown as Brought by Needs fiches Fiches every hub a saved view for the app's scope (without one the tab opens and says so) inbox Décisions every hub — chat Chat Pro (rag + llm) the AI switched on search Recherche a Search provider (search_pg or search_opensearch) a search index the user may read

docs.title: 1. Is it in the build?
docs.text:
What the image carries is fixed when the hub is built; no setting adds a module that is not there. Ask the hub what it carries:

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS  REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      ACTIVE
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        ACTIVE

That is a Pro hub: llm and rag are there, together. An Open hub lists core and identity only — it has no Chat tab to offer, and nothing to switch on:

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS  REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE

Search is added when you build the hub: the published image never carries a provider. See Deploy (up.sh --search or --search-cluster, closed edition) and choosing a provider. The provider then appears in the list:

$ lm module list
NAME       VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS  REASON
core       0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE
identity   0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE
llm        0.1.0    Model provider      ACTIVE
rag        0.1.0    Platform RAG        ACTIVE
search_pg  0.1.0    PostgreSQL search   ACTIVE

No lm command prints which tabs each module brings; the platform API does (integrator token). The hub offers the tabs of the active modules — here a Pro hub with the AI switched off:

$ curl -s "$LUMNIK_URL/api/platform/modules" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    | jq -c '.modules[] | select((.tabs|length)>0) | {id, active, tabs}'
{"id":"core","active":true,"tabs":["fiches","inbox"]}
{"id":"rag","active":false,"tabs":["chat"]}

A Search provider adds {"id":"search_pg","active":true,"tabs":["search"]}.

docs.title: 2. Is it switched on?
docs.text:
One setting switches off the whole AI family — chat, ask, view generation, embeddings — without rebuilding: LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false. The gesture per install is in Deploy — switch the AI off. It must be exactly true or false; anything else stops the hub at startup. What you see, and what keeps running: Switching the AI off.

The module list tells the difference between switched off and not there:

$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE    
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE    
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
  • Inactive (Pro, switched off): the data is kept, the images are the same, and putting the setting back restores what you had. Content that needed indexing while the AI was off is not there when it returns — re-apply the workflow or re-ingest the file (what comes back).
  • Absent (Open): the module is not in the build, so it is not in the list at all.

Either way the Chat tab is gone from every app. Search is not part of this switch: turning the AI off leaves Search exactly as it was.

docs.title: 3. Does the app ask for it?
docs.text:
Each métier app is a kind: App manifest. Without tabs it shows everything the hub offers (and whatever a later release adds). To show fewer tabs, or to change their order, list them:

kind: App
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: stock
spec:
  title: Stock
  scope: stock
  icon: stock
  tabs: [fiches, inbox]        # no Chat for the warehouse

$ lm app apply -f stock.yaml
Applied app "stock" → scope stock
  tabs: fiches, inbox

A tab the hub does not offer is kept, and shows up the day the hub offers it. The apply warns without failing — here tabs: [fiches, inbox, chat] on a hub without Chat:

$ lm app apply -f stock.yaml
Applied app "stock" → scope stock
  tabs: fiches, inbox, chat
! stock.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.tabs[2]
          tab 'chat' is not offered by this hub; the declaration is kept and takes effect when a module offering it is active
          → offered here: [fiches, inbox]

The last line is the hub's offer. Order, the opening tab and what is refused: Choosing the tabs.

Hiding a tab hides it, nothing more: who may read what is still decided by roles and scopes.

docs.title: 4. Is it ready to be used?
docs.text:
Tab Ready when Check Fiches a saved view exists for the app's scope (otherwise the tab opens and says so) lm view list --scope <app scope> Recherche the user may read a search index (otherwise the tab is not shown) lm search status

Recherche's full checklist: Enabling Recherche for an app.

Whether Search is installed: the TUI's :search page says so in its banner, and a query on a hub without a provider is refused, never answered with an empty list:

$ lm search query "Lyon"
Error: search is not installed on this hub — no Search provider is built into it, so there is nothing to query (this is not an empty result). The published hub image never carries one: build it from source with deploy/selfhost/up.sh --search (PostgreSQL) or --search-cluster (OpenSearch), both closed edition

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
A warehouse app with no Chat, on a Pro hub. Question 3 only: tabs: [fiches, inbox] in the app's manifest, then lm app apply -f. The other apps keep their Chat.

A client who forbids a model on their hub. Question 2: switch the AI off. Every app loses its Chat tab at once, no manifest changes, and the rest of the hub (including Oracle, SCIM and Search) is untouched.

One métier searching, the others not (questions 3 and 4, here for the stock app):

  1. In the stock app's manifest, list search in tabs; lm app apply -f.
  2. In each kind: Entity to search, set scopes: [stock] (the entity's scopes list — not the app's scope, not the users' scope:<tag> role); lm entity apply -f.
  3. Declare a search index over those entities: lm search apply -f.
  4. Give every other app a tabs list without search. An app that leaves tabs out shows Recherche to any user who may read some index.

Aucun résultat on every search

An app whose scope has nothing indexed still shows Recherche when its users can read another scope's index — and every search answers Aucun résultat. Check lm search status when a métier expects hits.

docs.title: When a tab is missing
docs.text:
Go down the questions; stop at the first one that answers no.

What you see Look at Likely answer No Chat tab on any app lm module list llm and rag missing: this is an Open build. Listed INACTIVE with disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled: switch the AI back on. No Recherche tab on any app lm module list no search_pg / search_opensearch: the hub was built without a Search provider. No Recherche tab, yet search_pg is ACTIVE lm search status no kind: SearchIndex is declared yet (the list is empty), or the users may read none of the entities the indexes cover. Recherche missing on one app only that app's manifest tabs leaves out search; or its users hold scopes that read none of the indexed entities (compare each entity's scopes with their scope:<tag> roles). Recherche there, but always Aucun résultat lm search status the index is not built yet (STATUS, DOCUMENTS). … and STATUS reads invalid lm search status an entity re-apply removed a column the index declares — re-apply the index. … and STATUS reads withheld lm search status an index re-apply removed or changed a field — it serves again once rebuilt. … and the index is ready lm search status no index covers the entities of the app's scope. A tab listed in tabs does not show lm app apply -f again the hub does not offer it (question 1 or 2): the apply warns. The warning reflects the offer when you apply; the tab appears once the hub offers it. Chat tab present, answers fail lm rag status the tab shows whenever rag and llm are active; a model that is not reachable is a different problem (models).

docs.title: Deploy on Windows
docs.text:
Your Windows PC can run all of lumnik — the hub, the database, the login server, even the AI. This page walks you there step by step: each one says where to type, what to type, and what you should see before moving on.

Total time: about an hour, most of it downloads. You need Windows 10 (version 21H2 or later) or Windows 11, and around 20 GB of free disk.

docs.title: The two windows you will type into
docs.text:
Everything below happens in one of two command windows — worth telling apart before starting:

  • PowerShell — Windows' own command window. Open it from the Start menu: type powershell, click the result. You'll use it for Windows-side things (installing tools, running lm.exe).
  • Ubuntu — a small Linux that lives inside Windows (installed in step 1). Open it from the Start menu: type ubuntu. lumnik itself runs here.

Three habits that save an hour

  • Paste with a right-click. In these windows Ctrl+V often does nothing; copy the command here, then right-click inside the window — it pastes.
  • One command, then Enter, then wait. The command is done when the prompt (the line ending in > or $) comes back.
  • Passwords are typed blind. When Ubuntu asks for a password, nothing appears while you type — no dots, no stars. That's normal: type it and press Enter.

docs.title: Step 1 — Install WSL2, the Linux inside Windows (~10 min, one restart)
docs.text:
1. Open PowerShell as administrator: Start menu → type powershell → right-click the result → Run as administrator → answer Yes.
  2. Type: 
    wsl --install
    Windows downloads WSL2 and Ubuntu. When it asks, restart the PC.
  3. After the restart, an Ubuntu window opens on its own (if not: Start menu → ubuntu). It asks you to pick a username and a password — this is a new, Linux-side account, not your Windows one. Remember the password: Ubuntu asks for it whenever a command starts with sudo.
  4. Check it worked — in a normal PowerShell window: 
    wsl --status
    You should see Default Version: 2.

It complains about virtualization or the BIOS?

Your PC's virtualization switch is off. Check: Ctrl+Shift+Esc → Performance → CPU → look for Virtualization: Enabled. If it says Disabled, it must be enabled in the BIOS (usually F2/Del at power-on, then an option named VT-x, SVM or "Virtualization Technology"). A search for "enable virtualization + your PC model" gives the exact keys.

docs.title: Step 2 — Install Docker Desktop (~10 min)
docs.text:
Docker runs lumnik's services in containers — you never have to install Java, a database, or anything else by hand.

  1. Download Docker Desktop for Windows from docker.com and run the installer. Keep every default. Restart if it asks.
  2. Open Docker Desktop. It suggests creating an account — you don't need one: look for the small Continue without signing in link.
  3. Two settings to verify (gear icon ⚙, top right):
    • General → Use the WSL 2 based engine — should already be checked.
    • Resources → WSL integration → turn the Ubuntu switch on → Apply & restart.
  4. Prove it — in the Ubuntu window: 
    docker run --rm hello-world
    You should see Hello from Docker! in the output. If instead you get docker: command not found, revisit the WSL-integration switch above.

docs.title: Step 3 — Get lumnik (in Ubuntu, ~5 min)
docs.text:
From here on, work in the Ubuntu window. One rule to know: keep the code in Ubuntu's own home folder (~), never under /mnt/c — the Windows disk seen from Ubuntu is slow and mangles scripts.

  1. Install the small tools lumnik's installer uses (Ubuntu arrives almost empty): 
    sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y git curl python3 openssl gawk
    (sudo asks for your Ubuntu password — typed blind, see above.)
  2. Fetch the code: 
    cd ~ && git clone https://github.com/icreated/lumnik-open.git && cd lumnik-open

Which edition you just cloned

This is the open edition: every step on this page applies to it except step 5. It has no chat and no natural-language ask. See also the Deploy page.

docs.title: Step 4 — Start the stack (one command; ~10–20 min the first time)
docs.text:
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build

This single command builds and starts everything inside Docker — nothing else to install on your PC. The first run compiles lumnik from source: it's the long one, a coffee's worth. Later runs take seconds.

What the end must look like — the last lines, in this order:

==> hub is healthy
  hubadmin: per-install password set (HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env)
  integrator: per-install password set (INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env)

  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)

Those two password set lines matter: they create your login accounts, with passwords unique to your install (stored in a file named .env).

The script stopped straight away, naming missing tools?

That's its preflight doing its job — run the sudo apt install line from step 3, then run ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build again. It's safe to re-run as often as you like.

If instead the very end says !! could not obtain a Keycloak admin token, the login server was slow to finish its first start — simply re-run ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build; the passwords get set on the next pass.

See it live: in your normal Windows browser, open http://localhost:8080/q/health. It starts like this (Windows sees Ubuntu's services on its own localhost — nothing to configure):

{
    "status": "UP",
    "checks": [
        {
            "name": "Database connections health check",
            "status": "UP",

docs.title: Step 5 — The AI, on the Windows side (~20 min, ~8 GB of downloads)
docs.text:
Ingestion and the REST API work without this step. The chat and the natural-language "ask" need a local AI runtime: Ollama, installed on Windows itself.

On the open edition, skip this step entirely

The modules that call Ollama are not in the tree you cloned at step 3, so nothing in your install will ever reach it — the ~8 GB of downloads below buy you nothing. Come back to this step only on a build that carries the chat extensions.

Graphics drivers first — the trap that looks like nothing

If your PC has an NVIDIA card, update its drivers before the first model run (GeForce Experience, or your PC maker's support page). Ollama uses the graphics card, and outdated drivers make the model silently fail to load — lumnik's ask then errors after ~20 seconds with no useful message.

  1. Download and run the Ollama for Windows installer from ollama.com. No settings to change.
  2. In PowerShell, download the three models lumnik uses at runtime (the names must be exactly these): 
    ollama pull nomic-embed-text
ollama pull llama3.2
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b
    A fourth model, gemma4, is used only by an offline evaluation; skip it.
  3. Prove it: 
    ollama run llama3.2 "say hello"
    A slow-ish sentence back means everything works. The hub finds Ollama on its own — nothing to wire.

16 GB of RAM or less? Give Windows room to breathe

Ubuntu/WSL grabs up to half your RAM by default, and the AI model needs ~6 GB free on the Windows side. Cap WSL once: in PowerShell, notepad $env:USERPROFILE\.wslconfig (say Yes to create the file), put exactly this in it, save and close: 

[wsl2]
memory=6GB
Then wsl --shutdown in PowerShell, reopen Docker Desktop, and wait a minute for the stack to come back.

docs.title: Step 6 — lm, the control room, on Windows
docs.text:
lm.exe is lumnik's command-line and terminal UI for Windows. Download the Windows x86-64 .zip from the Releases page and unpack lm.exe anywhere, e.g. your Downloads folder.

Windows protected your PC?

The first launch may show a blue SmartScreen box — the file is not signed. Click More info, then Run anyway.

In PowerShell, from the folder holding the file:

.\lm.exe config set-context local --server http://localhost:8080 --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
.\lm.exe config use-context local
.\lm.exe login

lm login shows a web address and a code — open the address in your browser, enter the code, and sign in as integrator. The password was minted for your install at step 4; read it in the Ubuntu window with:

grep INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD ~/lumnik-open/.env

Then just:

.\lm.exe

— the full terminal UI. Press ? inside for help, : for the command palette.

docs.title: Where to next
docs.text:
Walk The WOW, hands-on — ingest two fake legacy systems, watch lumnik fuse them, and ask the result a question in plain language. One habit to take along: after every lm connector run …, check lm run list — "run scheduled" is not "run succeeded", and the list is where the truth lives.

  • A phone on this stack: http://localhost:8080 is reachable from your PC only. Put the TLS façade in front.
  • Another port, an external PostgreSQL: see How to… — the port stays, use the façade; an external database is not an option on this path.

docs.title: Troubleshooting, Windows edition
docs.text:
Symptom What it means → what to do wsl --install is "not recognized" Windows too old — run Windows Update until version 21H2+, or install WSL from the Microsoft Store. WSL complains about virtualization / BIOS The VT switch is off — see the note in step 1. docker: command not found in Ubuntu The WSL-integration switch for Ubuntu is off — step 2, setting 3. !! could not obtain a Keycloak admin token at the end of up.sh Not a missing tool — the preflight would have stopped the script before this point. The login server was still finishing its first start; up.sh retries for ~25 s, then warns and leaves both accounts without a password. Re-run ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build — the passwords get set on the next pass (step 4). http://localhost:8080 suddenly unreachable (often after the PC slept) WSL's plumbing went stale — in PowerShell wsl --shutdown, reopen Docker Desktop, wait a minute. Logins fail with 401 after the laptop slept Ubuntu's clock drifted during sleep — same cure: wsl --shutdown, reopen Docker Desktop. The ask/chat errors after ~20 s The model failed to load on the Windows side: update your NVIDIA drivers (the classic), then check the RAM note in step 5. SmartScreen blocks lm.exe Expected: the file is not signed — More info → Run anyway (step 6).

For everything not Windows-specific: Troubleshooting, by symptom.

docs.title: Deploy lumnik
docs.text:
Installation

Get the hub running: one command on a single host, or the Helm chart on Kubernetes.

Fastest path

Self-host with Docker Compose and ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build.

What you get

Hub, Postgres, Keycloak, per-install secrets, and real OIDC.

Then do this

Point lm at the hub and log in.

Read this first

Back up the generated .env. Losing LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY makes stored secrets unrecoverable.

Before anything: the prerequisites checklist.
