docs.title: Self-host — one command
docs.text:
On a Windows PC?

Follow Deploy on Windows instead — a from-zero walkthrough, WSL2 and Docker Desktop included, with the expected result spelled out after every step. The commands below are for a Linux or macOS shell.

git clone https://github.com/icreated/lumnik-open.git && cd lumnik-open
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build

This is the open edition

icreated/lumnik-open ingests, fuses, and serves views, processes, workflows, outputs and the métier PWA. It has no chat and no lm ask, and needs no Ollama. See The two editions.

The stack you get:

flowchart LR
  lmop["lm — the integrator"] --> hub
  phone["the métier's phone"] -.->|"https, via the façade"| caddy
  subgraph machine["one machine — docker compose"]
    caddy["caddy — one https origin<br/>(optional TLS façade)"]
    hub["hub :8080<br/>API + PWA at /app/"]
    kc["keycloak :8180<br/>realm lumnik"]
    pg[("postgres<br/>internal")]
    caddy -->|"/*"| hub
    caddy -->|"/realms/*"| kc
    hub --> pg
    hub -.->|"OIDC"| kc
  end

Run it with --build: it compiles the hub inside Docker. The published image is private: the plain pull path works only if your GitHub account was granted access to it. What the launcher does:

1 2 3 The launcher, line by line 
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stand up the self-host lumnik stack (hub + postgres + keycloak) with one command.
# On first run, generates .env with strong random secrets; pulls the published image
# (or --build compiles from source); waits for the hub to be healthy; prints access URLs.
set -euo pipefail

# repo root = two levels up from deploy/selfhost/up.sh
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

# Preflight: every tool this script needs, checked NOW — a missing one must fail
# loud here, not half-succeed at the end. (First real Windows install: a minimal
# WSL Ubuntu lacked curl/python3; the stack came up healthy but both realm
# accounts stayed locked, behind a warn nobody read.)
missing=""
# The full inventory of external commands this script calls (grep-audited) — the
# claim "checked up front" must be true, not approximate.
for tool in docker curl python3 openssl awk grep sed cut mv cp chmod sleep seq dirname basename; do
  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing="$missing $tool"
done
if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
  {
    echo "!! up.sh needs these tools, not found on this machine:$missing"
    echo "   Debian/Ubuntu (incl. WSL): sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y curl python3 openssl gawk"
    echo "   Docker:                    https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/  (on Windows: Docker Desktop, with WSL integration enabled)"
  } >&2
  exit 1
fi
if ! docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "!! Docker is installed but 'docker compose' (v2 plugin) is not available — install the compose plugin, or on Windows enable Docker Desktop's WSL integration" >&2
  exit 1
fi

COMPOSE=(docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml)
BUILD=0
SEARCH_CLUSTER=0
SEARCH=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --build) BUILD=1 ;;
    --search) SEARCH=1 ;;
    --search-cluster) SEARCH_CLUSTER=1 ;;
    -h|--help) echo "Usage: $(basename "$0") [--build] [--search | --search-cluster]   (--build compiles the hub from source instead of pulling; --search is closed-edition only and builds in the PostgreSQL Search provider; --search-cluster, also closed-edition only, builds in the OpenSearch one; both imply --build and exclude each other)"; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown argument: $arg" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

if [[ "$SEARCH" -eq 1 && "$SEARCH_CLUSTER" -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "!! --search and --search-cluster are alternatives (two Search providers on one classpath is refused) — pick one" >&2
  exit 2
fi

if [[ "$SEARCH" -eq 1 ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f docker-compose.search.yml ]]; then
    echo "!! --search is not available in this edition" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  # The published hub image never carries a Search provider: the module is built in, from source.
  BUILD=1
  COMPOSE+=(-f docker-compose.search.yml)
fi

if [[ "$SEARCH_CLUSTER" -eq 1 ]]; then
  if [[ ! -f docker-compose.search-cluster.yml || ! -f deploy/selfhost/search-cluster.sh ]]; then
    echo "!! --search-cluster is not available in this edition" >&2
    exit 2
  fi
  # The published hub image never carries a Search provider: the module is built in, from source.
  BUILD=1
  COMPOSE+=(-f docker-compose.search-cluster.yml)
fi

# 1) ensure .env with secrets (never overwrite an existing one)
if [[ ! -f .env ]]; then
  echo "==> no .env found — generating one with fresh random secrets"
  [[ -f .env.example ]] || { echo "!! .env.example not found — run this from the lumnik repo (the template is at the root)" >&2; exit 1; }
  umask 077  # any file created below (.env.tmp holding the real secrets) is owner-only from the start
  cp .env.example .env
  for key in POSTGRES_PASSWORD KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY LUMNIK_CRYPTO_SECRET_KEY LUMNIK_ENTITY_RESOLUTION_HMAC_SECRET HUBADMIN_PASSWORD INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD LUMNIK_APP_DB_PASSWORD LUMNIK_ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD; do
    secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
    # fill the empty `KEY=` line; awk prints the secret literally (no shell/sed metachar issues)
    awk -v k="$key" -v v="$secret" 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="="} $1==k && $2=="" {print k"="v; next} {print}' .env > .env.tmp
    mv .env.tmp .env
  done
  # Stamp the bootstrap superuser explicitly: the volume freezes this name at first
  # init, and a .env that SAYS which name it froze never needs the probe below.
  printf 'POSTGRES_USER=lumnik\n' >> .env
  chmod 600 .env  # owner-only — these are secrets (cp + redirect would otherwise leave it world-readable)
  echo "    wrote .env (gitignored, mode 600). BACK IT UP — losing LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY makes stored secrets unrecoverable."
else
  echo "==> using existing .env"
  # Older .env files predate the per-install hubadmin/integrator passwords (C1, extended
  # 2026-08-11 to integrator) and the entity-resolution HMAC secret — grow them in place.
  for key in LUMNIK_ENTITY_RESOLUTION_HMAC_SECRET HUBADMIN_PASSWORD INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD LUMNIK_APP_DB_PASSWORD LUMNIK_ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD; do
    if ! grep -q "^${key}=..*" .env; then
      umask 077
      grep -q "^${key}=" .env || printf '%s=\n' "$key" >> .env
      secret="$(openssl rand -base64 32)"
      awk -v k="$key" -v v="$secret" 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="="} $1==k && $2=="" {print k"="v; next} {print}' .env > .env.tmp
      mv .env.tmp .env && chmod 600 .env
      echo "    added $key to .env"
    fi
  done
fi

if [[ "$SEARCH_CLUSTER" -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "==> preparing the search cluster (secrets and per-install TLS)"
  # shellcheck source=deploy/selfhost/search-cluster.sh
  source deploy/selfhost/search-cluster.sh
  search_cluster_prepare
fi

# 2) start the stack
if [[ "$BUILD" -eq 1 ]]; then
  echo "==> building the hub image from source and starting the stack"
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --build
else
  echo "==> pulling images and starting the stack"
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" pull || { echo "!! image pull failed — if the ghcr image is private run 'docker login ghcr.io', or use --build to compile from source" >&2; exit 1; }
  "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d
fi

# Align the live DB roles to .env on every run (P8): first boot's init script already
# used these values (no-op re-set); an older install rotates from the historic
# defaults the moment the keys land in .env. Idempotent — safe every run. Rotation
# is the same gesture: new value in .env, re-run up.sh. SQL rides stdin (never argv);
# values are openssl base64 (no quotes to escape).
echo "==> aligning database role passwords to .env"
pg_cid="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q postgres)"
env_val() { grep "^$1=" .env | cut -d= -f2-; }
# Superuser name: the VOLUME outranks the claim. The name is frozen into PGDATA at first
# init; .env can be silent (older installs) or WRONG (a regenerated .env stamps 'lumnik'
# over a pre-rename volume — deleting .env on a living stack did exactly that). So the
# claimed name is verified against the running database, and discovery runs whenever the
# claim is absent or false. pg_isready ignores auth, so it waits under any name.
pg_super="$(env_val POSTGRES_USER)" || [ $? -eq 1 ]
for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  docker exec "$pg_cid" pg_isready -U "${pg_super:-lumnik}" -d lumnik >/dev/null 2>&1 && break
  sleep 2
done
super_works() { docker exec "$pg_cid" psql -U "$1" -d lumnik -tAc 'SELECT 1' >/dev/null 2>&1; }
if [[ -z "$pg_super" ]] || ! super_works "$pg_super"; then
  if super_works lumnik; then
    pg_super=lumnik
  else
    pg_super=adempiere   # pre-rename volume — the only other name ever bootstrapped
  fi
  # Persist the discovery so compose interpolation and every later run agree with the volume.
  if grep -q '^POSTGRES_USER=' .env; then
    awk -v v="$pg_super" 'BEGIN{FS=OFS="="} $1=="POSTGRES_USER" {print "POSTGRES_USER="v; next} {print}' .env > .env.tmp
    mv .env.tmp .env
  else
    printf 'POSTGRES_USER=%s\n' "$pg_super" >> .env
  fi
  chmod 600 .env
  echo "    discovered bootstrap superuser '$pg_super' from the volume; recorded in .env"
fi
{
  printf "ALTER ROLE lumnik_app PASSWORD '%s';\n"      "$(env_val LUMNIK_APP_DB_PASSWORD)"
  printf "ALTER ROLE lumnik_admin PASSWORD '%s';\n"    "$(env_val LUMNIK_ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD)"
  printf "ALTER ROLE lumnik_readonly PASSWORD '%s';\n" "$(env_val LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD)"
} | docker exec -i "$pg_cid" psql -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$pg_super" -d lumnik \
  && echo "    roles aligned (lumnik_app / lumnik_admin / lumnik_readonly)" \
  || echo "  !! role-password alignment failed — the hub may not reach the DB; inspect: docker exec -it $pg_cid psql -U $pg_super lumnik" >&2

# Grants, schemas and extensions ride every run too (the whole file is idempotent):
# init scripts only run at FIRST volume init, so a volume older than 02-extensions.sql
# never received them — the first one-shot CSV ingest then fails its CREATE SCHEMA with
# "permission denied for database lumnik".
docker exec -i "$pg_cid" psql -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$pg_super" -d lumnik \
  < infra/postgres/init/02-extensions.sql \
  && echo "    grants/schemas/extensions aligned (02-extensions.sql, idempotent)" \
  || echo "  !! grants alignment failed — ingestion may hit 'permission denied'; inspect: docker exec -it $pg_cid psql -U $pg_super lumnik" >&2

# Neither hubadmin nor integrator ships in the realm WITH a credential — C1 posture
# (2026-07-25), extended 2026-08-11 to integrator (RealmAudienceContractTest): a known
# password must never survive an install, and infra/keycloak/*.json is on the
# open-edition allowlist so a static one would become world-readable at the flip. Set
# each one per install from .env via the Keycloak admin API. Failure is fail-closed
# (the user simply cannot log in) — warn, don't abort a healthy stack.
#   $1 = space-separated candidate usernames (aliases for the same logical account —
#        e.g. the pre-rename 'gardenadmin' — the loop heals older realm imports)
#   $2 = .env key holding the password to set
set_realm_user_password() {
  local candidates="$1" pw_key="$2"
  local admin_user admin_pw pw tok uid name
  # `|| [ $? -eq 1 ]` on every .env lookup: KEYCLOAK_ADMIN is a documented-optional key
  # that a fresh .env (copied from .env.example) legitimately lacks — under
  # `set -euo pipefail` an unguarded no-match grep kills the whole script before the
  # :-default or the warn below can run (bit on the first real cloud install,
  # 2026-08-18). Only grep's "no match" (rc 1) is tolerated; a real error (rc 2,
  # e.g. unreadable .env) still fails fast instead of masquerading as "missing".
  admin_user="$(grep '^KEYCLOAK_ADMIN=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)" || [ $? -eq 1 ]; admin_user="${admin_user:-admin}"
  admin_pw="$(grep '^KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD=' .env | cut -d= -f2-)" || [ $? -eq 1 ]
  pw="$(grep "^${pw_key}=" .env | cut -d= -f2-)" || [ $? -eq 1 ]
  if [[ -z "$pw" ]]; then
    echo "  !! $pw_key missing in .env — $candidates stays locked (no password)"; return 0
  fi
  # Password rides stdin (--data-urlencode password@-), never argv — no `ps` leak.
  # Retried: the hub can be healthy while Keycloak is still finishing its first
  # realm import (seen on slow first boots) — give it up to ~25s before warning.
  local attempt
  for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    # --max-time bounds each attempt: a hung connect must not turn the ~25s retry
    # budget into an unbounded stall.
    tok="$(printf '%s' "$admin_pw" | curl -fsS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 -X POST "http://localhost:8180/realms/master/protocol/openid-connect/token" \
        -d grant_type=password -d client_id=admin-cli \
        --data-urlencode "username=$admin_user" --data-urlencode password@- 2>/dev/null \
      | python3 -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("access_token",""))' 2>/dev/null)" || true
    [[ -n "${tok:-}" ]] && break
    [[ "$attempt" -lt 5 ]] && sleep 5
  done
  if [[ -z "${tok:-}" ]]; then
    echo "  !! could not obtain a Keycloak admin token (check KEYCLOAK_ADMIN / KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env) — $candidates stays locked (no password)"; return 0
  fi
  # Realms imported before the rename still carry the legacy 'gardenadmin' user (a realm
  # import is one-shot) — heal it under whichever name this install has.
  for name in $candidates; do
    # Non-fatal like the token call above — a lookup failure must keep the
    # warn-don't-abort contract (set -e would otherwise kill a healthy stack).
    uid="$(curl -fsS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 -H "Authorization: Bearer $tok" \
        "http://localhost:8180/admin/realms/lumnik/users?username=$name&exact=true" 2>/dev/null \
      | python3 -c 'import sys,json;u=json.load(sys.stdin);print(u[0]["id"] if u else "")' 2>/dev/null)" || true
    [[ -n "$uid" ]] && break
  done
  if [[ -z "$uid" ]]; then
    echo "  !! $candidates not found in the lumnik realm — skipped"; return 0
  fi
  PW="$pw" python3 -c 'import json,os;print(json.dumps({"type":"password","temporary":False,"value":os.environ["PW"]}))' \
    | curl -fsS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 -X PUT "http://localhost:8180/admin/realms/lumnik/users/$uid/reset-password" \
        -H "Authorization: Bearer $tok" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @- \
    && echo "  $name: per-install password set ($pw_key in .env)" \
    || echo "  !! $name password set failed — stays locked (no password)"
}

# 3) wait for the hub to be healthy (Flyway runs at boot)
echo "==> waiting for the hub to become healthy (this can take a minute on first boot)"
hub_cid="$("${COMPOSE[@]}" ps -q hub)"
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  status="$(docker inspect --format '{{if .State.Health}}{{.State.Health.Status}}{{else}}none{{end}}' "$hub_cid" 2>/dev/null || echo none)"
  if [[ "$status" == "healthy" ]]; then
    echo "==> hub is healthy"
    set_realm_user_password "hubadmin gardenadmin" HUBADMIN_PASSWORD
    set_realm_user_password "integrator" INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD
    echo ""
    echo "  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)"
    echo "  Keycloak:  http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik"
    echo "  Next:      point lm at the hub — server http://localhost:8080, OIDC http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik"
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 3
done
echo "!! hub did not become healthy in time — inspect with: ${COMPOSE[*]} logs hub" >&2
exit 1
The full self-host README 
# Self-host lumnik

Stand up the whole lumnik stack — hub + PostgreSQL (pgvector) + Keycloak (real OIDC) — on a single
host with Docker. It runs anywhere Docker runs: a laptop, or a VM on any cloud (GCP, AWS, Azure, Scaleway).

## Prerequisites

- Docker + Docker Compose v2 (`docker compose version`).
- The published hub image `ghcr.io/icreated/lumnik-hub` is **private pre-launch** — `docker login ghcr.io`
  authenticates you but grants **no access** unless your GitHub account was added to the package.
  The path that works for everyone: `--build` (compiles from source inside Docker — no image access
  and no local Maven/JDK needed, only Docker; the first build takes a few minutes).
- **For the natural-language layer (RAG chat, semantic search, analytic "ask"):** an
  [Ollama](https://ollama.com) running on the host, with the three models pulled. Without it,
  *structured* ingestion, canonical fusion, and the REST API still work — but the embedding model
  is unreachable, so RAG indexing **skips its chunks** (semantic search/chat return nothing) and
  "ask" has no model to call. The hub reaches the host Ollama via `host.docker.internal`
  (wired in the compose file); override with `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` in `.env` for a remote Ollama.

  ```bash
  ollama serve                      # if not already running
  ollama pull nomic-embed-text      # embeddings (RAG indexing)
  ollama pull llama3.2              # conversational RAG chat
  ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b      # text-to-SQL "ask" (4.7GB — the analytic model)
  # optional: ollama pull gemma4    # used only by an offline evaluation; skip it
  ```

  > **Linux host:** `host.docker.internal` resolves to the **docker bridge IP**, never to
  > the host's loopback — and the Ollama systemd service binds `127.0.0.1` by default, so
  > the hub cannot reach it as installed (Docker Desktop on macOS/Windows routes to the
  > host loopback and masks this). Bind Ollama on the bridge, container-only:
  >
  > ```bash
  > mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
  > printf '[Service]\nEnvironment="OLLAMA_HOST=172.17.0.1:11434"\n' \
  >   > /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/override.conf
  > systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart ollama
  > ```
  >
  > `172.17.0.1` is Docker's default bridge gateway — if you customized the bridge
  > (daemon.json `bip`, rootless), use what
  > `docker network inspect bridge -f '{{(index .IPAM.Config 0).Gateway}}'` prints.
  >
  > Nothing is exposed publicly (172.17.0.1 is only reachable from containers) — but if a
  > host firewall is active, allow the container range in:
  > `ufw allow from 172.16.0.0/12 to any port 11434 proto tcp`. Source-range matching is
  > deliberate: compose networks get their own `br-*` bridges (not `docker0`), so an
  > interface-scoped rule would miss them. The /12 covers Docker's default address
  > pools — narrow it if your host also carries VPN/corporate subnets in that range.
  > The same rule applies to
  > **any** host service the hub must reach through `host.docker.internal`. On a
  > CPU-only box, `Environment="OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1"` in the same override keeps the
  > model loaded — first-question cold loads take tens of seconds otherwise.

## Quick start

```bash
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build   # build from source — works for everyone (the image is private pre-launch)
# ...or, if your GitHub account has access to the published image:
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh           # pull the image, generate secrets, start, wait for healthy
```

On the first run, `up.sh` creates `.env` with strong random secrets (`openssl rand`). When the hub is
healthy it prints the URLs:

- Hub — `http://localhost:8080` (health: `/q/health` — unauthenticated; the `/api/platform/*` API needs a token)
- Keycloak — `http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik`

Then point `lm` at the hub (server `http://localhost:8080`, OIDC `http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik`).

```bash
./deploy/selfhost/logs.sh hub     # tail logs (omit the service name for all)
./deploy/selfhost/down.sh         # stop the stack
./deploy/selfhost/down.sh --volumes   # stop AND delete all data (full reset)
```

## Secrets

`up.sh` writes `.env` (gitignored, mode `600` — owner-only) with its secrets: the Postgres and Keycloak
admin passwords, the two hub encryption keys (`LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY`, `LUMNIK_CRYPTO_SECRET_KEY`),
the entity-resolution fingerprint secret (`LUMNIK_ENTITY_RESOLUTION_HMAC_SECRET`), the hub's three
database-role passwords (`LUMNIK_APP_DB_PASSWORD`, `LUMNIK_ADMIN_DB_PASSWORD`, `LUMNIK_READONLY_DB_PASSWORD`),
and the per-install passwords for the demo realm users (`HUBADMIN_PASSWORD`, `INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD`).
**Back `.env` up** —
losing `LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY` makes secrets stored by the hub unrecoverable. To pin a specific image
version instead of the latest `main` build, set `LUMNIK_VERSION` in `.env` (e.g. `LUMNIK_VERSION=1.0.0`
once a `hub-v*` release is tagged).

## Ports

By default the hub (`8080`) and Keycloak (`8180`) bind to `127.0.0.1` — reachable from the host only.
For a remote host, access them over an SSH tunnel, or see "Going public" below.

## Going public — the TLS façade

To expose lumnik beyond localhost with one HTTPS origin, use the **TLS façade overlay**
(`deploy/tls/`): a single Caddy origin fronting the hub and path-proxying Keycloak under
`/realms` — one issuer for every device. A LAN install gets an internal CA certificate;
setting a public `LUMNIK_TLS_HOST` gets Let's Encrypt automatically.

Runbook: [deploy/tls/README.md](../tls/README.md) — also summarized on the
[deploy page](../../docs/deploy.md).

## Postgres bootstrap user

Postgres runs with the superuser **`lumnik`**, recorded in `.env`. On every run `up.sh` checks that name
against the database volume and corrects `.env` if they differ. No action needed.

## Backup & restore

Nightly-able backup (hot pg_dump + Keycloak store) and restore, including onto a
fresh machine: `backup.sh` / `restore.sh` here — full runbook at
[docs/operations/backup-restore.md](../../docs/operations/backup-restore.md).
Back up `.env` separately: it holds the master key.

## Switching the AI off (optional)

`LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false` in `.env`, then re-run `up.sh` with the flags you installed with: the chat, the ask and the embeddings
stop, the PWA drops its Chat tab, `lm module list` shows `rag` and `llm` as `INACTIVE`, and the
data is kept. Exactly `true` or `false`; absent means on. What a switch back on does and does not
restore: [Switching the AI off](../../docs/rag/models.md#switching-the-ai-off).

## Email delivery (optional)

Rules (`lm notify add`) route matching events to email. Delivery is **mocked until both
of these knobs are set** in `.env` (set only one and the hub WARNs at boot):

```bash
LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
# optional: LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=587 LUMNIK_SMTP_USERNAME=… LUMNIK_SMTP_PASSWORD=… LUMNIK_SMTP_FROM=…
```

The delivery drill, end to end, with the bundled dev mailer:

```bash
docker compose --profile mailpit -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d
# .env: LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=mailpit  LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=1025  LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d hub
lm notify add --events 'decision.*' --to you@example.com
# trigger a decision (or lm integration test on a rule-matched type), then open:
# browse to http://127.0.0.1:8025 — the sent mail, visible
```

Stop / tail logs: deploy/selfhost/down.sh, deploy/selfhost/logs.sh.

The bundled Keycloak

  • Tokens are verified for real; the Keycloak runs start-dev on a file-H2 store, for a single-host install. Its backup: Backup & restore.
  • For your own directory (Keycloak, Okta, Entra ID): Bring your own IdP. JIT provisioning for an external issuer is not in the open edition.

docs.title: Generate secrets safely
docs.text: It creates an owner-only (mode 600) .env with fresh random secrets — Postgres, Keycloak admin, both crypto keys, the entity-resolution secret, the three database-role passwords, HUBADMIN_PASSWORD and INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD. It never overwrites an existing .env. Back it up.

docs.title: Build and start the stack
docs.text: It builds the hub image (--build) or pulls it, starts hub + Postgres + Keycloak, and waits for the hub to be healthy. The first boot can take a minute.

docs.title: Mint per-install passwords
docs.text:
It sets the hubadmin and integrator passwords in Keycloak and prints the URLs.

You know it worked when: the launcher ends like this:

==> hub is healthy
  hubadmin: per-install password set (HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env)
  integrator: per-install password set (INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env)

  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)
  Keycloak:  http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
  Next:      point lm at the hub — server http://localhost:8080, OIDC http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik

docs.title: One HTTPS origin — the TLS façade
docs.text:
The base stack is loopback-only http. An optional overlay puts one Caddy origin in front of everything — the hub (API + the /app/ PWA) at /, Keycloak path-proxied under /realms/* — so every device sees one origin and one token issuer, which is what installing the PWA on a phone requires. One command layers it on:

LUMNIK_TLS_HOST=erp.example.com \
  docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml up -d
  • A public LUMNIK_TLS_HOST gets a Let's Encrypt certificate automatically.
  • A LAN IP or localhost gets Caddy's internal CA for local testing.
  • Unlike the base compose, the overlay binds 443/80 on all interfaces by default, for phones on the LAN. LUMNIK_TLS_BIND restricts it.
  • Re-running up.sh later composes the base file alone and un-stacks the overlay (the hub reverts to the localhost issuer) — on a façade install, always follow an up.sh run with the overlay command above.

Certificates, trusting the internal CA on a phone, and the change-of-issuer caveat:

The full TLS façade README 
# TLS façade — one https origin for the self-host stack

Caddy in front of everything: the hub (API + the `/app/` PWA) at `/`, Keycloak
path-proxied under `/realms/*` + `/resources/*`. One origin means no mixed content,
no CORS, and **one token issuer for every device**.

> **Exposure:** unlike the base compose (loopback-only), this overlay binds 443/80 on
> **all interfaces** by default, so phones on the LAN can reach it. Restrict it with
> `LUMNIK_TLS_BIND` (e.g. `LUMNIK_TLS_BIND=127.0.0.1` behind your own reverse proxy, or a
> specific LAN address).

```bash
LUMNIK_TLS_HOST=erp.example.com \
  docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml up -d
# → https://erp.example.com        (hub + PWA)
# → https://erp.example.com/realms/lumnik   (Keycloak)
```

Layer it LAST when combining overlays — its `QUARKUS_OIDC_TOKEN_ISSUER` must win.

## Certificates, automatically

| `LUMNIK_TLS_HOST` | Certificate |
|---|---|
| a public domain | Let's Encrypt, obtained and renewed by Caddy (ports 80+443 reachable) |
| a LAN IP / localhost | Caddy's internal CA — for local testing |

## Trusting the internal CA (LAN testing)

Browsers warn on the internal CA until you trust its root. Extract it from the
running container and install it on the device (iOS: AirDrop the file, then
*Settings → General → VPN & Device Management*, and enable full trust under
*Certificate Trust Settings*):

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml \
  cp caddy:/data/caddy/pki/authorities/local/root.crt ./lumnik-local-ca.crt
```

With the root trusted, the PWA gets its full powers on the phone: the real install
prompt, `crypto.subtle`, service workers. (Without it you can still browse past the
warning, but the browser will not install the PWA.)

## What the overlay changes

- **Keycloak** honors `X-Forwarded-*` (`KC_PROXY_HEADERS`) and announces the façade
  origin in every URL it mints (`KC_HOSTNAME`); the hub keeps its internal
  back-channel (`keycloak:8180`, `KC_HOSTNAME_BACKCHANNEL_DYNAMIC`).
- **The hub** validates tokens against the façade issuer and honors forwarded headers.
- Nothing else moves: the plain-http workflow (`http://localhost:8080`) keeps working
  for a same-machine operator without this overlay.

## Things to know

- **Bare-IP clients send no SNI** (RFC 6066 forbids it), and without a `default_sni`
  global option Caddy matches no certificate and aborts every handshake with TLS
  alert 80. The shipped Caddyfile sets it.
- **Re-running `up.sh` silently un-stacks the overlays.** `up.sh` composes the base file
  alone, so the hub is recreated with the localhost issuer and every externally-minted
  token is refused until the overlay command runs again. On a façade install, bringing
  the stack up is a two-step gesture — `up.sh`, then
  `LUMNIK_TLS_HOST=erp.example.com docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml -f docker-compose.tls.yml up -d`
  (plus any other overlays you run; TLS last, its issuer must win).
- **Changing the public origin changes the token issuer — and orphans JIT-provisioned
  identities.** They are keyed `(idp_issuer, idp_subject)`; after a move to https the
  same human is a NEW identity, and that first login fails on the existing login name. Migrating an install to TLS means
  migrating identities too: update `idp_issuer` on existing rows, or accept
  re-provisioning by clearing the old-issuer users. Pick the origin once, early.

docs.title: Point lm at the hub
docs.text:
Install lm, then give it the server and the OIDC issuer — nothing else:

lm config set-context local \
     --server http://localhost:8080 \
     --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
lm config use-context local
lm login        # prints a URL + device code — open it, sign in as integrator
User Tenant Password in .env integrator 1 INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD — change it before anything real hubadmin (superadmin) 11 HUBADMIN_PASSWORD

--oidc-client-id defaults to lm-cli, the bundled realm's client; set it only for your own IdP. Check the login — on a fresh hub, headers only:

$ lm connector list
NAME  TYPE  TENANT  SCHED  WINDOW  STATUS  LAST RUN

docs.title: Pin the hub image instead of tracking main
docs.text:
Set LUMNIK_VERSION in .env. The generated file ships the line commented out (#LUMNIK_VERSION=main) — uncomment it, give it the tag you want (once a hub-v* release is tagged), and re-run the launcher:

./deploy/selfhost/up.sh

Result: the stack runs ghcr.io/icreated/lumnik-hub:$LUMNIK_VERSION instead of the rolling main build. up.sh never rewrites an existing .env, so the line survives every re-run.

docs.title: Point the hub at an Ollama that is not on this machine
docs.text: Uncomment the OLLAMA_BASE_URL=… line in .env and re-run up.sh. Left unset, the hub looks for Ollama on the machine running Docker (http://host.docker.internal:11434). The open edition does not use Ollama.

docs.title: Switch the AI off
docs.text:
The chat, the ask and the embeddings stop; the data is kept, and the PWA drops its Chat tab. The value is exactly true or false.

Install Gesture Self-host LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false in .env, then re-run up.sh with the flags you installed with (--build, --search…). Re-apply the TLS overlay after it if you use one. A plain docker compose restart keeps the old setting. Helm, first install LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false ./deploy/helm/up.sh (chart value ai.enabled) Helm, running cluster helm upgrade <release> deploy/helm/lumnik --reuse-values --set-string ai.enabled=false, then kubectl rollout restart deployment/<release>-hub. up.sh refuses to run on a running cluster — see Kubernetes / Helm

Check it with lm module list: rag and llm read INACTIVE disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled. What a switch back on restores: Switching the AI off.

docs.title: Turn on email delivery
docs.text:
Notification rules (lm notify add) route matching events to email. Delivery is mocked until both of these knobs are set in .env:

LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=smtp.example.com
LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
# optional: LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=587  LUMNIK_SMTP_USERNAME=…  LUMNIK_SMTP_PASSWORD=…
#           LUMNIK_SMTP_FROM=lumnik@example.com  LUMNIK_SMTP_STARTTLS=REQUIRED

Re-run up.sh, then check the boot log:

docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml logs hub | grep -E 'email delivery|LUMNIK_SMTP'
# email delivery live via smtp.example.com
Set Result host + LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false live delivery host only nothing delivered; the boot log warns LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false only sends to localhost; the boot log warns

To rehearse without a provider, start the bundled dev mailer:

docker compose --profile mailpit -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d
# .env: LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=mailpit  LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=1025  LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false

Result: rule-matched events land as mail — visible at http://127.0.0.1:8025 on the Mailpit drill, or in the recipient's inbox. On Helm the same knobs are values.smtp.* (up.sh reads the same LUMNIK_SMTP_* variables). A failed send is not retried — see Email notifications.

docs.title: Reach the hub from another machine
docs.text: The hub (8080) and Keycloak (8180) listen on 127.0.0.1 only. Two ways in: an SSH tunnel, or the TLS façade — the one a phone needs to install the PWA.

docs.title: Run against a managed or external PostgreSQL
docs.text: Not a knob on this path — the self-host stack wires the hub to its own Postgres container (DB_URL is fixed in docker-compose.selfhost.yml). An external database is the Kubernetes / Helm path's job — the next section.

docs.title: Kubernetes / Helm
docs.text: The cloud edition (commercial) ships a Kubernetes/Helm path — hub + Postgres + Keycloak with real OIDC, sealed secrets, and a managed-PostgreSQL mode. It is not part of this repository.

docs.title: The two editions
docs.text:
lumnik ships as two builds:

Build Licence What it does lumnik-open Apache-2.0, public repository ingest, fuse, react, serve the métier apps lumnik Pro commercial adds Ask (natural-language chat over your data), model providers and the external-identity loop

The open build has no Ask door at all: no stub, no licence key. One exception: direct Search has its commands in every build, and without a provider they answer not installed (see Feature by feature).

lumnik Open is the build behind the free Hub tier; lumnik Pro is the build behind both paid tiers — see Three tiers, two builds.

flowchart LR
  subgraph open["lumnik-open — the open edition (Apache-2.0)"]
    direction TB
    conn["Connectors — CSV · JDBC ·<br/>REST / GraphQL / SOAP"]
    tables[("Multi-tenant hub —<br/>RLS on every row")]
    ent["Entities — fused,<br/>conflicts kept"]
    apps["Views · Apps · Processes ·<br/>Workflows · Inbox · PWA"]
    out["Outputs — webhooks ·<br/>email · event registry"]
    sdoors["Search doors — declare · query<br/>answer <i>not installed</i> without a provider"]
    askcore["Ask pipeline + five guards —<br/>native, <b>no door onto it</b>"]
    conn --> tables --> ent --> apps
    tables --> out
  end
  subgraph closedx["closed extensions — what lumnik Pro adds"]
    direction TB
    doors["Chat + semantic search"]
    llm["Model providers — Ollama, …"]
    searchp["Search providers — PostgreSQL ·<br/>OpenSearch (opt-in build)"]
    kafka["kafka connector"]
    jit["JIT provisioning + SCIM"]
  end
  doors -.-> askcore
  llm -. powers .-> doors
  searchp -. "indexes declared entities" .-> sdoors
  kafka -. "one more connector" .-> conn
  jit -. "external-IdP logins" .-> tables

docs.title: Feature by feature
docs.text:
lumnik Open lumnik Pro Connectors: CSV (SFTP/S3), JDBC, REST + GraphQL/SOAP shapes ✓ ✓ Connector: kafka — ✓ JDBC dialect: Oracle (driver included) — ✓ Fusion: entities, _conflicts ledger ✓ ✓ Apps ladder: views, processes, workflows, inbox, métier PWA ✓ ✓ Outputs: webhooks (signed, journaled, replay), email notifications ✓ ✓ lm CLI / TUI, manifests, the whole integrator surface ✓ ✓ Multi-tenancy & RLS, audit trail, backup, rate-limited view-generate ✓ ✓ Search: declare an index (kind: SearchIndex), the search and capability doors — a hub without a provider answers not installed ✓ ✓ Search provider: PostgreSQL (-Psearch) or OpenSearch / Elasticsearch (-Psearch-cluster) — built in on request, never in the published image; it also brings the PWA's Recherche tab — ✓ opt-in build Ask: chat & analytic text-to-SQL doors, semantic search, rag.chunk store — ✓ Model providers (Ollama & friends) — ✓ JIT provisioning for external IdPs — ✓ SCIM deprovisioning — ✓ Chat rate-limit buckets (no such endpoints) ✓

The five ask guards are in every build; the open edition has no chat door onto them and no model behind them.

Switched off is not absent. A Pro hub can run with the AI switched off (LUMNIK_AI_ENABLED=false): the data is kept, and lm module list shows rag and llm as INACTIVE. An Open hub does not list them at all. Neither shows a Chat tab. How to switch it: Choosing what your hub offers.

docs.title: Which edition am I running?
docs.text:
$ lm module list
NAME      VERSION  SCHEMA              STATUS    REASON
core      0.1.0    Platform            ACTIVE    
identity  0.1.0    Identity & Tenancy  ACTIVE    
llm       0.1.0    Model provider      INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
rag       0.1.0    Platform RAG        INACTIVE  disabled:lumnik.ai.enabled
What you see Build core + identity only lumnik Open plus rag + llm (always together) lumnik Pro — INACTIVE means the AI is switched off, as above plus search_pg or search_opensearch a build with a Search provider

The hub's boot log lists the installed modules too. More: the full answer.

docs.title: Three tiers, two builds
docs.text:
The commercial ladder has three tiers; the builds are two:

Tier Runs the build Who operates it Hub — free, installed on your own machines lumnik Open your integrator, exploring and tooling up Pro lumnik Pro your integrator, running it for a client Enterprise — on quote lumnik Pro your own IT, in your own world

Enterprise is the Pro build, sold with your identity directory (external IdP, SCIM), a Kubernetes delivery and service commitments. These pages mark a capability "not in the open edition" — the build you can check with lm module list, not the tier.

Prices: contact@lumnik.fr. The open edition is the same hub, so an evaluation can start there.

docs.title: Email notifications
docs.text: A rule routes matching events to a recipient — one mail per event, rendered through a template you choose. Needs the lm_admin role. For tools rather than people, use a webhook.

docs.title: Route events to a mailbox
docs.text:
# The métier case: every minted decision, to the ADV inbox, in métier words
lm notify add --events 'decision.*' --to adv@example.com --template decision-alert

# The ops case: failed runs, to the integrator, raw payload included
lm notify add --events 'connector.run.failed' --to integrator@example.com

lm notify list
lm notify rm <ID>

$ lm notify add --events 'connector.run.failed' --to integrator@example.com
rule 1000: connector.run.failed → integrator@example.com
$ lm notify list
ID    EVENTS                RECIPIENT               TEMPLATE            ENABLED
1000  connector.run.failed  integrator@example.com  event-notification  true
  • --events takes an exact type or a prefix ending in .* — see the event registry.
  • One table only: no lm flag narrows a rule to one table. Over HTTP (POST /api/notifications) a rule takes an entity_filter with the table's full name (connector.t_customers); any other form is refused.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Templates are Qute HTML files at templates/email/<name>.html inside the hub. The rule picks one by name (--template), in kebab-case only; an unknown name is logged and the mail skipped.

$ lm notify add --events 'decision.*' --to adv@example.com --template '../x'
Error: API error 400: template must match [a-z0-9-]+ (a template name, not a path)

Two ship with the hub:

Template Voice Body event-notification (default) ops subject + source/entity/time line + the payload as JSON in a <pre> decision-alert métier the process message as headline ("Commande 12045 bloquée depuis 32 jours"), entity & key, the referenced fields as a table

docs.title: The variables a template sees
Add your own template
docs.text: Drop templates/email/<kebab-name>.html into the hub's resources and rebuild — templates ship inside the hub image; there is no runtime upload. Rehearse against the Mailpit drill before pointing rules at it.

docs.title: Delivery — what to expect
docs.text:
• Sweep: every 5 s, independent of webhooks.
  • Mocked until the deploy sets the SMTP knobs (turn on email delivery); the boot log says which.
  • Best-effort: a failed send is logged and skipped — no retry, no journal. One broken recipient does not block the others.
  • A hub crash can lose a batch of mails; it never sends one twice.

When delivery must be provable, wire a webhook as well.

docs.title: Mail the ADV every time an order gets blocked
docs.text:
One rule declares the watch, one rule routes the mail — the French sentence you write in the manifest is the headline the ADV reads:

# commande-bloquee.yaml — same shape as the WOW's lyon-process.yaml
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Process
metadata:
  name: commande-bloquee
spec:
  scope: ventes
  on:
    event: data.row.changed
    table: connector.t_commandes
  when:
    - statut=BLOQUEE
  emit:
    type: decision.commande-bloquee
    message: "Commande {num} bloquée ({montant} €)"

lm process apply -f commande-bloquee.yaml
lm notify add --events decision.commande-bloquee --to adv@example.com --template decision-alert

Result: the next ingestion run that lands a statut=BLOQUEE row sends a mail whose headline is Commande 12045 bloquée (8 400 €) — with num and montant in the fields table, because the message referenced them.

docs.title: Rehearse without a mail provider
docs.text:
docker compose --profile mailpit -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml up -d
# .env: LUMNIK_SMTP_HOST=mailpit  LUMNIK_SMTP_PORT=1025  LUMNIK_SMTP_MOCK=false
./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build    # re-run with the flags you installed with
# then browse to http://127.0.0.1:8025

Result: every rule-matched event lands in Mailpit's inbox, rendered exactly as your provider would send it — templates included.

docs.title: Show only the fields that matter
docs.text:
A template is ordinary HTML around the variables — this one renders two columns and nothing else:

<!-- templates/email/commande-courte.html -->
<h2>{payload.message ?: eventType}</h2>
<p>N° <strong>{payload.fields.num ?: '—'}</strong> · {payload.fields.montant ?: '—'} €</p>

Rebuild the hub (templates ship in the image), then point the rule at it: lm notify add --events decision.commande-bloquee --to adv@example.com --template commande-courte.

docs.title: kind: Entity — resolve
docs.text:
When two systems share no key, resolution: gives each real customer one identity. It matches rows rule by rule, keeps what it cannot decide for you to review, and takes your correction over any rule.

Kind Entity, with a resolution: block instead of match: Apply lm entity apply — lm_admin Resolve, correct lm entity resolve, lm entity assert-same, lm entity assert-distinct — lm_admin Review lm entity ambiguous, lm entity history — lm_user, scope-bound Edition Open

Use match: when every system carries the same customer code. Use resolution: when they don't: the ERP knows C-003, the CRM knows contact 9003, and only the email address ties them together.

docs.title: Quickstart — land, apply, resolve
docs.text:
Two small exports. The ERP has four customers. Two of them share one mailbox (compta@groupe-rhone.example). The CRM has five contacts with no ERP code, and one of them has no email at all.

code,name,email
C-001,Hydraulique Lyon,contact@hydraulique-lyon.example
C-002,Fixations Milano,ventes@fixations-milano.example
C-003,Filtration Lyon,compta@groupe-rhone.example
C-004,Levage Lyon,compta@groupe-rhone.example

contact_id,company,mail
9001,HYDRAULIQUE LYON,Contact@Hydraulique-Lyon.example
9002,Fixations Milano,ventes@fixations-milano.example
9003,Groupe Rhône,compta@groupe-rhone.example
9004,Transmission Aarhus,
9005,Pneumatique Porto,geral@pneumatique-porto.example

The manifests read the files from /tmp/acme-resolution/ on the hub's filesystem; no lm command places a file there. Copy them in, then land both sources:

docker exec lumnik-hub-1 mkdir -p /tmp/acme-resolution
for f in docs/entities-resolution/*.csv; do docker cp "$f" lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/acme-resolution/; done
lm apply -f docs/entities-resolution/10-erp.yaml
lm apply -f docs/entities-resolution/20-crm.yaml
lm connector run res-erp
lm connector run res-crm

$ lm run list --connector res-crm
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
3139233c  res-crm    default   Completed  5   5    0        0             2026-10-19 01:47  2026-10-19 01:47

The entity declares one rule: same email address, compared in lower case.

# 30-customer.yaml — one Customer across the ERP and the CRM, which share no key.
# The two are matched on the email address, compared in lower case.

kind: Entity
name: Customer
scopes: [sales]
sources:
  - table: t_res_erp
    map:
      code: code
      name: name
      email: email
  - table: t_res_crm
    map:
      contact_id: crm_id
      company: name
      mail: email
resolution:
  identity:               # the column that identifies a row in each source
    t_res_erp: code
    t_res_crm: crm_id
  cascade:
    - id: email
      exact:
        fields: [email]
        normalize: [lower]

Apply it, then resolve it once. After that, every source run that ends Completed or Partial resolves the rows it wrote. A Failed or Cancelled run is covered by the next lm entity resolve.

$ lm entity apply -f docs/entities-resolution/30-customer.yaml
Applied entity "Customer" → connector."v_customer"

$ lm entity resolve Customer
rows seen: 9
resolved: 7
ambiguous: 1
unresolved (no rule): 1
unresolved (provider): 0
newly minted: 5
provider calls: 0
provider failures: 0
rule hits:
  customer:email: 8

$ lm entity get Customer
CODE   NAME                 EMAIL                             CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-001  Hydraulique Lyon     contact@hydraulique-lyon.example  9001    {"name": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "Hydraulique Lyon"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "HYDRAULIQUE LYON"}], "email": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "contact@hydraulique-lyon.example"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "Contact@Hydraulique-Lyon.example"}]}
C-002  Fixations Milano     ventes@fixations-milano.example   9002    {}
C-003  Filtration Lyon      compta@groupe-rhone.example               {}
C-004  Levage Lyon          compta@groupe-rhone.example               {}
       Groupe Rhône         compta@groupe-rhone.example       9003    {}
       Pneumatique Porto    geral@pneumatique-porto.example   9005    {}
       Transmission Aarhus                                    9004    {}
  • 9001 joined C-001 even though the CRM writes the address in capitals: the rule compares in lower case. Where the two systems still disagree on a value, the row says so in _conflicts, exactly as with match:.
  • 9003 stayed on its own. Its address belongs to two ERP customers, and the rule cannot choose between them. It is ambiguous, and an ambiguous row is never merged.
  • 9004 stayed on its own. It has no email, so no rule could even try. Nothing is lost: the row is still there, waiting for a better rule or a correction.
  • 9005 is a new customer known only to the CRM. It gets an identity of its own.

A row already resolved is never moved silently. If a later pass would join it to a different customer (the data changed, or so did a rule), the row becomes ambiguous and waits for you. Only a correction moves it.

docs.title: Review what it could not decide
docs.text:
$ lm entity ambiguous Customer
IDENTITY_REF                          SOURCE     SOURCE_ID  CANDIDATES                                                                 DECIDED_BY  OCCURRED_AT
8b8d23db-749e-48d8-a256-e7fbcd268022  t_res_crm  9003       2e8eb5e3-d246-456a-a0a4-cda4d2e5260a,519ee7f9-d04c-4a56-ba6f-33517b107294  automatic   2026-10-19 01:47

lm entity history NAME SOURCE ID explains any decision, one line per pass:

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_crm 9003
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME    RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                                                                 SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID
2026-10-19 01:47:52  AMBIGUOUS  email            2e8eb5e3-d246-456a-a0a4-cda4d2e5260a,519ee7f9-d04c-4a56-ba6f-33517b107294             automatic

C-004 shares C-003's mailbox but comes from the same ERP. One customer never holds two rows of the same source, so C-004 got its own identity, and its history shows the one it was set aside from:

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_erp C-004
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME   RULE  PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                            SET_ASIDE                             DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID
2026-10-19 01:47:52  RESOLVED                  2e8eb5e3-d246-456a-a0a4-cda4d2e5260a  519ee7f9-d04c-4a56-ba6f-33517b107294  automatic

docs.title: Correct it
docs.text:
You know that Groupe Rhône is the billing name of Filtration Lyon. Say so, naming each row as SOURCE:ID, then resolve:

$ lm entity assert-same Customer --left t_res_crm:9003 --right t_res_erp:C-003 --reason "Groupe Rhône is Filtration Lyon's billing name"
recorded: t_res_crm:9003 and t_res_erp:C-003 are same

$ lm entity resolve Customer
rows seen: 9
resolved: 8
ambiguous: 0
unresolved (no rule): 1
unresolved (provider): 0
newly minted: 0
provider calls: 0
provider failures: 0
rule hits:
  customer:email: 7

$ lm entity get Customer --filter crm_id=9003
CODE   NAME             EMAIL                        CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-003  Filtration Lyon  compta@groupe-rhone.example  9003    {"name": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "Filtration Lyon"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "Groupe Rhône"}]}

The history records the correction as asserted. Since #1343 it also names who asserted it and why, in the ASSERTED_BY and REASON columns. ASSERTED_BY shows the reviewer's login, or the stored user id when that user no longer exists. In -o json the fields are assertedBy (the id), assertedByLogin and reason; all three are null on every other event. The capture below predates those columns:

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_crm 9003
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME    RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                                                                 SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID
2026-10-19 01:47:52  AMBIGUOUS  email            2e8eb5e3-d246-456a-a0a4-cda4d2e5260a,519ee7f9-d04c-4a56-ba6f-33517b107294             automatic
2026-10-19 01:47:57  RESOLVED                    519ee7f9-d04c-4a56-ba6f-33517b107294                                                  asserted
  • A correction outranks every rule and survives every later run and resolve.
  • It takes effect at the next resolve: a run of one of the sources, or lm entity resolve.
  • Two rows of the same source can't be the same customer: such an assertion is refused (400).

To undo it, assert the opposite, then resolve. C-003 stops being a candidate for 9003; only C-004 is left, so the pass joins 9003 to C-004:

$ lm entity assert-distinct Customer --left t_res_crm:9003 --right t_res_erp:C-003
recorded: t_res_crm:9003 and t_res_erp:C-003 are distinct
$ lm entity resolve Customer
…
$ lm entity get Customer --filter crm_id=9003
CODE   NAME         EMAIL                        CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-004  Levage Lyon  compta@groupe-rhone.example  9003    {"name": [{"src": "t_res_erp", "value": "Levage Lyon"}, {"src": "t_res_crm", "value": "Groupe Rhône"}]}

If that is wrong too, assert it distinct as well.

A row is named as the history names it. A mistyped one is refused: 

$ lm entity assert-same Customer --left t_res_crm:9030 --right t_res_erp:C-003
Error: API error 404: entity 'Customer' has no row t_res_crm:9030 — check it with lm entity history Customer t_res_crm 9030, or run lm entity resolve Customer if the row is new

docs.title: Every run resolves on its own
docs.text:
Add C-005,Pneumatique Porto,geral@pneumatique-porto.example to the ERP file and run the ERP again. The new row joins the CRM's 9005 with no other gesture:

$ lm connector run res-erp
run scheduled: dbdc0745-1ba9-446c-89cb-ff65d71e9e0d

$ lm entity get Customer --filter crm_id=9005
CODE   NAME               EMAIL                            CRM_ID  _CONFLICTS
C-005  Pneumatique Porto  geral@pneumatique-porto.example  9005    {}

$ lm entity history Customer t_res_erp C-005
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME   RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                            SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID
2026-10-19 01:48:01  RESOLVED  email            4295e78e-360a-4198-a74a-1b20d7bf1977             automatic   dbdc0745-1ba9-446c-89cb-ff65d71e9e0d

Run lm entity resolve NAME yourself after applying the entity, after changing its rules, and after a correction.

docs.title: In the TUI
docs.text:
Type :ambiguous, then the entity name and Enter: the screen lists the same rows as lm entity ambiguous.

  • Enter on a row loads its history.
  • Ctrl-R resolves the entity again.
  • r refreshes the list.

Corrections are made in :entities: Enter on the entity, m marks a row, = (same) or ! (distinct) on another, then Ctrl-R to resolve — see The TUI.

docs.title: With joins and Search
docs.text:
• joins[] work on a resolution: entity too. They are read on top of the resolved customers: each row gets the lookup's value. A key that the lookup holds more than once leaves the joined column empty and lists those rows in _conflicts; it never picks one.
  • A SearchIndex indexes one document per resolved customer.
  • A row nothing has decided yet (ambiguous, or with no rule) is not a document until it is decided.
  • A change in a lookup table re-indexes every customer whose rows hold the changed key.
  • A document's freshness (asOf) waits for the resolution. It moves only once the resolution pass has covered every run that wrote the entity's sources, and once the lookup tables have been read.
  • A Failed or Cancelled run holds asOf back until the next lm entity resolve.

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
Key What it says resolution.identity for each source table, the column that identifies one of its rows (t_res_crm: crm_id) — one column per source, every source listed resolution.cascade the rules, tried in order — at least one cascade[].id the rule's name, shown in the history cascade[].exact.fields canonical columns that must be equal — several fields must all be equal cascade[].exact.normalize how values are compared: lower, upper, remove-diacritics, strip-invisible, fix-mojibake, replace-smart-quotes, decode-html-entities, titlecase, clean. Here clean only removes a leading byte-order mark: it does not trim spaces cascade[].propose asks an external candidate provider (provider, acceptAbove, reviewAbove). No provider ships today, so such a rule leaves its rows unresolved (provider)

Rules run in order, and a later rule can settle what an earlier one left ambiguous. The same entity with a second rule on the name, applied as Customer2: a CRM contact Levage Lyon (9007) at the shared mailbox is ambiguous by email, then resolved to C-004 by name:

cascade:
  - id: email
    exact: { fields: [email], normalize: [lower] }
  - id: name
    exact: { fields: [name], normalize: [lower] }

$ lm entity history Customer2 t_res_crm 9007
OCCURRED_AT          OUTCOME    RULE   PROVIDER  CANDIDATES                                                                 SET_ASIDE  DECIDED_BY  RUN_ID
2026-10-15 15:04:03  AMBIGUOUS  email            b82d893a-9ff5-4de0-8f9f-a8893a375d04,f969ba42-8c76-403e-8a93-d5998bff3d4e             automatic
2026-10-15 15:04:03  RESOLVED   name             b82d893a-9ff5-4de0-8f9f-a8893a375d04                                                  automatic
  • match: and resolution: are two ways to fuse; an entity declares one or the other.
  • _entity_id, _resolution, _source_id, _handle and _canonical_key are reserved column names.
  • A resolved entity is read like any other: lm entity get, lm view, lm ask, an export, a SearchIndex.

docs.title: Operating it
docs.text:
• LUMNIK_ENTITY_RESOLUTION_HMAC_SECRET is required: the hub does not start without it. deploy/selfhost/up.sh generates it; with Helm, set secrets.entityResolutionHmacSecret. Changing it forces a full re-resolve at the next lm entity resolve and breaks open view page links. Back it up with your other secrets.
  • After upgrading the hub, apply each resolution: entity again with the same manifest, then run lm entity resolve NAME.
  • LUMNIK_ENTITY_RESOLUTION_BATCH_SIZE (default 500) sets how many rows a pass reads at a time.
