docs.title: Parcours — the guided path
docs.text:
Guided onboarding

From an empty machine to a running hub, a fused entity, a métier chat that cites its sources, and a workflow that flags what stopped moving — in three half-days.

Audience

An integrator or tester discovering lumnik — nothing assumed beyond Docker and a terminal.

Format

Three half-days. Every step gives a goal, the page to follow, and a checkpoint.

The spirit

Do the steps — don't just read them.

Before you start

Docker, a terminal, and Ollama for the steps marked Pro. Go 1.26+ only if you build lm yourself. The full list: Prerequisites.

The one rule

Run every command from the repository root unless a page says otherwise.

git clone https://github.com/icreated/lumnik-open.git && cd lumnik-open

That repository is the open edition. A step marked Pro needs lumnik Pro with the AI on (the chat, lm ask, the models); on the open edition, read it and skip its checkpoint. See The two editions.

docs.title: The three half-days at a glance
docs.text:
Half-day 1 Defrost reading

Deploy the hub, meet lm, run the WOW, and prove that ingestion stayed read-only and lost nothing.

Six steps, ≈ 3 h

Half-day 2 Defrost reasoning

Understand entities, the ask guards, scopes, models, and the TUI an integrator operates from.

Six steps, 3 h

Half-day 3 Defrost time

Move from a mirror of the source to views, processes, workflows, inbox decisions, and the métier PWA.

Six steps, ≈ 3 h 15

docs.title: Half-day 1 — defrost reading
docs.text:
Goal of the day: legacy data flows into the hub, read-only, and you can prove nothing was lost.

1 10 min The pitch

Read the Home page: what lumnik is (a read-only defrost of legacy systems) and what it is not (not a migration, not a BI project).

You know it landed when: you can explain why lumnik is neither a migration nor a BI project.

2 30 min Deploy the hub

Decide what the hub carries — The two editions, Choosing what your hub offers. Then follow Deploy lumnik: ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh. Your credentials are in the .env it writes.

You know it worked when: the script ends like this:

==> hub is healthy
  hubadmin: per-install password set (HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env)
  integrator: per-install password set (INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD in .env)

  Hub:       http://localhost:8080   (health: /q/health)
  Keycloak:  http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
  Next:      point lm at the hub — server http://localhost:8080, OIDC http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
3 20 min Meet lm

Follow the 60-second Quickstart: install lm, log in, put a first file into the hub.

You know it worked when: lm connector list shows the connector your first file registered.

$ lm connector list
NAME         TYPE      TENANT  SCHED  WINDOW  STATUS  LAST RUN
stock_count  csv-file  1
4 60–90 min The WOW

Read The WOW, step by step, then replay it with The WOW, hands-on: a SOAP Siebel and a CSV fused into one Customer.

You know it worked when: lm entity get customer lists the fused customers. Pro: a question asked in French answers with the SQL it ran.

5 30 min How a connector is built

Read Connectors overview and CSV & files, the manifest you just used. Every source type follows the same grammar.

You know it landed when: you can explain the relationship between manifest, endpoint, and ingestion report.

6 20 min What was ingested, skipped, quarantined

Read Seeing what was ingested, skipped, and quarantined.

You know it worked when: on your own run, lm run get shows IN = OUT + SKIPPED, and DEAD-LETTERS never exceeds SKIPPED.

$ lm run get f0466804
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
f0466804  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-09-05 05:38  2026-09-05 05:38
⚠ 2 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run f0466804-0824-4eb4-8aa2-54e263dccafe

docs.title: Half-day 2 — defrost reasoning
docs.text:
Goal of the day: the ingested data answers questions — sources shown, and only to the people entitled to ask.

1 40 min Fuse sources into one truth

Read Entities — fuse and read the Customer entity you applied during the WOW.

You know it worked when: you find the _conflicts ledger and can say why C-200 is in it.

$ lm entity get customer --filter customer_code=C-200
CUSTOMER_CODE  NAME   SEGMENT  EMAIL   CITY  _CONFLICTS
C-200          Marie  SILVER   m@x.fr  Lyon  {"name": [{"src": "cust_siebel", "value": "Marie"}, {"src": "t_cust_csv", "value": "MARIE A."}]}
2 30 min The five guards · Pro

Read Ask honesty — the five guards: when lm ask refuses to answer, and what it says.

You know it worked when: you can name the guard that stops a hallucinated table name.

3 30 min Scopes

Read Scopes: a scope is declared on the connector or entity (scopes:) and granted as a Keycloak role scope:<tag>. No scope role = tenant-wide; one or more = bound.

The bundled realm has no scope-bound user: create one in Keycloak with the realm role scope:desk (Add a user, Grant a métier scope).

To work as that second user, give lm a second context. Open the login link in a private browser window: a normal window signs you in as integrator again.

lm config set-context desk --server http://localhost:8080 \
    --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
lm config use-context desk
lm login

lm config use-context selfhost switches back to integrator.

You know it worked when: a user holding only scope:desk is refused the customer entity (scope clients), and a user holding scope:clients reads it.

$ lm entity get customer          # as a user holding scope:desk
Error: access refused (403): scope not granted
4 20 min Models & providers · Pro

Read Models & providers: which model answers, and how to swap it (local Ollama or a remote provider).

You know it worked when: you know whether your install answers from Ollama or a remote provider.

5 40 min The integrator's cockpit

Skim the CLI & TUI reference, then open the TUI with lm ui: type :runs and Enter, pick a run with the arrow keys, press d to describe it. ? lists every key.

You know it worked when: you can find any connector run and its report using only the TUI.

6 20 min Who may do what

Read Roles & permissions and skim RLS & database roles.

You know it worked when: signed in as hubadmin (tenant 11, password HUBADMIN_PASSWORD in .env), you see none of tenant 1's decisions from the WOW.

Give lm a hubadmin context and sign in as in step 3 (private window), then:

$ lm inbox --all
ID  WHEN  PROCESS  MESSAGE  ENTITY_KEY

docs.title: Half-day 3 — defrost time and the apps
docs.text:
Goal of the day: the hub stops being a mirror and starts finding things — and each métier gets a surface.

1 30 min Views — see

Read Views and save the WOW's view: lm view apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml.

You know it worked when: lm view list lists it and a user holding scope:clients renders it.

$ lm view list
NAME          SCOPE    TITLE
clients-desk  clients  Clients
$ lm view clients-desk --filter city=Lyon
Clients · city=Lyon

Code client  Nom            Ville  Segment
C-200        Marie          Lyon   SILVER
C-500        Claire Martin  Lyon   
C-800        Albert Camus   Lyon   
C-900        Saint Exupery  Lyon
2 30 min Processes — react

Read Processes: declarative reactions to data.row.changed, always refusable, never writing to the source.

You know it landed when: you can say what emits the event and what may refuse the action.

3 45 min Workflows — declare the lifecycle

Read Workflows: a declared lifecycle over a status column, and a dormancy threshold that turns a document left unmoved into an alert.

You know it worked when: lm workflow apply reports EN LITIGE as an undeclared value. Pro: the métier chat answers a lifecycle question from your declared graph.

4 20 min Inbox — decide

Read Inbox: where decision.* events (including decision.dormant.<workflow>) wait for a human, and lm inbox ack that closes them.

You know it worked when: an acked decision leaves lm inbox and shows [acked] in lm inbox --all.

5 30 min The métier PWA

Read The métier PWA, then:

  • open https://<your-host>/app/ — cards on a phone, a table on a tablet;
  • a phone cannot reach your laptop's localhost: put the TLS façade in front first;
  • choose each app's tabs with one line of its manifest: spec.tabs.

You know it worked when: you see the same scope boundary on the phone and on the desktop.

6 40 min Run it for real

Read Backup & restore and Upgrade, and practise both before you need them.

You know it worked when: ./deploy/selfhost/backup.sh ends with ==> done: <folder> and you know where that folder is.

docs.title: If you get stuck
docs.text:
Common stumbles:

  • Wrong directory. Commands assume the repository root. When a relative path fails, check where you are before checking anything else.
  • The first minute is not an outage. Right after the stack starts, the hub can briefly answer 401 or refuse connections. Wait a minute and retry before diagnosing.
  • The ghost binary. After rebuilding lm, run lm version. If it prints an old build, your PATH serves a stale copy — prefer a symlink to your build over cp.
  • Credentials. Everything is generated at install time into the .env next to up.sh. If a login page surprises you, the answer is in that file.
  • Ollama pulls one model at a time. One ollama pull <model> per line, and make sure ollama serve isn't already running before starting it again.

If a step does not match what you see, report it — it is a documentation bug.

docs.title: The reference shelf
docs.text:
Everything not on the walk above, for when you need it.

More source types — same manifest grammar as CSV: JDBC · REST · GraphQL · SOAP · Kafka inbound · Transform at ingestion

Integrations & API — HTTP API for ask · Admin API

Enterprise identity — Bring your own IdP · SCIM deprovisioning

Day-2 operations — Observability · Rate limits · Sizing & load tests

Deploying at scale — the cloud edition (commercial) ships a Kubernetes/Helm path; not part of this repository.

docs.title: How lumnik breathes — from frozen rows to decisions
docs.text: What happens when something changes in the source, and who is told.

docs.title: The moment this page is about
docs.text: A commande slips into EN LITIGE in the 02:00 batch. The row lands, a declared rule turns it into a decision seconds later, and your webhook pings the team's phone at 02:01 — before the client calls at 9:04.

docs.title: The chain, end to end
docs.text:
The chain in one picture:

flowchart LR
  erp[("legacy source")] -->|"your ingestion cron"| row["a new row lands<br/>(mirror table)"]
  row -->|"same transaction"| ev["an event —<br/>new rows only"]
  ev -->|"≤ 5 s"| proc["your declared rule<br/>when: statut=EN LITIGE"]
  proc --> dec["decision.litige"]
  dec --> inbox["Décisions tab<br/>lm inbox"]
  dec -->|"≤ 5 s, retried"| hook["your webhook →<br/>the tool that pings phones"]
  sweep["dormancy sweep<br/>every 15 min"] -->|"a document that STOPPED moving"| dec2["decision.dormant.*"]
  dec2 --> inbox
  dec2 --> hook
  inbox -->|"✓ Traiter"| ack["acked — an event,<br/>timestamped, with who"]
  • Only new rows emit. A re-ingested, unchanged row emits nothing. A table emits only once a rule, a webhook or a notification subscribes to it.
  • jdbc, CSV and kafka connectors emit. Tables ingested over REST, GraphQL or SOAP emit no event: a rule on them never fires.
  • Every rule emits decision.<your-name> — the prefix is enforced at apply.
Clock Value rule, webhook and email consumers every 5 s webhook retry sweep every 30 s, 3 attempts in total; journal in lm outputs list dormancy sweep every 15 min your ingestion the connector's own spec.schedule — the slow clock

docs.title: Where a human meets it — the channels
docs.text:
Channel What it does Mode Décisions tab (PWA, phone & desktop) the pile, newest first, badge on open; a treated decision stays visible, dimmed ✓ traité pull — it waits for you to open it lm inbox / TUI inbox page the same pile for keyboard people (untreated only, by default) same pull Your webhook (n8n, Make, your own endpoint) every subscribed event, in seconds, retried, journaled, replayable — the road to a Teams message or an SMS push. lm integration add; forwards from registration onward, never retroactively Email (lm notify add) one mail per matching event, payload included live once the deploy sets the SMTP knobs (Email notifications); a failed send is not retried

The inbox is per métier, not per person. Everyone holding a métier's scope sees all of its decisions; a user with no scope:* role sees every decision. There is no assignment, escalation or out-of-office.

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN   PROCESS             MESSAGE                             ENTITY_KEY
8   10min  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Camille Roux à Lyon  ff1027320a1acbe2646ce1b2d1e4a42111868a75bb30825dc4609d785e6aaa7f
$ lm inbox ack 8
acked.
$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN  PROCESS  MESSAGE  ENTITY_KEY

docs.title: The gesture: what ✓ Traiter is, and is not
docs.text:
• It clears the decision from everyone's untreated pile and shows who took it.
  • It is an event — annotation.decision.acked, timestamped, with who — that a webhook can forward.
  • It never writes to your source system (Reversibility): the correction itself is made in the legacy screen.

docs.title: Silence also emits
docs.text:
Rules catch what happens. The dormancy sweep catches what stopped happening: a declared workflow watches every document, and one that sits non-terminal past its threshold becomes decision.dormant.<workflow>.

  • The threshold counts from lumnik's first observation of the document, not from the source's history.
  • lm workflow apply names every status value your manifest missed, with its row count. An undeclared status is watched too.
$ lm observations stats
WORKFLOW            WATCHED  DORMANT  MEDIAN_DETECTION_S
commande-lifecycle  7        5        900

MEDIAN_DETECTION_S is the median time, in seconds, from a document's observed last move to its alert.

docs.title: What remains, three months later
docs.text:
Events — decisions and acks — are kept 30 days by default (LUMNIK_EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS). Three things outlive that window:

What Where to look the observation tape: every watched document — first seen, in its state since, alerted when lm observations list (--workflow NAME for one); per workflow: lm observations stats your webhook target: forward decision.* and annotation.* to the tool that keeps your proof your tool, on your retention the ingested tables themselves lm entity get, lm view

Wire the webhook on day one

It forwards from registration onward, never retroactively. If an auditor may ask "prove this alert was handled", register it the day you deploy.

docs.title: Named limits, in one place
docs.text:
• No push to métier surfaces — the tab and the CLI are pull; the webhook is the road to tools that push. (An event stream does exist for integrators, on the platform API.)
  • The inbox is per métier, time-ordered, without assignment or severity.
  • ✓ Traiter never writes to the source.
  • Webhooks forward from registration onward, never retroactively.
  • REST/GraphQL/SOAP-ingested tables emit no events — only jdbc, CSV and kafka ingestion does.
  • Declared status aliases (encours/EC…) serve the dormancy watch and the chat's background knowledge, not the chat's SQL or view filters: those match the literal values in the column.
  • Email is best-effort — a failed send is logged and skipped: no retry, no journal. Delivery stays mocked until the deploy sets the SMTP knobs. Webhooks retry and journal.
  • No usage/adoption dashboard — operational metrics (/q/metrics) are the only proxy, per endpoint, if your ops scrape them.

docs.title: Reversibility & exit
docs.text: If you stop using lumnik in two years, what do you get back, in what format — and what was never at risk in the first place?

docs.title: What was never at risk
docs.text:
Your source system. Stopping lumnik changes nothing in it:

  • databases — the connection account needs SELECT only, and there is no write path back (Architecture → Read-only first);
  • file sources — a CSV connector's after_process: move|archive|delete moves or deletes files on the drop zone you declared, nothing else (CSV & files).

No vendor copy to reclaim. Self-hosted, the data never left your infrastructure; the exit below runs on your own machines.

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
Asset Format How you take it The ingested mirror Plain PostgreSQL 16 tables in schema connector — ordinary columns, no application-layer encryption (what is and isn't encrypted) Any PostgreSQL client, or the dump below Fused entities SQL views over those tables (connector.v_*) Query the views, or lm entity export NAME -o FILE (CSV) while the hub runs The whole database A standard pg_dump -Fc — the same artifact the backup script produces (nightly once you install the documented cron; nothing schedules it for you) pg_restore into any PostgreSQL 16+ with the pgvector extension available (the rag schema needs it — or exclude that schema on restore), with or without lumnik Your configuration The YAML manifests In your repository for the files you applied; everything else is in the dump, and fetchable as YAML while the hub runs — see below The RAG corpus rag.chunk rows: chunk text in clear + pgvector embeddings The text is portable; see the embeddings caveat below

Fetch the configuration back as YAML while the hub runs:

Kind Command Connector lm connector get NAME — its stored definition, in the hub's own field names Entity no lm command returns the manifest; it is in the dump View lm view get NAME -o FILE Workflow lm workflow get NAME App lm app get NAME Export lm export get NAME Process no lm process get — the TUI's :processes, e on the row, opens the stored manifest 
$ lm entity export AcmeCustomer -o customers.csv
AcmeCustomer: 1099 bytes written to customers.csv (sha256 afa5c455ceaf9a2c6e0fae54b2fbc9b671893f22220c2c2c6a685969c0deceb5)

User accounts and the audit journal are in the same database, so the same dump carries them. Ask/chat history is not stored server-side (the trace is in each response). The exit artifact is the backup you already take.

docs.title: Two caveats to plan around
docs.text:
• Stored secrets die with the master key. Connector/webhook credentials and tenant secrets are pgcrypto-encrypted under LUMNIK_SECRET_MASTER_KEY / LUMNIK_CRYPTO_SECRET_KEY; individual secrets can be re-entered (rotated) at any time, but the master keys have no rotation or re-encryption tooling, and a lost key makes the stored values unrecoverable (the warning). For an exit this is usually irrelevant — the credentials point at your systems and you hold the originals — but export anything you'd miss before decommissioning.
  • Embeddings are model-bound. The vectors in rag.chunk only mean something to the embedding model that produced them (Models). Treat the chunk text as the portable asset; a future system re-embeds it with its own model.

docs.title: What leaving looks like, concretely
docs.text:
1. ./deploy/selfhost/backup.sh one last time — lumnik.dump is your data, complete.
  2. Keep the manifests you version in git where they live; guided-flow config is in the dump (or fetch it back as YAML while the hub still runs).
  3. pg_restore the dump wherever your next tool reads PostgreSQL — or just keep it as the archived, queryable record of what the mirror held.
  4. Decommission the stack. Your source system never noticed lumnik arriving; it will not notice it leaving.

docs.title: Where lumnik stands
docs.text:
beta. Nobody outside the lumnik team has run lumnik in production yet.

The latest release (v1.8.0) added:

  • entity resolution, one identity across systems that never shared a key;
  • managed exports, lumnik's first outbound path;
  • queued runs;
  • views read page by page beyond 1 000 rows (Views).

docs.title: What is deliberately not there
docs.text:
Each line is a decision, declared on the page of its surface and gathered here.

Surface What is not there Declared in GraphQL mutations, subscriptions, schema-introspection discovery, persisted queries, query batching, per-endpoint header overrides, on_error: warn GraphQL — Not yet supported REST mode: api_cursor — declaring it behaves like full; per-endpoint headers, which belong at spec.headers REST SOAP SOAP 1.1 envelopes only — a service that requires SOAP 1.2 (application/soap+xml) is refused SOAP Kafka (Pro) JSON only — no Avro, Protobuf or Schema Registry; one topic per connector, no filtering by key or header; no mapping block, so no hooks at ingestion; no pre-flight test; SASL/SCRAM, mTLS and OAuth Kafka — Limitations Transformers validate-row after split-row, and aggregator on a csv-file run — both refused at lm apply, with the arithmetic reason Transformers Events REST-, GraphQL- and SOAP-ingested tables are event-silent — the respiration rides jdbc, CSV and kafka ingestion How lumnik breathes Chat declared status aliases feed the dormancy watch and the chat's background knowledge, not the chat's SQL or a view's filters — the chat matches the literal values in the column How lumnik breathes Workflows the transition journal's retention is unbounded, and the dormancy sweep costs the database a full pass over the source table every tick Workflows Exports CSV only, one entity per export, mode: snapshot only (no delta, no resume); SFTP and S3 only; four formatters, a row filter with equals/in only; no back-fill of missed slots, no automatic retry Exports — Not in this version Search a row deleted straight from an ingested table — or by lm endpoint purge on a connector-schema hybrid target — stays searchable until the index is rebuilt SearchIndex — Rows deleted directly in the database SCIM (Pro) no /Groups; no bulk, sorting, etags or changePassword; no pagination beyond the two eq filters; not the full PATCH path grammar; no /Schemas or /ResourceTypes SCIM — Not supported Identity SAML-only IdPs are not supported by direct trust — front them with a broker and point lumnik at the broker Bring your own IdP Encryption rotating the master key. Rotating one secret's value is supported, and stamps rotated_at RLS and encryption

Kafka and SCIM are in the Pro build only: see The two editions.

docs.title: What is not finished
docs.text:
Known, and not yet closed — you may meet them:

  • A few 409 refusals do not name what holds the name — e.g. which integration took it.
  • The live event tail can miss an event when transactions run long. Webhooks and the inbox do not.
  • lm secret rm frees the name, but the stored row stays, encrypted.

docs.title: When beta goes away
docs.text: When What is not finished is empty and someone outside the lumnik team has run lumnik in production. To be that first outside run, start with the guided path.

docs.title: The WOW, step by step
docs.text:
Show, don't explain

A SOAP Siebel and a CSV become one canonical Customer — served over REST, then asked in natural language. The files below are the demo's real files.

What you will see

Connectors, entity fusion, sourced answers, and the first operational rungs above them.

Best reader

Someone who wants value before deep reference.

Then do this

Replay the same flow by hand on the deployed stack.

Why it matters

One fused customer shows what the hub does.

Read this one, run the other one

This page is the narrated WOW. To run it, follow The WOW, hands-on — same files, on the self-host stack, with the fake-siebel.py stub.

Three steps need lumnik Pro with the AI on:

  • §4, the ask;
  • §5's lm view generate (elsewhere it answers no chat model is available on this hub);
  • §8's lifecycle question to the chat.

Every other step runs on the open edition. See which edition you installed.

docs.title: 1. A SOAP source
docs.text:
The first source is a fake Siebel SOAP connector. The manifest:

# Source 1 — the "legacy CRM": our fake Siebel over SOAP CustomerQueryPage.
# kind: soap is a request-shape on the HTTP engine (connector_type stays rest-generic).
# Lands canonical hub table connector.cust_siebel — the manifest fuses on its promoted columns.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: siebel-customers
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [demo]                  # the same métier as its CSV sibling: one bound user, both sources
spec:
  # fake-siebel.py runs on the HOST. From the hub container (self-host stack) reach it via
  # host.docker.internal; if you run the hub with `quarkus:dev` on the host, use localhost:8077.
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8077
  endpoints:
    - id: customers
      kind: soap
      path: /eai
      soap_action: CustomerQueryPage
      body: |
        <In><PageSize>{{page_size}}</PageSize><StartRowNum>{{cursor}}</StartRowNum></In>
      pagination:
        kind: soap
        page_size: 100
        last_page_path: "$.Body.Out.LastPage"
        response_path: "$.Body.Out.ListOfCustomer.Customer"
      incremental:
        mode: full
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: connector.cust_siebel
        unique_key: "$.CustCode"
        promote:
          - { name: customer_code, path: "$.CustCode", type: text }
          - { name: name,          path: "$.Name",     type: text }
          - { name: segment,       path: "$.Segment",  type: text }

lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/siebel-connector.yaml
lm connector run siebel-customers   # applying declares it; this is what reads the source

docs.title: 2. A CSV source
docs.text:
The second source is a CSV export carrying the same customer universe from another angle.

# Source 2 — the "flat-file export": a CSV the second system spits out nightly.
#
# For csv-file connectors the hub table name is NOT configurable: it is
#   connector.t_<slug(metadata.name)>
# i.e. a hardcoded `t_` prefix + the slugified connector name. So:
#   metadata.name: cust-csv   ->   connector.t_cust_csv
# (that's the table the entity manifest fuses against). `target` is optional and carries
# only `indexes` — there is no table_prefix knob for csv-file.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: cust-csv                     # -> connector.t_cust_csv
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [demo]
spec:
  transport:
    kind: local
    # Path AS SEEN BY THE HUB. On the self-host stack the demo folder is mounted at /demo
    # (docker-compose.wow.yml); with `quarkus:dev` on the host, use ./customer.csv.
    path: /demo/customer.csv
  parser:
    has_header: true                 # header row drives the column names (code, cname, email, ville)
  after_process: none                # leave the source file in place

Its data:

code,cname,email,ville
C-100,Jean Dupont,jd@x.fr,Paris
C-200,MARIE A.,m@x.fr,Lyon
C-300,Solo,solo@x.fr,Nice
C-500,Claire Martin,claire@x.fr,Lyon
C-600,Pierre Corneille,corneille@x.fr,Paris
C-700,Maurice Druon,druon@x.fr,Paris
C-800,Albert Camus,camus@x.fr,Lyon
C-900,Saint Exupery,exupery@x.fr,Lyon

lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/csv-connector.yaml
lm connector run cust-csv

Both runs must be Completed before you fuse:

$ lm run list
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT   STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
9ef96149  cust-csv          default    Completed  8   8    0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
4197d406  siebel-customers  customers  Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38

The CSV manifests read /demo/…, a path inside the hub container, mounted by the overlay docs/demo/wow-customer/docker-compose.wow.yml. Without it the run reports Completed with IN=0 OUT=0.

docs.title: 3. Fuse into one canonical customer
docs.text:
The entity manifest declares how both sources match and merge:

# The hero entity: one Customer fused from the two legacy sources on customer_code.
# Siebel is listed first, so on a disagreement Siebel is the representative and the CSV
# value is preserved in the _conflicts ledger (nothing is silently dropped).
kind: Entity
name: Customer
description: "A customer, fused from the Siebel CRM and the nightly CSV export."
match: [customer_code]
scopes: [clients]               # the métier(s) whose chat can ask about this entity
columns:                        # grounding fed to the chat + human labels a kind:View renders
  customer_code:
    label: "Code client"        # shown by kind:View instead of the raw canonical name
  name:
    label: "Nom"
  segment:
    label: "Segment"
    description: "Commercial segment."
    values: [GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE]   # the domain — a filter on any other value is REFUSED, not run
  city:
    label: "Ville"
    description: "Billing city (free text, French city names)."
    example: "Lyon"
sources:
  - table: cust_siebel          # source 1 (SOAP/Siebel) — promoted columns
    map:
      customer_code: customer_code
      name: name
      segment: segment
  - table: t_cust_csv           # source 2 (CSV export) — header columns
    map:
      code: customer_code
      cname: name
      email: email
      ville: city

$ lm entity apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/customer-entity.yaml
Applied entity "Customer" → connector."v_customer"
$ lm entity get customer --filter customer_code=C-200
CUSTOMER_CODE  NAME   SEGMENT  EMAIL   CITY  _CONFLICTS
C-200          Marie  SILVER   m@x.fr  Lyon  {"name": [{"src": "cust_siebel", "value": "Marie"}, {"src": "t_cust_csv", "value": "MARIE A."}]}

Siebel and the CSV disagree on C-200's name: Siebel's value wins (it is listed first), and both are kept in _conflicts.

docs.title: 4. Ask it (Pro)
docs.text:
lm ask --scope clients "combien de clients à Lyon ?"
# → the answer, computed over the fused Customer, with the SQL that ran beneath it

docs.title: Act 2 — the data starts working for you
docs.text:
(The chain, the channels and the named limits: How lumnik breathes.)

See React Decide Remember

docs.title: View
docs.text: Render the fused customer as a declarative, read-only list — reference.

docs.title: Process
docs.text: Emit a decision when a new Lyon customer lands — reference.

docs.title: Inbox
docs.text: Let a human acknowledge the event with an idempotent action — reference.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text: Teach the substrate lifecycle and dormancy so silence becomes a signal — reference.

docs.title: 5. See it (kind: View)
docs.text:
# The first per-métier app surface: a list over the fused Customer entity (scope: clients).
# Read-only, card-backed — every column must exist in the clients SchemaCard or the render is refused.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: View
metadata:
  name: clients-desk
spec:
  scope: clients
  table: connector.v_customer
  title: "Clients"
  columns: [customer_code, name, city, segment]

$ lm view -f docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml --filter city=Lyon
Clients · city=Lyon

Code client  Nom            Ville  Segment
C-200        Marie          Lyon   SILVER
C-500        Claire Martin  Lyon   
C-800        Albert Camus   Lyon   
C-900        Saint Exupery  Lyon

Or describe the view and let the AI write it (Pro). The same checks apply: an unknown column is refused, and so is a request the scope cannot answer:

lm view generate clients "les clients gold avec leur ville et segment" -o gold.yaml
cat gold.yaml            # the first line is the ready-to-run render command
lm view -f gold.yaml --filter 'segment=GOLD'

docs.title: 6. React to it (kind: Process)
docs.text:
When a new Lyon customer lands, emit a decision — your webhooks (n8n here) receive it:

# The dragon's first rung, PROVEN LIVE: when a new customer from Lyon lands in the CSV,
# emit a decision event. The effect IS the event — delivery rides the existing webhook
# subscriptions (n8n/Make/Zapier), zero new code.
#
# Why `ville` and scope `demo` (not `segment`/`clients`): a process triggers on
# data.row.changed, born at the RAW write path — so on.table is the raw ingest table
# `connector.t_cust_csv`, and its columns are the CSV's own (code, cname, email, ville).
# `segment` is a Siebel field, absent from the CSV. The raw table lives in the `demo` scope
# card (the csv connector is tagged `demo`); the fused `clients` card names only v_customer.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Process
metadata:
  name: lyon-client-arrive
spec:
  scope: demo
  on:
    event: data.row.changed
    table: connector.t_cust_csv
  when:
    - ville=Lyon
  emit:
    type: decision.lyon-client-arrive
    message: "Nouveau client {cname} à {ville}"

lm process apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/lyon-process.yaml
# or create it in the TUI: `:new` → Process — the same living example opens in $EDITOR

docs.title: 7. Decide (inbox → ack)
docs.text:
A process fires only on a new row — not on rows already ingested, not on a re-run of the same file. Add a Lyon customer, then re-run the connector:

echo 'C-400,Camille Roux,camille@x.fr,Lyon' >> docs/demo/wow-customer/customer.csv
lm connector run cust-csv

Pick a code the file does not carry (C-400 is free) and ville = Lyon. A few seconds after the run, the decision is in the inbox; the human acks it:

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN      PROCESS             MESSAGE                             ENTITY_KEY
8   just now  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Camille Roux à Lyon  ff1027320a1acbe2646ce1b2d1e4a42111868a75bb30825dc4609d785e6aaa7f
$ lm inbox ack 8
acked.
  • MESSAGE is the process's "Nouveau client {cname} à {ville}", filled from the row.
  • ENTITY_KEY is the row's content hash, not a customer code.
  • Acking twice answers acked. twice and records one ack.

docs.title: 8. Declare the lifecycle (kind: Workflow)
docs.text:
A workflow declares what a status column means: the states, their aliases, which are terminal. It is declared over real rows, so this act brings its own source — a commandes export with dirty statuses:

# Act 3 source — the commandes export: the same nightly CSV habit as csv-connector.yaml,
# now landing the raw table the workflow act declares a lifecycle over.
#
# For csv-file connectors the hub table name is NOT configurable: it is
#   connector.t_<slug(metadata.name)>
# i.e. a hardcoded `t_` prefix + the slugified connector name. So:
#   metadata.name: commandes-csv   ->   connector.t_commandes_csv
# (that's the table commande-workflow.yaml's spec.on.table names). `target` is optional and
# carries only `indexes` — there is no table_prefix knob for csv-file.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: commandes-csv                # -> connector.t_commandes_csv
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [demo]
spec:
  transport:
    kind: local
    # Path AS SEEN BY THE HUB. On the self-host stack the demo folder is mounted at /demo
    # (docker-compose.wow.yml); with `quarkus:dev` on the host, use ./commandes.csv.
    path: /demo/commandes.csv
  parser:
    has_header: true                 # header row drives the column names (num, client, statut, date_expedition)
  after_process: none                # leave the source file in place

lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/commandes-connector.yaml
lm connector run commandes-csv       # lands connector.t_commandes_csv — seven commandes

Apply the workflow after the run: over a table that does not exist yet the apply still succeeds, but reports nothing.

# Declare the document lifecycle of a column instead of teaching the chat its values by
# hand: states + labelled aliases (Excel reality is dirty: "en cours"/"encours" both mean
# the same thing) + a transition graph. provenance MUST be `declared` — v1 accepts no
# other value. `on.table`/`on.column` name the raw ingest column whose values this
# taxonomy explains; apply reports the data-truth confrontation: undeclared VALUES found
# in the data (reality, never refused — 'EN LITIGE' is one) and unobserved CODES declared
# but never seen.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: commande-lifecycle
spec:
  scope: demo
  provenance: declared
  # the sweep alerts a non-terminal commande observed unchanged past 30 days —
  # observation-relative, see docs/apps/workflows.md
  dormancy:
    after: 30d
  on:
    table: connector.t_commandes_csv
    column: statut
    key: num
  states:
    - code: BROUILLON
      initial: true
    - code: EN_COURS
      label: "En préparation"
      aliases: [en cours, encours]
    - code: TERMINE
      aliases: [fini]
      terminal: true
  transitions:
    - { from: [BROUILLON], to: EN_COURS }
    - { from: [EN_COURS], to: TERMINE }

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/commande-workflow.yaml
{"name":"commande-lifecycle","scope":"demo","table":"connector.t_commandes_csv","column":"statut","dataTruth":{"undeclared":[{"value":"EN LITIGE","rows":2}],"unobserved":[],"nullOrBlank":0,"tableMissing":false,"keyColumnMissing":false,"keyNullOrBlank":0,"checkUnavailable":false,"unavailableReason":null}}

EN LITIGE is in the column and in no declared state: the apply names it, with its row count, and succeeds. On Pro, the chat then answers lifecycle questions from the declared graph.

The manifest also declares spec.on.key: num and spec.dormancy.after: 30d: a sweep alerts on every commande left unmoved in a non-terminal state for 30 days.

  • The 30 days count from lumnik's first observation of the commande, not from the source's history.
  • To see it fire without waiting, set after: 1m in your own copy; the sweep runs every 15 minutes.
  • The alert lands in lm inbox under workflow:commande-lifecycle — full wording in Dormancy.

With after: 1m, two sweeps after the run:

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN      PROCESS                      MESSAGE                                                                                                                              ENTITY_KEY
23  just now  workflow:commande-lifecycle  CMD-007: observed unmoved in "EN LITIGE" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in commande-lifecycle  CMD-007
22  just now  workflow:commande-lifecycle  CMD-006: observed unmoved in "EN_COURS" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in commande-lifecycle   CMD-006
21  just now  workflow:commande-lifecycle  CMD-005: observed unmoved in "EN LITIGE" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in commande-lifecycle  CMD-005
20  just now  workflow:commande-lifecycle  CMD-004: observed unmoved in "BROUILLON" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in commande-lifecycle  CMD-004

CMD-002 and CMD-003 never alert: they are TERMINE, a terminal state. CMD-005 and CMD-007 sit in the undeclared EN LITIGE, which is never terminal, and alert like the others. See Dormancy.

docs.title: After the demo — your data
docs.text:
The same road on the customer's own data:

  1. Point at the real database. lm source jdbc test checks the connection, discover lists tables with row estimates, add creates one connector per table. A SELECT-only account is enough (the guided flow).
  2. Repair at the door. Transformers fix mojibake and legacy dates; a workflow apply names the dirty statuses it finds.
  3. Tag a scope, run, ask. The run writes the scope's schema card; then the chat answers on the customer's rows (what makes a scope answerable).

What takes calendar time is outside lumnik: the SELECT account, the network path. The chat needs lumnik Pro (which edition includes what) and pulled models.

docs.title: Continue hands-on
docs.text: Continue with the by-hand replay on the self-host stack, with the fake-siebel.py stub and the demo credentials.

docs.title: ADR 0001: Search backend strategy — first provider (D1)
Status
docs.text:
Accepted (D1 only) — 2026-09-28.

D3 (cluster target) and D4 (cluster client) are not decided by this ADR. They remain open and are deferred to when #672 (the scale-out cluster adapter) is scheduled — see Deferred.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Optional Pro search across ingested data (#649) needs a backend behind the provider-neutral IndexedSearchPort (#668). #670 framed three decisions: which provider ships first (D1), the cluster target if a cluster is involved (D3), and the cluster client (D4). The constraint that frames all three: Pro must run without Elasticsearch/OpenSearch by default — a cluster must never be the price of entry, and Search stays an explicit packaging choice (#702).

Two candidate "first provider" tickets already existed before this ADR: #705 (a PostgreSQL-native provider) and #672 (a cluster adapter for OpenSearch/Elasticsearch). Each names the other as its fallback slot depending on D1.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
D1: the first Search provider is PostgreSQL-native (#705).

The cluster adapter (#672) becomes the scale-out provider, built afterward — it starts after #674 (the provider contract suite), instead of taking the first slot.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL-native reuses pg_trgm, unaccent, fuzzystrmatch and tsvector — all already present in the pgvector/pgvector:pg16 image used by DevServices, selfhost and helm. Zero new infrastructure to ship the first provider.
  • Isolation comes from RLS by construction, the same guarantee every other tenant table already gets, queried on the default datasource.
  • It de-risks the rest of the chain: #671 (projection lifecycle), #673 and #674 (contract suite) can all be built and proven against the existing pgvector DevServices before any new container lane exists.
  • The #669 matching vocabulary (exact / text / fuzzy / prefix) maps cleanly onto PostgreSQL primitives without needing a cluster's analyzer pipeline.
  • The #704 relevance-corpus harness informs this decision (it can measure PostgreSQL-native's baseline quality directly) but does not block it, per #670's own framing.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: • The known limit stated on #705 — projection writes and GIN maintenance share the primary database's resources — needs a measured sizing envelope (#704 + a loadtest/ scenario). That measurement, and the decision of when an installation should graduate to #672, was split out of #672 into #750 (2026-09-30), not restated here.

docs.title: 705 is unblocked and proceeds as scoped, against this ADR as an accepted constraint.
672 is the scale-out provider: it starts after #674, not right after #671. Its own body already reflects this ordering.
Deferred
docs.text:
D3 (cluster target — OpenSearch vs Elasticsearch) and D4 (cluster client — one shared adapter on the common JSON REST subset vs vendor-specific clients) are not decided by this ADR. #670's own non-goal states: "No production client dependency or backend module in this ticket" — and no cluster module is being designed now.

These two decisions will be settled when #672 is actually scheduled, the same way #672 already settles its own open decision (D14, index topology) "in spec" at build time. #670 stays open, scoped down to D3/D4, until then.

docs.title: 649 (search: optional Pro search across ingested data without RAG)
670 (backend strategy — this ADR resolves its D1 only)
672 (opt-in cluster adapter — now the scale-out provider)
ADR 0002: Search cluster target and client (D3/D4)
Status
docs.text: Accepted — 2026-09-30. Completes ADR 0001, which deferred D3 and D4 to the scheduling of #672.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The scale-out Search provider (#672) needs a cluster target (D3) and a client (D4). Pro must keep running without any cluster; the cluster stays an explicit packaging choice (#702).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
D3 — OpenSearch is the shipped target (2.x and 3.x; Apache-2.0, redistributable container). Elasticsearch 8.x/9.x is a test-matrix line, supported for customers who already operate a cluster; we do not bundle it.

D4 — one adapter on the JSON REST subset common to both families (index/mappings, _bulk, _aliases, _count, _delete_by_query, _search with bool.filter + multi_match/fuzziness + highlight + terms aggregations), over the JDK HttpClient and Jackson. The distribution and version are probed at boot (GET /) and checked against the supported matrix; an unsupported one is reported degraded, never a boot crash.

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text:
• Elasticsearch's licences (AGPLv3 / SSPL / ELv2 since 2024) are avoided in anything we redistribute; connecting to a customer's cluster is a separate matter.
  • The Elasticsearch Java client refuses non-Elastic servers and opensearch-java targets OpenSearch only: vendor clients would force two adapters and a heavy opt-in classpath. The common subset makes Elasticsearch a matrix line rather than a second module.
  • Authorization is a query input (#668), so no document-level-security plugin is required.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Module lumnik-search-opensearch; a required feature that leaves the common subset (vectors/kNN, #675) reopens D4.
  • The supported-version matrix is exercised by the container-backed IT lane of the Search lanes, run before each release (#1285).
  • Index topology (D14) and everything else is in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-30-search-opensearch-provider-design.md.

docs.title: Rejected
docs.text: Elasticsearch as the shipped target; two vendor-client adapters.

docs.title: The demo desk
docs.text:
Three small exports of the same fictional company — an ERP, a CRM that contradicts it, and an order book with twenty years of keyboard habits in its status column — and one manifest per rung of the ladder over them. The source every screen of the Entities, Views, Processes and Workflows pages reads.

It ships with the repo, under docs/apps/demo/. Nothing is generated: every fused row, every disagreement and every undeclared status below was counted by hand.

File Rows What it is for data/acme-erp.csv 12 the ERP's customers — the source of record. Two cells are empty on purpose: P-1005 has no city, P-1011 no segment data/acme-crm.csv 8 the CRM's customers, under its own column names. Five overlap the ERP — three of them disagreeing with it — two are known to the CRM only, and one has no customer code at all data/acme-orders.csv 12 the orders, with status spelled En cours, encours, fini, TERMINE (trailing space), BROUILLON, Terminé, EN LITIGE and, once, nothing data/acme-orders-day2.csv 13 the same export the next morning, with one new order in dispute — what makes a process fire data/acme-orders-day3.csv 14 the third morning: one more, in dispute and above 1 000 € — what makes two processes fire on one row

The customers are the same ACME partners the REST and Kafka demos serve; a partner has the same name and city on every page.

docs.title: Landing the sources
docs.text:
The manifests read the files from /tmp/acme-desk/ on the hub's filesystem. The self-host stack mounts nothing, so copy them into the container first — no restart needed:

docker exec lumnik-hub-1 mkdir -p /tmp/acme-desk
for f in docs/apps/demo/data/*.csv; do docker cp "$f" lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/acme-desk/; done
for n in 10-erp 20-crm 30-orders; do lm apply -f docs/apps/demo/sources/$n.yaml; done
for n in erp crm orders; do lm connector run acme-desk-$n; done

$ lm run list
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
7b972d2b  acme-desk-orders  default   Completed  12  12   0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
8869459c  acme-desk-crm     default   Completed  8   8    0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
bfb8a55e  acme-desk-erp     default   Completed  12  12   0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38

Three tables in the connector schema, every column text (an empty CSV cell lands as SQL NULL), and one scope card, desk, that lists all three:

$ lm source schema --scope desk
scope: desk

connector.t_acme_desk_crm
  customer                 TEXT
  company                  TEXT
  town                     TEXT
  email                    TEXT

connector.t_acme_desk_erp
  code                     TEXT
  name                     TEXT
  city                     TEXT
  segment                  TEXT
  credit_limit             TEXT

connector.t_acme_desk_orders
  order_no                 TEXT
  code                     TEXT
  status                   TEXT
  amount                   TEXT
  ordered_on               TEXT

The fused customer comes next — lm entity apply -f docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml, see Entities. Everything on the four pages is applied on top of this.

docs.title: Day 2 and day 3
docs.text:
Two pages need the next mornings' exports. Load one over the day-1 file, then re-run the source:

docker cp docs/apps/demo/data/acme-orders-day2.csv lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/acme-desk/acme-orders.csv   # or -day3
lm connector run acme-desk-orders

Each page says which day a capture needs. Copying acme-orders.csv back returns to day 1: the next run removes the newer orders, and lm run get <id> says so (from day 3: • 2 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them).

docs.title: The manifests
docs.text:
Folder Files The page entities/ 10-customer fuses the ERP and the CRM; 20-crm-first is the same fusion with the priority flipped; 60–65 must each be refused Entities views/ 10-customers over the fused entity, 20-orders straight over the raw order book; 60–62 must be refused Views processes/ 10-litige emits a decision when an order lands in dispute, 20-grosse-commande when it is above 1 000 €; 60–64 must each be refused Processes workflows/ 10-order-lifecycle declares what the status column means, with a dormancy threshold; 60–67 must be refused Workflows

The 6x files are not broken files to fix: each one is meant to be refused, with the message its page shows.

docs.title: What the fusion must give
docs.text:
The hand count for entities/10-customer.yaml, ERP first:

Code name city segment email _conflicts Why P-1000 Hydraulique Lyon 1000 Lyon GOLD contact@… name the CRM says HYDRAULIQUE LYON — the ERP wins, the CRM is kept P-1002 Fixations Milano 1002 Milano BRONZE ventes@… city the CRM says Milan P-1005 Transmission Aarhus 1005 Aarhus GOLD salg@… {} the ERP had no city; the CRM filled the gap — a gap is not a disagreement P-1008 Filtration Lyon 1008 Lyon GOLD contact@… city the CRM says Villeurbanne P-1003 — — — geral@… {} both sources agree verbatim P-1001, P-1004, P-1006, P-1007, P-1009, P-1010, P-1011 — — — NULL {} ERP only P-1012, P-1013 — — NULL — {} CRM only (blank code) — — — — — absent: a NULL match key can be matched to nothing

14 rows, three in dispute. Flip the source order (20-crm-first.yaml) and the count and the disputed set stay identical; only the representatives change.

docs.title: What the order book must report
docs.text:
For workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml, which declares BROUILLON, EN_COURS (aliases en cours, encours), TERMINE (alias fini) and ANNULE:

Status as written Rows Resolves to En cours, encours 4 EN_COURS — trim and case-insensitive alias matching fini, TERMINE 2 TERMINE BROUILLON 2 BROUILLON EN LITIGE 2 (3 after day 2, 4 after day 3) undeclared — real, and off the declared map Terminé 1 undeclared — the accent is not an alias anyone declared (empty) 1 nullOrBlank ANNULE 0 declared, unobserved

docs.title: Resetting
docs.text:
The desk is small enough to rebuild in a minute:

lm view rm acme-customers; lm view rm acme-orders
lm process rm litige-ouvert; lm process rm grosse-commande
lm workflow rm acme-order-lifecycle
lm entity delete AcmeCustomer --force; lm entity delete AcmeCustomerCrmFirst --force
for n in erp crm orders; do lm connector delete acme-desk-$n --force; done

--force skips the delete confirmation both commands ask for. Entities go before connectors: a connector whose table feeds an entity is refused with a 409 naming the entity. An rm of something you never applied answers 404; the next command still runs.

One scope for the whole desk

Every source connector carries scopes: [desk], and so does the entity. That is what lets a view over the raw order book and a process on it share a card with the fused customers. A scope-bound user needs the scope:desk realm role to see any of it — the same boundary as chat, see Scopes.

docs.title: kind: Export — deliver an entity as CSV
docs.text:
A kind: Export manifest is a stored delivery contract: one canonical entity, the columns you pick (renamed and formatted for the receiver if you want), one CSV, one destination, on demand or on a cron. Each execution is a managed run, recorded from claim to receipt. The file is published atomically and never overwrites anything.

Kind Export (apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1, strictly checked) Source one entity Format CSV, UTF-8 Shaping header names, per-column formatters, a row filter (below) Destinations sftp, s3 Schedulable cron, UTC Role lm_integrator for everything, reads included

docs.title: Quickstart — apply, run, read the receipt
docs.text:
# 10-sftp-daily.yaml — the desk's customers, every night at 04:00 UTC, to a partner's SFTP.
#
# The entity is the demo's AcmeCustomer (docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml); `desk` is
# one of its declared scopes. No credential is written here: key_env names a secret.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Export
metadata:
  name: customers-daily
spec:
  scope: desk
  source:
    entity: AcmeCustomer
  columns: [code, name, city, segment, email]
  order: [code]
  format:
    kind: csv
    delimiter: ";"
    header: true
  destination:
    kind: sftp
    host: sftp.partner.example
    port: 22
    user: lumnik
    path: /inbound/customers-${date}.csv
    key_env: PARTNER_SFTP_KEY
    host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc"
  mode: snapshot
  schedule: "0 4 * * *"

Store the private key once, then apply and run. The key is a multi-line PEM, so it goes in through stdin:

$ lm secret set PARTNER_SFTP_KEY - < partner_ed25519
Created secret "PARTNER_SFTP_KEY"
$ lm export apply -f docs/apps/exports/10-sftp-daily.yaml
Applied export "customers-daily" → entity AcmeCustomer, scope desk
$ lm export run customers-daily --wait
• export run 3f1c0a2b-9d4e-4b7a-a1c2-6e5f0d9b8c71 accepted — waiting for the hub to record its outcome
Run           3f1c0a2b-9d4e-4b7a-a1c2-6e5f0d9b8c71
Export        customers-daily
Entity        AcmeCustomer
Scope         desk
Destination   sftp
Status        Completed
Trigger       manual
Attempt       1
Started       2026-09-24 10:02:11
Ended         2026-09-24 10:02:12
Rows          14
Bytes         1187
SHA-256       9c1e5a0f3b7d2e48a6c4f19d0b3e7a25c8f61d4e0a9b72c35e8d1f6a4b0c9e27
Location      /inbound/customers-2026-09-24.csv
  • --wait exits 0 only on Completed. Without it, lm export run returns as soon as the hub has accepted the run (accepted; the run is Running, or Queued with the run queue on), which does not mean delivered.
  • The SHA-256 is computed over the exact bytes sent. Compare it with what the partner received.
  • Times are shown in your terminal's time zone. The hub stores them in UTC.

docs.title: The manifest, field by field
docs.text:
Field Required Rule metadata.name yes the export's name, a slug, stored lower-cased (Customers-Daily becomes customers-daily), one per tenant. Re-applying the same name updates it spec.scope yes one of the entity's declared scopes, and one you hold (below) spec.source.entity yes an existing entity, case-insensitive spec.columns yes canonical columns of the entity, no duplicates, in file order. Each one a bare name, or {name, as, format} (below). _entity_id, _conflicts, _resolution and _handle are refused spec.filter no the rows to keep: column plus equals or in (below) spec.order yes the sort, columns taken from spec.columns (ordering) spec.format.kind yes csv, the only format spec.format.delimiter no one character, default ,. Not ", a line break or NUL spec.format.encoding no UTF-8, the only value accepted spec.format.header no true (default) or false spec.destination yes kind: sftp or kind: s3, below spec.mode yes snapshot, the only mode spec.schedule no a 5-field UNIX cron, evaluated in UTC. Omit it for manual runs only

Everything is checked at apply time: unknown keys, wrong types, a column the entity does not have, a scope it does not declare, a bad cron or an unknown ${…} token. The error names the field:

$ lm export apply -f customers-daily.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.columns: 'phone' is not a canonical column of entity 'AcmeCustomer'

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text:
Credentials are never inline. password, private_key, access_key and secret_key are refused and the error names the *_env field to use instead. A *_env field holds the name of a secret stored with lm secret set, never the value:

$ lm export apply -f leaky.yaml
Error: API error 400: 'password' is not accepted — store the credential via `lm secret set` and reference it as `password_env`

docs.title: SFTP
docs.text:
destination:
  kind: sftp
  host: sftp.partner.example
  port: 22                          # optional, default 22
  user: lumnik
  path: /inbound/customers-${date}.csv
  key_env: PARTNER_SFTP_KEY         # OR password_env, exactly one of the two
  host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc"   # required
  • The host key is always verified. There is no strict_host_key: false on an export. Get the fingerprint from a machine you trust: ssh-keyscan -p 22 sftp.partner.example | ssh-keygen -lf -.
  • The directory in path must exist. The hub does not create it.
  • The file is written to customers-2026-09-24.csv.<uuid>.part in the same directory, then renamed to the final name. The rename refuses to replace an existing file.

docs.title: S3
docs.text:
# 20-s3-hourly.yaml — the same entity, every hour, to an S3 bucket (AWS, MinIO, R2…).
#
# ${timestamp} gives each run its own key, so two runs in a day never collide. Credentials
# are secret names; omitted, they default to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Export
metadata:
  name: customers-hourly
spec:
  scope: desk
  source:
    entity: AcmeCustomer
  columns: [code, name, credit_limit]
  order: [code]
  format:
    kind: csv
  destination:
    kind: s3
    bucket: acme-outbound
    prefix: customers/
    filename: customers-${timestamp}.csv
    region: eu-west-3
    access_key_env: OUTBOUND_S3_ACCESS_KEY
    secret_key_env: OUTBOUND_S3_SECRET_KEY
  mode: snapshot
  schedule: "0 * * * *"
  • The object key is prefix + filename. customers and customers/ both give customers/x.csv. A leading / is refused.
  • region defaults to eu-west-3. Set endpoint only for S3-compatible stores (MinIO, R2…).
  • access_key_env / secret_key_env default to AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.
  • The object is committed with If-None-Match: *, so an existing key is never replaced. The store must support conditional writes. AWS S3 does.
  • The upload is multipart above 8 MiB. Until it completes, nothing is visible under the key.
  • A write-only bucket works: a 403 on the pre-check is treated as "absent".

docs.title: File-name tokens
docs.text:
path (SFTP), prefix and filename (S3) accept two tokens, resolved in UTC against the run's artifact time: the moment you asked for a manual run, or the cron slot for a scheduled one.

Token Resolves to Two runs the same day ${date} 2026-09-24 the second one collides ${timestamp} 20260924T040000Z distinct names (one per second)

A literal name (/inbound/customers.csv) succeeds once. Every later run ends in collision. Pick the token that matches your cadence: ${date} for daily, ${timestamp} for anything more frequent.

docs.title: Scope and tenant
docs.text:
• An export belongs to its tenant. Another tenant never sees it, even under the same name. Rows are read through RLS for that tenant only.
  • spec.scope binds it. To apply, the scope must be one the entity declares. If you are bound to scopes, it must also be one of yours. To list, read or run an export, you need that scope too; otherwise you get the uniform 403 {"error":"scope not granted"}. See Scopes.
  • A scheduled run has no user. Its tenant and scope come from the stored manifest.
  • Every run checks the definition again before any byte moves. If the entity was dropped, the scope was removed from it or a column is gone, the run fails with definition. That is the same sentence the apply would give today.

docs.title: The CSV bytes
docs.text:
Encoding UTF-8, no BOM Line ending CRLF (\r\n), after every record including the last Delimiter spec.format.delimiter, default , Quoting every non-null value is quoted, header included. " inside a value is doubled NULL an empty, unquoted field Empty string "" (quoted), so it stays distinct from NULL Header the spec.columns names in order, when header: true No rows a file with only the header, or a 0-byte file with header: false. It is still published

With delimiter: ";", two rows where the second has no city (each line ends in \r\n):

"code";"name";"city"
"P-1000";"HYDRAULIQUE RHONE";"Lyon"
"P-1005";"ATELIERS DU ""NORD""";

Values are the canonical text in the entity view, as-is, unless the column declares format steps.

docs.title: Shape the file for a partner
docs.text:
A partner's file spec usually asks for its own header names, its own codes, its own number shape, no readable personal data, and only some rows. Declare it in the manifest. The hub then builds the partner's file itself, with the same receipt and never-overwrite guarantees:

# 40-partner-file.yaml — the same customers, in the shape a partner's file spec asks for.
#
# The partner wants its own header names, its own segment codes (A/B instead of GOLD/SILVER),
# amounts with a decimal comma, no readable email, and only GOLD and SILVER customers.
# The filter picks the rows; each column's `format` steps then run top to bottom.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Export
metadata:
  name: partner-customers
spec:
  scope: desk
  source:
    entity: AcmeCustomer
  columns:
    - name: code
      as: CUST_NO
    - name: name
      as: RAISON_SOCIALE
    - name: segment
      as: CAT
      format:
        - lookup: { table: { GOLD: A, SILVER: B }, on-missing: error }
    - name: credit_limit
      as: ENCOURS
      format:
        - format-number: { decimal-separator: ",", scale: 2 }
    - name: email
      as: EMAIL
      format:
        - mask: { keep-first: 2, keep-last: 8 }
  filter:
    - column: segment
      in: [GOLD, SILVER]
  order: [code]
  format:
    kind: csv
    delimiter: ";"
  destination:
    kind: s3
    bucket: acme-outbound
    prefix: partner/
    filename: customers-${date}.csv
    access_key_env: OUTBOUND_S3_ACCESS_KEY
    secret_key_env: OUTBOUND_S3_SECRET_KEY
  mode: snapshot

$ lm export apply -f docs/apps/exports/40-partner-file.yaml
Applied export "partner-customers" → entity AcmeCustomer, scope desk
$ lm export run partner-customers --wait
…
Status        Completed
Rows          8
Bytes         587
SHA-256       9599dfa99244aebf1677c2b0251bd07b37688761e46cd481b1cba97432e73c01
Location      s3://acme-outbound/partner/customers-2026-10-15.csv

The file the partner receives (; delimiter, each line ends in \r\n):

"CUST_NO";"RAISON_SOCIALE";"CAT";"ENCOURS";"EMAIL"
"P-1000";"Hydraulique Lyon 1000";"A";"500,00";"co**********************.example"
"P-1001";"Roulements Bruxelles 1001";"B";"637,00";
"P-1003";"Pneumatique Porto 1003";"A";"911,00";"ge*********************.example"
"P-1004";"Étanchéité Kraków 1004";"B";"1048,00";
…

A column is written in one of two ways. A bare name exports it as the entity holds it. The long form renames it, formats it, or both:

columns:
  - code                      # as the entity holds it, header "code"
  - name: segment             # the entity's column
    as: CAT                   # the header in the file
    format:                   # steps, run top to bottom on each value
      - lookup: { table: { GOLD: A, SILVER: B } }
  • Headers must be unique in the file.
  • order and filter always use the entity's names (segment, not CAT), and sort or filter on the entity's values, before any formatting.
  • An empty cell stays empty. No formatter touches it.
  • A date column is written in UTC, 2026-07-01 00:00:00+00 or 2026-07-01, whatever zone the hub runs in; format-date gives it the partner's shape. It sorts by date, and a filter on it with dates is equal as an instant: equals: "2026-07-01" keeps the rows at that day's midnight UTC, as in a view.
  • The same data still gives the same file and the same SHA-256, so you can compare a retry. One exception: after a hub upgrade, a format-date with a zone can move an hour if that zone's daylight-saving rules changed.

docs.title: Keep only some rows
docs.text:
filter:
  - column: segment
    in: [GOLD, SILVER]
  - column: city
    equals: Lyon
  • Each entry is column plus equals (one value) or in (a list), never both. A row is kept only when every entry matches.
  • column can be any column of the entity, even one you do not export.
  • Values must match exactly what the entity holds: Gold is not GOLD. An empty cell never matches.
  • Quote a value that looks like a number: equals: "2024".

docs.title: Formatters
docs.text: Four formatters exist. Each one below shows the manifest line, then what it writes.

docs.title: lookup: your codes to the partner's codes
docs.text:
format:
  - lookup: { table: { ACTIVE: A, CLOSED: C }, on-missing: error }
Value on-missing Written ACTIVE any A OTHER keep (default) OTHER OTHER UNKNOWN (any other text) UNKNOWN OTHER error the run fails, nothing is published (below)

on-missing: "" is refused when you apply: it would hand the partner empty cells without telling anyone.

docs.title: format-date: the partner's date shape
docs.text:
format:
  - format-date: { pattern: dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm, zone: Europe/Paris }
Value in the entity pattern Written 2019-12-31 dd/MM/yyyy 31/12/2019 2004-10-18 23:42:39+00 dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm 18/10/2004 23:42 (UTC, the default) 2004-10-18 23:42:39+00 dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm, zone: Europe/Paris 19/10/2004 01:42 2026-08-01 14:30:00 (no time zone in the value) HH:mm 14:30: zone only converts a value that carries one 2019-12-31 dd MMM yyyy 31 Dec 2019: month names are in English

Pattern letters: dd day, MM month, yyyy year, HH hour (00–23), mm minutes, ss seconds. Capital M is the month, lowercase mm the minutes: mixing them up is the classic mistake.

docs.title: format-number: decimal comma, fixed decimals
docs.text:
format:
  - format-number: { decimal-separator: ",", scale: 2 }
Value Parameters Written 1234.5600 none 1234.5600 1234.5600 decimal-separator: "," 1234,5600 1234.5650 decimal-separator: ",", scale: 2 1234,57 (rounded half up) -1234.5 scale: 0 -1235 42 scale: 2 42.00

No thousands separator is ever written.

docs.title: mask: hide personal data
docs.text:
format:
  - mask: { keep-first: 2, keep-last: 4 }      # mask-char: "*" by default
Value Parameters Written 4556123498761234 keep-last: 4 ************1234 contact@example.com keep-first: 2, keep-last: 4 co*************.com 1234 keep-last: 4 ****

A value too short to keep anything is masked entirely.

docs.title: What is checked, and when
docs.text:
Every formatter and filter is checked when you apply. The error names the field:

$ lm export apply -f partner.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.columns[3].format[0]: unknown formatter 'format-numbr' — expected one of [format-date, format-number, lookup, mask]
$ lm export apply -f partner.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.filter[0].column: 'segmnt' is not a canonical column of entity 'AcmeCustomer'

A value a formatter cannot write fails the run (generation). No file is published: a half-formatted column is worse than none. The reason names the column and the formatter, never the value. Here, the same manifest without its filter meets a BRONZE customer, which the table does not list:

$ lm export run partner-customers-all --wait
…
Status        Failed
Failure       generation
Reason        column 'segment', formatter 'lookup': no entry in table for this value

To find the value, look at the column as the entity holds it, then add the value to the table, choose an on-missing, or filter the row out:

$ lm entity export AcmeCustomer -o - | cut -d, -f1,4 | grep -v -e GOLD -e SILVER
"code","segment"
"P-1002","BRONZE"
"P-1006","BRONZE"
"P-1009","BRONZE"
"P-1011",
"P-1012",
"P-1013",

BRONZE is the value the table lacks. The three customers with no segment are not a problem: an empty cell never reaches the formatter, so it stays empty in the file.

format-date fails the same way on a value that is not a date, 2019-02-30 included: it is never moved to a valid day. It also fails when pattern asks for a field the value lacks (HH:mm on a date). format-number fails on a value that is not a number, or one with more than 1 000 digits on either side of the separator.

lm entity export (the one-shot download) never formats or filters: it always gives every column, as the entity holds it.

docs.title: Ordering and the receipt
docs.text:
• The order is deterministic. Rows are sorted by spec.order, then by the remaining spec.columns in their declared order. Each column is compared byte-wise (COLLATE "C"), with NULLs last.
  • The same data gives the same bytes and the same SHA-256. A retry over unchanged data can be checked against the failed attempt's target, byte for byte.
  • A completed run's receipt contains rowCount, byteCount, sha256 and location. S3 adds etag and versionId (versioned bucket only).
  • The ETag is not a checksum. It identifies the object and nothing more. Always compare the sha256.
  • There is no sidecar file. The receipt lives in the run ledger (lm export status). A single-part S3 object (≤ 8 MiB) also carries the checksum as x-amz-meta-lumnik-sha256.

docs.title: Managed export vs one-shot download
docs.text:
lm export run (managed) lm entity export (one-shot) Manifest a kind: Export none Columns, order, format from the manifest all canonical columns, in declared order, default format (,, header) Goes to the SFTP / S3 destination your machine Ledger, retry, schedule yes no. Audited as data egress (rows, bytes, SHA-256)

Use the one-shot for a quick look or a one-off hand-over:

$ lm entity export AcmeCustomer -o customers.csv
AcmeCustomer: 1099 bytes written to customers.csv (sha256 afa5c455ceaf9a2c6e0fae54b2fbc9b671893f22220c2c2c6a685969c0deceb5)
$ lm entity export AcmeCustomer -o customers.csv
Error: customers.csv already exists — refusing to overwrite it (use --force to replace it)
$ lm entity export AcmeCustomer -o - | head -3
  • The download goes to a hidden .customers.csv.*.part and gets its final name only once the whole body has arrived. An interrupted download leaves nothing behind.
  • An existing file is never replaced without --force. The file is created 0600.
  • With -o -, bytes already written to stdout cannot be taken back. On failure the command still exits non-zero.

docs.title: Runs from lm
docs.text:
$ lm export list
NAME              ENTITY        SCOPE  DESTINATION  SCHEDULE
customers-daily   AcmeCustomer  desk   sftp         0 4 * * *
customers-hourly  AcmeCustomer  desk   s3           0 * * * *
$ lm export runs customers-daily
ID        STATUS     TRIGGER   ATTEMPT  ROWS  BYTES  STARTED           ENDED             FAILURE
c7d0e913  Failed     manual    1                   2026-09-24 11:30  2026-09-24 11:30  collision
3f1c0a2b  Completed  manual    1        14    1187   2026-09-24 10:02  2026-09-24 10:02
$ lm export status customers-daily           # the latest run in full; add a RUN_ID for another
$ lm export retry customers-daily 5e8a41f0 --wait
$ lm export get customers-daily              # the stored manifest
  • --timeout (default 30m) and Ctrl-C only stop the waiting. The run carries on on the hub.
  • -o json|yaml gives every command a stable machine-readable shape for scripts.
  • Short ids from lm export runs are accepted everywhere.

docs.title: Stop a schedule
docs.text:
There is no lm export rm or disable. To stop the scheduled runs, re-apply the manifest without spec.schedule:

$ lm export apply -f customers-daily.yaml        # the same manifest, schedule: line removed
Applied export "customers-daily" → entity AcmeCustomer, scope desk
$ lm export list
NAME             ENTITY        SCOPE  DESTINATION  SCHEDULE
customers-daily  AcmeCustomer  desk   sftp

The export stays, for lm export run on demand, with its run history.

docs.title: Failures, and whether to retry
docs.text:
A run is Running, then exactly one of Completed or Failed (with the run queue on, it is Queued first). A failure carries a failureCode and a failureReason written by the hub. The reason never contains a credential or a raw third-party message.

failureCode What happened What is on the remote side Safe to retry? definition entity dropped, scope removed from the entity, column gone nothing after fixing the entity or the manifest generation reading or encoding the snapshot failed nothing (temporary file removed, multipart aborted) yes publication upload or commit refused (credentials, missing directory, network, host key) nothing yes, once the cause is fixed collision the final name already exists the existing file, untouched no, look first interrupted the hub stopped mid-run (crash, restart) possibly a leftover, below yes, and a collision then means it was delivered 
$ lm export status customers-daily c7d0e913
…
Status        Failed
Failure       collision
Reason        SFTP destination: /inbound/customers-2026-09-24.csv already exists — refusing to overwrite a previously delivered artifact
✖ export run c7d0e913-… failed (collision): … — retry with: lm export retry customers-daily c7d0e913

What a retry does. It creates a new run with retryOf set and attempt + 1. It regenerates the file from byte 0, since there is no resume. It keeps the original artifact time, so it aims at the same file name. So:

  • A retry is always safe: it can never overwrite. At worst it ends in collision.
  • collision on a retry means the earlier attempt did publish, even though the ledger says it failed. Compare the remote file's SHA-256 with a fresh one-shot (lm entity export … -o - | sha256sum, same columns and order). Then either leave it, or move it aside on the remote and retry.
  • Only Failed runs can be retried. A scheduled slot that was delivered since answers 409 {"error":"already delivered"}.

docs.title: Scheduling and concurrency
docs.text:
• The scheduler checks every minute and runs the export's latest due slot, once.
  • There is no back-fill. After an outage, only the latest slot runs. An export applied after today's slot waits for the next one.
  • There is no automatic retry. A failed slot stays Failed until someone runs lm export retry. The next slot runs normally.
  • Only one run is in flight per export. A second trigger gets 409 … already has a run in flight. A slot that is due while a manual run is going is picked up on a later tick, if it is still the latest.
  • With several hub replicas, a slot is still delivered only once.
  • When several slots are due, the one owed longest starts first. A due slot that finds no free place is picked up on a later tick, if it is still the latest.
Property (environment variable) Default Bounds lumnik.export.max-concurrent-scheduled-runs (LUMNIK_EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCHEDULED_RUNS) 2 scheduled runs in flight per hub instance. With the run queue off, lm export run and retry do not count quarkus.datasource."admin".jdbc.max-size 20 the admin pool; each run holds one connection for its whole life — raise it with the bound above lumnik.export.snapshot.timeout-seconds 1800 the time a run has to generate its snapshot

docs.title: Runs can queue
docs.text:
With LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED=true (off by default; read Turning on the run queue first):

  • lm export run and lm export retry leave a run in status Queued; the hub starts it as a slot frees, on the LUMNIK_EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCHEDULED_RUNS budget.
  • lm export runs lists it Queued, with no start time yet.

  • --wait waits through Queued to the outcome.

  • A queued manual run's ${date} and ${timestamp} file-name tokens are fixed when the hub accepts it, not when it starts: a run queued at 23:59 and started after midnight keeps the previous day's name.

  • An export holds at most one queued-or-running run: a second request gets 409 … already has a run in flight, naming the queued run.
  • A run not started within LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_MAX_AGE (default 1h) ends Failed, failure interrupted, "expired in queue". One whose manifest was re-applied while it waited ends Failed, failure definition.
  • There is no export cancel door: a queued run cannot be cancelled and leaves the queue by starting, by failing on its definition, or by expiring.
  • While a queue stands, it can win the permit race against a due scheduled slot. That slot is skipped, tried again on the next tick, and dropped when the next occurrence replaces it (there is no back-fill).

docs.title: Recovering from a crash
docs.text:
A run whose hub died is closed as Failed / interrupted within a minute (at startup, and on every scheduler tick). Run lm export retry: it either delivers or ends in collision, and a collision means the lost run had already published. The hub cannot clean up what the lost run left on the remote side:

  • SFTP. A <name>.<uuid>.part file stays next to the target. It never takes the final name. Remove it by hand, or with a housekeeping job that deletes *.part files older than a day.

  • S3. An incomplete multipart upload stays invisible but its parts are billed. Add a lifecycle rule to the bucket once:

    {
  "Rules": [{
    "ID": "abort-incomplete-exports",
    "Status": "Enabled",
    "Filter": {"Prefix": ""},
    "AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload": {"DaysAfterInitiation": 1}
  }]
}

docs.title: Not in this version
docs.text:
• Never overwrites and never appends. A delivered name is final.
  • No resume. A retry rewrites the whole file.
  • No delta or incremental export. mode: snapshot means the full entity every time.
  • CSV only, UTF-8 only. No JSON, Parquet or Excel, no compression, no encryption.
  • One entity per export. No joins. The filter knows only equals and in: no ranges, no patterns, no OR between entries.
  • Four formatters. No computed or constant columns, no fixed-width output, no inbound repair hooks (fix-mojibake, parse-*). Clean the data on the way in, and shape it on the way out.
  • No other destinations: no local disk, email or HTTP push. No sidecar or .done marker file.
  • No delete or disable of an export: stop its schedule by re-applying it without spec.schedule.
  • No back-fill of missed slots and no automatic retry.

docs.text:
