  • Scopes: what spec.scope binds.
  • Secrets: lm secret set for *_env names.
  • CSV & files (SFTP/S3): the same transports, on the way in.
  • CLI reference: every lm export flag.

docs.title: Inbox — the human side of the decision
docs.text:
The third rung: the tenant's recent decision.* events, newest first — what needs a human. And the disposal gesture: ack.

lm inbox                 # open decisions (ID, WHEN, PROCESS, MESSAGE, ENTITY_KEY)
lm inbox --limit 100     # 1..200, default 50
lm inbox --all           # include disposed ones, marked [acked]
lm inbox --process litige-ouvert         # one process's decisions (as PROCESS shows it)
lm inbox --type decision.litige-ouvert   # one decision type
lm inbox ack 42          # dispose of decision 42

On the demo desk after day 3 (see Processes), two processes fired on the same order; a human disposes of one:

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN  PROCESS          MESSAGE                                                    ENTITY_KEY
25  2min  grosse-commande  Grosse commande SO-000014 : 5000.00 € pour P-1003          3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
24  2min  litige-ouvert    Commande SO-000014 du client P-1003 en litige — 5000.00 €  3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
$ lm inbox ack 25
acked.
$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN  PROCESS        MESSAGE                                                    ENTITY_KEY
24  2min  litige-ouvert  Commande SO-000014 du client P-1003 en litige — 5000.00 €  3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
$ lm inbox --all
ID  WHEN  PROCESS          MESSAGE                                                           ENTITY_KEY
25  2min  grosse-commande  Grosse commande SO-000014 : 5000.00 € pour P-1003 [acked]         3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
24  2min  litige-ouvert    Commande SO-000014 du client P-1003 en litige — 5000.00 €         3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
18  3min  litige-ouvert    Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 € [acked]  96357a4a5750f97026f9ec5b8ce0f986517179f470e8a74b9fd013befe0e3622
Column Reads WHEN a humanized age: just now, 2min, 2h, yesterday, 3d PROCESS the process name, or workflow:<name> for a dormancy alert ENTITY_KEY a process decision: the row's content hash. A workflow alert: the document's business key (SO-000014) [acked] after the message: a disposed decision

--process and --type narrow the hub's read, not the page it returns: --limit 5 --process litige-ouvert is that process's five newest decisions, however many others came after them. A workflow alert's process is workflow:<name>, as the PROCESS column shows it. A blank or repeated filter is refused (400).

Re-acking is harmless: it answers the same acked.. In the TUI, :inbox shows the same list live — a acks, A toggles disposed entries. The inbox needs the lm_user role.

docs.title: Who sees which decision
docs.text:
Each decision belongs to the scope of the kind: Process or kind: Workflow that raised it, as the manifest stands now:

  • a user with no scope:* role sees the whole tenant's decisions;
  • a user holding scope:<tag> roles sees, and can ack, only those métiers' decisions — another one's id answers 404, like an id that does not exist (or another tenant's);
  • re-scope a manifest and its past decisions move with it; remove or rename it and they belong to no métier, so only users with no scope:* role still see them.

Above, litige-ouvert has since been removed (lm process rm). A user holding scope:desk therefore sees only grosse-commande's decision, and a scope:stock user sees none:

$ lm inbox --all                      # as a scope:desk user
ID  WHEN  PROCESS          MESSAGE                                                    ENTITY_KEY
25  2min  grosse-commande  Grosse commande SO-000014 : 5000.00 € pour P-1003 [acked]  3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
$ lm inbox ack 24                     # as a scope:stock user
Error: API error 404: no decision 24 in your inbox

Retention

Decisions age out with the event log (lumnik.events.retention-days, default 30). The inbox is a work surface, not an archive.

docs.title: Decision sources
docs.text:
• decision.<process-name> — a kind: Process reacting to a row landing (the end-to-end story: How lumnik breathes).
  • decision.dormant.<workflow-name> — a kind: Workflow's dormancy sweep: a non-terminal document observed unchanged past its declared threshold. See Dormancy for its wording.

The ack is itself an event (annotation.decision.acked), so a webhook can react to it.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Processes — where decisions come from.
  • Workflows — declares what the values behind a decision mean.
  • Admin API guide — Integration Hub — how a decision also reaches an external system.
  • The WOW walkthrough — the whole ladder in one thread: see → react → decide, with declare underneath.

docs.title: kind: Process — react
docs.text:
The second rung: a declarative watcher on ingested rows. When a row lands that matches your conditions, the process emits a decision.* event. It always lands in the inbox; a webhook subscription carries it on to n8n, Make, Zapier or your own endpoint.

Kind Process — apps.lumnik.io/v1 Trigger data.row.changed on a raw connector.t_* table — the only trigger Conditions the view filter grammar, ANDed, over the table's own columns Emits one decision.<name> event per matching row, {col}-templated, fields included Commands lm process apply · list · disable · enable · rm — all need lm_admin Edition Open

A process changes nothing and calls no one: it says, once, that a row worth a human's attention just landed, in the row's own words. The métier story is How lumnik breathes.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Fires on rows that land, not rows that exist. Re-running the same export emits nothing.
  • Conditions in the view grammar. status=EN LITIGE, amount>1000, city~lyon — validated at apply against the trigger table.
  • The row's own words. {col} placeholders are validated at apply; every referenced column also rides in the event as data.
  • Refused at apply, never silent at fire time. Each refusal is a 400 that names the fix.
  • Reversible, and removable. lm process disable stops it firing and keeps the manifest; lm process rm removes it.
  • Fail-closed per process. A process that breaks at runtime is skipped; its siblings keep firing.
  • Delivery is a subscription. The inbox always has the decision; a webhook has it once one is registered.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads the demo desk that ships with the repo

An order book whose export arrives every morning, under docs/apps/demo/. Land it first — The demo desk has the commands.

# 10-litige.yaml — when an order lands in dispute, say so.
#
# A process fires on data.row.changed, born at the raw write path — so on.table is the raw
# orders table and `when` speaks its own columns. The effect IS the event: decision.litige
# lands in the outbox and in `lm inbox`; reaching n8n or a webhook needs a subscription.
#
# Expect: nothing on apply (a process fires on rows that LAND, not on rows already there),
#         then one decision per genuinely new EN LITIGE row on the next run.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Process
metadata:
  name: litige-ouvert
spec:
  scope: desk
  on:
    event: data.row.changed
    table: connector.t_acme_desk_orders
  when:
    - status=EN LITIGE
  emit:
    type: decision.litige-ouvert
    message: "Commande {order_no} du client {code} en litige — {amount} €"

$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/10-litige.yaml
{"name":"litige-ouvert","table":"connector.t_acme_desk_orders","emit":"decision.litige-ouvert"}
$ lm process list
NAME           TABLE                         EMIT                    ENABLED
litige-ouvert  connector.t_acme_desk_orders  decision.litige-ouvert  true
$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN  PROCESS  MESSAGE  ENTITY_KEY

Nothing fired: the two orders already in EN LITIGE were there before the process. Now load day 2 — the next morning's export, with one new order in dispute:

$ docker cp docs/apps/demo/data/acme-orders-day2.csv lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/acme-desk/acme-orders.csv
$ lm connector run acme-desk-orders
run scheduled: dc0a38a3-3caf-40b8-9461-4fd202978dfb
$ lm run list --connector acme-desk-orders
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
dc0a38a3  acme-desk-orders  default   Completed  13  13   0        0             2026-10-19 01:42  2026-10-19 01:42
7b972d2b  acme-desk-orders  default   Completed  12  12   0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38

(lumnik-hub-1 is the self-host stack's hub container; the file goes on the hub's disk.) Thirteen rows read, one of them new. A few seconds later:

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN      PROCESS        MESSAGE                                                   ENTITY_KEY
18  just now  litige-ouvert  Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 €  96357a4a5750f97026f9ec5b8ce0f986517179f470e8a74b9fd013befe0e3622

One decision for the one new row. ENTITY_KEY is the row's content hash: it points at exactly that row. The event itself, checked in the database:

$ echo "select payload from core.event_outbox where id = 18" | psql …
{"entity": "connector.t_acme_desk_orders", "fields": {"code": "P-1007", "amount": "860.00", "order_no": "SO-000013"}, "message": "Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 €", "process": "litige-ouvert", "entity_key": "96357a4a5750…"}

(entity_key abridged.) fields carries every column the message references, as data — an automation reads values, not a sentence. A timestamp field is the text the message shows, its UTC instant, "2026-07-01T00:00:00Z".

A value an automation needs but a reader should not see — a full bank account sent to a SIEM — goes in spec.emit.fields, not in the message: the payload carries it, the inbox sentence does not.

emit:
  type: decision.supplier-bank-account-observed
  message: "Bank account observed for supplier {supplier_id} ({supplier_name})"
  fields: [iban]

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
Field Required Meaning metadata.name yes kebab-case ([a-z0-9-]+); becomes the event's process spec.scope yes the scope whose schema card declares on.table spec.on.event yes must be data.row.changed spec.on.table yes the raw ingest table (connector.t_<name>) — see Trigger at the raw write path spec.when[] yes (≥ 1) conditions in the view filter grammar, ANDed spec.emit.type yes must start with decision. spec.emit.message yes the human sentence, {col}-templated spec.emit.fields no columns the payload's fields carries besides those the message names — what an automation needs but a reader should not see; each must be a column of on.table

apply refuses a key it does not know and names it — a misspelled mesage: is a 400, not a decision with no text.

A stored process is enabled by default (the ENABLED column of lm process list); only enabled processes fire. See Turn a process off.

docs.title: Trigger at the raw write path
docs.text:
on.table is the raw table a connector fills, and when columns are that table's own. A fused entity view (connector.v_*) and an ext.* table a kind: hybrid target fills are refused: no connector writes rows into them. A view gets the better sentence:

$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/63-refused-fused-view.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.on.table 'connector.v_acmecustomer' is a fused entity view — data.row.changed is born on the raw table a connector writes, never on a view, so this process could never fire — declare it on connector.t_acme_desk_erp or connector.t_acme_desk_crm

Declare one process per raw source, or move the condition to the source that carries it.

docs.title: Message templating
docs.text:
{col} inserts the row's value — "Commande {order_no} du client {code} en litige — {amount} €".

  • A NULL renders as an empty string.
  • A timestamp column renders as its UTC instant, 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z, whatever zone the hub runs in. A date column renders as its day, 2026-07-01. A text column renders as stored: a CSV date stays as the file wrote it until a parse-date types the column.
  • A placeholder is exactly {letters_digits_}; anything else ({}, {a-b}, a lone brace) stays literal.
  • Every {col} is checked at apply against the trigger table:
$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/61-refused-placeholder.yaml
Error: API error 400: message references {customer_name} — not a column of connector.t_acme_desk_orders

docs.title: Firing it
docs.text:
A decision appears a few seconds after the run that landed the row.

Only new rows fire. Re-running the unchanged day-2 file leaves the inbox as it was:

$ lm connector run acme-desk-orders
run scheduled: 20db972d-f540-4c0d-80b6-05ed4d4a534d
$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN      PROCESS        MESSAGE                                                   ENTITY_KEY
18  just now  litige-ouvert  Commande SO-000013 du client P-1007 en litige — 860.00 €  96357a4a5750f97026f9ec5b8ce0f986517179f470e8a74b9fd013befe0e3622

A row that matches two processes fires two decisions, one per process — shown below.

docs.title: Delivery is opt-in
docs.text:
A decision always lands in the inbox. Reaching an external system also needs a webhook subscription for the tenant; none exists by default. A human disposes of it:

$ lm inbox ack 18
acked.

The ack is itself an event (annotation.decision.acked), so a webhook subscribed to annotation.* learns that someone handled it. Register a subscription with lm integration add (needs lm_integrator and lm_admin) — the Admin API guide walks the whole gesture, and the WOW demo plays it against a stand-in n8n.

docs.title: Failure contract
docs.text:
• Refused at apply: structural errors, a trigger table that cannot fire, an unknown when column, an unknown placeholder, an emit type outside decision., a quoted or out-of-domain value.
  • Fail-closed per process at runtime: a process whose table vanished is skipped and logged; sibling processes keep firing.
  • Declarative only: there is no script hook for processes.

docs.title: Refusals
docs.text:
$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/60-refused-unknown-column.yaml
Error: API error 400: when: column 'montant' is not in connector.t_acme_desk_orders — fix the column name or rediscover the scope
$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/61-refused-placeholder.yaml
Error: API error 400: message references {customer_name} — not a column of connector.t_acme_desk_orders
$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/62-refused-emit-type.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.emit.type is required and must start with 'decision.' — the governed taxonomy
$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/63-refused-fused-view.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.on.table 'connector.v_acmecustomer' is a fused entity view — data.row.changed is born on the raw table a connector writes, never on a view, so this process could never fire — declare it on connector.t_acme_desk_erp or connector.t_acme_desk_crm
$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/64-refused-quoted-value.yaml
Error: API error 400: filter value 'EN LITIGE' is quoted; a value here is a bare literal, so the quotes would be compared to status too — write status=EN LITIGE

The last one is the view grammar: a value is a bare literal.

Who What they can do lm_admin, no scope: role declare, list, disable, enable and remove processes for the whole tenant lm_admin bound to scopes the same, for the granted scopes only; anything else is 403 scope not granted without lm_admin nothing — API error 403 (forbidden)

In the TUI, :processes lists the declared rules; e re-opens a stored manifest in the :new authoring loop.

docs.title: Get told when an order lands in dispute
docs.text:
lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/10-litige.yaml
lm inbox

Result: every new EN LITIGE row lands as one decision in lm inbox (and the PWA's Décisions tab), with the order's number, customer and amount.

docs.title: Watch a second condition on the same table
docs.text:
# 20-grosse-commande.yaml — a second watcher on the same table.
#
# Two processes on one table are independent: a row that matches both fires two decisions, one
# per process, each under its own type. `amount` is a text column, as every CSV column is; the
# ordering filter casts it, exactly as a kind:View filter does.
#
# Expect: nothing on apply; on the day-3 export, SO-000014 (EN LITIGE, 5 000 €) fires this one
#         AND litige-ouvert.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Process
metadata:
  name: grosse-commande
spec:
  scope: desk
  on:
    event: data.row.changed
    table: connector.t_acme_desk_orders
  when:
    - amount>1000
  emit:
    type: decision.grosse-commande
    message: "Grosse commande {order_no} : {amount} € pour {code}"

Apply it, then load day 3 — one more order, in dispute and above 1 000 €:

$ lm process apply -f docs/apps/demo/processes/20-grosse-commande.yaml
{"name":"grosse-commande","table":"connector.t_acme_desk_orders","emit":"decision.grosse-commande"}
$ docker cp docs/apps/demo/data/acme-orders-day3.csv lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/acme-desk/acme-orders.csv
$ lm connector run acme-desk-orders
run scheduled: 36f56e82-40cf-4ec1-9604-b48e46a1a327
$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN      PROCESS          MESSAGE                                                    ENTITY_KEY
25  just now  grosse-commande  Grosse commande SO-000014 : 5000.00 € pour P-1003          3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b
24  just now  litige-ouvert    Commande SO-000014 du client P-1003 en litige — 5000.00 €  3a47cea8e762663021d4c5bba36b5a410ad0731a1271e17706ce6976ee8c138b

Result: two processes, two decisions, the same ENTITY_KEY. amount is a text column (every CSV column is); amount>1000 compares it as a number, like a view filter.

How a number is compared:

Value arrives as Rule text (every CSV cell) must be a plain decimal: 1e5 never matches amount>100. = stays an exact text comparison a number compared by value: 0.00002 matches x>1e-5; x=5 matches 5, 5.0 and 5.00 NaN, infinities never match

How a date is compared, against an operand written YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC) or as an ISO date-time:

Value arrives as Rule a DATE column (a JDBC source) the day it names, at midnight UTC: the same day whatever time zone the hub runs in a timestamp column to the microsecond text (every CSV cell) read as an ISO date or date-time, UTC when it carries no offset; anything else never matches

= with a date against a DATE or timestamp column is equal as an instant, as in a view: at=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z matches the row stamped at that instant. Against text, = stays an exact text comparison.

docs.title: Know the processes have read a run
docs.text:
A run ends before its rows are evaluated: the process consumer reads them a few seconds later. An inbox read in between shows nothing new, whether or not something will fire. --wait-evaluated waits until every enabled process has read the rows the run wrote:

$ lm connector run acme-desk-orders
run scheduled: 704ee81c-8b17-4feb-b4b8-4a8a7061ddee
$ lm run get 704ee81c
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED             EVALUATED
704ee81c  acme-desk-orders  default   Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-21 23:11  2026-10-21 23:11  no
$ lm run get 704ee81c --wait-evaluated
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED             EVALUATED
704ee81c  acme-desk-orders  default   Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-21 23:11  2026-10-21 23:11  yes

Result: once EVALUATED reads yes, lm inbox --process litige-ouvert is that run's final answer — an empty list then means no decision, not "not yet". The column appears once the tenant has an enabled process. --wait-evaluated exits 1 when the hub cannot say: no enabled process, or one applied, re-applied, enabled or disabled since the run started — re-run it.

docs.title: Turn a process off
docs.text:
$ lm process disable litige-ouvert
process litige-ouvert enabled=false
$ lm process list
NAME             TABLE                         EMIT                      ENABLED
grosse-commande  connector.t_acme_desk_orders  decision.grosse-commande  true
litige-ouvert    connector.t_acme_desk_orders  decision.litige-ouvert    false
$ lm process enable litige-ouvert
process litige-ouvert enabled=true
$ lm process rm litige-ouvert
process litige-ouvert deleted
$ lm process rm litige-ouvert
Error: API error 404: unknown process: litige-ouvert

Result: disable stops it firing and keeps the manifest; enable puts it back. rm removes it for good, with no prompt. In the TUI's :processes, the same gestures are ^P and Del on the row under the cursor. There is no lm process get: e in the TUI re-opens the stored manifest.

Each gesture is recorded in the audit trail, within seconds; a refused one leaves no row:

$ echo "select operation, changes from core.audit_event where entity_key='litige-ouvert' order by id desc limit 4" | psql …
 operation |                                                                      changes
-----------+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 DELETE    | {"scope": "desk"}
 UPDATE    | {"scope": "desk", "enabled": true}
 UPDATE    | {"scope": "desk", "enabled": false}
 APPLY     | {"scope": "desk", "table": "connector.t_acme_desk_orders", "manifest_sha256": "2ada066a02e114c10e8390a00254fb995d56d25dfac438db8cd97c81f3b362e9"}
(4 rows)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture apply refused: unknown key(s) in the manifest: … a misspelled field (mesage:) the message lists what kind:Process honors — fix the spelling apply refused 404: no schema for scope '…' — run discovery first spec.scope is not a discovered scope lm source rediscover --scope <tag> (lm_integrator + lm_admin, a scope you hold); lm source schema --scope <tag> shows what it holds apply refused: spec.on.table '…' is not in the '…' scope the scope's card does not carry that table lm source schema --scope <tag>, then fix the name apply refused: spec.on.table '…' is a fused entity view … the trigger is a connector.v_* view declare the process on one of the raw tables the message names apply refused: spec.on.table '…' cannot fire … the table is in the card but no connector writes rows into it (an ext.* hybrid target) declare the process on a connector.t_* table apply refused: when: column '…' is not in …, or '…' is not an allowed value for … an unknown column, or an = value outside its declared domain fix the condition against the card apply refused: message references {…} — not a column of … a placeholder that is not a column of the trigger table fix the placeholder, or drop it apply refused: spec.emit.type … must start with 'decision.' an emit type outside the taxonomy decision.<something> a process never fires on a re-run the rows were already in the table expected: only new rows fire a declared, enabled process stopped firing its trigger table vanished or broke at runtime check the hub's log; sibling processes keep firing a process still fires after you meant to turn it off it is still enabled lm process disable <name>, or lm process rm <name> decisions show in lm inbox but never reach an external system no webhook subscription for the tenant lm integration add (lm_integrator + lm_admin) 403 … scope not granted you are scope-bound and spec.scope is not one of your grants ask for that scope: role, or declare under a granted scope API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server you do not hold lm_admin ask your administrator; no lm command lists your roles (GET /api/bff/v1/me returns them under roles)

docs.text:

docs.title: The métier PWA — your data in your pocket
docs.text:
The hub rendered on a phone. /app/ is served by the hub itself — no app store, no build step — and installs from the browser like any PWA. One deployment carries every métier; the ?m= parameter decides whose app it is.

The UI speaks French — it is built for the métier user, not the integrator.

docs.title: Reaching it
docs.text:
https://<your-host>/app/            # the app declared default: true
https://<your-host>/app/?m=stock    # the stock métier

After sign-in the PWA looks ?m= up in the apps the user may see (lm app list):

?m= Opens a name in the list that app, with its own title, icon and theme absent the app declared default: true the user sees — or their only app; otherwise the refusal below unknown, or an app of a scope the user does not hold Application inconnue — vérifie le lien ou contacte ton intégrateur.

Each app installs as its own home-screen icon: "Clients" and "Stock" are two apps on the same phone.

What a métier user actually sees inside is decided elsewhere: by the saved views the integrator has applied for that scope, and by the scope:<tag> role on the user's account.

docs.title: Installing it on a phone
docs.text:
At fleet scale: your MDM, not AirDrop

The gestures below are per-device — right for a pilot. For a managed fleet, push the same two artifacts through your MDM: the TLS façade's root CA as a trusted certificate, and the PWA URL as a managed web app / home-screen shortcut. The per-device steps then disappear entirely.

The PWA needs a secure origin: service workers and the real install prompt only exist over https. The self-host stack ships a TLS façade for exactly this — one Caddy origin fronting hub and Keycloak, with automatic Let's Encrypt for a public LUMNIK_TLS_HOST (see deploy/tls/README.md). On a LAN address Caddy uses its internal CA; trust its root on the device, or the browser will not offer a real install.

Then, on the phone:

  1. Open https://<host>/app/?m=<métier> and sign in.
  2. iOS Safari: Share → Add to Home Screen. Android Chrome: the install prompt, or ⋮ → Add to Home screen.
  3. The icon and name are the métier's own; the app opens standalone, no browser chrome.

docs.title: The tabs
docs.text:
The tabs an app shows are the ones its hub offers, narrowed by what the app declares (Choosing the tabs):

Tab Shown Fiches always Décisions always Chat on a build with the AI, switched on Recherche on a hub with Search, for a user who may read an index

A tab the hub does not offer is absent, not greyed out. Bottom tabs on a phone, a left rail on a display.

docs.title: Fiches — the saved views
docs.text:
The tab lists the saved views of the app's scope:

Views applied for your métier What you see One It opens directly. Several A picker to choose from. None An amber message naming the cause — ask your integrator to apply one (lm view apply -f).

The refusal rules are those of lm view. A view opens on its first 50 rows, under its spec.title:

On screen Means header count 50+, Première page — d'autres résultats existent more rows exist; no total is counted Suivant › / ‹ Précédent one page forward / back (above and below the rows) « Début back to the first page Page N — dernière page, count without + the last page this page link is no longer valid — reload the view from its first page the data or the filter changed under the page; tap « Début

Changing a filter goes back to the first page; moving between pages keeps the filters. A phone shows cards, a tablet or a display a table.

Filters are built, not typed:

  • pick a column by its label, then an operator, then a value — a text box, a number, a date, or a list when the column declares its values;
  • a money or time column offers only contient and =;
  • each filter is a chip; tap it (or Enter) to remove it; chips combine with AND;
  • a refused filter or page move shows the hub's message, and the last good page stays on screen.

Tapping a row opens the detail, ending with the sources' disagreements (_conflicts) or aucune ambiguïté ni divergence.

docs.title: Décisions — the inbox
docs.text:
The inbox, newest first: open decisions with a ✓ Traiter button (the same ack as lm inbox ack), handled ones dimmed with ✓ traité. The open count is a badge on the tab.

It shows the decisions of the métiers the user holds — every decision of the tenant for a user with no scope: role (who sees which decision). It is not narrowed to the open app: a user holding desk and stock sees both in either app, at most the 50 newest, handled ones included.

docs.title: Recherche — search the business data
docs.text:
A search box over your business data — the search lm search query runs. Type a word or two and press Chercher: ranked results, matched words highlighted. Nothing is searched while you type.

  • Each result is headed by the index's business title, or the entity name.
  • A field the index links to your ERP opens the other system in a new tab.
  • Fields carry their entity's human names.
  • ✕ next to the box empties the screen — query, filters, results and open record.
Situation The tab hub without Search, or a user with no index to read absent Search installed but struggling present, with a line saying why the app could not find out at start-up (network) present a search fails says why, and how long to wait when the hub says so
  • What it searches. Only the app's métier: the stock app searches the entities tagged stock, even for a user holding other scopes too.
  • Narrowing. Counted values (a city, a segment) appear as chips under the box; tap one to keep only those results, again to lift it. Plus de résultats loads the next page.
  • Opening a result. The record opens read-only, with each source's value where they disagree. A record changed since the search, or a key shared by several records, is said so.
  • No result reads Aucun résultat: nothing matched. Expected results? Check that an index exists for the métier (Enabling Recherche for an app).
  • How fresh it is. A line under the chips gives the index's age.

docs.title: Chat — ask your data
docs.text:
The guarded analytic ask (as lm ask), bound to the app's scope. An answer shows the SQL it ran and the row count, folded under the reply. An answer that ran no SQL is an abstention, in the amber refusal tone — the ask contract. The thread survives tab switches, not a reload; nothing is stored.

When the answer filtered on a value a source disagrees about:

  • an amber block « Désaccord sur une valeur filtrée » sits above the SQL, one entry per record — P-1008 · Ville — comptée avec « Lyon », or écartée, alors qu'une source indique « Villeurbanne » — closed by « … et d'autres fiches » past ten;
  • the button « Ouvrir les fiches — les désaccords sont sur chaque fiche » opens them, when the app shows the Fiches tab;
  • no block is not a guarantee: some query shapes are skipped (OR, joins, ranges…).

docs.title: Follow-up questions
docs.text:
The chat speaks as lumnik: the input reads « Demande à lumnik… », and a question may start with « lumnik, … ». A question can continue the previous one — « Et HAWARD ? » after a question about Badu, « Et seulement celles de la catégorie Pompes ? » to narrow it. On a phone, over a catalogue of eight articles (bubbles marked by who wrote them, the SQL folded):

[you]     Donne-moi les références dont la description contient Badu.
[lumnik]  Il y a 3 références dont la description contient "Badu". Les références sont : 2195.300.037, 2195.300.038 et 3000.000.001.
          ▶ le SQL exécuté · 3 lignes
[you]     Et HAWARD ?
[lumnik]  Il y a 2 références dont la description contient HAWARD :

          1. 4100.000.001
          2. 4100.000.002

          Total de références : 2
          Compris comme : Donne-moi les références dont la description contient HAWARD.
          ▶ le SQL exécuté · 2 lignes
[you]     Et seulement celles de la catégorie Pompes ?
[lumnik]  Les références de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient HAWARD sont : 4100.000.001.
          Compris comme : Donne-moi les références de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient HAWARD.
          ▶ le SQL exécuté · 1 ligne
[you]     Et le deuxième, il coûte combien ?
[lumnik]  Je n'ai pas pu rattacher cette question à la précédente. Posez-la en entier, avec la valeur ou le nom auquel elle renvoie.
          [ suite de : Donne-moi les références de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient HAWARD. ✕ ]
          Nouvelle conversation
  • « Compris comme : … » sits under an answer whose question lumnik completed: it is the question that was really answered, and the SQL is that question's. Read it before trusting the figure. A question asked on its own gets no such line.
  • The chip « suite de : … », just above the input, is the one sentence the next question continues: the last question lumnik answered, as it understood it. A refusal or an error does not replace it, so you can rephrase and try again. A long sentence loses its middle on the chip, never its end. Tap the chip to ask the next question on its own.
  • « Nouvelle conversation » clears the thread and the chip.
  • What lumnik remembers is that sentence, nothing else — not the answers, not the questions before it. « Le deuxième », « celui-ci » point at a row of an answer lumnik does not keep, so they are refused, and the refusal asks for the value. A reload forgets the sentence, like the whole thread; and each app opens on its own page, so a thread never carries from one métier to another.

How a follow-up is resolved, and when it is refused, is in A question that follows the previous one; the field the PWA sends is previous.

docs.title: Responsive modes
docs.text:
One codebase, three postures — CSS breakpoints, not separate apps:

Width Fiches Navigation Detail phone (< 640px) cards bottom tabs bottom sheet tablet (≥ 640px) table bottom tabs bottom sheet display (≥ 900px) table left rail pinned side panel

docs.title: Identity & scope
docs.text:
The PWA is an OIDC public client: lumnik-spa, authorization code + PKCE (S256) against the realm. Tokens live in sessionStorage for the tab's lifetime; a silent refresh renews them ~60 s before expiry; logout is RP-initiated (Keycloak session ends too, not just the local one). Under the TLS façade, Keycloak is reached same-origin at /realms/lumnik — one issuer for every device.

External IdP: lumnik-spa needs an audience mapper

The hub requires aud=lumnik-backend on every token. The bundled realm carries the mapper for lumnik-spa; if you broker or replace Keycloak with your own IdP, the SPA client must add the same audience mapper — without it, every PKCE token is a plain 401 at the hub, with nothing wrong visible on the login side.

Access is the métier-scope boundary, nothing PWA-specific: the user needs the scope:<tag> role for their métier. Views, entities, and chat all refuse uniformly — 403 {"error":"scope not granted"} — and the PWA renders that as the amber refusal, never a broken screen.

docs.title: Offline behavior
docs.text:
Only the app shell (HTML, CSS, modules, icons) is cached on the device. Data and tokens never are: every data call goes to the network.

Offline, the app opens and shows Hors ligne — tes données reviendront avec le réseau. with a Réessayer button — never stale rows.

docs.title: How old is what I'm looking at?
docs.text:
A change in the source appears at the next run that reads it (its schedule, or lm connector run). The Fiches list and every chat answer carry a « données : il y a … » line: the age of the scope's last completed run. It is absent when the scope has none.

The integrator reads the run history with lm run list (or the TUI's :runs); what a run skipped or quarantined is in ingestion transparency.

docs.title: Add a métier
docs.text:
A métier app — title, scope, icon, colours — is a kind: App manifest applied with lm app apply -f. The PWA reads the apps at every login: no rebuild, no redeploy.

kind: App
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: lumilait
spec:
  title: Lumilait
  scope: lumilait
  icon: generic
  theme:
    accentColor: "#4fd1a5"
    backgroundColor: "#f4f1ea"
  default: false
  • icon — one of a curated set: clients, stock, generic, event, alert, contract. There is no upload path for a custom icon; generic is the right choice for a métier with no dedicated one.
  • theme — both colours are optional, defaulting to #8b7ff0/#14121f. accentColor is contrast-checked (WCAG AA): it is also the chat bubble's background.

  • default — the app an absent ?m= opens. At most one app holds it. To move it, apply another app with default: true; re-applying the current default with default: false is refused. Here clients-nodefault.yaml is the seeded clients app with default: false:

    kind: App
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: clients
spec:
  title: Clients
  scope: clients
  icon: clients
  default: false

    $ lm app apply -f clients-nodefault.yaml
Error: API error 400: cannot remove the last default app — apply a different app with default: true first, which demotes this one automatically

  • tabs — optional: which tabs the app shows, and in what order. Absent means every tab the hub offers. See Choosing the tabs.

$ lm app apply -f docs/apps/demo/apps/10-lumilait.yaml
Applied app "lumilait" → scope lumilait

Then apply at least one saved view for the scope (lm view apply -f) and grant the users their scope:<tag> role in Keycloak. Without them the app still opens: Fiches says that no view is applied, and every scoped call is refused.

docs.title: See what is declared
docs.text:
lm app list shows the registry the PWA reads, so you can check an apply, or find the app a login resolves to:

$ lm app list
NAME      TITLE     SCOPE     ICON     ACCENT   BACKGROUND  DEFAULT  TABS
clients   Clients   clients   clients  #8b7ff0  #14121f     yes      (all)
lumilait  Lumilait  lumilait  generic  #4fd1a5  #f4f1ea              (all)
stock     Stock     stock     stock    #8b7ff0  #14121f              (all)

A new hub carries clients (the default) and stock. DEFAULT marks the app an absent ?m= opens; (all) means the app declares no tabs. For a script, -o json (or -o yaml) gives every field, theme included:

$ lm app list -o json | jq -e '.[] | select(.name == "lumilait") | .accentColor == "#4fd1a5" and .backgroundColor == "#f4f1ea"'
true

The list is scope-bound like the PWA's own: an account holding scope: roles sees the apps of its scopes. If the hub refuses the call (an expired login, a missing role), that refusal is the error and the exit code is non-zero — never an empty list. A word that is not a subcommand (lm app foo) is an error too.

docs.title: Choosing the tabs
docs.text:
This page covers the app's own list. What a hub offers in the first place — the build, the AI switch, a Search provider — is in Choosing what your hub offers.

An app shows every tab its hub has: Fiches and Décisions everywhere, plus Chat when your edition includes it and Recherche when your hub has Search. To show fewer — no Chat for the warehouse, say — or to change the order, list the tabs in the app's manifest, then apply it with lm app apply -f app.yaml:

spec:
  tabs: [fiches, inbox]
  • Leave tabs out and the app shows every tab the hub has and the app can draw, including one added by a later release.
  • The app opens on the first tab of your list that the hub has.
  • The names are fiches, inbox (shown as Décisions), chat and search (shown as Recherche).

  • Asking for a tab your hub does not have is fine: lm app apply warns, and the tab appears the day the hub has it. The same manifest works on an Open hub and on a Pro hub:

    kind: App
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: desk
spec:
  title: Desk
  scope: desk
  icon: generic
  tabs: [fiches, inbox, search]

    $ lm app apply -f desk-app.yaml
Applied app "desk" → scope desk
  tabs: fiches, inbox, search
! desk-app.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.tabs[2]
          tab 'search' is not offered by this hub; the declaration is kept and takes effect when a module offering it is active
          → offered here: [fiches, inbox]

  • If none of the tabs you listed exists on the hub, the app says that no feature is available for it, instead of showing an empty screen.

  • Hiding a tab does not lock anything: who may read what is still decided by roles and scopes.
  • lm app apply refuses a value that is not a list, an empty list (leave tabs out instead), a tab named twice, more than 16 tabs, and a name that is not a lowercase word (letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter).

docs.title: Enabling Recherche for an app
docs.text:
Recherche shows up for a métier once four things are in place:

  1. A Search provider in the hub — the hub is built with one (choosing a provider).
  2. Entities carrying the app's scope — the entities you want searched are tagged with the same scope as the app's spec.scope. The app searches those and no others.
  3. A search index over them — apply a kind: SearchIndex (declare one) with lm search apply -f index.yaml. The hub builds it within about a minute; lm search rebuild NAME --wait builds it now and waits.
  4. The tab in the app's list — if the app's manifest has no tabs, Recherche is there on its own. If it lists its tabs, add search:
spec:
  tabs: [fiches, inbox, search]

Check it from the terminal with lm search status (every index) or lm search status NAME (one): an index that is built and fresh is what the métier's search runs over. A user must also hold the roles that let them read those entities; the tab does not widen anyone's access.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• kind: View — the manifests the Fiches tab renders.
  • Inbox — the decisions fold behind the Décisions tab.
  • Scopes — the boundary the whole app lives within.

docs.title: kind: View — see
docs.text:
The first rung of the per-métier app ladder: a declarative, read-only list over a scope's table, rendered by the hub and displayed by lm, the TUI or the PWA. One YAML says which columns; a filter it cannot apply is refused instead of showing an empty table.

Kind View — apps.lumnik.io/v1 Over any table of a scope's card: a raw connector.t_*, or a fused connector.v_* Renders lm view -f FILE or lm view NAME (list, filters, one record's detail); the TUI's :view; the PWA's Fiches tab Store lm view apply / lm view rm — lm_integrator, scope-bound; reads lm_user Bounds 1 000 rows and a 5-second statement timeout per read, read-only, tenant-isolated; when more rows match, lm view ends with first 1000 rows shown; more match — narrow with --filter (-o json: "truncated": true) Edition Open

A view is a title, a table and the columns worth looking at. Over an entity it uses the entity's labels, and a record's detail ends with the sources' disagreements on it. The file is the app — hand-written, or drafted by the AI.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Over a raw table or a fused entity. A freshly landed export is viewable as it is; an entity's view carries its labels and its _conflicts ledger.
  • A filter grammar that refuses. An unknown column, a column the view does not show, a malformed filter or a value outside a declared domain is refused.
  • One record's detail, disagreements included. lm view KEY prints a record and, under Ambiguïtés et divergences, which source said what.
  • A store the PWA discovers. lm view apply publishes a manifest; anyone holding the scope finds it on their phone.
  • Drafted by the AI, gated like a render. The model picks table, columns and filters; the hub validates them and writes the YAML.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads the demo desk that ships with the repo

Land the three sources as The demo desk shows, then apply the customer entity: lm entity apply -f docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml.

# 10-customers.yaml — the desk's customer list, over the fused entity.
#
# Column headers are the labels the entity manifest declares; the detail of one record ends
# with its _conflicts ledger when the sources conflict on it.
#
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter city=Lyon
#   lm view P-1000 -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
kind: View

  table: connector.v_acmecustomer

  columns: [code, name, city, segment, credit_limit]

docs.title: The manifest
Linking views
docs.text:
A cell can lead somewhere. Declare it on the view the user starts from:

apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: View
metadata:
  name: categories
spec:
  scope: catalogue
  table: connector.v_category
  title: Catégories
  columns: [category_id, name, description, active]
  links:
    # click the name: open the articles view, already filtered on this category
    - column: name
      targetView: articles
      filters:
        category_id: "{category_id}"
    # click the id: open the same category in the ERP
    - column: category_id
      url: "https://erp.example.com/categories/{category_id}"
  • To another view. Tapping Pompes opens the articles view with category_id=1000021 already applied, on its first page. The filter shows in the filter bar like one the user typed, and removes the same way.
  • To an external page. Tapping a category id opens https://erp.example.com/categories/1000021 in a new tab.
  • {column} is the value of that column on the row tapped. It must be one of this view's spec.columns. Literal text around it is kept (CAT-{category_id}). Nothing else is substituted.
  • One destination per link: targetView (with at least one filter) or url, never both. One link per column, at most 16 links, at most 8 filters per link.
  • A row whose value is empty has no link on that cell.

The target view judges the link's filters, like any filter: an unknown column, a value outside a declared domain or a malformed value is refused. The target must be a view of the same scope. If it is missing or refuses the filter, the user stays on the current view and reads why; the target is never opened unfiltered.

Order of apply. A target that does not exist yet is accepted with a warning (stderr, exit 0); the link works once the target is applied:

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/30-categories-links.yaml
applied: categories (scope catalogue)
! 30-categories-links.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.links[0].targetView
          targetView 'articles' is not a view of scope 'catalogue' (yet); the declaration is kept, and following the link is refused until that view is applied

If the target exists but does not show a filtered column, the warning names the column.

External links:

  • https:// only, with the host written out — no {column} before the first /, no credentials.
  • The value is percent-encoded, so an id like a/b?x stays inside its segment.
  • The page opens in a new tab without a referrer.
  • The other system receives the value — link only to systems you trust with it.

The same rules apply to a search result's link to your ERP.

docs.title: A view over a raw table
docs.text:
No entity is needed: a view can point straight at a raw table the scope's connectors land — here the order book, as the ERP exported it:

# 20-orders.yaml — a view straight over a raw ingest table, no entity needed.
#
# A scope's card lists the raw tables as well as the fused views, so a freshly landed export
# is viewable as it is. The status column is shown exactly as the ERP spells it.
#
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'status~litige'
#   lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'amount>1000'
kind: View
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
metadata:
  name: acme-orders
spec:
  scope: desk
  table: connector.t_acme_desk_orders
  title: Commandes
  columns: [order_no, code, status, amount, ordered_on]

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'status~litige'
Commandes · status~litige

order_no   code    status     amount   ordered_on
SO-000006  P-1008  EN LITIGE  4100.00  2026-08-07
SO-000010  P-1004  EN LITIGE  77.00    2026-08-12

The headers are the raw column names, because nothing declared a label. A kind: Workflow is what declares what the status values mean.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
lm view -f FILE                                # the list, from a manifest file
lm view -f FILE --filter city=Lyon             # filtered; repeatable, ANDed
lm view KEY -f FILE                            # one record — KEY matches the first declared column
lm view NAME [KEY]                             # the same, from a view saved in the store

A saved view renders without a file:

$ lm view acme-customers --filter segment=GOLD
Clients ACME · segment=GOLD

Code client  Raison sociale            Ville   Segment  Encours autorisé
P-1000       Hydraulique Lyon 1000     Lyon    GOLD     500
P-1003       Pneumatique Porto 1003    Porto   GOLD     911
P-1005       Transmission Aarhus 1005  Aarhus  GOLD     1185
P-1008       Filtration Lyon 1008      Lyon    GOLD     1596

Rendering needs lm_user and stays inside the métier-scope boundary: a view whose spec.scope you do not hold answers 403 scope not granted.

Bound What happens 1 000 rows per read lm view prints the first 1 000 rows and does not say the list was cut. The hub's JSON answer carries "truncated": true; narrow the list with filters 5-second statement timeout refused with a 400 that says so Order the first declared column, nulls last, then the record's own id (for a fused entity, the remaining declared columns)

A timestamp cell, in a render or a record's detail, is its UTC instant with the microseconds stored, "2026-07-01T00:00:00.000500Z": the text lm data row shows. Numbers and booleans stay JSON numbers and booleans.

The PWA reads a view page by page (50 rows); lm view has no paging flag. Over HTTP the door is POST /api/views/render?pageSize=N (1 to 200):

  • the answer carries "hasMore": true and an opaque "nextCursor" when more rows exist;
  • send it back as &cursor=… with the same manifest, filters and pageSize;
  • any change (filter, page size, view, scope) makes the cursor 400 this page link is no longer valid — reload the view from its first page;
  • no total is counted;
  • on a table no row is skipped or repeated between pages; a fused entity is paged by position, so a row ingested between two page reads can shift its boundary by one.

A slow page on a large table? Narrow it with filters first. Then add an index matching the paging order, (tenant_id, first_column, id) — the hub never creates one.

In the TUI, :view opens the same file interactively:

Key Action f add a filter F clear the filters r re-render Enter one record's detail o open another manifest g generate a manifest from a sentence a apply the rendered view to the store

docs.title: Filter grammar
docs.text:
Form Meaning col=value exact match; a date against a date or timestamp column is equal as an instant (due=2026-07-01 is midnight UTC); a number against a number column by value (amount=1500.00 finds 1500); on a column with declared values, an out-of-domain value is refused col~text substring, case-insensitive col>v col<v col>=v col<=v ordering — v must be a number or an ISO-8601 date; a row whose value has neither shape is not matched

The ordering forms work on the text columns a CSV or a fusion produces — credit_limit>1000 above, and on the order book:

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml --filter 'ordered_on>2026-08-10'
Commandes · ordered_on>2026-08-10

order_no   code    status     amount   ordered_on
SO-000009  P-1010             120.00   2026-08-11
SO-000010  P-1004  EN LITIGE  77.00    2026-08-12
SO-000011  P-1006  BROUILLON  3000.00  2026-08-12
SO-000012  P-1011  En cours   55.00    2026-08-13

Whether a column takes an ordering filter depends on its type:

Column type Ordering (< > <= >=) number (floating-point included), date, timestamp yes text holding numbers or dates yes money, time, interval, boolean, uuid refused, naming the column and its type — use = or ~

A bound may be written in scientific notation (1e-5, 6.022e23); on a floating-point column it must fit a double. A number orders a number or text column, a date a date or text column.

A date or date-time written without an offset is read as UTC, in the bound and in the column alike: ordered_on>2026-08-10 starts at midnight UTC, whatever time zone the hub runs in. A process reads a date the same way, so a view and a process given the same filter pick the same rows (how a process compares a date). ~ on a timestamp column searches its text written in UTC, 2026-01-01 00:30:00+00.

docs.title: Refusal rules
docs.text:
Each refusal names the fix:

$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/60-refused-unknown-column.yaml
Error: API error 400: column 'phone' is not in the 'desk' schema for table connector.v_acmecustomer — fix the column name or add it to the scope's entity
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter email~example
Error: API error 400: cannot filter on 'email' — the view does not show it; declare it in spec.columns to filter on it
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter 'city~'
Error: API error 400: filter 'city~' needs a column and a value — col=value, col~text, or col>value
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter segment=PLATINUM
Error: API error 400: 'PLATINUM' is not an allowed value for segment (allowed: GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)
$ lm view -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml --filter "city='Lyon'"
Error: API error 400: filter value 'Lyon' is quoted; a value here is a bare literal, so the quotes would be compared to city too — write city=Lyon
Refused Why an unknown column in columns: the scope's card does not have it a filter on a column the view does not show filters run over the view's own columns a malformed filter — an ordering filter on a type that cannot be ordered see the operator table above an = value outside the column's declared domain the entity's values — the same rule as the chat's domain guard a quoted value write city=Lyon. A lone apostrophe is data: name~l'ecole works

A zero-row result is then meaningful: the filter is valid and matches nothing.

docs.title: The saved-view store
docs.text:
A manifest can also live in the hub, where the métier PWA at /app/ finds it under its scope:

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml
applied: acme-customers (scope desk)
$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/20-orders.yaml
applied: acme-orders (scope desk)
$ lm view list
NAME            SCOPE  TITLE
acme-customers  desk   Clients ACME
acme-orders     desk   Commandes
$ lm view get acme-customers -o acme.yaml
manifest written to acme.yaml — review it, then: lm view -f acme.yaml

lm view get NAME without -o prints the stored YAML, comments included, byte for byte.

Command Effect Role lm view apply -f FILE validate-then-upsert: a view that cannot render is never saved; re-applying a name overwrites lm_integrator lm view list [--scope TAG] NAME · SCOPE · TITLE — a scope-bound user sees only the granted scopes' views lm_user lm view get NAME [-o FILE] the manifest YAML verbatim lm_user lm view rm NAME removes the view for good, no prompt lm_integrator 
$ lm view rm acme-orders
view acme-orders deleted
$ lm view rm acme-orders
Error: API error 404: no saved view named 'acme-orders'
  • There is no disable: a saved view is live from apply until rm.
  • apply and rm are scope-bound: a scope-bound integrator cannot publish or remove a view outside their grants.
  • Every apply and removal is recorded in the audit trail — actor, name, scope, and for an apply the manifest's SHA-256.
  • The store is shared by all tenants of the deployment; every render reads only your tenant's rows.

A user holding only scope:stock sees nothing of the desk:

$ lm view list
NAME  SCOPE  TITLE
$ lm view list --scope desk
Error: access refused (403): scope not granted

The stored name must be a URL-safe slug, and four names are reserved:

$ lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/62-refused-reserved-name.yaml
Error: API error 400: metadata.name must be a URL-safe slug ([a-z0-9_-], starting with a letter or digit) and not one of [detail, render, apply, generate]

docs.title: Generate a view with the AI
docs.text:
Describe the need; the hub's model selects the table, the columns and the filters, the hub validates them like a render, and writes the YAML. The manifest is yours to review and keep.

$ lm view generate desk "les clients de Lyon" -o lyon.yaml
manifest written to lyon.yaml — review it, then: lm view -f lyon.yaml
$ cat lyon.yaml
# asked for: les clients de Lyon
# kept: city=Lyon — a condition of that description not listed here is NOT enforced
# lm view -f clients_of_lyon.yaml --filter 'city=Lyon'
apiVersion: "apps.lumnik.io/v1"
kind: "View"
metadata:
  name: "clients_of_lyon"
spec:
  scope: "desk"
  table: "connector.v_acmecustomer"
  title: "Clients of Lyon"
  columns:
  - "code"
  - "name"
  - "city"
  - "segment"
  - "credit_limit"
Header line Tells you # asked for: your sentence, on one line # kept: the filters the view enforces — anything else in your sentence is not enforced # lm view -f … a ready-to-run render; it names the file by the manifest's name, not your -o

Within generate, -o is the output file, not the output format.

  • A quoted value the model writes (city='Lyon') is unquoted before validation.
  • A filter on a column the model left out of columns adds that column.
  • Generation is rate-limited per tenant: lumnik.ratelimit.view-generate.rpm, default 10 per minute; past it, lm prints rate limited (429): rate limit exceeded, retry in Ns.

docs.title: Generation contract
docs.text:
Case Answer The scope cannot serve the description ("les commandes" over a scope with no orders) the model abstains; you get its reason, never invented columns The selection fails validation (unknown column, invalid filter) one retry with the exact error; a second failure returns the error and the model's raw output No card for the scope no schema for scope '…' — run discovery first No chat model on the hub generation abstained: no chat model is available on this hub — view generation needs one

Nothing checks that the model kept everything you asked for — read the # kept: line:

$ lm view generate desk "les commandes en litige de plus de 500 euros" -o litiges.yaml
manifest written to litiges.yaml — review it, then: lm view -f litiges.yaml
$ head -3 litiges.yaml
# asked for: les commandes en litige de plus de 500 euros
# kept: amount>500 — a condition of that description not listed here is NOT enforced
# lm view -f commandes_en_litige.yaml --filter 'amount>500'

Two conditions asked, one kept: en litige was dropped. Add the filter by hand, or rephrase.

"Run discovery first": lm source rediscover --scope <tag> rebuilds the schema card (needs lm_integrator and lm_admin, and a scope you hold). lm source schema --scope <tag> shows what the card holds.

docs.title: Show one métier a filtered list on their phone
docs.text:
lm view apply -f docs/apps/demo/views/10-customers.yaml

Result: anyone holding scope:desk finds Clients ACME under the Fiches tab of the PWA at /app/, with the same filter grammar as the CLI.

docs.title: Let the AI draft a view, then check it before anyone else sees it
docs.text:
lm view generate desk "les clients de Lyon" -o lyon.yaml
cat lyon.yaml                                             # review it — the third line is the suggested render
lm view -f lyon.yaml --filter city=Lyon                   # test it yourself
lm view apply -f lyon.yaml                                # only once it looks right

Result: only apply writes to the store. Nobody else sees the draft before that.

docs.title: Look at an export before any entity exists
docs.text: Point spec.table at the raw connector.t_* table — 20-orders.yaml above. Result: the export's own columns, unlabelled, filterable the same way.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture apply refused: unknown key(s) in the manifest: … a misspelled field (titel:) the message lists what kind:View honors — fix the spelling render or apply refused: column is not in the '…' schema for table … spec.columns names a column the scope's card does not have fix the column name, or add it to the scope's entity filter refused: cannot filter on '…' — the view does not show it filtering on a column not listed in spec.columns add the column to spec.columns filter refused: '…' is not an allowed value for … the entity declares a values domain for that column one of the listed values — or fix the domain in the entity filter refused: '…' is not a number or ISO date — > needs an ordered value an ordering filter with a value that is neither a number, or YYYY-MM-DD apply answers with a warning on spec.links[…].targetView the target view is not applied yet in that scope apply the target; the link then works apply refused: spec.links[…].url: an external link is https://… http:, a relative address, or a host that is not written out write the full https://host/path/{column} following a link answers Lien refusé : … the target refused the filter fix the filter in links[].filters, or the target's columns 403 … scope not granted you do not hold the spec.scope role ask for that scope: role apply refused: metadata.name must be a URL-safe slug … the name is not a lowercase slug, or is apply/render/detail/generate rename metadata.name rate limited (429): rate limit exceeded, retry in Ns on generate over 10 lm view generate calls per minute for the tenant wait the seconds it names, then retry 404 … no schema for scope '…' — run discovery first discovery has never run for that scope lm source rediscover --scope <tag> (lm_integrator + lm_admin) generation abstained: … / generation failed: … the card cannot serve the description, the selection failed twice, or the hub has no chat model rephrase, or write the filter by hand; lm source schema --scope <tag> shows what the card has the title reads like a table name no spec.title, and the entity declares no label: set spec.title, or give the entity a label: a list stops at exactly 1 000 rows the render cap narrow it with filters API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server you lack the role: lm_integrator for apply and rm, lm_user for the rest ask your administrator; no lm command lists your roles (GET /api/bff/v1/me returns them under roles)
