docs.title: kind: Workflow — declare
docs.text:
The fourth rung: a declarative document lifecycle over a status column ingestion already landed — states, aliases for the spellings the source really uses, the transition graph, and a threshold past which a document that has not moved is a decision.

Kind Workflow — apps.lumnik.io/v1 Over one column of one table: a raw connector.t_*, or a fused connector.v_* (taxonomy only) Declares states with aliases, transitions, provenance: declared; optionally a business key and a dormancy threshold Produces a data-truth report at apply; one chunk in the scope's corpus; decision.dormant.<name> alerts and an observation tape when watched Commands lm workflow apply · list · get · disable · enable · rm — lm_integrator, scope-bound; one lifecycle per column Edition Open

Legacy exports carry dirty statuses — En cours, encours, fini, TERMINE with a trailing space. A workflow declares what they mean, so the chat answers lifecycle questions from a declared graph instead of inventing one.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Dirty values resolve to declared states. Alias matching is trim and case-insensitive.
  • A data-truth report that never blocks. Apply compares the declaration with the column — undeclared values, unobserved codes, blanks — and stores the manifest either way.
  • Grounded answers. The lifecycle is one chunk in the scope's corpus.
  • Dormancy. A key and a threshold turn the declaration into a watch: a document unmoved in a non-terminal state past the threshold is a decision.dormant.* in the inbox.
  • A tape that outlives the alert. Every watched document's state, since when, and whether it alerted.
  • One column, one lifecycle. A second lifecycle on the same column is refused, naming the first.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Every screen on this page reads the demo desk that ships with the repo

An order book whose status column carries seven spellings and one blank, under docs/apps/demo/. Land it first — The demo desk has the commands and the hand count. The screens below start on day 1.

# 10-order-lifecycle.yaml — the lifecycle the orders' status column already has.
#
# Four declared states with aliases for the spellings the export really carries, a
# transition graph, and a dormancy threshold that turns the declaration into a watched one.
# `ANNULE` is declared and never seen; `EN LITIGE` and `Terminé` are seen and never declared.
# Apply reports both — and refuses neither: a fact about the data is not a contradiction in
# the declaration.
#
# Expect: 200, dataTruth.undeclared = EN LITIGE (2 rows) + Terminé (1), unobserved = [ANNULE],
#         nullOrBlank = 1, keyNullOrBlank = 0.
apiVersion: apps.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: acme-order-lifecycle
spec:
  scope: desk
  provenance: declared
  on:
    table: connector.t_acme_desk_orders
    column: status
    key: order_no
  dormancy:
    after: 30d
  states:
    - code: BROUILLON
      label: "Brouillon"
      initial: true
    - code: EN_COURS
      label: "En préparation"
      aliases: [en cours, encours]
    - code: TERMINE
      label: "Terminée"
      aliases: [fini]
      terminal: true
    - code: ANNULE
      label: "Annulée"
      terminal: true
  transitions:
    - { from: [BROUILLON], to: EN_COURS }
    - { from: [BROUILLON, EN_COURS], to: ANNULE }
    - { from: [EN_COURS], to: TERMINE }

The same manifest, as the graph it declares:

stateDiagram-v2
  direction LR
  [*] --> BROUILLON
  BROUILLON --> EN_COURS
  BROUILLON --> ANNULE
  EN_COURS --> ANNULE
  EN_COURS --> TERMINE
  TERMINE --> [*]
  ANNULE --> [*]
  note right of EN_COURS
    «En préparation»
    aliases: "en cours", "encours"
    dormancy: unmoved 30d → alert
  end note
  note right of TERMINE
    alias: "fini" — terminal
  end note
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml
{"name":"acme-order-lifecycle","scope":"desk","table":"connector.t_acme_desk_orders","column":"status","dataTruth":{"undeclared":[{"value":"EN LITIGE","rows":2},{"value":"Terminé","rows":1}],"unobserved":["ANNULE"],"nullOrBlank":1,"tableMissing":false,"keyColumnMissing":false,"keyNullOrBlank":0,"checkUnavailable":false,"unavailableReason":null}}
$ lm workflow list
NAME                  TABLE                         COLUMN  SCOPE  ENABLED
acme-order-lifecycle  connector.t_acme_desk_orders  status  desk   true

One 200, stored and indexed, with what the declaration and the data disagree on:

  • EN LITIGE sits on two orders and nobody declared it; Terminé (with its accent) on one;
  • ANNULE is declared and no order has reached it;
  • one order has no status at all.

EN LITIGE is deliberately not in the graph: it stays visible in the report, and the dormancy sweep still watches it.

docs.title: The manifest
The scope must exist, the table need not
docs.text:
spec.scope must be a discovered scope; an unknown one is a 404, as for a process:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/65-refused-unknown-scope.yaml
Error: API error 404: no schema for scope 'dsk' — run discovery first

The table is not checked: you may declare a lifecycle before ingesting the data. The report then says tableMissing: true.

docs.title: Names the source chose
docs.text:
on.column and on.key are the names your source uses, copied as they are — a Kafka message's JSON keys become columns verbatim:

on:
  table: connector.t_Commandes
  column: "Statut Commande"
  key: "N° Commande"

Quote them in the YAML if they contain spaces or punctuation; the hub adds the SQL quotes.

on.table must be a table ingestion owns — connector.t_<table>, or connector.v_<entity> — spelled the way the hub created it (a connector's target keeps your capitals, a fused view is lower case, neither contains a space). Anything else is refused, the hub's own tables included:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/66-refused-foreign-table.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.on.table is required and must name a table in the 'connector' schema that ingestion owns (connector.t_<table>) or a fused entity view (connector.v_<entity>, always lower-case), spelled the way the hub created it (letters, digits and underscores — a space is a typo): identity.app_user

A fused view can carry a taxonomy but not a dormancy: declare the dormancy on the ingest table the entity fuses, or drop spec.dormancy.

docs.title: One column, one lifecycle
docs.text:
A different name declaring an already-declared on.table + on.column is refused, naming the holder:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/64-refused-same-column.yaml
Error: API error 400: column connector.t_acme_desk_orders.status already has a declared lifecycle: workflow 'acme-order-lifecycle' — a column has exactly one lifecycle; re-apply under the name 'acme-order-lifecycle' to update it

apply on the same name is the update. The rule is per tenant.

docs.title: Alias semantics
docs.text:
Alias and code matching is trim + case-insensitive: "TERMINE ", "fini", "En cours" all resolve. On the demo desk, day 1:

Status as written Rows Resolves to En cours, encours 4 EN_COURS fini, TERMINE 2 TERMINE BROUILLON 2 BROUILLON EN LITIGE 2 undeclared Terminé 1 undeclared — an accent is not an alias anyone declared (empty) 1 nullOrBlank

Contradictions in the declaration are refused:

$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/61-refused-alias-collision.yaml
Error: API error 400: alias 'en_cours' on state BROUILLON collides with state code
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/60-refused-two-initial.yaml
Error: API error 400: exactly one state must be initial: true (found 2)
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/62-refused-terminal-outgoing.yaml
Error: API error 400: terminal state 'TERMINE' has an outgoing transition
  • an alias that collides with a state code;
  • an alias declared on two different states;
  • not exactly one initial: true;
  • a terminal: true state with an outgoing transition.

docs.title: The data-truth report — never blocks
docs.text:
apply stores the manifest first, then compares it with what the column contains. The comparison never becomes a refusal:

Field Meaning On the demo desk (day 1) undeclared values in the data with no matching state or alias, each with its row count EN LITIGE ×2, Terminé ×1 unobserved declared codes never seen in the column ANNULE nullOrBlank rows with no status at all 1 tableMissing the table does not exist (yet, or any more) false keyColumnMissing spec.on.key names a column the table does not have — the only signal a misspelled key produces false keyNullOrBlank rows whose key is NULL or blank: documents the dormancy sweep skips. null = not measured 0 checkUnavailable + unavailableReason the comparison could not run (timeout, dropped column, revoked grant); the other fields are empty, not "the data agrees". Re-apply once fixed false

keyNullOrBlank counts presence only — a row with neither key nor status is in both counters, and a present key is not proof it is unique or stable.

The comparison looks at the 200 most frequent distinct values: on a high-cardinality column a rare undeclared value can fall below the cut.

docs.title: What the chat answers from it
docs.text:
Applying a workflow indexes it as one chunk in the manifest's scope: states, aliases, transitions, provenance. Two doors read differently:

Door Gesture Answers about semantic lm chat, then :scope desk (or lm scope set desk first) the graph: transitions, states, aliases analytic lm ask --scope desk "…", the PWA's Chat tab the rows: a document's current status

The semantic door, asked over HTTP (the same chat lm chat reaches):

curl -s "$HUB/api/rag/chat" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"question":"Pourquoi je ne peux pas clôturer la commande SO-000004 ? Quelles sont les étapes avant TERMINE ?","scope":"desk"}'

Its answer field:

Les étapes autorisées pour passer du statut BROUILLON sont : BROUILLON -> EN_COURS, BROUILLON -> ANNULE.
Les étapes autorisées pour passer du statut EN_COURS sont : EN_COURS -> ANNULE, EN_COURS -> TERMINE.
Aucune étape n'est autorisée pour passer directement de BROUILLON à TERMINE. […]

Every transition it names is declared. It does not know which state SO-000004 is in — the chunk carries the graph, not the table. The analytic door does:

$ lm ask --scope desk "Dans quel statut est la commande SO-000004 ?"
La commande SO-000004 est en statut "BROUILLON".
  data as of: 2026-10-16T08:43:46.474408Z (last completed run)

  STATUS
  BROUILLON
  1 row returned

  SQL: SELECT status FROM "connector"."t_acme_desk_orders" WHERE order_no = 'SO-000004'
LIMIT 500

Asked "why can't I close it", the analytic door abstains: it does not read the lifecycle chunk.

docs.title: Dormancy — the memory of the breathing
docs.text:
A legacy status is overwritten in place: the raw table says an order is EN_COURS, not since when. A scheduled sweep records each document's state from the moment lumnik starts watching, and alerts when one has sat unmoved, in a non-terminal state, past the declared threshold.

  • Two fields switch it on: spec.on.key (order_no — links a document's successive rows) and spec.dormancy.after (30d, any [0-9]+[mhd]).
  • The sweep runs every 15 minutes (lumnik.workflow.sweep.every, Observability).
  • The clock starts at lumnik's first sighting, not at the real stall: declare after: 14d today over orders stuck for weeks, and the earliest alert is in fourteen days.
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/63-refused-dormancy-no-key.yaml
Error: API error 400: spec.dormancy requires spec.on.key (dormancy is per-document; the key links a document's versions)

The tape after the first sweep that saw the desk (day 1):

$ lm observations list
WORKFLOW              DOC        STATE      SINCE             ALERTED
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000001  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000002  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000003  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000004  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000005  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000006  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000007  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000008  Terminé    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000010  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000012  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  
$ lm observations stats
WORKFLOW              WATCHED  DORMANT  MEDIAN_DETECTION_S
acme-order-lifecycle  11       0        -

SO-000009 is absent: it has no status, so there is no state to watch. The states are the resolved codes where an alias matched (fini reads TERMINE), the raw value where none did.

For the next screens the threshold was shortened to after: 1m and the manifest re-applied under the same name (the shipped file keeps 30d). Then day 2 was loaded:

docker cp docs/apps/demo/data/acme-orders-day2.csv lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/acme-desk/acme-orders.csv
lm connector run acme-desk-orders

Two ticks later:

$ lm observations list
WORKFLOW              DOC        STATE      SINCE             ALERTED
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000001  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000002  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000003  TERMINE    2026-10-19 01:51  
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000004  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000005  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000006  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000007  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000008  Terminé    2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000010  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011  BROUILLON  2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000012  EN_COURS   2026-10-19 01:51  2026-10-19 02:06
acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000013  EN LITIGE  2026-10-19 02:06  2026-10-19 02:21
$ lm observations stats
WORKFLOW              WATCHED  DORMANT  MEDIAN_DETECTION_S
acme-order-lifecycle  12       10       900
  • Ten alerts: nine at the first tick past the threshold, then SO-000013 — new on day 2, first seen at 02:06 — one tick later.
  • The two TERMINE orders never alert: a terminal state is excluded.
  • SO-000008 does alert: Terminé, with its accent, matched no alias, and an undeclared value can never be terminal.
  • The median detection delay is 900 s — one sweep interval, the floor.

What each alert says, in the inbox:

$ lm inbox --limit 3
ID  WHEN      PROCESS                        MESSAGE                                                                                                                                  ENTITY_KEY
47  just now  workflow:acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000013: observed unmoved in "EN LITIGE" since 2026-10-19 (first observed 2026-10-19) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000013
46  15min     workflow:acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000012: observed unmoved in "EN_COURS" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle   SO-000012
45  15min     workflow:acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011: observed unmoved in "BROUILLON" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle  SO-000011
note: result hit the limit of 3 — there may be more

ENTITY_KEY is the business key. The wording names the date lumnik started watching, the date it first saw the document and the declared threshold — never how long the order sat in the ERP. The message's dates are UTC, while lm observations list shows your terminal's time zone: the 01:51 (Paris) sighting was 23:51 UTC the day before.

docs.title: Applying it
docs.text:
lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml
lm workflow list
lm workflow get acme-order-lifecycle      # the stored manifest, verbatim, comments included
lm observations list                      # the tape: what has not moved, stillest first
lm observations stats                     # per workflow: watched, dormant, median detection delay
lm inbox                                  # where decision.dormant.<name> lands

Turn it off, or remove it:

$ lm workflow disable acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle enabled=false
$ lm workflow list
NAME                  TABLE                         COLUMN  SCOPE  ENABLED
acme-order-lifecycle  connector.t_acme_desk_orders  status  desk   false
$ lm workflow enable acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle enabled=true
$ lm workflow rm acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle deleted
$ lm workflow rm acme-order-lifecycle
Error: API error 404: unknown workflow: acme-order-lifecycle

disable stops the sweep (no new alerts) and removes the lifecycle from chat, keeping the manifest and the tape; enable restores both. rm removes it for good, with no prompt — its tape too (lm observations stats no longer lists it). Each gesture, and every apply, is recorded in the audit trail.

Command Role Scope-bound lm workflow apply, list, get, disable, enable, rm lm_integrator yes — outside your grants, 403 scope not granted; list shows only your scopes lm observations list, stats lm_integrator and lm_admin (or lm_superadmin) yes — they list only the workflows of your scopes

docs.title: Declare the lifecycle a legacy status column already has
docs.text:
lm workflow apply -f docs/apps/demo/workflows/10-order-lifecycle.yaml
lm workflow get acme-order-lifecycle

Result: the manifest is stored and indexed in one 200, with the data-truth report. The semantic chat in that scope now answers transition questions from the declared graph.

docs.title: Get told when a document stops moving
docs.text:
The demo manifest already carries spec.on.key and spec.dormancy.after: applying it switches the sweep on. Alerts land in lm inbox (and the PWA's Décisions tab) for users holding the workflow's scope and for users with no scope: role. To push them to an external system, lm integration add (Processes).

Don't treat the inbox as a register of everything asleep. A document alerts once per stall, and the alert ages out with the event log (30 days by default). The tape keeps it — see Re-alert semantics.

docs.title: Add the value the report says nobody declared
docs.text: dataTruth.undeclared named EN LITIGE. Add it as a state (or an alias of one) and re-apply under the same name. Result: the report no longer lists it, the chat knows what it means, and the sweep watches it as a declared state. The documents the tape held as EN LITIGE, and the source still holds, read the declared code from the next tick; a meaning is not a movement, so their SINCE, their alert and the transition journal stay as they were.

docs.title: Checking a proposal dossier
docs.text:
A business person can describe a problem on lumnik.fr and download a proposal dossier. Before turning it into manifests, ask the hub what it can establish on your data, against a workflow you already applied. No lm command does this; the door is HTTP:

curl -X POST "$HUB/api/proposal/check?workflow=<name>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --data-binary @dossier.md > dossier-checked.md

It needs lm_integrator; $TOKEN is the token lm login stored (see the HTTP API quickstart). The answer is the same file, checked; nothing is applied, and the original answers are untouched. Without workflow=, the dossier is only recomputed.

Point Confirmed when Refuted when a status column exists the comparison read the column the table is there and the column is not an identifier column exists the table has the spec.on.key column the table is there and does not have it (judged only if the status column exists) the target is accepted by the watch validation the workflow is stored never
  • What only a person can establish (the column describes the lifecycle, the identifier is stable) stays to be established.
  • A table not ingested yet, a timeout or a missing grant leave a point unchanged.
  • The proof is about your data today.
  • A dossier for another catalogue version is returned recomputed, unverified.
  • The answer is the same whether the workflow does not exist, is not yours, or no longer parses.
  • A malformed dossier is a 400 with the reason (duplicate-key); a file that is not UTF-8 is a 400 malformed-header.

docs.title: Drafting a manifest from a dossier
docs.text:
lm proposal draft writes the start of the manifest a dossier proposes. It does not contact the hub:

lm proposal draft dossier.md \
  --name orders-lifecycle --scope sales \
  --table connector.t_commandes --column statut --key n_commande --after 14d \
  -o orders-lifecycle.yaml
  • Every flag is optional; a value you leave out is left out of the file, with a comment saying where it goes.
  • States and transitions are never generated: you write them before lm workflow apply.
  • --after without --key is accepted here and refused at apply.
  • The header comments list each point, refuted first, then missing, unverified, confirmed; what no tool can check is marked to establish yourself.
  • -o never overwrites a file; without it the draft goes to stdout. The dossier can come from stdin (lm proposal draft -).
  • A dossier with no stalled-documents@1 lead, or two, is refused; other leads are named on stderr.

The loop: draft → complete and lm workflow apply -f → check the dossier against the stored workflow (the curl above) → draft again from the checked dossier, to a new file.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture apply refused: unknown key(s) in the manifest: … a misspelled or misplaced field the message lists what kind:Workflow honors, level by level apply refused 404: no schema for scope '…' — run discovery first spec.scope is not a discovered scope lm source rediscover --scope <tag> (lm_integrator + lm_admin, a scope you hold), then re-apply apply refused: column … already has a declared lifecycle: workflow '…' a different name declares this on.table + on.column re-apply under the existing name, or point at a different column apply refused: column … already has a declared lifecycle, in a métier you do not hold the same, in a scope you do not hold ask the integrator who owns that scope apply refused: spec.dormancy requires spec.on.key … spec.dormancy.after without spec.on.key add spec.on.key apply refused: spec.dormancy cannot be declared on a fused entity view … on.table is a connector.v_* view with spec.dormancy declare it on the ingest table, or drop it apply refused: spec.on.table … must name a table in the 'connector' schema that ingestion owns another schema, or one of the hub's own tables connector.t_<the connector's target> apply refused: alias '…' … collides with state code / exactly one state must be initial / terminal state '…' has an outgoing transition a contradiction in the declaration fix the graph dormancy declared, but no alert ever arrives spec.on.key names a column the table does not have check keyColumnMissing in the apply response a document stuck for weeks does not alert on day one the threshold counts from lumnik's first sighting wait after from the apply date; lm observations list shows SINCE a document is missing from lm observations list its key or its status is NULL or blank fix it at the source; keyNullOrBlank and nullOrBlank count them a status value never shows up in chat answers undeclared check dataTruth.undeclared, add it, re-apply lm ask abstains on a "why can't I close it" question the analytic door does not read the lifecycle lm chat with the scope 403 … scope not granted you do not hold the spec.scope role ask for that scope: role API error 403 (forbidden): no details from the server you lack lm_integrator, or lm_admin for lm observations ask your administrator; no lm command lists your roles (GET /api/bff/v1/me returns them under roles)

docs.title: Advanced: the sweep in detail
docs.text: What the sweep skips, the alert's wording, re-alerts, the tape, and scale

docs.title: What the sweep does not see
docs.text: A document with a NULL or blank key, or a NULL or blank status, is skipped — permanently: there is nothing to follow it by, or no state to watch (SO-000009 on the demo desk). The apply report counts both: keyNullOrBlank and nullOrBlank.

docs.title: The alert, verbatim
docs.text:
From the demo desk, with dormancy.after shortened to 1m:

SO-000004: observed unmoved in "BROUILLON" since 2026-10-18 (first observed 2026-10-18) — declared threshold 1m in acme-order-lifecycle

The default shape — <key>: observed unmoved in "<state>" since <date> (first observed <date>) — declared threshold <after> in <workflow> — never asserts how long the document sat in the source. It is emitted as decision.dormant.<workflow> and appears in the inbox as workflow:<workflow>.

A workflow writes the sentence in its métier's language with spec.dormancy.message:

dormancy:
  after: 14d
  message: "{doc_key} : immobile en « {state_label} » depuis le {since} — seuil {threshold}"

{state_label} is the state's declared label (its code when the state is undeclared); dates are the UTC day. A placeholder outside the seven is refused at apply, naming it.

docs.title: Re-alert semantics
docs.text:
A document alerts once per stall. It alerts again only after it moved (a new state resets its clock) and then sat unmoved past the threshold once more.

A permanently stuck document alerts once; the alert leaves lm inbox with the event retention (lumnik.events.retention-days, 30 by default) What to do ack the alert into your own tracker, or raise lumnik.events.retention-days beyond your review cadence What stays the tape: lm observations list keeps ALERTED until the document moves

docs.title: Reading the tape
docs.text:
lm observations list — the watched documents of every workflow in your scopes, stillest first (--limit, default 200, at most 1000). SINCE is when lumnik started observing that state; ALERTED is empty until the sweep alerts. lm observations stats sums it up per workflow. The TUI's :observations screen shows the same, with humanized ages. Both need lm_admin (or lm_superadmin) on top of lm_integrator.

lm observations transitions reads the journal: every observed move, newest first (--workflow, --doc, --limit). IN_FROM_S is the seconds the document spent in FROM, from ENTERED — its previous move, or its first observation for its first one (a lower bound, like SINCE). Moves are seen at sweep granularity: a document that moved twice between two ticks shows one move.

docs.title: Scale
docs.text:
Each tick reads the latest state of every business key, in the database. On a table with millions of distinct documents, lengthen lumnik.workflow.sweep.every. That read spills to temporary files and counts against PostgreSQL's temp_file_limit; past it, the tick logs dormancy sweep failed ….

The tape and its transition journal are never pruned; only lm workflow rm clears them.

A workflow whose table, status column or key column is gone is skipped, logged once: dormancy sweep standing down for tenant … workflow …; it resumes by itself, with one log line, when the table is readable again. Any other failure (timeout, revoked grant) logs dormancy sweep failed for tenant … workflow … — skipped on every tick. Other workflows are never affected.

docs.title: An undeclared value can never be terminal
docs.text: EN LITIGE is not declared, so it cannot be terminal: true: a document sitting in it is watched like any non-terminal state. The apply report names the value; the sweep names the documents asleep in it.

docs.title: lm — CLI & TUI reference
docs.text:
lm is the integrator's single binary: a kubectl-style CLI plus a k9s-style TUI. This page maps the whole surface; every command also documents itself with lm <cmd> --help.

Every command takes the global flags:

$ lm --help
…
Flags:
      --context string   Override the current context from ~/.lm/config.yaml
  -h, --help             help for lm
  -o, --output string    Output format: table|json|yaml (default "table")
      --server string    Override the server URL
      --token string     Override the auth token (sent as-is; the context's refresh is not run)
  -v, --verbose          Verbose output (debug logs)
  • --token skips the context's stored session and its refresh, so a token from elsewhere works even when the stored one has expired.
  • Five commands use -o for an output file instead: lm source rest from-openapi, lm view get, lm view generate, lm entity export and lm proposal draft.

A command that only groups others (lm connector, lm entity, lm module…) prints its subcommands when typed alone. A word that is not one of them is an error with a non-zero exit:

$ lm connector lst; echo "exit=$?"
Error: unknown command "lst" for "lm connector"
exit=1

docs.title: Context & auth
docs.text:
Command What it does lm config set-context NAME --server URL --oidc-issuer URL create/update a context (--oidc-client-id defaults to lm-cli, the bundled realm client) lm config use-context NAME switch context (the default for every later command; inside lm ui, :context switches the session only) lm config view print ~/.lm/config.yaml with each credential shown as REDACTED — safe to paste into a ticket; --raw prints the tokens in clear lm login OIDC device flow: prints a URL + code, stores tokens in the context lm version binary version

First run? The deploy page walks through standing up a hub and pointing lm at it.

docs.title: Environment & TLS
docs.text:
Setting Where Effect LUMNIK_URL env var replaces the current context's server, per run LUMNIK_TOKEN env var replaces the current context's Bearer token, per run — no lm login needed in CI ca-file: /path/to/root.crt ~/.lm/config.yaml, by hand trust an internal CA (the TLS façade's LAN certificate) insecure-skip-verify: true ~/.lm/config.yaml, by hand disable TLS verification; ca-file wins when both are set tenant: / user: ~/.lm/config.yaml dev-bypass hubs only; a real hub ignores them

The env vars need an existing current context: create it once with lm config set-context ci --server … && lm config use-context ci.

docs.title: Manifests
docs.text:
Command What it does lm validate -f FILE validate a kind: Connector manifest without applying it — field-by-field errors, exit code 1 on error. Other kinds are checked by their own apply lm apply -f FILE apply a kind: Connector manifest — upserts by metadata.name, so re-applying an edited file updates it. Not lm connector apply, which takes the flat stored fields lm entity apply -f FILE apply a kind: Entity fusion manifest lm entity delete NAME remove an entity and its view (lm_admin). Names the view and the search indexes over it, then asks you to type delete (--force skips the question). This is what frees a connector blocked by the 409 below lm entity list the entities you may read — name, sources, scopes, match or resolution lm entity get NAME [--filter COLUMN=VALUE]… [--limit N] [--offset N] one page of an entity's canonical rows (Read API). --filter is an exact match — a date on a date column is equal as an instant — repeatable; --limit is 1..1000 (default 100); a full page is announced on stderr lm entity resolve NAME resolve a resolution: entity over every row now (lm_admin); prints what was resolved, ambiguous and unresolved lm entity ambiguous NAME [--limit N] [--offset N] the rows a resolution: entity could not decide, with their candidates lm entity history NAME SOURCE ID every decision about one source row: outcome, rule, candidates, automatic or asserted lm entity assert-same\|assert-distinct NAME --left SOURCE:ID --right SOURCE:ID [--reason TEXT] a correction that outranks every rule, applied at the next resolve (lm_admin) lm entity export NAME -o FILE [--force] download the entity's canonical CSV through the one-shot door. An existing file is refused without --force; -o - streams to stdout lm app apply -f FILE declare a kind: App métier app — title, scope, icon and theme lm app list / lm app get NAME the declared apps; one app as an applyable manifest (lm app get NAME > app.yaml, edit, re-apply) lm app rm NAME delete a declared app for good (no prompt); the last default app is refused lm view apply -f FILE / lm view list / lm view get NAME / lm view rm NAME saved kind: View manifests: store, list, fetch, delete (no prompt) lm process apply -f FILE / lm process list apply/list kind: Process notify rules lm process enable/disable NAME start or stop a process firing — the manifest stays stored lm process rm NAME delete a process for good (no prompt) lm workflow apply -f FILE apply a kind: Workflow lifecycle — prints the data-truth report lm workflow list / lm workflow get NAME declared lifecycles (name, table, column, scope, enabled); one manifest's YAML on stdout lm workflow enable/disable NAME serve a workflow again, or stop serving it — the manifest stays stored lm workflow rm NAME delete a workflow for good (no prompt) lm export apply -f FILE declare a kind: Export lm search apply -f FILE declare a kind: SearchIndex lm proposal draft DOSSIER write a draft kind: Workflow from a proposal dossier (- for stdin); flags --name --scope --table --column --key --after -o. Offline, never applies; -o FILE refuses an existing file lm describe connector-type KIND field reference for a connector kind 
$ lm validate -f docs/apps/demo/entities/10-customer.yaml
✗ 10-customer.yaml — 4 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    apiVersion
          apiVersion is required
          → Use: apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1

  ERROR    kind
          kind must be "Connector"
…
$ lm workflow disable acme-order-lifecycle
workflow acme-order-lifecycle enabled=false
$ lm app rm clients
Error: API error 400: cannot remove the last default app — apply a different app with default: true first, which demotes this one automatically
$ lm app rm lumilait
app lumilait deleted

docs.title: Connectors, endpoints, sources
docs.text:
Command What it does lm connector list / get NAME the connector instances; one connector's flat stored fields lm connector apply -f FILE create or edit a connector from its flat stored fields (name, typeId, schedule, enabled, config) — the shape lm connector get prints. Creates csv-file and hello-world only — see Creating from flat fields. A kind: Connector manifest is refused here, naming lm apply -f lm connector delete NAME erases the connector's data: its tables, run history and RAG chunks — the erasure gesture. States what goes and asks you to type delete; --dry-run stops there, --force skips the question; with no keyboard (a script) and no --force, nothing is deleted: aborted: no confirmation read. A table an entity reads blocks it with a 409 lm connector run NAME trigger an immediate run lm connector pause/resume NAME stop/restart scheduling; lm connector list shows a paused connector's cron followed by (paused), and lm connector run still runs it lm connector scope ls/set/add/rm/sync manage the connector's métier scopes; sync re-stamps its already-indexed chunks lm endpoint enable/disable/reset-cursor C/E per-endpoint scheduler and cursor lm endpoint purge C/E delete one endpoint's rows after stating how many and asking you to type purge (--dry-run only counts, --force skips the question). For rest-generic endpoints and one-shot lm csv ingest tables; refused for jdbc-generic, csv-file and kafka — see Emptying one endpoint lm source rest test C pre-flight every enabled endpoint — the request a run would send, nothing written; non-zero exit if one fails lm source rest probe C --endpoint PATH sample one path with the connector's connection and credential; drafts the endpoint fragment to paste under spec.endpoints lm source rest from-openapi URL --name N generate a manifest (--scope repeatable, -o FILE, --apply upserts it). lm source rest run is a stub — use lm connector run lm source jdbc test/discover/add open a JDBC source directly; the password is prompted without echo, or piped with --password-stdin. There is no --password lm source jdbc list-tables NAME the tables registered under a source the hub already holds lm source schema --scope TAG / lm source rediscover --scope TAG show / rebuild the scope's schema card (--scope is required) lm csv ingest FILE\|sftp://…\|s3://… one-shot CSV ingest into an ext.* table, no run recorded — flags on CSV & files lm source csv ingest … the same command, same flags 
$ lm connector delete orders --dry-run
Would delete connector orders (csv-file) — 8 rows of connector.t_orders, its run history and RAG chunks (dry run, nothing deleted)
$ lm connector delete acme-desk-erp --dry-run
Error: API error 409: table connector.t_acme_desk_erp feeds entity acmecustomer — remove the entity first (lm entity delete acmecustomer)

A one-shot ingest, on a hub with the AI on:

$ lm csv ingest stock.csv --scope retail --name stock-count
Ingested stock.csv into ext.stock_count
  • rows written:    3
  • promoted cols:   4
      - sku (text)
      - label (text)
      - qty (bigint)
      - warehouse (text)

  • askable:         scope 'retail' — try: lm ask --scope retail "how many rows are in ext.stock_count?"
A dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.

With the AI switched off, the last two lines read:

A one-shot: no run recorded, nothing indexed for chat.
The rows are in ext.stock_count, and a dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.

docs.title: Creating from flat fields
docs.text:
lm connector apply -f without an id creates the connector. A csv-file connector made this way gets the same endpoint lm apply -f would give it, so it runs at once:

$ cat clients.yaml
name: erp-clients
typeId: csv-file
enabled: true
config:
  kind: csv-file
  after_process: none
  parser: {has_header: true}
  transport: {kind: local, path: /tmp/imports/clients.csv}
tags: [sales]
$ lm connector apply -f clients.yaml
applied
$ lm connector run erp-clients
run scheduled: ba6041df-be91-4878-90ec-aba18d36aa60
$ lm run list --connector erp-clients
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ba6041df  erp-clients  default   Completed  3   3    0        0             2026-10-18 17:49  2026-10-18 17:49

A name is unique in your tenant. Applying a file without an id under a taken name is refused with the holder's id; add it to the file and the same command updates that connector:

$ lm connector apply -f clients.yaml
Error: API error 409: connector "erp-clients" already exists (id e9fc0700-07e5-4869-b4d5-4eab9122bf96) — to update it, add that id to the file you apply
$ head -2 clients.yaml
id: e9fc0700-07e5-4869-b4d5-4eab9122bf96
name: erp-clients
$ lm connector apply -f clients.yaml
applied
  • A rename onto a taken name is refused the same way.
  • A name held in a métier you do not hold answers 403 scope not granted.
  • Two applies of one new name at once (two CI jobs): one creates, the other gets the 409.

jdbc-generic, rest-generic and kafka connectors are created from their kind: Connector manifest with lm apply -f; once created, any of them is edited here except its typeId. A tenantId other than yours is refused:

$ lm connector apply -f orders-db.yaml
Error: API error 400: a jdbc-generic connector is created from its kind: Connector manifest with lm apply -f — this door creates csv-file and hello-world connectors, and updates any
$ lm connector apply -f other-tenant.yaml
Error: API error 400: tenantId (2) does not match the authenticated tenant (1) — omit it, the connector is written in yours

docs.title: Data, runs & answers
docs.text:
Command What it does lm run list / lm run get ID connector runs, one row per endpoint (records in/out/skipped); list is newest first, --connector NAME, --limit N. An EVALUATED column appears once the tenant has an enabled Process: whether it has evaluated the rows the run wrote. get --wait-evaluated [--timeout D] [--interval D] waits for it, and exits 1 when the hub cannot say (no enabled Process, processes changed since the run started, or a run from before the hub recorded it) lm run cancel ID request cancellation of a Running run — cooperative, not immediate; see Stopping a run for the refusals lm dlq list / lm dlq get ID dead-letter entries (reason + offending row); --run RUN, --connector NAME, list --limit N lm dlq replayed/discard ID mark an entry handled (replayed --new-run-id RUN, required: the Completed run of the same connector, started after the entry, that carried the row again — none, discard; an entry is closed once) lm conflicts list fused-entity rows with a source conflict or a lookup ambiguity (--limit N) lm observations list the workflow tape: watched documents, stillest first (--limit N); --workflow NAME narrows the hub's read to one workflow lm observations transitions the journal: each observed move, newest first, with the seconds spent in the state it left (IN_FROM_S, counted from the first observation for a document's first move); --workflow NAME, --doc KEY, --limit N lm observations stats the tape per workflow: watched, dormant, median detection delay (seconds; - when nothing is dormant) lm integration add NAME --url U --events T [--secret-stdin] register a webhook target — the secret arrives on stdin, never as a flag lm integration list / describe ID registered targets; the table shows scheme and host only, -o json\|yaml the full URL lm integration test ID [--event T] fire a catalog event at the target and report the delivery; decision.* events cannot be fired here lm integration rm ID remove a target — delivery history is kept lm notify add --events T --to EMAIL [--template N] / list / rm ID email rules (needs the deploy's SMTP settings — see the self-host guide) lm outputs list what was sent out and whether it arrived, failures first (--limit N) lm outputs replay ID re-send one failed delivery as a new attempt lm data tables / lm data row HASH dynamic tables with your row count (unknown when it could not be counted); the raw row behind a citation, a timestamp as its UTC instant lm secret set/list/describe/rm encrypted secrets; values never returned. set NAME prompts without echo, set NAME - reads stdin, set NAME VALUE warns (shell history). --description, rm --force. rm does not check references: a connector naming the secret fails at its next run

The two tables you will read most:

$ lm run list --connector orders
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
884f487d  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
$ lm dlq list --run 884f487d
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
b6bc9601  orders     884f487d  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/orders.csv:9 — Index for header 'status' is 2 b…
b4176d39  orders     884f487d  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/orders.csv:8 — Record has 6 values but only 5 c…

The ID columns are abbreviated — and the abbreviation works

lm run list and lm dlq list show the first 8 characters of each id. get, discard, replayed and --run accept those 8 characters; an ambiguous prefix is refused. -o yaml prints every id in full.

A full page says so

lm run list, lm dlq list, lm conflicts list, lm observations list, lm outputs list and lm inbox answer in pages. Each takes --limit N, up to 200 (runs, dead letters, inbox), 500 (deliveries) or 1000 (conflicts, workflow tape).

A full page prints note: result hit the limit of N — there may be more on stderr, so pipes and -o json stay clean. Raise --limit to see further back. --connector filters on the hub, so a quiet connector's old runs are still found.

docs.title: Ask your data
docs.text: Command What it does lm ask [--scope S] [--lang XX] "question" analytic text-to-SQL over the fused hub: the answer, a data as of line, any disputed rows, the rows the query returned and the SQL that ran (the guards). --lang sets the answer language (default: from LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES or LANG). Without --scope, asks your default scope. -o json\|yaml for a script lm chat interactive REPL chat — in-REPL commands: :corpus NAME (or all), :scope TAG (or default), :topK N (1 to 50), :clear, :help, :exit lm scopes / lm scope / lm scope set TAG list scopes (a scope-bound user sees only granted ones); show/set your default (404 no user record on this hub…: see Tenants, users & scopes) lm rag search/status/reindex semantic search (--top-k N, 1 to 50, default 5); corpus status; re-index of the platform corpus (manifests, API, hooks)

docs.title: The rows under the answer
docs.text:
lm ask prints the rows its query returned under the answer, then how many there are, then the SQL. When the hub withholds a phrased answer, these rows are the answer. Played on the demo desk:

$ lm ask --scope desk "Quels clients GOLD sont à Lyon ? Donne leur code et leur nom."
Il y a 2 clients GOLD à Lyon :

- Code : P-1000, Nom : Hydraulique Lyon 1000
- Code : P-1008, Nom : Filtration Lyon 1008

Total de clients : 2
  data as of: 2026-10-16T08:50:37.235585Z (last completed run)

  disputed — a source disagrees on a value this answer filtered on:
    P-1008  city = 'Lyon'  counted  t_acme_desk_erp: Lyon · t_acme_desk_crm: Villeurbanne

  CODE    NAME
  P-1000  Hydraulique Lyon 1000
  P-1008  Filtration Lyon 1008
  2 rows returned

  SQL: SELECT v.code, v.name
FROM connector."v_acmecustomer" v
WHERE v.segment = 'GOLD' AND v.city = 'Lyon'
LIMIT 500

  try: lm conflicts list  — where this scope has source conflicts or lookup ambiguities, row by row
  • The query stops at 500 rows; every row returned is printed. A line break inside a value shows as \n.
  • no rows returned when the query found nothing; no table when the answer ran no query.

For a script, ask for JSON (or -o yaml): one document, nothing else on stdout.

$ lm ask -o json --scope desk "Quels clients GOLD sont à Lyon ? Donne leur code et leur nom." | jq -r '.rows[] | .code + "  " + .name'
P-1000  Hydraulique Lyon 1000
P-1008  Filtration Lyon 1008

The document holds answer, sql, rowCount, columns, rows (numbers stay numbers), dataAsOf, disputed and abstained. Tell a refusal by "abstained": true, never by the wording of answer.

docs.title: The apps ladder
docs.text: Command What it does lm view -f FILE [--filter …] render a kind: View list — filters col=v · col~text · col>v (>= < <=, number/ISO date), repeatable (AND). The value is a bare literal: --filter 'city=Lyon'; city='Lyon' is refused lm view KEY -f FILE one record's detail (with the _conflicts ledger) lm view NAME [KEY] [--filter …] the same for a saved view of lm view list. A view named like a subcommand (list, get, apply, generate, rm) runs the subcommand instead lm view generate SCOPE "DESCRIPTION" [-o FILE] ask the AI to write a kind: View manifest over a scope; review it, then render with lm view -f lm view list [--scope S] the saved views you may read lm view get NAME [-o FILE] one saved view's manifest YAML — to stdout, or to a file lm view apply -f FILE / lm view rm NAME store a kind: View manifest; delete one (no prompt) lm app apply -f FILE / list / get NAME / rm NAME métier apps — see Manifests lm workflow … lifecycles — see Manifests lm export apply -f FILE declare a kind: Export; inline credentials are refused, naming the field lm export list / lm export get NAME the exports your scopes can see; one export's manifest YAML (user:password@ printed as ***@) lm export run NAME [--wait] start a managed run. Without --wait it returns once the run is accepted; --wait follows it to Completed (prints the receipt) or Failed (exit 1). --timeout (default 30m) and an interrupt stop the waiting, never the run lm export retry NAME RUN_ID [--wait] a new attempt of a Failed run, regenerated from byte 0 lm export runs NAME [--limit N] / lm export status NAME [RUN_ID] the export's run ledger, newest first; one run in full (latest by default) lm inbox [--limit N] [--all] [--process NAME] [--type TYPE] recent decision.* events — what needs you; --process/--type narrow the hub's read lm inbox ack ID dispose of a decision (idempotent)

docs.title: Admin & platform
docs.text:
Command What it does lm module list installed business modules, with ACTIVE/INACTIVE and the reason lm migration status migration status per schema: version, pending count, last applied (— when none). No apply: the hub migrates at every startup lm hook list / lm hook get NAME the Kotlin platform hooks loaded at startup lm hook apply/delete/reload not implemented: hooks come from deployment manifests lm hook generate not implemented lm search apply -f FILE declare a kind: SearchIndex — validate, then create or update; -f - reads stdin (integrator) lm search rm NAME delete a declared index and queue the purge of its documents (Deleting); asks you to type delete (--force skips the question; in a script without it: aborted: no confirmation read) lm search query "TEXT" [--entity E] [--facet field=value]… [--limit N] [--cursor C] keyword search over the declared indexes, no model — the full guide lm search status [INDEX] every index (name, status, lag, documents, last rebuild), or one index's detail lm search rebuild INDEX [--wait] full rebuild; without --wait it prints the run id once claimed, --wait follows it to ready/failed/cancelled (--timeout, default 30m) lm search cancel INDEX request cancellation of an index's active rebuild; refused once it has reached publish 
$ lm migration status
SCHEMA    VERSION  PENDING  LAST APPLIED
core      75       0        2026-10-19 01:36
identity  18       0        2026-10-19 01:36
rag       6        0        2026-10-19 01:36
$ lm hook apply
Error: `lm hook apply` is not implemented: hooks are loaded from deployment manifests at startup

docs.title: The TUI
docs.text:
Bare lm (or lm ui) launches the k9s-style TUI. : opens the command palette.

Full tour by task, plus the complete key reference, on The TUI.

docs.title: The TUI
docs.text:
Bare lm (or lm ui) opens the k9s-style console — the installer's daily screen. : is the command palette (type a page name, Tab/Enter to commit); ? opens the in-app help; q quits.

This page tours the TUI by task: watch an ingestion, decide on a pending item, ask your data, create something new. The key reference at the bottom lists every gesture.

docs.title: Getting around
docs.text:
: opens the palette — type the start of a page name (:so offers :sources), then Tab or Enter.

Group Pages Your data :sources (alias :connectors) :endpoints :runs :dlq :tables :entities :conflicts :ambiguous Decide :inbox :outputs :observations Explore & ask :ask :view :scopes :search Create & declare :new :processes :views :apps :workflows :exports Admin :modules :hooks :migrations :rag :secrets :integrations :notify

Global keys, from any page:

Key Effect : open the command palette r refresh the current page d toggle the describe panel (full detail on the selected row) Tab with the describe panel open: give it the keys, so ↑ ↓ PgUp PgDn scroll a long record; Tab or Esc gives them back to the list / on list pages: filter the table to the rows holding a text (Esc clears) — the key reference lists the pages y yank the current row — copies it to your local clipboard, even over SSH q quit ? help screen (the same table, always at hand) Esc close a modal, cancel an input, or back out one level
  • :sources, :endpoints, :runs, :dlq and :inbox live-update; the cursor stays on your row.
  • The header names the hub (context and host) and the event stream: [CONNECTING], [LIVE✓], or [RECONNECTING] with the reason in the footer.
  • A key that acts on the hub (run, toggle, delete, apply) is ignored while its first press still waits on the hub; the footer says it is in progress.

Another hub. :context (or :ctx) lists the contexts of ~/.lm/config.yaml, the current one marked ●. Enter switches for this session only: every page is rebuilt on the chosen hub, and lm config use-context still sets the default for the next command. The session scope starts over on the new hub, and the --server/--token flags lm ui was started with stay behind.

Session expired. If your login expires mid-session, a session-expired modal opens. L logs in again with the same device flow as lm login and the TUI resumes; Esc dismisses it until the next request needs the session.

docs.title: Watch an ingestion
docs.text:
:sources is the home page — one row per connector instance.

Column / key Where What it tells you SCHED :sources the connector's schedule ENABLED :sources whether the connector is on at all Enter :sources REST or JDBC source → its :endpoints (one per spec entry / per table); any other kind → its :runs SCHEDULE, LAST_RUN, STATUS :endpoints per endpoint — for a REST source, where to check "did it even fire?" Enter :endpoints that endpoint's own :runs (Esc clears it) T / P :endpoints test the endpoint — the request a run would send, nothing written · probe a path of the API and draft its endpoint fragment ^P / C / Del :endpoints enable/disable the endpoint · reset its cursor — the next run re-reads from the start (asks first) · purge the rows it landed D :sources, :runs the connector's / the run's dead letters in :dlq — Esc there clears the filter at: (under ── last run ──) d describe panel the exact last-run time

Del on an endpoint asks the hub first. A jdbc-generic, csv-file or kafka endpoint shows the hub's refusal; an endpoint with no rows says there is nothing to purge; otherwise the question names the count.

In :sources:

  • Del asks the hub what the delete would take. A table an entity reads shows the refusal naming the entity; otherwise the confirmation names each table and its rows: Delete connector "cust-csv"? Goes with it: 3 rows of connector.t_cust_csv, its run history and RAG chunks.
  • t edits the connector's tags, then offers to re-stamp its indexed RAG chunks (lm connector scope sync). Re-stamp says how many chunks changed; Cancel leaves the old scopes on them.

Reading a run. :runs shows CONNECTOR, ENDPOINT, STATUS, STARTED, DURATION, RECORDS (in/out/skip) and TRIGGER — one row per endpoint. d adds the run id, the chunk count and, for a failed or cancelled run, an error: section with the full message.

Stopping a run. Select a Running row and press c. The chunk in flight finishes and the run ends at the next chunk boundary. On a Queued row, c ends the run at once (it had not started).

Refusal toasted Meaning run … already ended (STATUS) nothing left to stop run … is being started; try again in a moment a Queued run is starting — retry run … is not in flight on this hub the run started a moment ago — retry; refused again, no process runs it, and the hub marks it Failed on its own

STATUS takes six values. Check them in this order when a run's outcome isn't obvious:

What you see What happened Where the detail lives STATUS = Queued Accepted, waiting for a free slot — only with the run queue on :runs; it starts on its own STATUS = Running Still going :runs live-updates; d shows progress so far STATUS = Failed The run itself failed: source unreachable, bad credentials, a refused config The error: section in d STATUS = Completed, a row is in :dlq A quality failure on that one row (e.g. validate-row) :dlq — reason and payload STATUS = Completed, row counted in skip but not in :dlq Excluded by a declared filter (filter-where, skip-empty-rows), not rejected The skip figure in RECORDS STATUS = Partial Read less than the source held when it started; nothing written twice, the next run resumes from the kept position The error: section in d names the target and what was not reached STATUS = Cancelled Cancelled by a user, or skipped because another run for the endpoint was already active d: cancelled by user or skipped: another run is already active for this endpoint No entry in :runs at all The schedule hasn't fired yet :sources / :endpoints

Every dead letter is also counted in skip, so in/out/skip alone tells you whether a run dropped anything.

Once you have the cause, fix it (e edits the connector's YAML) and press R to run again. The full walk is Diagnosing a failed run.

:dlq is the dead-letter queue: each row a connector could not place, with its reason and payload. ^R marks one replayed, ^D discards it.

docs.title: Decide
docs.text:
Four pages answer "what needs me":

  • :inbox — your métiers' decision.* events, raised by processes and workflows (never run failures: those are in :runs). a acks the selected one (idempotent); A shows or hides disposed entries.
  • :outputs — what was sent out and whether it arrived, failures first. ^R replays a failed delivery.
  • :observations — the workflow tape: documents that have NOT moved, stillest first. The title shows, per workflow, the documents watched, the dormant ones and the median detection time.
  • :conflicts — the fused rows with a source conflict or a lookup ambiguity. Read-only: d shows which source said what; the fix is a source or manifest change.

docs.title: Explore & ask
docs.text:
:ask is analytic chat: a plain-language question comes back as generated SQL, rows and an answer. It asks the session scope shown in the header — your default (lm scope) at startup, changed with :scopes → Enter or :scope <tag>.

Key Effect Enter run the question y yank the generated SQL e export the result rows to a CSV file n new question

:view opens a kind: View manifest file and renders it — Enter on an empty path opens the living example.

Key Effect Enter (on a rendered row) record detail, with the _conflicts ledger f add a server-side filter (a bad one is refused with the reason) F clear all filters g generate a view from a sentence over the active scope (AI) — set the scope first with :scopes or :scope <tag> a apply the rendered view into the hub's saved-view store o open another file r refresh

docs.title: Create
docs.text:
:new is the authoring loop. Pick a kind; every kind you can apply is offered — the connector types, Entity, Process, Workflow, App, View, Export and SearchIndex — each with a real example from these docs.

Key Effect Enter open the kind's example in $EDITOR; on save it validates and applies, then jumps to where you observe it v edit, then validate without applying; a then applies the buffer you checked e after refusals (shown field by field): re-open the same buffer Esc abandon — your edits are kept in a temp file w guided setup: jdbc-generic (name, JDBC URL, user, password typed masked, schema → test → pick tables → one connector per table) · csv-file (ingest a local file once, then opens :tables) d the kind's example and, for a connector kind, its type's configuration schema (lm describe connector-type)
  • v checks a connector through the hub's validator; any other kind by its YAML and kind only.
  • graphql and soap show rest-generic's schema: they are request shapes of that type.
  • In the JDBC picker, a table of an unsupported shape is listed but cannot be ticked.

:processes lists declared kind: Process rules: e re-opens one in the same edit → validate → apply loop, ^P enables or disables it (the manifest stays), Del deletes it after a confirmation.

docs.title: Admin corner
docs.text:
Page What it lists Keys :modules installed business modules — :hooks installed Kotlin hooks (read-only: they load from deployment manifests at startup) d the binding: handler, events, priority (lm hook get) :migrations migration status per schema;
