docs.title: Connectors
docs.text: Connectors ingest your legacy sources — files, databases, APIs, event topics — into hub tables, read-only and declaratively: one YAML manifest, three commands — validate, apply, run.

docs.title: Which connector for which source?
docs.text:
Your source Connector Page CSV exports — dropped locally, on SFTP, or in S3 csv-file CSV & files A live database — PostgreSQL; Oracle (Pro) jdbc-generic JDBC An HTTP/JSON API (Stripe, HubSpot, …) rest-generic REST A GraphQL API rest-generic, GraphQL shape GraphQL A SOAP middleware (Siebel, SAP PI, …) rest-generic, SOAP shape SOAP An event broker (Kafka, Redpanda, Event Hubs) kafka — Pro Kafka

There are five connector types: csv-file, jdbc-generic, rest-generic, kafka and hello-world (a smoke-test connector with no page of its own). GraphQL and SOAP are not types: they are request shapes of a rest-generic endpoint, with the same auth, retry and rate limits.

docs.title: The pipeline
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  src["legacy source"] --> t["transport / engine"] --> p["parser"]
  p --> m["mapping & transforms"] --> tbl["hub table"] --> rag["RAG chunks"]

Every connector reads the source, parses it, optionally transforms it (Transformers), writes a tenant-isolated hub table, and indexes it for scoped chat.

docs.title: The lifecycle — every connector, same three commands
docs.text:
Assumes a deployed hub and an authenticated lm — see Quickstart.

  1. Write a manifest (kind: Connector) — every connector uses the same envelope:

    apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: <kebab-case-name>
  connector_type: <csv-file|jdbc-generic|rest-generic|kafka>
  scopes: [<métier>]          # the scope(s) this connector's tables are askable in
spec:
  # type-specific — see your connector's page
  ...

  2. lm validate -f manifest.yaml — check it without touching anything.

  3. lm apply -f manifest.yaml — register or update the connector (safe to re-run).

  4. lm connector run <name> — run it now. Or schedule it:

    • spec.schedule: "0 6 * * *" — cron, evaluated in UTC (here: daily at 06:00 UTC).
    • spec.window: "22:00-07:00" — scheduled runs start only inside this UTC window; the end is exclusive, so 07:00 keeps the 06:00 slot inside.

    What the three commands print, on a small orders export:

    $ lm validate -f orders.yaml
✓ orders.yaml — valid
$ lm apply -f orders.yaml
{"name":"orders","connectorId":"36bb1629-6b7f-418a-9bd8-c903148ab86d","endpointsApplied":1}
$ lm connector run orders
run scheduled: 6806802f-ed3c-46d6-8eeb-a0f7cff94e77

    "Scheduled" is not "done" — the result lands in the run ledger a few seconds later:

    $ lm run list --connector orders
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
6806802f  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
$ lm dlq list --run 6806802f-ed3c-46d6-8eeb-a0f7cff94e77
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
7c863b7a  orders     6806802f  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/sales-orders.csv:10 — Record has 5 values but o…
004c3b56  orders     6806802f  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/sales-orders.csv:7 — Record has 4 values but on…

    Ten rows read, eight written, two set aside in the dead-letter queue with their reason.

    lm connector run prints one run id. A connector with several endpoints starts one run per endpoint: lm run list --connector <name> shows them all. 5. Watch it in the TUI (CLI & TUI): :sources (connectors), :runs (history), :dlq (rejected rows).

docs.title: Scheduled runs take turns
docs.text:
• A scheduled connector runs each endpoint as its own run; a hub instance drives at most 4 at once (LUMNIK_CONNECTOR_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCHEDULED_RUNS, property lumnik.connector.max-concurrent-scheduled-runs). An endpoint still waiting has no run in lm run list yet.
  • Each run uses up to two connections of the hub's admin pool: raise quarkus.datasource."admin".jdbc.max-size along with the bound.
  • With the run queue off (the default), lm connector run does not count against the bound and never waits — a manual run of a connector with many endpoints can fill the admin pool on its own (turn on the run queue below).
  • A waiting scheduled endpoint does not start if the connector was paused or deleted, its window closed, or the endpoint already ran (a manual run).

docs.title: Manual runs can queue
docs.text:
With LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_ENABLED=true (off by default; read Turning on the run queue first), lm connector run queues one run per enabled endpoint in status Queued (no start time yet). The hub starts each as a slot frees, on the same budget as scheduled runs. lm run cancel ends a queued run.

Situation What lm run list shows A second run requested for an endpoint that already has one queued or running a new run, Cancelled: "another run is already active" Not started within LUMNIK_RUN_QUEUE_MAX_AGE (default 1h) Cancelled: "expired in the queue" Endpoint disabled or deleted, connector paused or deleted, or manifest re-applied while it waited Cancelled, with that reason A run left Running by a hub that died (until the reaper fails it, within a minute) a new request is answered with a run already Cancelled lm run cancel on a run the hub is just starting refused: "is being started; try again in a moment"

On-demand exports queue the same way (Exports).

docs.title: Freshness follows the schedule
docs.text: A change in the source appears at the next run that reads it. Deletes never propagate, and watermark mode re-reads only rows whose watermark advanced.

docs.title: Validate before apply
docs.text: Command Purpose lm validate -f manifest.yaml Validate without applying. Exit 0 if valid (warnings allowed), 1 if errors. lm apply -f manifest.yaml Apply. The server runs the same checks: on errors nothing is written and you get the same report. Warnings do not block the apply. lm describe connector-type <kind> Show the schema (fields, types, required/optional, docs) of a connector type.

docs.title: Valid
docs.text:
$ lm validate -f stripe.yaml
✓ stripe.yaml — valid

docs.title: Errors only
docs.text:
$ lm validate -f bad.yaml
✗ bad.yaml — 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.auth.token_env
          bearer auth requires token_env (or inline token_value)
          → Use `lm secret set <NAME> ...` then reference via token_env: <NAME>

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].id
          must match kebab-case identifier

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f bad.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 2 error(s)

docs.title: Warnings only (still valid, exit 0)
docs.text:
$ lm validate -f noscopes.yaml
! noscopes.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     metadata.scopes
          no scopes declared — the connector's tables will not be askable in any métier
          → Add: scopes: [compta]  (the métier a user must hold as scope:compta)

lm apply writes the JSON body (with its warnings) to stdout, then the same report to stderr:

$ lm apply -f noscopes.yaml
{"name":"noscopes","connectorId":"dd1cf69e-6742-41b7-9ebb-2543521ed521","endpointsApplied":1,"warnings":[{"path":"metadata.scopes","severity":"WARNING","message":"no scopes declared — the connector's tables will not be askable in any métier","recommendations":["Add: scopes: [compta]  (the métier a user must hold as scope:compta)"]}]}
! noscopes.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     metadata.scopes
          no scopes declared — the connector's tables will not be askable in any métier
          → Add: scopes: [compta]  (the métier a user must hold as scope:compta)

The exit code is 0: a warning never fails lm validate or lm apply.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Exit Meaning 0 No errors (warnings allowed) 1 Validation errors, and every other failure (file not found, unparsable YAML, hub unreachable)

docs.title: CSV & files (SFTP/S3)
docs.text:
Ingest CSV files — dropped locally, on an SFTP server, or in an S3 bucket — into a hub table on a schedule, with per-row error isolation.

Type csv-file Transports local, sftp, s3 Target connector.t_<name> Schedulable cron Edition Open

docs.title: Quickstart — one local file, three commands and a look at the ledger
docs.text:
# 10-local-simple.yaml — the simplest CSV ingest: one local file, full load.
#
# Apply and run:
#   lm apply -f docs/connectors/csv/10-local-simple.yaml
#   lm connector run csv-local-simple
#
# A file that has not changed since its last run is skipped; one that has changed
# (replaced in place, or grown) is read again in full, and the table then holds
# exactly what the file holds: rows the file no longer has are removed — a run that
# would shrink the table by more than 30% fails instead, unless refresh.max_removed
# says otherwise (docs/connectors/csv.md, full refresh). Suitable for reference
# files fully replaced on each load cycle. after_process: none means the source is
# never moved or deleted.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: csv-local-simple          # unique connector name within the workspace
  connector_type: csv-file        # selects the CSV-file connector implementation
  scopes: [demo]                  # the métier(s) this table is askable in — a scope-bound user needs scope:demo

spec:
  transport:
    kind: local                   # no remote fetch — the path below is on the HUB's filesystem,
                                  # not on yours (mount a volume, or use sftp/s3 / lm csv ingest)
    path: docs/connectors/csv/data/customers.csv   # plain path = single file

  parser:
    has_header: true              # first row holds column names; they drive target column mapping

  after_process: none             # leave the source file untouched after ingestion

The manifest's path: is read by the hub. On the self-host stack, copy the sample file into the container first (docker cp docs/connectors/csv/data/customers.csv lumnik-hub-1:/tmp/exports/) and point path: there; a hub in dev mode reads the repo-relative path as is. From the repository root:

$ lm validate -f docs/connectors/csv/10-local-simple.yaml
✓ 10-local-simple.yaml — valid
$ lm apply -f docs/connectors/csv/10-local-simple.yaml
{"name":"csv-local-simple","connectorId":"f59d18ef-d308-4015-8e84-7fd8cb3a8250","endpointsApplied":1}
$ lm connector run csv-local-simple
run scheduled: 2e37cb12-0a66-4c4c-a4c2-b796b2d40540

"Scheduled" is not "done" — the result lands in the run ledger a second later:

$ lm run get 2e37cb12
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2e37cb12  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39

STARTED / ENDED are in your terminal's time zone (these screens: Paris, UTC+2); schedule is evaluated in UTC.

What landed in connector.t_csv_local_simple — the header row became the columns:

lumnik=> select row_id, email, signup_date from connector.t_csv_local_simple;
 row_id |    email    | signup_date
--------+-------------+-------------
 1      | alice@x.com | 02/06/2026
 2      | bob@x.com   | 15/01/2026
(2 rows)

Run it again on the unchanged file, then once more after a third line is appended:

$ lm run list --connector csv-local-simple
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2565ea5a  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  3   3    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
52d1ac0b  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
2e37cb12  csv-local-simple  default   Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
  • A file already read is not read again — the second run says IN 0, and lm run get adds • 1 file(s) unchanged since they were last read — not read again. A file that changed (replaced in place, or grown) is read again in full: the third run says IN 3, even when the copy kept the file's size and date.
  • The table deduplicates: after three runs it holds 3 rows, not 5.
  • SKIPPED and DEAD-LETTERS are explained below.

docs.title: The three transports
docs.text:
The manifest's transport: block picks one:

local sftp s3 files are on the hub's filesystem a remote server a bucket selected by path or glob path or glob prefix + suffix a new run reads files whose name sorts after the last one read files modified since the last run files modified since the last run after_process none only all four all four credentials — key_env or password_env access_key_env / secret_key_env

docs.title: Local — the hub's disk, not yours
docs.text:
transport:
  kind: local
  path: /imports/*.csv        # glob OK
  • The path is on the hub's filesystem. The self-host stack mounts nothing: mount a volume, use sftp/s3, or upload one file with lm csv ingest.
  • Glob: * and ? only, in the final filename segment — /imports/*/x.csv never matches, and there is no **.
  • No name is excluded implicitly — use *.csv to keep .tmp files out.
  • A path that matches nothing is not an error: the run completes with IN 0.
  • A path without * or ? names one file, and that file is the whole table — see full refresh.

A drop folder, run by run. A 1 200-row export 2026-09-01-orders.csv, then two more files:

$ lm run list --connector orders-drop
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b159e727  orders-drop  default   Completed  0     0     0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
393a2729  orders-drop  default   Completed  10    10    0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
165a4c6d  orders-drop  default   Completed  0     0     0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
ff5b8f80  orders-drop  default   Completed  1200  1200  0        0             2026-10-19 01:39  2026-10-19 01:39
run the folder holds IN why 1 2026-09-01 (1 200 rows) 1 200 first read 2 the same file 0 already read in full 3 plus 2026-09-02 (10 rows) 10 only the new file — it sorts after the last file read 4 plus 2026-08-31 (5 rows) 0 it sorts before the last file read — never read

Drop-folder contract: names must grow lexically

A run resumes after the last file it read, in name order. Name incoming files monotonically (date-prefixed: 2026-07-25-orders.csv), or use sftp/s3, which track modification time instead.

situation what happens what to do a file arrives with a name sorting before the last file read never read name files monotonically a file arrives while a run is going waits for the next run; read only if its name sorts after where that run ended have the producer write under a name the glob does not match, then rename it in a listed file is removed before the run reaches it the run fails, naming the file run again a file is archived before its run is Completed (or after a run that failed midway) if later files are waiting, the next run fails, naming that file lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint>: the next run reads from the first file, the table deduplicates

Files read by a Completed run may be archived safely.

docs.title: SFTP — a remote folder, a secret, a fingerprint
docs.text:
transport:
  kind: sftp
  host: sftp.example.com
  port: 22                    # optional, default 22
  user: lumnik
  path: /erp-export/*.csv     # glob OK
  password_env: SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD           # OR key_env (the PEM private key) — one is required
  host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc"  # required unless strict_host_key: false
  # strict_host_key: true     # the default — refuses unless the fingerprint above matches
# spec level, next to transport:
after_process: archive
archive_path: /archive/       # default /archive/; required when after_process: move

Credentials are never inline. key_env / password_env name a secret stored with lm secret; an OS env var of that name is the fallback:

$ lm secret set SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD
Value for SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD:
Created secret "SFTP_ERP_PASSWORD"

A manifest with neither credential is refused:

$ lm validate -f sftp-nocred.yaml
✗ sftp-nocred.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.transport
          SFTP transport requires key_env or password_env
          → Use `lm secret set <NAME> ...` then reference via key_env: <NAME>

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f sftp-nocred.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

One session per run. Your server sees one connection per running endpoint, for the whole run:

  • its idle timeout and its limit on concurrent sessions apply to that connection;
  • a session lost between two chunks is reopened, and a silent one is detected within 15 seconds;
  • a session lost in the middle of a chunk fails the run with the connection error.

The host key is verified. With strict_host_key: true (the default), host_key_fingerprint must match what the server presents. Here a wrong fingerprint is declared:

$ lm run get b31b1efe
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
b31b1efe  sftp-badkey  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-09-06 22:13  2026-09-06 22:13
✖ run failed: SFTP host key refused for sftp.example.com:22 — the server presented SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc, and it does not match the declared SHA256:0000000000000000000000000000000000000000000. Confirm that fingerprint out of band (ssh-keyscan -p 22 sftp.example.com | ssh-keygen -lf -), then set host_key_fingerprint: "SHA256:M0Is0aG8ubOr0cLpQs6QcDwVSxMkvmlfuW4K9Q6CJuc" in the transport block. Setting strict_host_key: false connects without checking at all — which accepts an impostor as readily as the real server.
  • Confirm the presented fingerprint out of band (the ssh-keyscan | ssh-keygen -lf - line, from a machine you trust), then paste it.
  • strict_host_key: false skips the check: an impostor would receive the password and feed rows. Use it only for a throwaway container whose key changes at every restart — as the demo manifest 30-sftp-key.yaml does.

A wrong password, or a user who cannot read the folder:

$ lm run get 22957eeb
ID        CONNECTOR                    ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
22957eeb  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-09-04 14:23  2026-09-04 14:23
✖ run failed: SFTP error (SSH_FX_PERMISSION_DENIED): Permission denied

A file is read once while it is unchanged; one rewritten later (newer modification time) is read again, even under the same name and at the same size. Oldest first; a run that finds nothing new reads nothing. Zero-byte files are never listed — never ingested, never archived:

$ lm run list --connector sftp-c-bpartner-credentials
ID        CONNECTOR                    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN     OUT    SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a9533cb5  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Completed  0      0      0        0             2026-09-06 22:09  2026-09-06 22:09
80032250  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Completed  6      5      1        1             2026-09-04 15:27  2026-09-04 15:27
8358fb91  sftp-c-bpartner-credentials  default   Completed  19009  19009  0        0             2026-09-04 14:40  2026-09-04 14:41

docs.title: S3 — a prefix in a bucket (AWS, MinIO, R2, GCS S3-compat)
docs.text:
transport:
  kind: s3
  bucket: acme-exports         # required
  prefix: billing/             # optional key prefix filter, default ""
  suffix: .csv                 # optional filename filter, default "" (no filter)
  region: eu-west-3            # optional, default eu-west-3
  endpoint: http://minio:9000  # optional — only for non-AWS S3
  access_key_env: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID       # optional, default AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
  secret_key_env: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY   # optional, default AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  archive_bucket: acme-archive # optional, for after_process archive|move (default: source bucket)
  archive_prefix: archive/     # optional, default archive/
  • billing/ + .csv reads billing/2026-09-01.csv and ignores billing/2026-09-01.csv.tmp.
  • Same rule as SFTP: an object is read when new or rewritten, oldest first; zero-byte objects are skipped.
  • access_key_env / secret_key_env are secret names (lm secret set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID). A rotated key takes effect at the next run.

One export, archived after commit — the manifest of the S3 how-to:

$ lm run list --connector s3-c-bpartner
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN     OUT    SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ee860da1  s3-c-bpartner  default   Completed  10     5      5        5             2026-09-06 16:30  2026-09-06 16:30
dda81fcb  s3-c-bpartner  default   Completed  0      0      0        0             2026-09-06 16:21  2026-09-06 16:21
7329d11d  s3-c-bpartner  default   Completed  19009  19009  0        0             2026-09-06 16:03  2026-09-06 16:03
  • 16:03 — the 19 009-row export, read and archived.
  • 16:21 — nothing new under billing/ (the file is in the archive bucket now): IN 0.
  • 16:30 — a 10-record file, half malformed on purpose: 5 rows in, 5 dead-lettered.

docs.title: Parser
docs.text:
parser:
  delimiter: ","                # optional, auto-detected if absent
  encoding: UTF-8               # optional, auto-detected if absent
  has_header: true              # default true
  bom_strip: true               # default true
  null_values: ["", "NULL", "null", "#N/A"]  # default as shown
  columns: [code, name, email]  # REQUIRED when has_header: false; ignored otherwise
  • Auto-detection is per file. encoding: detected, fallback UTF-8. delimiter: the most frequent of , ; TAB | over the first 8 KB, fallback ,. An explicit key overrides it.

  • Headerless files need names, in file order ("\t" is a tab in YAML):

    parser:
  delimiter: "\t"
  has_header: false
  columns: [c_bpartner_id, name, created, isactive]

    Without columns:

    $ lm validate -f hl.yaml
✗ hl.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.parser.columns
          columns is required when has_header: false — headerless rows need names
          → Add parser.columns: [code, name, ...] in file order

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f hl.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

  • An empty value is a present column. 1, against two columns is written, the second value null (because "" is in null_values; override the list to keep "").

  • Runs commit in fixed 500-row chunks; a chunk_size key is ignored (the validator warns).

docs.title: Malformed rows — the per-row DLQ
docs.text:
A malformed row never fails the file. It goes to the dead-letter queue (DLQ), reason MalformedSource, and the run continues. A 6-row file with two bad rows:

"c_bpartner_id","name"
1004194,"DUPONT SARL"
1019809,"MARTIN"
BADROW,"trop de colonnes","erp legacy glitch"
1030001,"LAMBERT & FILS"
BADROW2
1030002,"NAUTILUS SAS"

$ lm run get 0a4af97d
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
0a4af97d  csv-malformed  default   Completed  6   4    2        2             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
⚠ 2 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 0a4af97d-cac0-4de0-a299-1db4599b8b31
$ lm dlq list --run 0a4af97d-cac0-4de0-a299-1db4599b8b31
ID        CONNECTOR      RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
556c4da1  csv-malformed  0a4af97d  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv:6 — Index f…
a2867c28  csv-malformed  0a4af97d  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv:4 — Record …

The entry keeps every raw value, with the file and line:

$ lm dlq get a2867c28
ID:        a2867c28-0424-44f7-86dd-77f3a0d86872
Connector: csv-malformed (434507c6-df49-4a09-a59f-dfb5df0589e9)
Run:       0a4af97d-cac0-4de0-a299-1db4599b8b31
Reason:    MalformedSource
Attempts:  1
Message:   /tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv:4 — Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared
Detail:    {"file":"/tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv","line":4,"message":"Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared"}
Payload:   {"raw":["BADROW","trop de colonnes","erp legacy glitch"],"file":"/tmp/exports/erp-export/c_bpartner_malformed.csv","line":4}

Malformed = the value count differs from the declared columns, in either direction:

the row against 2 declared columns result BADROW,"trop de colonnes","erp legacy glitch" 3 values DLQ — Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared BADROW2 1 value DLQ — Index for header 'name' is 1 but CSVRecord only has 1 values! 1, 2 values, one empty written, name is null 1,2, 3 values — a trailing delimiter is one column too many DLQ 3,"open (unclosed quote) swallows the rest of the file DLQ — one entry; the lines after it are never rows
  • An extra value is never dropped to make the row fit.
  • A trailing delimiter on every line sends the whole file to the DLQ — strip it producer-side.
  • SKIPPED and DEAD-LETTERS move together for malformed rows.
  • lm dlq: list, get, then discard, or replayed. The hub never re-reads a dead letter — fix the export and run again, then close each entry on that run: lm dlq replayed ID --new-run-id RUN takes only a Completed run of the same connector that started after the entry was captured. An entry no run carried is closed with discard.
  • Rows a validate-row hook drops land here too, reason ValidationFailed.
  • The one-shot lm csv ingest has no DLQ: its first malformed row refuses the whole ingest with a 400 naming the line (below).

docs.title: One file is the table — full refresh
docs.text:
A local path with no * or ? names one file, and that file is the table's whole state. A run that reads it to the end and succeeds removes the rows the file no longer holds.

transport:
  kind: local
  path: /imports/articles.csv    # one file: full refresh
after_process: none
refresh:
  max_removed: 30%               # the default — off, or 100%, lifts the guard

Ten articles, then A07 deleted from the file:

$ lm run get 2a1c346f
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2a1c346f  articles   default   Completed  9   9    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
• 1 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them

The removed count sits outside IN = OUT + SKIPPED: the run never read those rows.

Four guards: the run fails and nothing is removed. The next run reads the whole file again.

  • The table would shrink by more than refresh.max_removed (30% unless declared). A truncated export looks exactly like a purge. Here the file is cut to 4 lines; the purge is real, so the threshold is raised:
$ lm run get d4fa0d53
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
d4fa0d53  articles   default   Failed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
✖ run failed: 5 of 9 rows would be removed: the file holds 4 where the table held 9, more than refresh.max_removed (30%) allows — nothing was removed. If the file really lost them, raise refresh.max_removed (or set it to off) and run again.
$ tail -3 articles.yaml
  after_process: none
  refresh:
    max_removed: 60%
$ lm apply -f articles.yaml
{"name":"articles","connectorId":"96636ab2-3a72-4f9e-a351-eb9d497de081","endpointsApplied":1}
$ lm connector run articles
run scheduled: 54de3ded-1939-449a-bd99-73eb36813a1d
$ lm run get 54de3ded
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
54de3ded  articles   default   Completed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
• 5 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them
  • A row of the file went to the dead letters while rows would be removed: its last good version stays. A row a validate-row hook drops counts the same way.
$ lm run get 08cb8fb5
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
08cb8fb5  articles   default   Failed  4   3    1        1             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
⚠ 1 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 08cb8fb5-286b-4fe0-84bd-eafec50d10f5
✖ run failed: 1 row(s) of the file went to the dead letters this run (lm dlq list --run 08cb8fb5-286b-4fe0-84bd-eafec50d10f5): a full refresh removes nothing while a row of the file is in the dead letters, whatever its reason (unreadable, dropped by validate-row…) — nothing was removed. Fix the cause each dead letter reports (lm dlq get <id>) and run again.
  • An empty file (a header and no rows) never empties the table:
$ lm run get 4f61dcf3
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
4f61dcf3  articles   default   Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
✖ run failed: the file is empty: a full refresh never empties a table from an empty file — nothing was removed. If the source really is empty, delete the connector's data instead (lm connector delete).
  • The file changed while the run read it (rewritten between two chunks): the run fails with the file changed while this run was reading it.

The guards speak only when rows would be removed. A dead letter on a new row, with nothing to remove, completes as usual (IN 5 OUT 4 DEAD-LETTERS 1).

New values are not a loss. Every price of the 4-line file changed: the 4 old versions go, the table holds the 4 new rows, and the guard sees no shrink:

$ lm run get 16ad0bee
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
16ad0bee  articles   default   Completed  4   4    0        0             2026-10-19 01:41  2026-10-19 01:41
• 4 row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them

What never removes a row:

the run why finds the file unchanged it is not read again (size and modification time) resumes a file a failed run left half-read it did not read the whole file reads a glob (*.csv) a drop folder only adds reads an sftp or s3 transport each file is read when new or rewritten; nothing is compared

A refresh block on a drop folder is flagged:

$ lm validate -f drop.yaml
! drop.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.refresh
          refresh is read only for one local file (transport kind: local, a path without * or ?): this source is a drop folder and never removes rows, so the block does nothing here
          → Remove the refresh block, or point transport.path at the one file that holds the table

Only this connector's rows are removed; a row another connector landed in the same table stays. A removed row also leaves the entities fused from it, lm ask, and any Search index over them.

docs.title: Scheduling & lifecycle
docs.text:
• schedule — optional cron, 5 fields, in UTC (0 6 * * * = daily at 06:00 UTC), checked at apply. The hub fires it — no OS cron. A re-apply without schedule unschedules the connector. window: "22:00-06:00" (UTC, end exclusive) fences scheduled runs.
  • after_process — required. What happens to a file once its rows are committed:
none archive move delete does leaves the file in place relocates it relocates it — same action, archive_path mandatory removes it sftp ✓ → archive_path (default /archive/) → archive_path ✓ s3 ✓ → archive_bucket/archive_prefix (defaults: source bucket, archive/) same ✓ local ✓ refused refused refused
  • The archived name carries the file's modification time: livraisons.csv read with its mtime at 16:35:44 UTC on 22 October 2026 is archived as livraisons.20261022T163544Z.csv. An export that drops the same name every night keeps one archive per night; none replaces another. A source with sub-second times keeps them: on s3, livraisons.20261022T163544.047Z.csv.
  • Only the version that was read is archived. A new file dropped under the same name before the earlier one was archived is read first, then archived in its turn. The check runs just before the move, not with it: have the producer write under a name the glob does not match, then rename it in, and nothing can land in between.
  • A file that cannot be archived is said on the run — an archive folder the user cannot write, say. The file was read; it stays in the source folder, and lm run get says so:
• 1 file(s) read but not archived — still in the source folder (after_process failed; see the hub log)

$ lm validate -f local-archive.yaml
✗ local-archive.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.after_process
          after_process: archive is not executed on local connector runs — files stay in place (honored by one-shot lm csv ingest and by sftp/s3)
          → Set after_process: none for a local connector, or move the files with an sftp/s3 transport

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f local-archive.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

lm csv ingest offers no after_process: the message's mention of it does not apply to lm.

A file and its rows are never lost together (sftp/s3):

  • a file is archived or deleted only once a later commit proves its rows landed;
  • after a crash in between, the file stays; the next run skips its rows and archives it then.

A misspelled key is flagged in every block except inside mapping — the manifest still applies:

$ lm validate -f typo.yaml
! typo.yaml — 0 error(s), 1 warning(s)

  WARN     spec.windo
          unknown key — ignored by the runtime
          → Remove it, or check the spelling

docs.title: Target table
docs.text:
• One table per connector, connector.t_<name>, columns from the header (or parser.columns).
  • Seven reserved columns are always there: id, _row_hash, _ingested_at, _source, _run_id, _mapping_version, tenant_id. A table fed by one local file adds _seen_run, used by the full refresh. A source column with one of these names is refused — rename it with a map-columns hook.

  • target.indexes declares Postgres indexes — { columns: [...], unique: <bool> } (unique defaults to false); a malformed entry fails validation:

    target:
  indexes:
    - { columns: [email], unique: true }
    - { columns: [bpartner_id, dateordered] }

  • The métier scope is on the connector: metadata.scopes (see Scopes); the validator warns when none is declared.

  • lm connector delete removes the connector's rows, its run history and its RAG chunks (the table goes with the last connector writing into it):

    $ lm connector delete csv-local-simple --dry-run
Would delete connector csv-local-simple (csv-file) — 3 rows of connector.t_csv_local_simple, its run history and RAG chunks (dry run, nothing deleted)

  • lm endpoint purge refuses a csv-file endpoint — delete the connector instead (see Emptying one endpoint on its own). The table of a one-shot lm csv ingest is the exception: lm endpoint purge quick_look/quick_look empties it.

    $ lm endpoint purge csv-local-simple/default --force
Error: API error 400: This endpoint writes to a connector table whose rows are not tracked per endpoint, so it cannot be purged on its own. Deleting the connector removes its data, along with its run history.

docs.title: Transform at ingestion
docs.text:
An optional mapping block repairs legacy data as it flows in — dataset → row → cell hooks, in that order, on every connector run:

mapping:
  cell:
    - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name, city] }      # "BÃ©nÃ©dict" → "Bénédict"

Every hook, with an input → output example: Transformers. Parse hooks fail soft — an unreadable value becomes null, the row is still written, and the run's cell_errors counts it.

docs.title: Connector runs vs one-shot lm csv ingest
docs.text:
Connector manifest (scheduled runs) One-shot lm csv ingest Source local, sftp, s3 a file on your machine (uploaded), sftp://…, s3://… schedule (cron) yes no mapping hooks (dataset/row/cell) yes (aggregator refused) no after_process sftp/s3: all four; local: none not available — the source file stays in place File size limit none an uploaded file: 10 MB (larger: Error: API error 413); a remote file: 500 MB Malformed rows per-row DLQ, run continues the first one fails the whole ingest, nothing written Target table connector.t_<name> ext.<name> (JSONB + typed columns) Several files one connector over a glob one dataset per file; --name needs a single file

A connector manifest carrying file_filter, pre_process, post_process or max_file_size is refused:

$ lm validate -f oneshot-keys.yaml
✗ oneshot-keys.yaml — 2 error(s), 2 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.transport.file_filter
          file_filter runs only on one-shot lm csv ingest — scheduled connector runs ignore it
          → Drop it from the connector manifest, or ingest this source via lm csv ingest

  ERROR    spec.transport.max_file_size
          max_file_size runs only on one-shot lm csv ingest — scheduled connector runs ignore it
          → Drop it from the connector manifest, or ingest this source via lm csv ingest

  WARN     spec.transport.max_file_size
          unknown key — ignored by the runtime
          → Remove it, or check the spelling

  WARN     spec.transport.file_filter
          unknown key — ignored by the runtime
          → Remove it, or check the spelling

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f oneshot-keys.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 2 error(s)

lm csv ingest has no flag for these keys either: drop them.

$ lm csv ingest ./clients.csv --name quick-look --scope demo
Ingested ./clients.csv into ext.quick_look
  • rows written:    2
  • promoted cols:   3
      - row_id (bigint)
      - email (text)
      - signup_date (text)

  • askable:         scope 'demo' — try: lm ask --scope demo "how many rows are in ext.quick_look?"
A dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.

With the AI switched off, the last lines read A one-shot: no run recorded, nothing indexed for chat. and The rows are in ext.quick_look, and a dormant connector is registered.

docs.title: What one-shot actually does
docs.text:
One transaction: sample → infer → write. A dormant connector (enabled: false, no schedule) then sits in lm connector list under the slugged name (quick-look → quick_look) — inspect it, promote it to a manifest, or lm connector delete quick_look.

  • Type inference, widest type over the first 100 rows: integers → BIGINT, decimals → DECIMAL, true/false → BOOLEAN, anything else TEXT. Dates stay TEXT — signup_date (text) above.
  • Reserved columns are never typed columns: id, tenant_id, external_id, data, indexed_at, connector_id, endpoint_id. Their values stay in the JSONB data.
  • Askable at once in the scope you pass (--scope, default system), with the AI on.

  • Re-ingesting the same name refreshes the table: rows deduplicate by key, new columns are added:

    $ lm csv ingest ./clients.csv --name quick-look --scope demo
Re-ingested ./clients.csv into ext.quick_look — one more breath (rows dedup by key)
  • rows written:    3
  • promoted cols:   3
      - row_id (bigint)
      - email (text)
      - signup_date (text)

A one-shot: no run recorded, nothing indexed for chat.
The rows are in ext.quick_look, and a dormant connector is registered — see `lm connector list`.

    (AI off.) A different --scope moves the dataset to that scope.

  • A name held by a configured connector is refused:

    $ lm csv ingest ./clients.csv --name articles
Error: API error 409: the name 'articles' belongs to a configured connector — pass a different --name, or delete that connector first (lm connector delete)

  • A malformed row fails the whole ingest and nothing is written. lm names the line: Error: API error 400: malformed CSV row at line 3 — Record has 3 values but only 2 columns are declared.

  • An uploaded file over 10 MB is refused before anything is read: Error: API error 413 (request too large): the hub accepts a request body up to 10 MB — put a larger CSV on sftp:// or s3://.
  • Remote files (sftp/s3) are fetched one by one, each up to 500 MB, and left in place.
  • Delimiter and encoding are auto-detected per file.

--name needs a single file

sftp://host/dir/ reads *.csv by default (--pattern), so a folder is several files. With --name, the hub refuses before downloading anything: name 'clients' would ingest 3 files into one dataset, which the one-shot path cannot register: …. Three ways forward:

  • one dataset per file — drop --name; each file gets ext.<filename>.
  • one specific file — point the URL at it, or narrow --pattern / --suffix.
  • the whole folder as one dataset — a connector manifest with a glob path.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
lm csv ingest <local-file>
lm csv ingest sftp://user@host[:port]/path-or-glob --key-secret X | --password-secret X [--host-key-fingerprint "SHA256:…"]
lm csv ingest s3://bucket/prefix --region eu-west-3 [--endpoint X] [--suffix .csv]

docs.title: Ingest an SFTP folder nightly
docs.text:
1. Store the secret the manifest names:

    $ lm secret set CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD
Value for CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD:
Created secret "CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD"

  2. Apply the manifest — this one targets the docker-compose demo server:

    # 30-sftp-key.yaml — pull CSVs from an SFTP server into the hub.
#   lm apply -f docs/connectors/csv/30-sftp-key.yaml
#   lm connector run csv-sftp
#
# Credentials are NEVER inline: `password_env` names an environment variable the PLATFORM process
# holds (resolved at run time via the secret store, then system property, then env). Use `key_env`
# instead for SSH key auth (the value is the PEM private key).
#
# Cursor: the connector tracks a per-file watermark — each run ingests only files newer than the
# last processed one (atomic per file; replays are idempotent via _row_hash dedup).

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: csv-sftp
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [demo]

spec:
  transport:
    kind: sftp
    host: localhost
    port: 2222                       # the docker-compose 'sftp' service
    user: csvuser
    path: /upload/seed/*.csv         # glob on the remote side (seed/ subdir from the read-only mount)
    password_env: CSV_SFTP_PASSWORD  # env var the platform holds (never the password itself)
    strict_host_key: false           # DEMO ONLY. The docker-compose 'sftp' service mounts no volume
                                     # for /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key, so the container generates a new
                                     # host key every time it is recreated — there is no stable
                                     # fingerprint to pin here. Against a real server drop this line
                                     # (the default is true) and declare host_key_fingerprint: false
                                     # accepts an impostor as readily as the real host.

  parser:
    has_header: true

  after_process: none              # validator vocab: archive|delete|move|none ('none' = leave file in place)

  3. lm connector run csv-sftp reads every file under /upload/seed/*.csv. Once it looks right, add schedule: "0 6 * * *", and after_process: archive with an archive_path.

Watch it in the TUI (CLI & TUI): :runs for the run's status, :dlq for rejected rows.

docs.title: Ingest a headerless export under an S3 prefix, and archive it
docs.text:
# 45-s3-headerless-archive.yaml — a headerless, tab-separated ERP export under an S3 prefix,
# archived to another bucket once its rows are committed.
#   lm validate -f docs/connectors/csv/45-s3-headerless-archive.yaml
#   lm apply    -f docs/connectors/csv/45-s3-headerless-archive.yaml
#   lm connector run s3-c-bpartner
#
# No `endpoint:` → real AWS; set `region` to the region the bucket lives in (the default is eu-west-3).
# `access_key_env` / `secret_key_env` name secrets held by the platform
# (`lm secret set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID -`), never the values.
# `has_header: false` makes `parser.columns` mandatory — the names, in file order.
# `after_process: archive` moves each file to `archive_bucket`/`archive_prefix` only after a later
# committed cursor proves its rows landed; the next run then finds nothing new and reads 0 rows.
# Walk-through: docs/connectors/csv.md.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: s3-c-bpartner
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [s3-scenario]

spec:
  transport:
    kind: s3
    bucket: lumnik-exports
    prefix: billing/
    region: us-east-1
    suffix: .csv
    access_key_env: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    secret_key_env: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
    archive_bucket: lumnik-archive
    archive_prefix: archive/

  parser:
    delimiter: "\t"
    has_header: false
    columns: [c_bpartner_id, name, created, isactive]

  after_process: archive

Result: the run ledger above — 19 009 rows on the first run, IN 0 on the next because the file is in lumnik-archive now. Column 1 lands as c_bpartner_id, column 2 as name, and so on. For MinIO or another S3-compatible store, add endpoint: — see 40-s3-prefix.yaml in docs/connectors/csv/.

docs.title: Load one file for a quick look
docs.text:
$ lm csv ingest ./clients.csv

Result: a dormant connector plus a table ext.clients, askable in the system scope (AI on) — inspect, then promote it into a manifest or lm connector delete clients.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix SFTP host key refused for host:22 — the server presented SHA256:… host_key_fingerprint absent or wrong, with strict_host_key: true (the default) confirm the presented fingerprint out of band (ssh-keyscan -p 22 HOST \| ssh-keygen -lf -), paste it into host_key_fingerprint SFTP error (SSH_FX_PERMISSION_DENIED): Permission denied wrong password/key, or the user cannot read path lm secret list, then lm secret set <NAME> (a private key is many lines — pipe it with <NAME> -); check the folder's rights SFTP transport requires key_env or password_env neither credential declared lm secret set <NAME>, then password_env: <NAME> or key_env: <NAME> S3 403 Forbidden invalid S3 credentials check the secrets named by access_key_env / secret_key_env columns is required when has_header: false a headerless parser without names parser.columns: [a, b, …] in file order after_process: archive is not executed on local connector runs a relocation on a local transport after_process: none, or an sftp/s3 transport … runs only on one-shot lm csv ingest file_filter, pre_process, post_process or max_file_size in a connector manifest drop the key run Failed: connector.t_… is already written by connector '…' another connector of the tenant already writes the table named after this one apply it under another metadata.name, then lm connector delete the refused one — see JDBC run completes with IN 0 nothing new — or the local path matches nothing on the hub's disk lm connector get NAME shows the path (config.transport.path); check it exists on the hub a file dropped in a local folder is never read its name sorts before the last file read (drop-folder contract) name incoming files monotonically, or switch to sftp/s3 run Failed: The cursor's file … is gone, but files sorting after it are waiting a file was archived before the run that read it completed lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/<endpoint>; archive only after Completed DEAD-LETTERS > 0, reason MalformedSource value count differs from the declared columns — trailing delimiter, unclosed quote lm dlq get ID shows the raw values, file and line; fix the export or parser: rows missing, DLQ empty filter-where / skip-empty-rows excluded them (counted in SKIPPED) see Transformers § Troubleshooting a mapped column is blank for some rows a parse-* or lookup hook nulled a value it could not read cell_errors on lm run get <id> — see Transformers run Failed: N of M rows would be removed: the file holds … the one local file lost more rows than refresh.max_removed allows check the file; for a real purge raise refresh.max_removed (or off), re-apply, run again — see full refresh run Failed: the file is empty: a full refresh never empties a table the one local file holds a header and no row fix the export; to empty the table, lm connector delete run Failed: N row(s) of the file went to the dead letters this run a line of the one local file could not be read lm dlq list --run <id>, fix the export, run again run Failed: the file changed while this run was reading it the producer rewrote the file mid-run run again; have the producer write elsewhere and rename the file in rows gone from a local table after a run the file no longer holds them lm run get <id> says N row(s) removed; to keep history, ingest a folder (*.csv) a source column shares a reserved column name one of the seven reserved columns rename it with map-columns lm csv ingest fails with API error 400: malformed CSV row at line N — … line N does not have the header's column count fix that line, ingest again

docs.title: GraphQL
docs.text:
Ingest a GraphQL API by putting the query in the manifest — a request shape on the REST engine (connector_type stays rest-generic), with Relay pagination required.

Type rest-generic (shape graphql) Protocol GraphQL over POST Target ext.* hybrid Schedulable cron Edition Open

Auth, retry, rate limiting and the hybrid JSONB + typed storage are all shared with REST. This page covers what is different: the query, Relay pagination, and what happens when the server answers 200 and still says no.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
The screens below read the demo API that ships with the repo — the same one the REST page uses, under its POST /graphql shape. Start it, and put its key in the registry:

python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/acme-api.py
lm secret set ACME_API_KEY        # demo-key

# 70-graphql-relay.yaml — GraphQL is a request SHAPE on the REST engine, not a second connector.
#
# `connector_type` stays rest-generic. What changes: the request is a POST carrying
# {"query": ..., "variables": ...} to a single URL, and the cursor rides in the body.
#
# ── The hard rule ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A graphql endpoint must declare `kind: relay` with `cursor_binding: variable`, and that
# binding is valid nowhere else. The reason is mechanical: the binding writes the cursor into
# the POST body's `variables.<cursor_var>`, and a GET has no body to write it into. Both halves
# are refused at apply.
#
# ── Relay, concretely ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The Connections spec puts rows under edges[].node and the paging state under pageInfo:
#   cursor_path    → $.data.partners.pageInfo.endCursor   (an OPAQUE string — base64 here)
#   has_more_path  → $.data.partners.pageInfo.hasNextPage
#   response_path  → $.data.partners.edges[*].node        (a JSONPath projection)
#   cursor_var     → after — the same name as $after in the query, without the sigil
#
# Note the asymmetry with the `cursor` strategy, which unwraps a one-element list from
# $.data[-1:].id: relay does not — cursor_path must resolve to a scalar directly.
#
# Page size lives in the query (`first: 500`): GraphQL has no size parameter to bind.
# `graphql_path` is spec-level and defaults to /graphql — spelled out here for readability.
#
# Expect: 2 400 rows in ext.acme_graphql_partners.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-graphql
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099
  graphql_path: /graphql

  auth:
    kind: api-key
    in: header
    name: X-API-Key
    value_env: ACME_API_KEY

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      kind: graphql
      query: |
        query($after: String) {
          partners(first: 500, after: $after) {
            edges { cursor node { id name city credit_limit } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
          }
        }
      pagination:
        kind: relay
        cursor_binding: variable
        cursor_var: after
        cursor_path: "$.data.partners.pageInfo.endCursor"
        has_more_path: "$.data.partners.pageInfo.hasNextPage"
        response_path: "$.data.partners.edges[*].node"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_graphql_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name,         path: "$.name",         type: text }
          - { name: city,         path: "$.city",         type: text }
          - { name: credit_limit, path: "$.credit_limit", type: bigint }

$ lm apply -f docs/connectors/rest/demo/70-graphql-relay.yaml
{"name":"acme-graphql","connectorId":"35e9c66a-ec11-4ea5-a9f8-12cca9829c69","endpointsApplied":1}
$ lm source rest test acme-graphql
ENDPOINT  METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
partners  POST    200     500    ok

The pre-flight sends the request a run sends (POST): one page, 500 nodes, nothing written.

$ lm connector run acme-graphql
run scheduled: f26868f0-641e-471a-8719-e6c4c2957fee
$ lm run list --connector acme-graphql
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
f26868f0  acme-graphql  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45

docs.title: The manifest
docs.text:
Field Where Required Notes graphql_path spec no The single POST endpoint; requests go to base_url + graphql_path (default /graphql) kind: graphql endpoint no An endpoint carrying a query is treated as GraphQL either way — the examples declare it for readability query endpoint yes The query document; declare the cursor variable it expects (e.g. $after) variables endpoint no Static variables sent with every request; the relay cursor is injected on top pagination endpoint yes Hard rule: kind: relay with cursor_binding: variable — anything else is refused at apply cursor_var pagination yes The variable that receives endCursor (e.g. after) cursor_path, has_more_path, response_path pagination yes JSONPaths to endCursor, hasNextPage and the node list target endpoint yes The same hybrid target as REST: table, unique_key, promote incremental endpoint no Leave it at full — see Incremental does not reach a GraphQL server

path and method are implicit — the request is always a POST to graphql_path.

  • In the query the variable carries its sigil ($after); cursor_var: after names it without.
  • There is no page-size field: page size is in the query itself (first: 500 above).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
• The query is POSTed as { "query": ..., "variables": ... } to base_url + graphql_path.
  • Relay pagination reads pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }, and re-injects endCursor into variables.<cursor_var> for the next request — the Relay Connections convention.
  • response_path: ...edges[*].node extracts the node list (a JSONPath projection), so the rows that land are the nodes, without the edges wrapper.
  • A relay cursor is opaque: point cursor_path at pageInfo.endCursor; it must resolve to a scalar.

docs.title: The hard rule, and its two refusals
docs.text:
A graphql endpoint must declare kind: relay with cursor_binding: variable, and that binding is valid nowhere else:

$ lm apply -f bad-gql.yaml
✗ bad-gql.yaml — 1 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].pagination
          graphql endpoints require pagination.kind=relay with cursor_binding=variable
          → Use pagination: { kind: relay, cursor_binding: variable, cursor_var: <name>, cursor_path: ..., has_more_path: ..., response_path: ... }

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f bad-gql.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 1 error(s)

The other half — cursor_binding: variable on a non-graphql endpoint — is refused the same way; see Cursor binding.

docs.title: The two ways a GraphQL server says no on HTTP 200
docs.text:
A GraphQL server may answer 200 with an errors array, or with "data": null. Both are refused — by lm source rest test before any run:

$ lm source rest test acme-graphql-errors
ENDPOINT      METHOD  STATUS  ITEMS  VERDICT
errors-array  POST    200     0      GraphQL response carried 1 error(s); first: Cannot query field 'boom' on type 'Query'
null-data     POST    200     0      GraphQL response has no errors and null/absent data (malformed envelope): {"data": null}
Error: 2 of 2 enabled endpoint(s) did not answer with readable data

and by a run, with the same message:

# 80-graphql-errors.yaml — the two ways a GraphQL server says no on HTTP 200.
#
# GraphQL does not use status codes to report a failed query. A server that cannot resolve a
# field answers 200 with an `errors` array; one whose resolver blew up answers 200 with
# `"data": null`. Read as transport, both are successes — and a run that reads them as data
# ingests nothing and completes green.
#
# Both endpoints below must FAIL, and `lm source rest test acme-graphql-errors` must refuse
# them before any run is started.
#
# The demo API triggers them from the query text: a query mentioning `boom` gets the errors
# array, one mentioning `nullData` gets the null envelope.
#
# Expect: both endpoints Failed, each naming what came back.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-graphql-errors
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099
  graphql_path: /graphql

  auth:
    kind: api-key
    in: header
    name: X-API-Key
    value_env: ACME_API_KEY

  endpoints:
    - id: errors-array
      kind: graphql
      query: |
        query($after: String) {
          boom(first: 500, after: $after) {
            edges { cursor node { id } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
          }
        }
      pagination:
        kind: relay
        cursor_binding: variable
        cursor_var: after
        cursor_path: "$.data.boom.pageInfo.endCursor"
        has_more_path: "$.data.boom.pageInfo.hasNextPage"
        response_path: "$.data.boom.edges[*].node"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_gql_errors
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

    - id: null-data
      kind: graphql
      query: |
        query($after: String) {
          nullData(first: 500, after: $after) {
            edges { cursor node { id } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
          }
        }
      pagination:
        kind: relay
        cursor_binding: variable
        cursor_var: after
        cursor_path: "$.data.nullData.pageInfo.endCursor"
        has_more_path: "$.data.nullData.pageInfo.hasNextPage"
        response_path: "$.data.nullData.edges[*].node"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_gql_nulldata
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-graphql-errors
ID        CONNECTOR            ENDPOINT      STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2ca12c44  acme-graphql-errors  null-data     Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45
84f519e9  acme-graphql-errors  errors-array  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45

$ lm run get 84f519e9
ID        CONNECTOR            ENDPOINT      STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
84f519e9  acme-graphql-errors  errors-array  Failed  0   0    0        0             2026-10-19 01:45  2026-10-19 01:45
✖ run failed: GraphQL response carried 1 error(s); first: Cannot query field 'boom' on type 'Query'

Nothing is ingested and nothing is dead-lettered. Fix the query, or the permission it needs, and run again.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text: spec.headers[] applies to every request, as for REST request headers.

docs.title: Incremental does not reach a GraphQL server
docs.text:
incremental: { mode: watermark } is accepted on a graphql endpoint, but the mark is sent as a URL query parameter, not as a GraphQL variable:

19/Oct/2026 07:26:36  "POST /graphql?updated_since=2026-01-02T15%3A59%3A00Z HTTP/1.1" 200 -

A GraphQL server ignores it, so every run reads everything — acme-graphql with incremental added, run twice:

$ lm run list --connector acme-graphql
ID        CONNECTOR     ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
df7023ae  acme-graphql  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 07:26  2026-10-19 07:26
b108a108  acme-graphql  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 07:26  2026-10-19 07:26

Filter in the query itself — a static variables: entry or a literal argument — and leave incremental at full.

docs.title: Not yet supported
docs.text: Mutations, subscriptions, schema-introspection discovery, persisted queries, query batching, per-endpoint header overrides, and on_error: warn (partial-success ingestion).

docs.title: Send static variables with every request
docs.text:
endpoints:
  - id: partners
    kind: graphql
    variables: { locale: fr-FR }   # merged into every request

Result: every request carries locale: fr-FR in its GraphQL variables, beside the relay cursor.

docs.title: Read a second collection from the same API
docs.text: Add a second endpoint with its own query, its own pagination paths (they name the collection: $.data.<collection>.pageInfo.endCursor) and its own table. One connector, one API, one credential; the ledger records one run per endpoint.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Gesture Run fails though the HTTP status was 200 an errors[] array, or data: null with no errors read the message in lm run get — it carries the server's first error verbatim Run completed with IN 0 response_path does not match the envelope lm source rest test <connector> prints the item count it read from one page cursor_binding: variable refused at apply that binding is only valid on relay on a graphql endpoint use query or header binding on a plain REST endpoint Pagination never ends cursor_path resolves to a value that does not change it must point at pageInfo.endCursor, the opaque cursor the server hands back
