docs.text:
• REST — the engine underneath (auth providers, retry, rate limit, storage layout)
  • GraphQL — the other request shape on that engine
  • The demo API — the services these screens read
  • Overview
  • The WOW walkthrough ingests a fake Siebel over this connector — see it end to end
  • Diagnosing a failed run

docs.title: Transformers
docs.text: Repair legacy data as it flows in — mojibake, DD/MM/YYYY dates, numbers in parentheses — declared in the manifest's spec.mapping block, no code.

docs.title: Where this applies
docs.text:
• csv-file connector runs only. The csv-file connector applies the spec.mapping hooks before writing.
  • jdbc and kafka write a 1:1 dump — no spec.mapping. jdbc has one narrow knob for a source column colliding with a hub system column: source.tables[].rename, see JDBC: the hub table.
  • REST/GraphQL/SOAP transform in the promote: block's transform: enum — a short fixed list, see REST: the transform: enum.
  • Not the one-shot lm csv ingest. That path writes directly; its spec.mapping (if any) is ignored. To transform, apply a csv-file connector manifest and run it.
  • Dirty status values are a different tool's job — declare them as workflow aliases, which map legacy statuses without touching the data.
  • Rehearse before the live feed. lm validate checks the manifest's shape, not your data. Run against a sample file first, read the result, then point the same manifest at the real feed.

docs.title: Three tiers, one order
docs.text:
spec:
  mapping:
    dataset:                    # tier 1 — the whole chunk, once
      - skip-empty-rows: {}
    row:                        # tier 2 — one record; may emit 0..N rows
      - map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name } }
    cell:                       # tier 3 — one value, mutated in place
      - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name] }

flowchart TB
  F["file chunk"] --> D
  subgraph D["1 · dataset — the whole chunk, once"]
    D1["require-headers · skip-empty-rows · filter-where · sort-by · enrich-context"]
  end
  D --> R
  subgraph R["2 · row — one record in, 0..N out"]
    R1["map-columns · coalesce · defaults · validate-row · split-row"]
  end
  R --> C
  subgraph C["3 · cell — one value, in place"]
    C1["clean · fix-mojibake · parse-* · lookup · mask · regex-* · split · to-uuid · kotlin …"]
  end
  C --> T[("target table")]
  D1 -. "filter-where / skip-empty-rows" .-> S["SKIPPED"]
  R1 -. "validate-row" .-> Q["SKIPPED + DLQ"]
  C1 -. "unreadable value → null" .-> E["cell_errors"]
  • Across tiers the order is fixed: dataset → row → cell, always.
  • Within a tier, hooks run top to bottom as listed — order is yours, and it matters (validate-row before split-row; regex-extract before the default that fills its misses).
  • One entry per hook: - hook-name: { params }. A misspelled name passes lm validate and fails the run: ✖ run failed: unknown cell hook: fix-mojibak.

Three exits, three counters — nothing is dropped silently:

what happens to the row hook counted in excluded by a declared filter filter-where, skip-empty-rows SKIPPED dropped for a missing field validate-row SKIPPED and the DLQ written, one value null a cell hook that cannot read the value cell_errors

docs.title: Dataset hooks — the whole chunk, once
docs.text:
• Run once per chunk (500 rows), before the row and cell tiers. A dataset hook never sees the whole file.
  • So sort-by orders within a chunk — not the file, not the run. On a local glob run a chunk may hold the end of one file and the start of the next.

docs.title: require-headers — refuse a file with the wrong shape
docs.text:
dataset:
  - require-headers: { columns: [c_bpartner_id, name], any-of: [created, isactive] }
the file's header result c_bpartner_id,name,created,isactive passes c_bpartner_id,name,created passes — columns all present, one of any-of present c_bpartner_id,name fails the run: none of required headers found: [created, isactive] name,created fails the run: required header missing: c_bpartner_id
  • columns — every name must exist. any-of — at least one must.
  • With has_header: false, "the header" is the parser.columns list you declared.
  • An empty chunk passes: there is no header to check.

docs.title: skip-empty-rows — blank lines in the export
docs.text:
dataset:
  - skip-empty-rows: {}

Before:

code,name
C1,Acme Corp
,
C2,Globex

After: C1 and C2. The blank row (every cell null or whitespace) is counted in SKIPPED, not dead-lettered.

docs.title: filter-where — keep only the rows you asked for
docs.text:
dataset:
  - filter-where: { column: status, in: [ACTIVE, PENDING] }
status in: [ACTIVE, PENDING] equals: ACTIVE regex: "[0-9]+" ACTIVE kept kept dropped PENDING kept dropped dropped 1042 dropped dropped kept 10a dropped dropped dropped — regex is a full match (null) dropped dropped dropped — a null compares as ""
  • Declare any of equals, in, regex; several combine with AND.
  • A dropped row is counted in SKIPPED, not dead-lettered.
  • A bad regex is refused when the run starts, naming the hook and the knob.

docs.title: sort-by — order within the chunk
docs.text:
dataset:
  - sort-by: { columns: [c_bpartner_id] }        # max-rows: 100000 by default
before after 1000280, 1000001, (null), 1000117 (null), 1000001, 1000117, 1000280
  • Lexicographic (text order — 9 sorts after 10), within the 500-row chunk: a longer file is sorted piecewise, never as a whole.
  • Nulls sort first, as empty strings.
  • Over max-rows the run refuses: sort-by max-rows exceeded: <n> > <max> (input must be pre-sorted or increase max-rows).

docs.title: enrich-context — stamp provenance on every row
docs.text:
dataset:
  - enrich-context: { source_system: siebel, ingested_at: "${now}" }

Before:

code,name
C1,Acme Corp

After:

code,name,source_system,ingested_at
C1,Acme Corp,siebel,2026-08-20T14:03:11.482Z
  • Adds a constant column to every row of the chunk; ${now} resolves once, to the ingestion instant.
  • An existing value in that column is never overwritten.
  • Handy to feed a cell hook a test value — the full example mints its dirty inputs this way.

docs.title: Row hooks — one record in, 0..N out
docs.text: A row hook can drop, duplicate, or reshape rows.

docs.title: map-columns — legacy column names (CUST_NM)
docs.text:
row:
  - map-columns:
      rename: { CUST_NM: name, CUST_CITY: city }
      drop: [internal_flag]

Before:

CUST_NM,CUST_CITY,internal_flag
Bénédict Martin,Montréal,X

After:

name,city
Bénédict Martin,Montréal
  • Renames first, then drops — so drop names a renamed column by its new name. Naming the old one removes nothing.
  • A renamed column always appears, even when the value is empty.
  • Renaming a column away from a hub system column (id, tenant_id, _row_hash, …) is what this hook is for.

lm validate (and lm apply) refuse six shapes, naming the entry — here all six in one manifest:

row:
  - map-columns:
      rename: { CUST_NM: , CUST_CITY: 2city, CUST_ID: id, A: same, B: same }
      drop: internal_flag
  - map-columns:
      rename: [CUST_NM]

$ lm validate -f map-bad.yaml
✗ map-bad.yaml — 6 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[0].map-columns.rename.CUST_NM
          must name a target column — a colon with nothing after it is null, not a rename target, and 'null' would otherwise become the column's literal name
          → Example: map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name }, drop: [flag] }

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[0].map-columns.rename.CUST_CITY
          must be a plain identifier (letters, digits, underscore; not starting with a digit): 2city
          → Example: map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name }, drop: [flag] }

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[0].map-columns.rename.CUST_ID
          targets 'id', a hub system column (_ingested_at, _mapping_version, _row_hash, _run_id, _source, id, tenant_id) — renaming a source column AWAY from one of these is what the rename is for, renaming into one only recreates the collision
          → Example: map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name }, drop: [flag] }

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[0].map-columns.rename
          targets 'same' from more than one source column — one of them would be silently lost
          → Example: map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name }, drop: [flag] }

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[0].map-columns.drop
          must be a list of column names (got string) — for example drop: [internal_flag]
          → Example: map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name }, drop: [flag] }

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[1].map-columns.rename
          must be a map of source column to target column (got array) — for example rename: { CUST_NM: name }
          → Example: map-columns: { rename: { CUST_NM: name }, drop: [flag] }

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f map-bad.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 6 error(s)

One shape depends on the data and is not refused: the target already exists in the row. rename: { customer_id: ref } on a file that already has ref overwrites it and counts one cell error per row.

docs.title: coalesce — first non-blank of several columns
docs.text:
row:
  - coalesce: { column: display_name, from: [trade_name, name] }
display_name trade_name name → display_name (absent) Dupont DUPONT SARL Dupont (absent) (blank) DUPONT SARL DUPONT SARL Kept Dupont DUPONT SARL Kept — a filled target is never touched (absent) (absent) (blank) (absent) — nothing to take
  • Copies the value as it stands in the row tier, before any cell hook: in the full example display_name keeps DUPONT SARL while name is title-cased.

docs.title: defaults — fill blanks in several columns
docs.text:
row:
  - defaults: { is_active: "Y", country: FR }
is_active → N N — never overwrites (blank) Y (absent) Y — the column is created

The cell-tier twin is default (one column) — pick by where you need it in the order.

docs.title: validate-row — rows missing mandatory fields
docs.text:
row:
  - validate-row: { required: [code, name] }

Before:

code,name
C1,Acme Corp
C2,

After: C1 only. C2 (blank name) is counted in SKIPPED and dead-lettered:

$ lm run get fc9b4ba6
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
fc9b4ba6  csv-customers  default   Completed  2   1    1        1             2026-10-19 07:19  2026-10-19 07:19
⚠ 1 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run fc9b4ba6-5b32-49a3-af64-f96b8c344a2c

$ lm dlq list --run fc9b4ba6-5b32-49a3-af64-f96b8c344a2c
ID        CONNECTOR      RUN       REASON            ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
c20e8610  csv-customers  fc9b4ba6  ValidationFailed  1         required column 'name' is missing or blank
  • The dead letter holds the row as it stood in the row tier — raw, before any cell hook (mask included) ran.
  • lm dlq get <id> shows it; discard drops it, replayed --new-run-id RUN names the run that carried it again. The hub never re-reads a dead letter (lm dlq).
  • On a single-file connector (full refresh), a validate-row drop counts like an unreadable row: a run that would remove rows ends Failed and removes nothing — see full refresh. For example, after C1 was deleted from the file and a row C3,Beta Ltd added:
$ lm run get 270592cb
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
270592cb  csv-customers  default   Failed  2   1    1        1             2026-10-19 07:19  2026-10-19 07:19
⚠ 1 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 270592cb-c512-4601-9a1c-ba6927c4afd4
✖ run failed: 1 row(s) of the file went to the dead letters this run (lm dlq list --run 270592cb-c512-4601-9a1c-ba6927c4afd4): a full refresh removes nothing while a row of the file is in the dead letters, whatever its reason (unreadable, dropped by validate-row…) — nothing was removed. Fix the cause each dead letter reports (lm dlq get <id>) and run again.

C3 is written; C1 stays in the table.

validate-row placed after split-row is refused at validate (it would drop fragments, not source rows). So is aggregator:

row:
  - split-row: { by: tags, sep: ";" }
  - validate-row: { required: [code] }
  - aggregator: { emit-on-change: code }

$ lm validate -f order.yaml
✗ order.yaml — 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[2].aggregator
          aggregator is not supported on csv-file connector runs — each chunk commits separately, buffered rows would be silently lost at chunk boundaries
          → Pre-aggregate in the source (e.g. a grouped export), or drop the aggregator hook

  ERROR    spec.mapping.row[1].validate-row
          validate-row after split-row is not supported — validation would drop fanned fragments and corrupt the run arithmetic. Validate before splitting.
          → Validate before splitting, or drop the validate-row hook

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f order.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 2 error(s)

docs.title: split-row — one row per value of a;b;c
docs.text:
row:
  - split-row: { by: tags, sep: ";" }

Before:

id,tags
1,a;b;c

After:

id,tags
1,a
1,b
1,c
  • Parts are trimmed; every other column is copied onto each fragment.
  • explode: <column> does the same over a column that already holds a list.
  • Its cell-tier cousin split stays within the row.

docs.title: aggregator — exists, but csv-file runs refuse it
docs.text: lm validate / lm apply refuse it on a csv-file connector (refusal shown above). Pre-aggregate in the source (a grouped export), or drop the hook.

docs.title: Cell hooks — one value, in place
docs.text:
Two parameter conventions:

  • Multi-column hooks take columns: [a, b]; omitting columns (or columns: ["*"]) applies the hook to every column of the row.
  • Single-column hooks take column: <name> and refuse to guess.

Cell hooks fail soft: the row is still written, nothing is dropped or dead-lettered, and cell_errors counts what a hook did not deliver as declared — reading cell_errors.

docs.title: clean — BOM, stray whitespace, control characters
docs.text:
cell:
  - clean: { columns: [name, note], strip: true, remove-control-chars: true, normalize-unicode: NFC }
in out ﻿ hello\t (a BOM, two spaces, a tab) hello Café as e + combining accent Café as one precomposed é (NFC)
  • A leading BOM is always stripped; the three knobs are off by default.
  • remove-control-chars also removes tabs and newlines inside a value.
  • normalize-unicode: NFC, NFD, NFKC or NFKD. Use NFC when two exports spell the same accent two ways and your keys stop matching.

docs.title: fix-mojibake — accents came out as BÃ©nÃ©dict
docs.text:
Mojibake is text written as UTF-8 and read back as Latin-1. This hook recovers it — and only when it recognizes the pattern.

cell:
  - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name, city] }
in out BÃ©nÃ©dict Martin Bénédict Martin CÃ´te d'Azur Côte d'Azur Bénédict Martin unchanged — no mojibake pattern, a clean value is never touched BÃ©nÃ©dict € unchanged, +1 cell_errors — declined, see below
  • Not the parser's encoding detection (CSV & files → Parser): fix-mojibake fixes values already stored garbled in the source system.
  • A multi-line cell (a quoted postal address) is one value: every line is repaired.

When the repair is declined

A value mixing mojibake with a character outside Latin-1 (Japanese, Cyrillic, Greek, €, an emoji) is not repaired at all:

  • it lands exactly as it arrived, and the run counts one cell_errors;
  • the fix is at the source: re-export with the right encoding.

docs.title: decode-html-entities — & in text
docs.text:
cell:
  - decode-html-entities: { columns: [slogan] }
in out Eau & Soleil Eau & Soleil Coffee <hot> Coffee <hot> café café (the HTML4 entity set)

docs.title: replace-smart-quotes — curly quotes from Word and Excel
docs.text:
cell:
  - replace-smart-quotes: { columns: [slogan] }
in out “Eau & Soleil” – depuis 1998… "Eau & Soleil" - depuis 1998... l’été l'été «bonjour» "bonjour"

Also: en/em dash → -, ellipsis → ..., non-breaking space → space.

docs.title: strip-invisible — a code that "looks equal" but never matches
docs.text:
cell:
  - strip-invisible: { columns: [code] }
in out AB​CD (a zero-width space inside) ABCD soft­hyphen softhyphen

Removes every Unicode format character (Cf): zero-width space/joiner/non-joiner, BOM, word joiner, soft hyphen.

docs.title: remove-diacritics — ASCII-only identifiers
docs.text:
cell:
  - remove-diacritics: { columns: [city] }
in out Montréal Montreal ñoño nono

docs.title: upper / lower / titlecase — case
docs.text:
cell:
  - upper: { columns: [legal_form] }
  - lower: { columns: [city] }
  - titlecase: { columns: [name] }
hook in out upper sarl SARL lower Montreal montreal titlecase DUPONT SARL Dupont Sarl titlecase MARTIN DUPONT (two spaces) Martin Dupont — whitespace normalised
  • Text cells only: a date, a number or binary data is left as it is.
  • Locale-independent folding.
  • titlecase collapses runs of spaces, tabs and newlines to one space and drops trailing space.

docs.title: truncate — hard cut
docs.text:
cell:
  - truncate: { column: name, length: 60 }
in out a 75-character name its first 60 characters a 12-character name unchanged

A negative length is refused when the run starts.

docs.title: regex-replace — normalise with a pattern
docs.text:
cell:
  - regex-replace: { column: name, pattern: "\\s+", replacement: " " }
in out DUPONT SARL DUPONT SARL DUPONT\tSARL DUPONT SARL
  • replaceAll over the cell; replacement defaults to "" (delete the match).
  • In replacement, $ and \ are group references: a lone $ or a group the pattern does not have fails the run naming the hook — escape them (\\$).
  • A bad pattern is refused when the run starts.

docs.title: regex-extract — pull a piece into its own column
docs.text:
cell:
  - regex-extract:
      column: name
      pattern: ".*\\b(SARL|SAS|EURL|SCI)\\b.*"
      groups: { 1: legal_form }
name → legal_form DUPONT SARL SARL Standard (null) — no match, not counted (empty) (null) — no cell, no extraction
  • Tries a full match, then a find; each groups entry writes one capture group into a named column (0 is the whole match).
  • Every named column exists on every row — matched, missed, or empty. An all-null column means the pattern never matched.
  • A miss is not counted in cell_errors.
  • Refused when the run starts: a groups key that is not a number, is negative, or exceeds the pattern's group count.
  • Follow it with default to give the misses a value.

docs.title: default — fill one blank column
docs.text:
cell:
  - default: { column: legal_form, value: "NONE" }
in out SARL SARL — never overwrites (null or blank) NONE

Row-tier twin, several columns at once: defaults.

docs.title: lookup — translate codes with an inline table
docs.text:
cell:
  - lookup: { column: is_active, table: { "Y": true, "N": false }, on-missing: null }
in on-missing: keep (default) null error INACTIVE (any literal) Y true true true true ? ? (null), +1 cell_errors run fails: lookup: no match for '?' in column 'is_active' INACTIVE
  • table must be a map — a list or a scalar is refused when the run starts.
  • Replacement values land as text (true, not a boolean).

docs.title: parse-date — dates are 31/12/2019
docs.text:
cell:
  - parse-date: { column: signup_date, formats: ["dd/MM/yyyy", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"] }
in out 31/12/2019 2019-12-31 — a date 2004-10-18 23:42:39 2004-10-18 23:42:39+00 — a timestamp 12/31/2019 (null), +1 cell_errors — no format matched already a date unchanged
  • Formats are tried in order. A pattern with no H/h/m/s parses to a date; one with a time component parses to a timestamp.
  • Cheat sheet: dd = day, MM = month — capital M, lowercase mm means minutes, the classic trap — yyyy = year. Add H/h/m/s only when the source carries a time.

docs.title: Which time zone a time is in
docs.text:
An ERP export writes 2026-08-02 23:30:00 with no time zone. Say which one it is with zone:

cell:
  - parse-date: { column: stamp, formats: ["yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"], zone: Europe/Paris }
in zone stored (shown in UTC) 2026-08-02 23:30:00 (none) 2026-08-02 23:30:00+00: read as UTC 2026-08-02 23:30:00 Europe/Paris 2026-08-02 21:30:00+00: Paris is UTC+2 in summer 2026-01-15 23:30:00 Europe/Paris 2026-01-15 22:30:00+00: UTC+1 in winter 2026-08-02 Europe/Paris 2026-08-02: a date has no time, zone changes nothing
  • Without zone (or with an empty one), a time is always read as UTC, wherever the hub runs.
  • Fused with an ERP's dates in an entity, see Dates across sources: a date-only format makes the CSV agree with an ERP date, and a time parsed with the zone the ERP's connection declares agrees with an ERP time (A time without a time zone).
  • An unknown zone stops the run before its first row: parse-date hook: 'zone' is not a time zone: "Europe/Pariss" (for example Europe/Paris or UTC).

docs.title: parse-number — numbers are 1 234,56 € or (123)
docs.text:
cell:
  - parse-number: { column: balance, decimal-separator: ",", negatives-in-parens: true }
in out 1 234,56 € 1234.56 (123) -123 $1,234.50 with decimal-separator: "." 1234.50 n/a (null), +1 cell_errors
  • Strips currency symbols ($€£¥) and spaces, then resolves which of ./, is the decimal separator (auto by default). The result is a decimal: a column the hub creates from such values is NUMERIC(18,4), so 1024944 reads 1024944.0000.

docs.title: An integer column: integer: true
docs.text:
An identifier or a count is a whole number. Say so, and a column the hub creates from those values is BIGINT:

cell:
  - parse-number: { column: m_product_id, integer: true }
in out 1024944 1024944 — an integer 7.0000 7 1 024 944 1024944 7.1 (null), +1 cell_errors — not a whole number 9223372036854775808 (null), +1 cell_errors — past the BIGINT range a value already a number that is not finite (NaN) (null), +1 cell_errors
  • The value is converted exactly: never rounded, never truncated. Separators, currency symbols and negatives-in-parens follow the rules above.
  • integer is true or false (the default). Anything else stops the run before its first row — integer: "yes": parse-number hook: 'integer' must be true or false (got string).
  • The type is decided by the chunk that first carries the column, from its values: a column whose every value in that chunk is empty — blank, or not a number — is created TEXT instead, and stays text. A CSV whose first rows leave the column blank lands it as text; fill them, or create the table again once they are.
  • A table the hub created keeps its column types: adding integer: true to a connector that already ran leaves its TEXT or NUMERIC(18,4) column as it is. Create the table again, as for a date: the four steps, with parse-number in place of parse-date.

docs.title: parse-email — trim, lowercase, validate
docs.text:
cell:
  - parse-email: { column: contact_email, lower: true }
in out Contact@Example.COM contact@example.com contact at example (null), +1 cell_errors

docs.title: parse-phone — one format for every phone
docs.text:
cell:
  - parse-phone: { column: phone, default-region: FR }     # default-region: US by default
in out 06 12 34 56 78 +33612345678 +1 415 555 2671 +14155552671 — a full international number ignores the region abc (null), +1 cell_errors

default-region is the country assumed for a number with no + prefix — set it to the source's country or every national number lands wrong.

docs.title: mask — a column holds card/PII data
docs.text:
cell:
  - mask: { column: card_number, keep-last: 4 }       # keep-first: 0, mask-char: "*"
in out 4556123498761234 ************1234 contact@example.com with keep-first: 2, keep-last: 4 co*************.com 1234 1234 — unmasked: not longer than keep-first + keep-last

Counts raw characters — spaces and separators in 4556 1234 9876 1234 count like digits.

Two things to know before trusting mask for PII

  • A value not longer than keep-first + keep-last passes through unmasked. For a column that must never land readable, add a regex-replace matching the whole cell as a backstop.
  • A dead-lettered row keeps its raw, unmasked value — a malformed row or a validate-row drop never reaches the cell tier. What lm dlq shows is unmasked.

docs.title: split — parts into new columns
docs.text:
cell:
  - split: { column: tags, by: ";", into: [tag1, tag2, tag3] }
tags tag1 tag2 tag3 cell_errors retail;online;b2b retail online b2b — retail;online retail online (null) +1 — fewer parts than declared a;b;c;d a b c +1 — d has nowhere to go
  • Stays within the row; the original cell is untouched. The row-tier cousin split-row duplicates rows instead.
  • Parts are trimmed. Every name in into gets its column on every row (null when unfilled).
  • A trailing separator produces a part: A,B,, split on , is four values.
  • into-array: true replaces the cell with an array instead:
the chunk that creates the column column type later arrays holds at least one array jsonb — WHERE tags @> '["A"]' works, USING GIN (tags) indexes it jsonb holds only nulls text, never widened land as JSON text

docs.title: to-uuid — an id column holds junk like N/A or 0
docs.text:
Two separate knobs: generate decides an empty cell, on-invalid a cell holding junk.

cell:
  - to-uuid:
      column: customer_id
      generate: true          # an EMPTY cell gets a fresh id
      on-invalid: keep        # a cell holding "N/A" is left alone for you to look at
the cell holds generate on-invalid result cell_errors a valid UUID anything anything unchanged — nothing (empty) false (default) anything stays empty — nothing (empty) true anything a fresh id — N/A anything null (default) emptied +1 N/A anything generate a fresh id in place of N/A +1 N/A anything keep N/A, untouched —

A column that does not exist yet counts as empty — generate: true on row_uuid mints one per row.

on-invalid: generate invents an identifier — use it only for a surrogate key

  • The minted id replaces a value your source sent, joins to nothing elsewhere, and looks like a real id. Each one counts in cell_errors.
  • Only a few rows dirty? Run once with keep and look at them first — on-invalid applies to the whole column.

docs.title: kotlin — the escape hatch
docs.text:
cell:
  - kotlin:
      script: classpath:hooks/samples/normalize-date.kts
      context: { defaultCountry: FR }    # optional; the script reads it as `context`
signup_date in out 31/12/2019 2019-12-31 2019-12-31 unchanged — the sample script only rewrites DD/MM/YYYY

Details in Kotlin escape hatch below.

docs.title: One manifest, every transformer
docs.text:
Every transformer except aggregator, in one manifest over an S3 bucket: a headerless, tab-separated business-partner export (four columns). Every other input is minted by enrich-context so each hook has something to work on.

# 60-s3-every-transformer.yaml — one real manifest that runs EVERY transformer the csv-file
# connector offers (all but `aggregator`, which the validator refuses on chunked csv runs).
#   lm validate -f docs/connectors/csv/60-s3-every-transformer.yaml
#   lm apply    -f docs/connectors/csv/60-s3-every-transformer.yaml
#   lm connector run s3-c-bpartner-clean
#
# The source is a headerless, tab-separated ERP export with four columns. Every other column is
# minted by enrich-context so that each hook has something to bite: a dirty e-mail, a phone,
# a "1 234,56 €" amount, a "31/12/2019" date for the Kotlin script, tags to split, a channel to
# fan out, mojibake, HTML entities, smart quotes, an invisible character. Reads billing/ from the
# bucket and leaves the files in place. Walk-through: docs/connectors/transformers.md.
apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: s3-c-bpartner-clean
  connector_type: csv-file
  scopes: [s3-scenario]

spec:
  transport:
    kind: s3
    bucket: lumnik-exports
    prefix: billing/
    region: us-east-1
    suffix: .csv
    access_key_env: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID
    secret_key_env: AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY

  parser:
    delimiter: "\t"
    has_header: false
    columns: [c_bpartner_id, name, created, isactive]

  after_process: none

  mapping:
    # ── tier 1: dataset — the whole chunk, once ─────────────────────────────────────────
    dataset:
      - require-headers: { columns: [c_bpartner_id, name], any-of: [created, isactive] }
      - skip-empty-rows: {}
      - filter-where: { column: c_bpartner_id, regex: "[0-9]+" }
      - sort-by: { columns: [c_bpartner_id] }
      - enrich-context:
          ingested_from: erp-export-s3
          loaded_at: "${now}"
          contact_email: "  Contact@Example.COM "
          phone_raw: "06 12 34 56 78"
          balance_raw: "1 234,56 €"
          signup_date: "31/12/2019"
          tags_raw: "retail;online;b2b"
          channel_raw: "web;store"
          region_raw: "CÃ´te d'Azur"
          slogan_raw: "“Eau & Soleil” – depuis 1998…"
          city_raw: "Montréal"
          code_raw: "AB​CD"
          note_raw: "﻿  hello\t"
          junk: "dropped by map-columns"
    # ── tier 2: row — one record, may emit 0..N rows ────────────────────────────────────
    row:
      - map-columns:
          rename: { created: created_at, isactive: is_active }
          drop: [junk]
      - coalesce: { column: display_name, from: [trade_name, name] }   # trade_name never exists → raw name, BEFORE titlecase
      - defaults: { is_active: "Y" }
      - validate-row: { required: [c_bpartner_id, name] }             # must sit BEFORE split-row
      - split-row: { by: channel_raw, sep: ";" }                       # one row per channel: ×2
    # ── tier 3: cell — one value, in listed order ───────────────────────────────────────
    cell:
      - clean: { columns: [name, note_raw], strip: true, remove-control-chars: true, normalize-unicode: NFC }
      - fix-mojibake: { columns: [name, region_raw] }
      - decode-html-entities: { columns: [slogan_raw] }
      - replace-smart-quotes: { columns: [slogan_raw] }
      - strip-invisible: { columns: [code_raw] }
      - remove-diacritics: { columns: [city_raw] }
      - lower: { columns: [city_raw] }
      - regex-replace: { column: name, pattern: "\\s+", replacement: " " }
      - regex-extract:
          column: name
          pattern: ".*\\b(SARL|SASU|SAS|SA|EURL|SCI|SNC|SCP|MAIRIE|COMMUNE)\\b.*"
          groups: { 1: legal_form }
      - default: { column: legal_form, value: "NONE" }
      - upper: { columns: [legal_form] }
      - titlecase: { columns: [name] }
      - truncate: { column: name, length: 60 }
      - parse-date: { column: created_at, formats: ["yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"] }
      - lookup: { column: is_active, table: { "Y": true, "N": false }, on-missing: null }
      - parse-email: { column: contact_email, lower: true }
      - regex-extract: { column: contact_email, pattern: ".*@(.+)", groups: { 1: email_domain } }
      - mask: { column: contact_email, keep-first: 2, keep-last: 4 }
      - parse-phone: { column: phone_raw, default-region: FR }
      - parse-number: { column: balance_raw, decimal-separator: ",", negatives-in-parens: true }
      - split: { column: tags_raw, by: ";", into: [tag1, tag2, tag3] }
      - to-uuid: { column: row_uuid, generate: true }                 # column absent → empty → minted
      - kotlin:
          script: classpath:hooks/samples/normalize-date.kts          # "31/12/2019" → "2019-12-31"
          context: { defaultCountry: FR }
      - parse-date: { column: signup_date, formats: ["yyyy-MM-dd"] }   # after the script: a real date

$ lm validate -f docs/connectors/csv/60-s3-every-transformer.yaml
✓ 60-s3-every-transformer.yaml — valid

docs.title: One source row, column by column
docs.text:
One line of the file (tab-separated, no header), traced as it ran:

1000117 "DUPONT SARL"   "2004-10-18 00:00:00"   "N"

What lands in connector.t_s3_c_bpartner_clean — twice, because split-row fans web;store into two rows — as SELECT shows it:

column arrives as lands as done by c_bpartner_id 1000117 1000117 passes filter-where ([0-9]+), ordered by sort-by name DUPONT SARL Dupont Sarl clean → fix-mojibake → regex-replace → titlecase → truncate display_name — DUPONT SARL coalesce copied name in the row tier, before titlecase legal_form — SARL regex-extract on name, then upper; a name with no legal form gets NONE from default created → created_at 2004-10-18 00:00:00 2004-10-18 00:00:00+00 (timestamp) map-columns rename, parse-date isactive → is_active N false map-columns rename, defaults (Y when blank), lookup channel_raw web;store web on one row, store on the other split-row contact_email Contact@Example.COM co*************.com parse-email (trim + lower), then mask 2/4 email_domain — example.com regex-extract — placed before mask, or it would see stars phone_raw 06 12 34 56 78 +33612345678 parse-phone, default-region: FR balance_raw 1 234,56 € 1234.5600 parse-number signup_date 31/12/2019 2019-12-31 (date) kotlin script, then parse-date tags_raw retail;online;b2b unchanged, plus tag1/tag2/tag3 = retail/online/b2b split region_raw CÃ´te d'Azur Côte d'Azur fix-mojibake slogan_raw “Eau & Soleil” – depuis 1998… "Eau & Soleil" - depuis 1998... decode-html-entities, replace-smart-quotes city_raw Montréal montreal remove-diacritics, lower code_raw AB​CD (zero-width space inside) ABCD strip-invisible note_raw a BOM, hello, a tab hello clean row_uuid — c91c9560-6f8e-4572-89be-3a1397586a21 — a fresh one per row to-uuid, generate: true ingested_from, loaded_at — erp-export-s3, 2026-09-06T18:10:17.899174761Z enrich-context junk dropped by map-columns (no column) map-columns drop

Three placements to notice:

  • validate-row sits before split-row (the validator refuses the other order).
  • regex-extract on contact_email sits before mask — after it, the domain is stars.
  • default: NONE sits after regex-extract — a miss leaves legal_form null, and the default is what turns that null into a value.

docs.title: The run, as lm shows it
docs.text:
$ lm run get 53ec702e
ID        CONNECTOR            ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN     OUT    SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
53ec702e  s3-c-bpartner-clean  default   Completed  19019  19014  5        5             2026-09-06 20:09  2026-09-06 20:10
⚠ 5 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 53ec702e-4c92-4eb6-877d-f66f5ea383f8

$ lm dlq list --run 53ec702e-4c92-4eb6-877d-f66f5ea383f8
ID        CONNECTOR            RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
c47ecf87  s3-c-bpartner-clean  53ec702e  MalformedSource  1         billing/C_BPartner_Format_malformed.csv:10 — java.io.IOExc…
8870766c  s3-c-bpartner-clean  53ec702e  MalformedSource  1         billing/C_BPartner_Format_malformed.csv:7 — Index for head…
9c3d0c40  s3-c-bpartner-clean  53ec702e  MalformedSource  1         billing/C_BPartner_Format_malformed.csv:5 — Record has 5 v…
dee41893  s3-c-bpartner-clean  53ec702e  MalformedSource  1         billing/C_BPartner_Format_malformed.csv:4 — Index for head…
50548d10  s3-c-bpartner-clean  53ec702e  MalformedSource  1         billing/C_BPartner_Format_malformed.csv:2 — Record has 5 v…

How to read it:

  • IN 19019 — every record read from the two files under billing/: the export, and a small malformed one placed beside it.
  • SKIPPED 5 = DEAD-LETTERS 5 — five malformed records (a fifth column, a missing one, an unclosed quote), rejected by the reader before any hook: reason MalformedSource.
  • OUT 19014 — the source rows that landed. The table holds 38 028 rows: split-row doubled each one, and the run counts source rows (IN = OUT + SKIPPED).
  • No cell_errors alert — every parse hook read every value.

docs.title: Reference — cell hooks
docs.text:
cell_errors counts the cells a hook did not deliver as declared — one per cell:

shape hooks emptied — written null parse-date, parse-number, parse-email, parse-phone, lookup with on-missing: null, to-uuid with on-invalid: null (default) left as it arrived fix-mojibake declined; split found more or fewer parts than into replaced by a value the source never sent to-uuid with on-invalid: generate overwritten map-columns renamed onto a column the row already had

A parse-date that cannot read 12/31/2019 with formats: ["dd/MM/yyyy"]:

$ lm run get ea396e45
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
ea396e45  csv-signups  default   Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
⚠ 1 cell(s) a hook did not deliver as declared — the rows were still written
  • The alert prints only when the count is above zero, and does not name the hook.
  • lm run get <id> -o json carries cellErrors; -o yaml carries cellerrors.
  • The TUI's run describe panel (:runs, select a run, d) shows cell_errors:.
  • It counts cells, not rows: it is not a column of the lm run table.
Hook Params (default) One line clean columns; strip (false); remove-control-chars (false); normalize-unicode (off; NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD) always strips a leading BOM; then optional trim, control-char removal, Unicode normalization fix-mojibake columns BÃ©nÃ©dict → Bénédict; declines (+1 cell_errors, value untouched) when a non-Latin-1 character would be lost decode-html-entities columns & → & (HTML4 entity set) replace-smart-quotes columns curly quotes/guillemets → ASCII quotes, en/em dash → -, ellipsis → ..., NBSP → space strip-invisible columns removes every Unicode Cf character (ZWSP, ZWJ, BOM, soft hyphen…) remove-diacritics columns Café → Cafe upper / lower columns case, text cells only, locale-independent titlecase columns DUPONT SARL → Dupont Sarl; text cells only; normalises whitespace truncate column; length (unlimited) hard cut at length characters; negative refused regex-replace column; pattern; replacement ("") replaceAll over the cell; $/\ in replacement are group references regex-extract column; pattern; groups (map group-index → column) capture groups into named columns; a miss writes null, not counted; bad groups keys refused at start default column; value fills a null or blank cell; never overwrites lookup column; table (inline map); on-missing (keep; or null / error / any literal) replaces via the map; on a miss: keep, null (+1), fail the run, or the literal parse-date column; formats (list of Java DateTimeFormatter patterns); zone (UTC) first matching format wins; H/h/m/s → timestamp in zone, else date; no match → null +1 parse-number column; decimal-separator (auto; or ","/"."); negatives-in-parens (false); integer (false) strips $€£¥ and spaces, (123) → -123; decimal out, or with integer an exact BIGINT (7.0 → 7); failure, or not a whole BIGINT with integer → null +1 parse-email column; lower (false) trim, optional lowercase, validate; invalid → null +1 parse-phone column; default-region (US) E.164 (+33612345678); failure → null +1 mask column; keep-first (0); keep-last (0); mask-char (*) masks the middle; a value not longer than keep-first + keep-last is left untouched split column; by (,); into (list) or into-array (false) parts into named columns (or an array); part-count mismatch → +1 to-uuid column; generate (false); on-invalid (null) generate fills an empty cell; on-invalid decides a non-UUID — every case kotlin script (required, classpath: only); context (map) the escape hatch — below

docs.title: Reference — row hooks
docs.text: Hook Params (default) One line map-columns rename (map old → new); drop (list) renames, then drops coalesce column; from (list of source columns) when the target is null/blank, the first non-blank source value defaults a map column: value fills every listed column that is null or blank validate-row required (list of columns) drops the row: SKIPPED + DLQ (ValidationFailed, raw payload); refused after split-row split-row by (column) + sep (,) — or explode (column holding a list) one row per part, the other columns copied aggregator emit-on-change; keep-first; merge groups consecutive rows — refused on csv-file runs

docs.title: Reference — dataset hooks
docs.text: Hook Params (default) One line require-headers columns (all must exist); any-of (at least one) fails the run: required header missing: <col> / none of required headers found: [...] skip-empty-rows — drops all-blank rows; counted in SKIPPED, no DLQ filter-where column; equals; in (list); regex (full match) keeps rows matching every criterion; null compares as ""; drops counted in SKIPPED, no DLQ sort-by columns (list); max-rows (100000) lexicographic sort within the chunk, nulls first; over the cap the run refuses enrich-context a map column: value; ${now} = the ingestion instant adds constant columns; existing values are not overwritten

docs.title: Kotlin escape hatch
docs.text:
When no built-in fits, a kotlin cell hook runs a .kts script over the whole row:

mapping:
  cell:
    - kotlin:
        script: classpath:hooks/samples/normalize-date.kts
        context: { defaultCountry: FR }    # optional; the script reads it as `context`

The script that ships with the platform, the one the full example runs:

// normalize-date.kts — a cell hook: rewrite legacy "DD/MM/YYYY" into ISO "YYYY-MM-DD".
// KotlinScriptHost injects 'bindings' with a mutable "cells" map (the current row's columns).
@Suppress("UNCHECKED_CAST")
val cells = bindings["cells"] as MutableMap<String, Any?>
val raw = cells["signup_date"] as? String
if (raw != null && Regex("""\d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4}""").matches(raw)) {
    val (d, m, y) = raw.split("/")
    cells["signup_date"] = "$y-$m-$d"
}
  • The script gets bindings["cells"] (the row, mutable) and bindings["context"] (the hook's context: values, read-only by convention). Changes to cells reach the hooks that follow and the table.
  • Full JVM trust — no sandbox, no timeout, no memory cap. A script failure fails the run.
  • classpath: refs only — the script ships on the hub's classpath; a file: path is refused (only classpath: scripts supported in v1).
  • Runnable example: docs/connectors/csv/50-kotlin-row-hook.yaml.

docs.title: REST: the transform: enum
docs.text:
REST/GraphQL/SOAP endpoints do not use spec.mapping. Their transformation point is the promote: block of a hybrid target — each promoted column takes an optional transform:

Value Effect from_epoch Unix epoch seconds → timestamp (UTC); for milliseconds, divide upstream parse_iso8601 ISO-8601 string → timestamp (UTC when the text carries no offset) to_lower / to_upper case conversion trim whitespace trim to_json_string serializes the extracted value to a JSON string

parse_iso8601 accepts these shapes:

Source text Stored instant 2008-04-18T00:00:00 2008-04-18T00:00:00Z — no offset means UTC 2008-04-18 00:00:00 2008-04-18T00:00:00Z — PostgreSQL's space separator 2008-04-18 2008-04-18T00:00:00Z — a date alone is midnight 2026-08-01T14:30:00+02:00 2026-08-01T12:30:00Z — an explicit offset is honoured

Anything else fails the run, naming the column and the transform. A view filter accepts the same shapes.

See the REST connector for the promote: block itself.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix rows missing, but the DLQ is empty filter-where or skip-empty-rows excluded them — counted in SKIPPED, not dead-lettered check SKIPPED in lm run get (or the TUI's :runs RECORDS in/out/skip); find the filtering hook in spec.mapping DEAD-LETTERS > 0 with reason MalformedSource the reader rejected the row (wrong column count, unclosed quote) before any hook ran lm dlq get <id> shows the raw line; fix the export or the parser: block run fails: unknown <tier> hook: <name> (lm validate passed) typo in a hook name, or the hook under the wrong tier check the reference tables above for the exact name and its tier single-file run Failed: a full refresh removes nothing while a row of the file is in the dead letters a dead letter this run, whatever its reason, while rows would be removed — e.g. a malformed row or a validate-row drop lm dlq list --run <id> names each reason; fix the cause each dead letter reports (lm dlq get <id>) and run again mapping block seems to have no effect applied via the one-shot lm csv ingest, which never runs spec.mapping apply a csv-file connector manifest and run it instead only classpath: scripts supported in v1 a kotlin hook's script: points at a file: path move the script under the platform classpath and reference it as classpath:... a parsed column is blank for some rows, but the row itself landed a cell hook could not read that value and wrote null check cell_errors: lm run get <id> (stderr alert when > 0, or -o json/-o yaml), or the TUI describe panel (:runs, select the run, d) a regex-extract column is null on every row the pattern never matched — a miss is not counted, the empty column is the signal test the pattern on a real value; remember the match is tried in full first, then as a find

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• CSV & files — the envelope spec.mapping lives in.
  • docs/connectors/csv/ in the repository — the runnable manifests, including the full example.

docs.title: Writing a JDBC provider
docs.text:
jdbc-generic reads one database per connector. The database it speaks is decided by a provider: a module that owns that database's SQL dialect and its JDBC driver. PostgreSQL ships with every edition, Oracle with lumnik Pro; any other database is one more provider.

This page is for a Java developer adding a database. Using an installed provider needs no code — see JDBC → Connection.

docs.title: What a provider is
docs.text:
• A Maven module io.lumnik:lumnik-jdbc-<db>, classes under the package io.lumnik.jdbc.<db>.
  • It depends on lumnik-jdbc-spi and on its own driver, even when the hub already carries it.
  • It exposes one CDI bean implementing JdbcDialect. The hub never imports a provider class; it collects every installed bean.

Two build details decide whether the hub sees the provider at all:

  • the module builds a jandex index (jandex-maven-plugin) — without it the hub boots with that dialect missing, and says nothing;
  • the hub depends on it with runtime scope.

Providers add up: several live in one image, and each connector picks its own.

docs.title: What each method owes
docs.text:
Method Contract id() The lowercase name used in dialect:. Unique across installed providers. aliases() Other accepted spellings (PostgreSQL: postgresql). Unique too. acceptsUrl(url) Whether this provider recognises the JDBC scheme. Used to infer a missing dialect:. driverClass() The driver the pool loads. A provider installed without its driver fails with JDBC driver 'X' of dialect 'Y' is not on the classpath. quoteIdentifier(id) Quote one identifier. The query builder never concatenates a raw name. keyComparison(columns, comparison) The > (cursor) or <= (run ceiling) comparison over the quoted key columns, and the bind plan. No default. limitClause(n) The row limit appended after ORDER BY (LIMIT 100, FETCH FIRST 100 ROWS ONLY, …). No default. defaultSkipPatterns() Table-name globs excluded from discovery when the request gives none. unsupportedReason(column) Why this provider cannot read a column, or empty. Discovery lists the table with the column named; the guided add refuses it. Default: every column is readable. readColumn(rs, index) The value of a cell. Default getObject; override for a LOB locator or a driver-specific timestamp class, and throw to refuse a type you cannot read. isWallClock(metadata, index) Whether the column holds a date and time written with no time zone, which the hub then reads in the connection's zone, UTC without one. Default: the column's JDBC type is TIMESTAMP. Override it when your driver reports a zoned type under that same code. sessionInitSql() A statement run on every new connection of this dialect's pool — for a database whose session settings (sort order, number format) change what a query means. Default: none. introspection listTables, tableExists, listColumns, listPrimaryKey, listForeignKeys, estimateRowCount, inferWatermarkColumn.

keyComparison and limitClause have no default so that a provider cannot compile while emitting SQL its database rejects, or reads differently.

docs.title: The bind plan
docs.text:
keyComparison returns a KeyComparison(sql, parameterIndexes). The i-th ? of the SQL takes the value of key column parameterIndexes[i].

Dialect SQL for (a, b) > cursor Plan PostgreSQL (row value) ("a", "b") > (?, ?) [0, 1] a database without tuple comparison (("a" > ?) OR ("a" = ? AND "b" > ?)) [0, 0, 1]
  • The SQL is one self-contained, parenthesised predicate: the builder joins it with AND, and for a watermark ceiling with OR <watermark> IS NULL.
  • The builder refuses a plan that is empty for a non-empty key, or that names a column that does not exist.

docs.title: How a connector picks its provider
docs.text:
Manifest Result dialect: names an installed provider, URL accepted that provider dialect: names a provider that is not installed refused: JDBC dialect 'X' is not installed. Available: … dialect: set, URL not accepted by it refused, naming the dialect and the URL scheme dialect: absent, exactly one provider accepts the URL that provider dialect: absent, none accepts it refused, listing the installed providers dialect: absent, several accept it refused as ambiguous
  • Names are compared trimmed and lowercased.
  • Two providers claiming the same id or alias stop the hub at startup, naming both.
  • A connection pool is kept per URL, user, tenant, driver and dialect: two providers that accept the same URL never share one.

docs.title: The demo broker
docs.text:
One Redpanda in a container and one Python file that fills it with eleven topics over the same 2 400 fictional ACME partners the REST demo API serves — the source every screen of the Kafka page reads.

It ships with the repo. Two commands start and fill it:

docker compose -f docs/connectors/kafka/demo/docker-compose.yml up -d
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py

  ▸ created acme.partners
  ▸ created acme.orders
  ▸ created acme.partners-drift
  ▸ created acme.partners-poison
  ▸ created acme.partners-compacted
  ▸ created acme.partners-reserved
  ▸ created acme.partners-raw
  ▸ created acme.partners-trimmed
  ▸ created acme.empty
  ▸ created acme.live
  ✓ filled
  ✓ eleven topics as declared (acme.absent is absent)

The script needs the Kafka client for Python: python3 -m pip install confluent-kafka.

docs.title: The eleven topics
docs.text:
A partner has the same name and city here and on the REST demo. Each topic serves one section of the Kafka page:

Topic Shape Used by acme.partners 2 400 JSON objects, one partition Quickstart acme.orders 24 000 orders, keyed by partner over six partitions Partitions and the cursor acme.partners-drift 2 400, and two new fields appear at message 1 201 Schema evolution acme.partners-poison 1 000, of which 143 are not a JSON object Poison messages acme.partners-compacted cleanup.policy=compact; 1 000 rows then 300 tombstones Tombstones acme.partners-reserved 500, each carrying a top-level id — the REST record verbatim Seven reserved names acme.partners-raw 500 with Partner Name, credit.limit, MONTANT_€, an object and an array Names the producer chose acme.partners-trimmed 5 000, and trim moves its log start on demand A log that moved under the cursor acme.empty created, zero messages An empty poll acme.live empty until feed writes to it while a run reads The head is the target acme.absent never created A topic that does not exist

The poison is placed deterministically (every index where i % 7 == 3: a truncated object, a JSON array, a JSON scalar), so every fill gives the same counts.

docs.title: The three gestures that change the broker
docs.text:
These three write to the broker; the Kafka page says when to use each:

python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py feed --rate 200 --seconds 30     # a producer racing the run, on acme.live
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py feed --topic acme.partners-trimmed --rate 500 --seconds 2
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py trim 5500                        # acme.partners-trimmed: offsets 0..5499 are gone

trim moves the partition's log start at once, as retention would over days. It runs rpk in the container lumnik-demo-redpanda; set KAFKA_DEMO_CONTAINER to use another one.

docs.title: Checking it before you blame the manifest
docs.text:
python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py verify

It checks every topic's count and partitions, and that acme.absent does not exist. After trim, or feed --topic acme.partners-trimmed, verify reports acme.partners-trimmed: expected. reset drops the topics and fills them again:

python3 docs/connectors/kafka/demo/acme-topics.py reset

Reset the hub's cursors too. With the old cursor, a run on a refilled topic reads nothing and completes. After reset, for each connector to read from the start:

lm endpoint reset-cursor <connector>/default

host.docker.internal:29092, not localhost:19092

  • Your shell (and acme-topics.py) reaches the broker at localhost:19092.
  • The hub, in its container, reaches it at host.docker.internal:29092 — what the manifests carry. The wrong listener ends in the broker timeout after about 60 s.

Check both:

docker exec lumnik-demo-redpanda rpk cluster info --brokers localhost:9092
docker exec lumnik-hub-1 bash -c 'exec 3<>/dev/tcp/host.docker.internal/29092 && echo REACHABLE'

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
• Automatic topic creation is off, so acme.absent stays absent.
  • Authenticates nobody. Every topic is plaintext. The sasl-plain manifest on the Kafka page shows its refusals, not a successful handshake.
  • A throwaway rig. One node, no replication, no persistence to count on.

docs.title: The demo API
docs.text:
One Python file, no dependencies, 2 400 fictional ACME partners served under ten path dialects, a GraphQL endpoint and eight SOAP services — the source every screen of the REST, GraphQL and SOAP pages reads.

It ships with the repo. Start it in a terminal of its own and leave it running:

python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/acme-api.py

ACME Partners API on http://0.0.0.0:8099 — 2400 partners, dialects: down, drf, flaky, hdr, liar, link, offset, open, spring, v1 + POST /graphql
SOAP services (POST /<service>/start.swe): fault, fault200, flaky, mute, sap, session, siebel, tail

It logs one line per request on stdout: the query string a pagination strategy composed, the watermark a run sent.

docs.title: The ten dialects
docs.text:
The first path segment picks the envelope; the data is the same under every dialect.

Path What it imitates Used by /spring/partners Spring Data Page — $.content + $.totalPages Quickstart /v1/partners Stripe-style opaque cursor — ?starting_after= Pagination /drf/partners Django REST — $.results + a whole next URL in $.next Pagination /link/partners an RFC 5988 Link: …; rel="next" header Pagination /offset/partners offset + limit with a published $.total Incremental sync /open/partners the same, with no auth wall at all auth: none /hdr/partners 400 to any request without X-Api-Version Request headers /liar/partners serves 2 300 rows while declaring 2 400 The declared total /down/partners 500, forever When the source misbehaves /flaky/partners 429 then 503 before each page, then 200 When the source misbehaves POST /graphql Relay edges / pageInfo GraphQL

docs.title: The eight SOAP services
docs.text:
One POST path per service; the operation and the row offset are in the XML body. Same partners, in XML, with ns: prefixes on every payload element.

Path What it imitates Used by POST /siebel/start.swe Siebel QueryPage — LastPage, and a SOAPAction it checks Quickstart POST /sap/start.swe SAP PI — a MoreRecords flag instead Where the loop stops POST /mute/start.swe a service that announces nothing at all Where the loop stops POST /tail/start.swe 201 rows, so the last page holds one element Where the loop stops POST /fault/start.swe <soap:Fault> on HTTP 500 A Fault fails the run POST /fault200/start.swe the same Fault on HTTP 200 A Fault fails the run POST /flaky/start.swe two 500s without a Fault, then the page The same 500, retried POST /session/start.swe 401 unless a token rides in <soap:Header> A credential inside the envelope

/tail ends on a page holding a single element: a correct run ingests 201 rows, not 200.

docs.title: Its three credentials
docs.text:
Put them in the hub's secret registry; the manifests name them:

lm secret set ACME_BASIC_PW        # demo-pass   — /spring, /offset, /hdr, /liar, /down, /flaky and every SOAP service
lm secret set ACME_BEARER_TOKEN    # demo-token  — /v1 and /drf
lm secret set ACME_API_KEY         # demo-key    — /link and /graphql
lm secret set ACME_SESSION_TOKEN   # demo-session-42 — /session, inside the SOAP envelope

host.docker.internal, not localhost

The manifests point at http://host.docker.internal:8099. The hub runs in a container, and localhost inside it is that container — the address above is how it reaches your machine. The demo API listens on every interface for the same reason; pass it an address (acme-api.py 8099 127.0.0.1) to keep it to your own shell.

docs.title: Checking it before you blame the manifest
docs.text:
python3 docs/connectors/rest/demo/selftest.py

It walks every dialect and SOAP service to its last page and checks that the 2 400 ids arrive exactly once, /flaky answers 429, 503, 200, /tail yields 201 rows and both fault services carry a <soap:Fault>. It exits non-zero when something is off.

Reset the flaky counters between retry tests

/flaky fails twice per query string, then serves that page for good: a second run retries nothing. curl http://127.0.0.1:8099/admin/reset puts it back.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text:
• Not a GraphQL or SOAP engine. It answers fixed shapes; what is under test is the connector.
  • A throwaway rig. /open/ has no auth wall, and the credentials are fixed test values: run it on loopback or a developer machine only.

docs.title: The manifests that read it
docs.text:
Fourteen manifests live beside it, each transcluded into the page that explains it:

File Reads Page 10-quickstart.yaml /spring Quickstart 20-two-endpoints.yaml /v1 + /drf One connector, one API 30-link-header.yaml /link Pagination 40-watermark.yaml /offset Incremental sync 50-total-witness.yaml /liar + /hdr The declared total 60-source-down.yaml /down + /flaky When the source misbehaves 70-graphql-relay.yaml POST /graphql GraphQL 80-graphql-errors.yaml POST /graphql GraphQL 90-soap-querypage.yaml /siebel SOAP 91-soap-stop-signals.yaml /sap + /mute + /tail Where the loop stops 92-soap-fault.yaml /fault + /fault200 A Fault fails the run 93-soap-retry.yaml /flaky The same 500, retried 94-soap-session.yaml /session A credential inside the envelope 95-soap-watermark.yaml /siebel Incremental

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• REST — the connector these manifests drive
  • Pagination
  • GraphQL
  • SOAP

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
How an endpoint asks for the next page. Most APIs follow a convention that already has a name — declare the preset. When none fits, six strategies are written out by hand.

This page serves REST and GraphQL: both are the same engine, and relay is what a GraphQL endpoint declares.

docs.title: Presets
docs.text:
Declare the preset; it is expanded at apply time into the real strategy:

Preset For Expands to spring-page Spring Data Page page ($.content, $.totalPages, 0-indexed) spring-slice Spring Data Slice (no total) page + last_path: $.last spring-hateoas Spring Data REST body-link ($._links.next.href, $._embedded.{items} — needs items) micronaut Micronaut Data Page page ($.content, $.totalPages) drf-page Django REST PageNumberPagination body-link ($.next, $.results) drf-limit-offset Django REST LimitOffsetPagination offset ($.count, $.results) fastapi fastapi-pagination page ($.items, $.pages, 1-indexed) nestjs nestjs-paginate body-link ($.links.next, $.data) json-api JSON:API body-link ($.links.next, $.data) sequelize Node/Sequelize offset ($.count, $.rows) stripe Stripe-style cursor cursor ($.has_more, $.data) 
pagination: { kind: spring-page }                       # 7 lines → 1
pagination: { kind: spring-page, size: 500 }            # override any expanded field
pagination: { kind: spring-hateoas, items: products }   # {items} → $._embedded.products

nestjs and json-api expand identically. Only spring-hateoas requires an override: items fills its $._embedded.{items} placeholder.

docs.title: Strategies
docs.text:
When no preset fits, write the strategy out:

Strategy Use for Required fields Optional fields (default) cursor Stripe, OpenAI, most modern APIs cursor_param, cursor_path, has_more_path, response_path cursor_binding (query), total_path page Spring, Laravel, anything with page numbers page_param, response_path size_param, size (50), start_page (1), total_pages_path, total_path, has_more_path, last_path, empty_check (true) offset legacy REST offset_param, limit_param, response_path limit (100), total_path link-header GitHub response_path rel (next), total_path body-link Django REST, JSON:API, NestJS, HATEOAS link_path, response_path total_path relay GraphQL Connections cursor_path, has_more_path, response_path; plus cursor_param or cursor_var cursor_binding (query), total_path custom — — refused — see below

page stops on whichever of total_pages_path / has_more_path / last_path is present — and, with empty_check: true (the default), on the first empty page.

total_path is accepted by every strategy; it also checks the run's row count — see The declared total.

kind: custom is refused

lm validate and lm apply stop on it with custom pagination is not supported; use page, offset, cursor, link-header or body-link. A connector applied before that check still meets the same sentence in its run. Use one of the six strategies above.

Page size is a knob on page and offset only

cursor, body-link and link-header send no size parameter: the server's default page size governs the run.

To ask for a larger page, put it in path:, as 20-two-endpoints.yaml does with path: /drf/partners?page_size=500. relay takes its size from first: in the query.

The link-header strategy written out, with an API key — the next page is in an RFC 5988 Link header:

# 30-link-header.yaml — the next page is in a HEADER, and the credential is an API key.
#
# RFC 5988: the response body says nothing about paging; `Link: <url>; rel="next"` does. The
# strategy follows that URL until the header stops carrying a `next` relation. `rel` defaults
# to next and is spelled out here for readability; `response_path` is what unwraps the rows.
#
# Where the key goes is declarative — `in: header` + `name:`. Use `in: query` and the key rides
# the query string instead, which is what APIs that pre-date bearer tokens tend to want.
#
#   lm secret set ACME_API_KEY        # the demo API answers to demo-key
#
# Expect: 2 400 rows in ext.acme_header_partners.

apiVersion: connectors.lumnik.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: acme-header
  connector_type: rest-generic
  scopes: [billing]

spec:
  base_url: http://host.docker.internal:8099

  auth:
    kind: api-key
    in: header
    name: X-API-Key
    value_env: ACME_API_KEY   # ApiKeyAuthProviderFactory has NO inline value field

  endpoints:
    - id: partners
      path: /link/partners?limit=500
      method: GET
      pagination:
        kind: link-header
        rel: next
        response_path: "$.data"
      target:
        kind: hybrid
        table: ext.acme_header_partners
        unique_key: "$.id"
        promote:
          - { name: name, path: "$.name", type: text }

$ lm run list --connector acme-header
ID        CONNECTOR    ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN    OUT   SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
539d998f  acme-header  partners  Completed  2400  2400  0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40

docs.title: Cursor binding
docs.text:
For cursor and relay, cursor_binding picks where the next-page cursor is injected:

Binding Cursor goes into Needs query (default) a query parameter cursor_param header an HTTP header cursor_param (the header name) variable the POST body's variables.<name> cursor_var — relay on a graphql endpoint only

Both halves of that last rule are refused at apply:

$ lm apply -f bad-binding.yaml
✗ bad-binding.yaml — 2 error(s), 0 warning(s)

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].pagination.cursor_binding
          cursor_binding=variable is only valid for graphql endpoints; non-graphql endpoints use cursor_binding=query|header

  ERROR    spec.endpoints[0].pagination.cursor_binding
          cursor_binding=variable is only valid for pagination.kind=relay; cursor pagination uses cursor_binding=query|header

Fix errors above before running 'lm apply -f bad-binding.yaml'.
Error: validation failed: 2 error(s)

Both errors must be fixed.

A pure GraphQL API (POST a query, cursor in variables): see GraphQL.

docs.text:

docs.title: WOW demo — one Customer, fused from two legacy systems, alive over REST
docs.text:
Take Customer, fuse it from two legacy sources — a SOAP/Siebel CRM and a nightly CSV export — and serve one Customer, conflicts kept, over REST. One manifest over the live hub; no ETL job, no warehouse.

You have no Siebel at hand, so this folder ships fake-siebel.py (Python standard library only), which answers the CustomerQueryPage SOAP call. Everything else is real lumnik.

┌─ fake-siebel.py  (SOAP QueryPage) ─→ siebel-customers ─→ connector.cust_siebel ┐
│                                                                                 ├─→ Customer entity
└─ customer.csv    (flat-file export) ─→ cust-csv ────────→ connector.t_cust_csv ──┘   (fuse on customer_code)
                                                                                              │
                                                                                              ▼
                                                        lm entity get customer  →  fused rows + _conflicts

docs.title: What's in this folder
docs.text: File Role fake-siebel.py Stand-in Siebel — answers a CustomerQueryPage SOAP call. customer.csv The second source: a flat-file customer export. siebel-connector.yaml rest-generic connector with a kind: soap endpoint → lands connector.cust_siebel. csv-connector.yaml csv-file connector → lands connector.t_cust_csv. customer-entity.yaml The kind: Entity manifest — fuses both on customer_code. clients-view.yaml kind: View — a list over the fused Customer. lyon-process.yaml kind: Process — emits a decision when a Lyon customer lands (Act 2). fake-n8n.py Stand-in webhook receiver for Act 2. commandes.csv Act 3's source: commandes with dirty statuses, EN LITIGE undeclared. commandes-connector.yaml csv-file connector → lands connector.t_commandes_csv (Act 3). commande-workflow.yaml kind: Workflow — the declared commande lifecycle (Act 3). docker-compose.wow.yml Overlay for the self-host stack: mounts this folder at /demo, adds host.docker.internal.

docs.title: Replay it by hand (on the self-host stack)
docs.text:
On the stack deploy/selfhost/up.sh brings up. Run every command from the repo root. On Windows, run them in the Ubuntu window (Deploy on Windows), or spell lm as .\lm.exe in PowerShell.

Three prerequisites — run each ✔ check: a missing one fails silently later.

  • The stack, with the demo folder mounted: 

    ./deploy/selfhost/up.sh --build
docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml \
               -f docs/demo/wow-customer/docker-compose.wow.yml up -d hub
# wait until the restarted hub is healthy — an early lm call answers 401
until [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Health.Status}}' \
      "$(docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml ps -q hub)")" = healthy ]; do sleep 3; done

    • ✔ Check the mount: docker compose -f docker-compose.selfhost.yml exec hub ls /demo lists customer.csv. Without it the CSV run reports Completed with 0 rows.
    • A later up.sh run removes the overlay: run the up -d hub line again after it.
    • The ask step (Pro) also needs Ollama and its models: Prerequisites.

  • The fake Siebel, on the host, left running: python3 docs/demo/wow-customer/fake-siebel.py ("address already in use" means it is already up). ✔ Check it answers: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8077/eai | head -c 60 prints <soap:Envelope xmlns:soap=…. Without it the Siebel run fails.

  • lm on your PATH — Install lm.

Log in. The demo user integrator (tenant 1) gets a per-install password from up.sh, written to .env as INTEGRATOR_PASSWORD. Change it for anything real.

lm config set-context selfhost --server http://localhost:8080 \
    --oidc-issuer http://localhost:8180/realms/lumnik
lm config use-context selfhost
lm login        # open the URL it prints, sign in as integrator

docs.title: 1. Land both sources
docs.text:
lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/siebel-connector.yaml
lm connector run siebel-customers
lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/csv-connector.yaml
lm connector run cust-csv

$ lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/siebel-connector.yaml
{"name":"siebel-customers","connectorId":"eab3cb2e-0b84-4b78-b805-6027b36d3c2c","endpointsApplied":1}
$ lm connector run siebel-customers
run scheduled: 4197d406-fdf1-4904-a9a6-e435ef1f57ef

✔ Checkpoint — "run scheduled" is not "run succeeded". Both runs must read Completed:

$ lm run list
ID        CONNECTOR         ENDPOINT   STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
9ef96149  cust-csv          default    Completed  8   8    0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
4197d406  siebel-customers  customers  Completed  2   2    0        0             2026-10-19 01:38  2026-10-19 01:38
You see Fix siebel-customers Failed the fake Siebel is not running cust-csv Completed with 0 / 0 the /demo mount is missing — fix it, re-run the connector

docs.title: 2. Fuse them
docs.text:
Only once both runs above landed their rows:

$ lm entity apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/customer-entity.yaml
Applied entity "Customer" → connector."v_customer"

An error naming a relation that "does not exist" means a run above did not land.

docs.title: 3. Read the fused Customer
docs.text:
$ lm entity get customer
CUSTOMER_CODE  NAME              SEGMENT  EMAIL           CITY   _CONFLICTS
C-100          Jean Dupont       GOLD     jd@x.fr         Paris  {}
C-200          Marie             SILVER   m@x.fr          Lyon   {"name": [{"src": "cust_siebel", "value": "Marie"}, {"src": "t_cust_csv", "value": "MARIE A."}]}
C-300          Solo                       solo@x.fr       Nice   {}
C-500          Claire Martin              claire@x.fr     Lyon   {}
C-600          Pierre Corneille           corneille@x.fr  Paris  {}
C-700          Maurice Druon              druon@x.fr      Paris  {}
C-800          Albert Camus               camus@x.fr      Lyon   {}
C-900          Saint Exupery              exupery@x.fr    Lyon   {}
  • C-100 — both systems agree on the name; email and city come from the CSV.
  • C-200 — the systems disagree on the name (Siebel Marie, CSV MARIE A.). Siebel is listed first in the manifest, so its value is shown; both are kept in _conflicts.
  • C-300 and the others — only in the CSV. Fused, no conflict, no segment.

lm entity get customer -o json prints the same rows as JSON. Each tenant sees only its own customers.

docs.title: 4. Ask it (Pro)
docs.text:
The entity declares scopes: [clients], so applying it makes the fused Customer askable in that scope:

lm ask --scope clients "combien de clients à Lyon ?"
# → the answer, computed over the fused Customer, with the SQL that ran

docs.title: It refuses an unknown value
docs.text:
customer-entity.yaml declares segment.values: [GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE]. A question about any other value is refused before anything runs — never answered with "0":

lm ask --scope clients "combien de clients Platinum ?"     # Pro
# → I won't run this: 'PLATINUM' is not a declared value of segment (known: GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE).
#   If it should exist, add it to the entity manifest.

A view filter on the same value is refused the same way, on every edition:

$ lm view -f docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml --filter segment=PLATINUM
Error: API error 400: 'PLATINUM' is not an allowed value for segment (allowed: GOLD, SILVER, BRONZE)

If PLATINUM is real, declare it in the entity manifest.

docs.title: See it — the first app surface (kind:View)
docs.text:
clients-view.yaml declares a read-only list over the fused Customer (reference):

$ lm view -f docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml --filter city=Lyon
Clients · city=Lyon

Code client  Nom            Ville  Segment
C-200        Marie          Lyon   SILVER
C-500        Claire Martin  Lyon   
C-800        Albert Camus   Lyon   
C-900        Saint Exupery  Lyon   
$ lm view C-200 -f docs/demo/wow-customer/clients-view.yaml
Clients / C-200

  Code client   C-200
  Nom           Marie
  Ville         Lyon
  Segment       SILVER

  (!) Ambiguïtés et divergences
  Nom   cust_siebel «Marie» · t_cust_csv «MARIE A.»
  • A bad filter is refused with the reason: an unknown column, a malformed comparison, a value out of the declared domain.
  • Thresholds: --filter "montant>1000", --filter "echeance<2026-08-01" (> < >= <=; a number or an ISO date). Quote the filter — an unquoted > is a shell redirect.

Let the AI write the view (Pro, reference):

lm view generate clients "les clients gold avec leur ville et segment" -o gold.yaml
cat gold.yaml        # the first line is the render command: lm view -f gold.yaml --filter 'segment=GOLD'
lm view generate clients "les commandes du mois de mars"
# → generation abstained: no order data in this scope

On a hub without a chat model, lm view generate answers:

Error: API error 400: generation abstained: no chat model is available on this hub — view generation needs one

docs.title: Act 2 — the process (kind:Process, notify)
docs.text:
A declared rule watches the CSV and emits a decision when a new customer from Lyon arrives.

Why ville and scope demo. A process watches the raw ingest table, connector.t_cust_csv, whose columns are the CSV's own (code, cname, email, ville). That table is in the demo scope (the CSV connector's tag), so the process declares scope: demo. A process whose on.table is not in its scope is refused at apply, with the reason.

# a fake n8n on the host, left running — prints every delivery it receives
python3 docs/demo/wow-customer/fake-n8n.py

# subscribe it to decision.* (the secret is required; fake-n8n does not check it)
echo -n "demo-secret" | lm integration add fake-n8n \
    --url http://host.docker.internal:9099/hook --events 'decision.*' --secret-stdin

lm process apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/lyon-process.yaml
lm process list

$ lm process apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/lyon-process.yaml
{"name":"lyon-client-arrive","table":"connector.t_cust_csv","emit":"decision.lyon-client-arrive"}
$ lm process list
NAME                TABLE                 EMIT                         ENABLED
lyon-client-arrive  connector.t_cust_csv  decision.lyon-client-arrive  true

A process fires only on a new row. Add a Lyon customer with a code the file does not carry (the file ships C-100 to C-900 without C-400, which the WOW uses), then re-run:

echo 'C-1000,Colette Vidal,colette@x.fr,Lyon' >> docs/demo/wow-customer/customer.csv
lm connector run cust-csv

About ten seconds later, fake-n8n prints the decision (entity_key shortened):

[fake-n8n] POST /hook received:
{
  "entity": "connector.t_cust_csv",
  "fields": {
    "cname": "Colette Vidal",
    "ville": "Lyon"
  },
  "message": "Nouveau client Colette Vidal à Lyon",
  "process": "lyon-client-arrive",
  "entity_key": "23a25a92a997…"
}

fields carries the columns the message names, so n8n reads values instead of parsing text.

The same decision waits in the inbox (here next to the WOW's C-400). Acking it is itself an event (annotation.decision.acked), which a webhook subscribed to annotation.* receives:

$ lm inbox
ID  WHEN      PROCESS             MESSAGE                              ENTITY_KEY
12  just now  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Colette Vidal à Lyon  23a25a92a99755a85b5b050f9c3d510d48769ce9aa22141fe4a3ff9db0a0a004
8   just now  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Camille Roux à Lyon   ff1027320a1acbe2646ce1b2d1e4a42111868a75bb30825dc4609d785e6aaa7f
$ lm inbox ack 12
acked.
$ lm inbox ack 12
acked.
$ lm inbox --all
ID  WHEN      PROCESS             MESSAGE                                      ENTITY_KEY
12  just now  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Colette Vidal à Lyon [acked]  23a25a92a99755a85b5b050f9c3d510d48769ce9aa22141fe4a3ff9db0a0a004
8   just now  lyon-client-arrive  Nouveau client Camille Roux à Lyon           ff1027320a1acbe2646ce1b2d1e4a42111868a75bb30825dc4609d785e6aaa7f
  • lm inbox shows what still needs you; lm inbox --all shows everything, treated ones marked [acked].
  • Acking twice records one ack.
  • Decisions and acks are kept 30 days (LUMNIK_EVENTS_RETENTION_DAYS).

docs.title: Act 3 — the lifecycle (kind:Workflow)
docs.text:
commandes.csv carries dirty statuses: En cours, fini, TERMINE (trailing space), BROUILLON, encours — and twice EN LITIGE, which nobody declared. commande-workflow.yaml declares three states, two transitions, provenance: declared.

lm apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/commandes-connector.yaml
lm connector run commandes-csv
lm workflow apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/commande-workflow.yaml

$ lm run list --connector commandes-csv
ID        CONNECTOR      ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
2af6db4c  commandes-csv  default   Completed  7   7    0        0             2026-10-19 01:40  2026-10-19 01:40
$ lm workflow apply -f docs/demo/wow-customer/commande-workflow.yaml
{"name":"commande-lifecycle","scope":"demo","table":"connector.t_commandes_csv","column":"statut","dataTruth":{"undeclared":[{"value":"EN LITIGE","rows":2}],"unobserved":[],"nullOrBlank":0,"tableMissing":false,"keyColumnMissing":false,"keyNullOrBlank":0,"checkUnavailable":false,"unavailableReason":null}}
Field Here Means undeclared EN LITIGE, 2 rows a value in the column that no state declares — reported, not refused unobserved empty every declared state was seen at least once

The manifest also declares on.key: num and dormancy.after: 30d: a commande left unmoved in a non-terminal state for 30 days — counted from lumnik's first observation — raises an alert in lm inbox, under workflow:commande-lifecycle. Wording and rules: Dormancy.

On Pro, the chat answers lifecycle questions from the declared graph:

lm ask --scope demo "pourquoi je ne peux pas clôturer la commande CMD-001 ?"

Captured with llama3.2, abridged:

« D'après le workflow, il est possible que la commande CMD-001 soit en cours de traitement (EN_COURS) et qu'elle nécessite encore certaines étapes pour être clôturée. Vous pouvez vérifier son statut actuel en consultant la table connector.t_commandes_csv. Vous pouvez également vérifier si les transitions autorisées sont correctement configurées entre les états BROUILLON, EN_COURS et TERMINE. »

The workflow carries the lifecycle, not the rows: the model answers from the declared states and transitions, and points at the table for CMD-001's actual status instead of guessing it. The wording changes from run to run; the states and transitions it cites must match commande-workflow.yaml.

docs.title: Backup & Restore (self-host)
docs.text:
A hot pg_dump for PostgreSQL and a briefly-stopped copy for Keycloak. A restore drops and recreates the database. .env is not covered.

The self-host stack holds customer data in two stores:

Store Contents Backup method PostgreSQL (selfhost_pg volume) ALL hub data: ingested tables, RAG chunks, saved views, identities, audit hot pg_dump -Fc — no downtime Keycloak dev-file H2 (selfhost_kc volume) realm changes made at runtime: users created by hand, password hashes cold copy — Keycloak stops ~15 s

During the Keycloak stop, new logins fail; issued tokens keep working.

docs.title: Take a backup
docs.text:
deploy/selfhost/backup.sh              # keeps the newest 7
deploy/selfhost/backup.sh --keep 30
deploy/selfhost/backup.sh --no-keycloak
