  • Offboarding the integrator · GDPR & personal data

docs.title: Ask honesty — the five guards
docs.text:
Which builds can run this

The guards run in every edition. Asking needs the rag and llm modules: an Open build lists only core and identity in lm module list, and a hub with the AI switched off lists rag and llm as INACTIVE.

When you ask your data an analytic question, lumnik translates it to SQL and runs it read-only over the hub. lm ask, the TUI's :ask and the PWA chat all go through the same guards. Semantic chat (lm chat) cites ingested chunks and generates no SQL, so the guards do not apply there.

The guards enforce one principle — the asymmetry of harm:

A refusal costs you a retry. A confident wrong answer — especially a confident "there are none" when there are some — costs you a business decision. lumnik always prefers the refusal.

Every refusal below is deterministic (no model judges the veto), and each message says what to do next. In the quoted messages, <bracketed> parts and … stand for your actual value, column, table and lists.

docs.title: The pipeline, in order
docs.text:
Seven stages: abstention counts once though it stands at two points, and SQL safety sits beneath the guards.

flowchart TB
  q(["your question"]) --> g1
  g1["1 · abstention floor"] --> gen["SQL generation"]
  gen --> g2["2 · abstention exit"]
  g2 --> g3["3 · SQL safety"]
  g3 --> g4["4 · leak guard"]
  g4 --> g5["5 · undocumented-column guard"]
  g5 --> g6["6 · domain guard"]
  g6 --> exec["read-only execution"]
  exec --> g7["7 · zero-row honesty"]
  g7 --> ans(["the answer — always with the SQL that ran"])
  g1 -.-> ref(["honest refusal,<br/>with what to do next"])
  g2 -.-> ref
  g3 -.-> ref
  g4 -.-> ref
  g5 -.-> ref
  g6 -.-> ref

Stages 1–6 each eject to a refusal when they trigger. Stage 7 never refuses — an empty result is delivered with a caveat, never phrased as a confident "there are none".

docs.title: 1. Abstention floor — nothing declared yet
docs.text:
Trigger: the scope has no schema at all (no tables, or tables without columns).

I have no data declared for this scope yet, so I can't answer that. Ingest a source for this scope first.

Do next: apply a connector with metadata.scopes: [<your-scope>] and run it.

A stored schema card that cannot be read is refused the same way:

The stored schema card for scope '<scope>' cannot be read (…) — re-run discovery, or apply the entity again, to replace it.

docs.title: 2. Abstention exit — the model's honest "I can't"
docs.text:
Trigger: the SQL-generation model concludes the question doesn't map to the declared schema and emits its sentinel (NO_ANSWER) instead of guessing a query.

Before refusing, the hub asks the model once to rewrite the question as one complete sentence, and tries again. This is what lets a terse lookup such as status SO-000004 through. The answer is still phrased for the question as you typed it.

I can't answer that from the data available for this scope — the question doesn't map to the declared schema.

Do next: rephrase using the columns the scope actually declares (lm view shows them), or ingest/declare the missing data.

Two questions abstain because the analytic door cannot read what answers them. The refusal adds a sentence saying where the answer is:

Question The refusal adds Where you go next "why can't this document move on?" this scope does declare a kind: Workflow lifecycle lm chat (semantic chat reads the lifecycle) "where do the ERP and the CRM disagree?" the disagreement is recorded on each fused record lm conflicts list, or the record's detail view in the PWA
  • The sentence appears only when the question is about a disagreement or a lifecycle (stages, a transition, a blocked document; in French or English). A plain status lookup does not get it.
  • lm ask then prints a try: line naming lm chat or lm conflicts list.

Sometimes the abstention fires before a more specific guard

Ask about a value outside a declared domain (a segment that doesn't exist) and the model may abstain before the domain guard names the mismatch. Re-ask with a declared value to see the specific hint.

docs.title: 3. SQL safety — read-only, bounded
docs.text:
Trigger: the generated SQL is anything but one clean read: not a single SELECT/WITH statement, multiple statements, or a banned token (DML/DDL keywords, pg_sleep, pg_catalog, information_schema, dblink, …).

I couldn't translate that into a safe query.

Accepted queries are capped with LIMIT 500 (a larger LIMIT is lowered) and run read-only. Every table must be schema-qualified (connector.v_acmecustomer).

docs.title: 4. Leak guard — the métier boundary
docs.text:
Trigger: the query reads a table that is not declared in this scope's card — the scope boundary within a tenant. A scope-bound user asking a scope they do not hold gets 403 scope not granted before any SQL is generated.

I won't run this: '<schema.table>' is not a table in this scope (declared: …). The query may not read data outside this métier's declared scope.

Do next: switch to the scope that owns the table (lm scopes), or add this scope to the connector's metadata.scopes and re-run it.

docs.title: 5. Undocumented-column guard
docs.text:
Trigger: the query filters a column that is declared in no table of the scope — an invented column, or an internal one (tenant_id, _row_hash) the chat was never meant to reason over.

I won't run this: '<column>' is not a declared column of this scope (known: …). If it should exist, add it to the entity manifest.

(The "known" list is capped at 12 names to keep the message readable.)

docs.title: 6. Domain guard — the declared-values contract
docs.text:
Trigger: the query filters a column on a literal that is not in that column's declared values: list (entity manifest). Without it, the query would return 0 rows for the wrong reason.

I won't run this: '<value>' is not a declared value of <column> (known: …). If it should exist, add it to the entity manifest.

Do next: if the value is legitimate, add it to the entity manifest's declared values and re-apply; if it was a typo, re-ask with a declared value.

docs.title: 7. Zero-row honesty — never a confident negative
docs.text:
Trigger: the query ran fine and returned 0 rows.

The query returned no rows. That can mean there are genuinely none, or that the query did not capture your question — verify the SQL before reporting that there are none.

The SQL that ran is always shown with the answer (lm ask prints it; the TUI yanks it with y).

Two more answers come from the query run itself, not from a guard:

  • A filter matches more than one row — e.g. a customer name that isn't unique:

That filter matches <N> rows, so the question has no single answer. Matching <column>: <id-1>, <id-2>, …. Ask again naming one of them — for example by filtering on <column> instead of the name.

<N> may read "at least <N>". The list stops at 10 values, then ", and <k> more".

  • Any other read failure (a syntax error, a permission or timeout issue):

I couldn't run that query — the database refused it: <reason> The SQL is below; if it looks wrong for this scope, re-run discovery.

<reason> is the database's first line for SQLSTATE classes 21, 42, 53, 54 and 57. Any other class reads SQLSTATE <code> (the message is withheld — that class can carry stored values; the server log has it).

docs.title: A long result — what the answer is written from
docs.text:
A question can match hundreds of rows. The answer is written from the first rows only (about fifty catalogue rows), and its first sentence says so — a sentence the hub writes, not the model:

$ lm ask --scope pwa-chat "Give me the references and descriptions of the items whose description does not contain Badu"
The answer summarises the first 48 of the 312 rows returned.
312 references do not mention Badu in their description; they are pumps and pool accessories.
  data as of: 2026-10-14T17:21:04Z (last completed run)

…
  312 rows returned

  SQL: SELECT "reference", "description" FROM "connector"."v_pwachatproduct" WHERE "description" NOT ILIKE '%Badu%'
LIMIT 500
  • Nothing is lost. lm ask prints every row (cut at … above), then the count and the SQL; lm ask -o json gives the whole result (see both). The PWA chat shows the answer and the SQL, not the rows.
  • The summary does not count for you. For an exact figure, ask for it: "how many items do not contain Badu?" is answered by a query.
  • A result cut at its limit says so. A query returns at most 500 rows; when it stops there, or at a smaller LIMIT of its own, the answer ends with a line:
$ lm ask --scope pwa-chat "List all the items"
The answer summarises the first 48 of at least 500 rows.
The catalogue holds pumps, filters, covers and chemical products.

The SQL query stops at 500 rows: there may be more.
  • The figures are still checked against the rows (see below); the hub's own sentences are not.
  • If the answer could not be written (the model was too slow, or failed), you get the rows and the SQL, and abstained: true. Ask again, or narrow the question.

Tune the size of the sample with LUMNIK_ASK_ANSWER_BUDGET_CHARS (default 6000; see models).

docs.title: Unbacked figures — the phrased answer checked against its rows
docs.text:
Every standalone number in the model's sentence must be backed by the rows: the row count, a cell, or a numeric column's sum, minimum, maximum or average at the precision written. A figure the query compares a column against backs it too: "orders over 15 000 euros" restating amount_eur > 15000, or "in 2025" restating order_date >= '2025-01-01'. Otherwise the sentence is withheld, never the rows:

The phrased answer stated a figure these rows do not back, so it is withheld. The rows and the SQL below are the answer.

lm ask prints those rows in a table under that sentence, then the SQL. For a script, lm ask -o json marks the result "abstained": true (see both).

  • It catches a figure the model took from an ingested text that reads like an instruction.
  • A figure the question wrote but the query did not use is not backed: "50 cancelled orders?" answered "yes, 50" over a count of 26 is withheld. Nor are numbers the query does not compare a column against: LIMIT 500, ROUND(…, 2), GROUP BY 1, WHERE 9999 = 9999, current_date = '2025-01-01'. A column the check cannot read — qualified (o.amount_eur) or inside a function — backs nothing either. Of a date, only its year backs a figure.
  • Not numbers: identifiers (SO-000004), dates, list markers. Grouped thousands (1,250, 312 480) are one figure. A number quoted from a text cell with its words is a quote, not a claim.
  • It cannot see a cell that already holds a false sentence: an answer repeating it passes.

docs.title: Disputed rows — a disclosure, not a veto
docs.text:
This one never stops an answer: it adds to one.

A fused entity keeps one value per column; the other sources' values are in its _conflicts ledger. P-1008 is Lyon in the ERP and Villeurbanne in the CRM, so "GOLD customers in Lyon" counts it and "customers in Villeurbanne" does not. The answer names such records, per filtered column:

  • counted — a record the answer counted on a value its sources dispute;
  • not counted — a record the filter left out although a source holds the filtered value.
  disputed — a source disagrees on a value this answer filtered on:
    P-1008  city = 'Villeurbanne'  not counted  t_acme_desk_erp: Lyon · t_acme_desk_crm: Villeurbanne
Appears on answered and zero-row results; never after a guard refusal or a read failure Query shapes one fused entity view, filtered with col = 'v' or col IN (…) joined by AND No disclosure for OR, NOT, <>, !=, NOT IN, ranges, LIKE, joins, subqueries, UNION/INTERSECT/EXCEPT, resolution: entities, a lookup that fails or takes over 5 s Counted entries only when the record demonstrably contributed: never with HAVING; on an aggregate-only query, not with OFFSET; otherwise not with LIMIT, OFFSET, FETCH or at the 500-row cap Cap 10 entries, not-counted first; disputedTruncated says when more exist Isolation your tenant only, read-only

A missed disclosure is possible; a false one is not. The model's answer text is untouched. Each door renders it: lm ask, the analytic response, the PWA chat.

docs.title: Fail-open by design
docs.text: The value, column and table guards inspect only clean SQL shapes (bare identifiers compared to string literals). A function-wrapped column (lower(col) = …), a column qualified by anything but the table's alias, or a name ambiguous across tables is not refused.

docs.title: Names the source chose
docs.text:
A column keeps the name its source gave it: c_bpartner.id, Partner Name, MONTANT_€. The schema card lists every column quoted, the generated SQL quotes them, and a refusal names one in full (montant_€_ht stays montant_€_ht). Use the name exactly as lm source schema lists it.

A kafka source has no rename step, so the producer's field name is the column name; a CSV or JDBC source can rename on the way in. A kind: Workflow uses the column's real name too.

docs.title: Asking for a name, asking for a text
docs.text:
A question pins a value in one of two ways; the SQL under the answer shows which.

The question says The SQL Example a name: a category, a status, a code exact match « … de la catégorie Pompes ? » → "category_name" = 'Pompes' (not Pompes à chaleur) a text column contains a text anywhere in the value, any case « dont la description contient Badu » → "description" ILIKE '%Badu%' both the name exact, the text searched « … de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient Badu » a negation the opposite set « qui ne contient pas Badu » another wording left to the model: it may abstain or miss BADU « Quels articles mentionnent Badu ? » names no column and abstains
  • Search wordings name a text column (description, libellé, désignation, nom, texte, intitulé, titre, commentaire, or the English words) with contient, inclut, mentionne / contains, includes, mentions, or put the text in the column (« Badu dans la description »).
  • A value named right after catégorie, statut or code (category, status, code) is always matched exactly: the hub turns an ILIKE '%Pompes%' on it back into = 'Pompes', and the SQL shown is the one that ran.
  • « Combien d'articles contient la catégorie Pompes ? » is not a text search: a category is not a text column.

A count that looks too high on a named value: check the SQL for = (a name) or ILIKE (a search).

docs.title: Asking about a date
docs.text:
A date the question writes is a filter, and the column's type decides how:

The question says On a date column On a timestamp column a day, « … le 2026-07-02 » = '2026-07-02' the whole day: >= '2026-07-02' AND < '2026-07-03' a month, « … en juillet 2026 après le 4 » >= '2026-07-05' AND < '2026-08-01' the same range a day no row holds no row, with the zero-row caveat — not a refusal the same
  • The wordings are an ISO date (2026-07-02, a time after it allowed) or a month with its year (juillet 2026, 1er juillet 2026, July 2026, July 2, 2026). 01/07/2026 (first of July or seventh of January?), hier, an abbreviated month (juil. 2026), a year alone, a code built from a date (SO-2026-07-02, SO/2026-07-02, asked for by its exact value) or a day the calendar does not have (2026-02-31) are left to the model.
  • A day is the platform's midnight UTC, as everywhere else: Ask reads in UTC whatever zone the hub runs in.
  • The column must carry a date type. A date a source landed as text (a CSV without parse-date) is compared as text; on an entity, see Dates across sources.
  • The model may count where you asked for the list (« Quelles commandes… » answered with COUNT(*)): the range is right, the SQL shows the shape.

docs.title: A question that follows the previous one
docs.text:
« Et HAWARD ? » means nothing on its own. The PWA chat sends the previous question with it (the previous field of the chat door); lm ask does not. The hub rewrites the follow-up as one complete question and answers that through every guard above.

The memory is one sentence — the previous question, never its rows or SQL:

Donne-moi les références dont la description contient Badu.
Et HAWARD ?                                   → Donne-moi les références dont la description contient HAWARD.
Et PENTAIR ?                                  → Donne-moi les références dont la description contient PENTAIR.
Et seulement celles de la catégorie Pompes ?  → Donne-moi les références de la catégorie Pompes dont la description contient PENTAIR.
The follow-up Effect « Et X ? », "And X?" — a bare value replaces a value: HAWARD then PENTAIR searches PENTAIR, never both « seulement », « uniquement », « parmi elles », "only", "among them" narrows: the earlier conditions stay, the new one is added « aussi », « également », "also", "as well" widens: the new value is accepted beside the old one a complete question answered as asked

A value is recognised when written in capitals (HAWARD), with a digit (SO-000005), between quotes, or capitalised inside the sentence (Pentair). All in lower case (as on a phone), it is recognised only when the previous question searched exactly one text, one word or quoted text ending its clause:

Donne-moi les références dont la description contient badu.
et haward ?    → Donne-moi les références dont la description contient haward.
et pentair ?   → Donne-moi les références dont la description contient pentair.
  • Words of conversation (« et alors ? », « Et Ensuite ? », "and then?") are never taken as a value; a word not on that list is (« et bof ? » searches bof).
  • When in doubt, write the value as the data spells it, or ask in full.

Every other follow-up is written by the model, and the hub checks it before using it. It is refused, not guessed, when:

  • a value of your follow-up is not in it exactly as you wrote it (HAWARD corrected to Hayward would search something else);
  • it names a value that is in neither sentence (an invented filter);
  • it adds a value where « Et X ? » should replace one (contient badu ou haward);
  • it searches a text when neither sentence asked for a text search (above: that is the asker's call, never the model's);
  • the model says the follow-up points at something the previous question does not name.

A follow-up that points at a row of the answer (« le deuxième », « la première est… », « celui-ci », « ce client-là », "the second one", "that one") is refused before the model is asked: the rows are never remembered. An ordinal on a noun (« le mois dernier », « le premier trimestre ») is not a row.

I couldn't tie this question to the previous one. Ask it in full, with the value or the name it refers to.

Do next: ask the question in full.

The answer comes with the question it answers (understoodAs). Read it the way you read the SQL: it is what was really asked.

A leading address to the chat is removed: « lumnik, combien de clients ? », « Dis lumnik … », "Hey lumnik …" (followed by a comma, a colon or !, or after a greeting). « lumnik a combien de commandes ? » keeps lumnik as a value.

docs.title: When an answer looks wrong
docs.text:
The guards lower the odds; they do not abolish them.

  1. Detect — read the SQL that came with the answer.
  2. Report — to your integrator (the security contact is for vulnerabilities only).
  3. Fix — a value or column the guards should have known: add it to the entity manifest and re-apply it (lm source rediscover --scope <tag> rebuilds the card if needed).
  4. Re-verify — ask the same questions again; the SQL makes each one replayable.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Ingestion honesty — the same principle on the way in (DLQ, quarantine, run transparency).
  • Scopes — what a scope is and what the leak guard guarantees.
  • View generation contract — the same abstention ethos when the AI writes a kind: View: unanswerable ask → refusal with the reason, never invented columns.

docs.title: Seeing what was ingested, skipped, and quarantined
docs.text:
A connector run cannot look clean while it lost rows. This page reads a run's arithmetic — what the counters mean, which non-writes are benign, and how to get from a count to the exact row that fell out, with its reason.

flowchart LR
  src[("source rows — IN")] --> pipe["read → map → write"]
  pipe --> outp[("written — OUT")]
  pipe --> skip["benign skips<br/>Duplicate · PolicyExcluded"]
  pipe -.-> dlq["quarantined — the DLQ<br/>MappingFailed · ValidationFailed ·<br/>WriteFailed · MalformedSource"]

Every row is written, benignly skipped, or quarantined with its reason and payload: IN = OUT + SKIPPED. The dashed path is what DEAD-LETTERS counts.

docs.title: The two kinds of "not written"
docs.text:
Kind Reasons In DEAD-LETTERS? Benign skip Duplicate (the row already existed), PolicyExcluded (a filter-where or skip-empty-rows hook excluded it) no Quarantined (dead letter) MalformedSource, MappingFailed, ValidationFailed (a validate-row hook), WriteFailed yes

OUT counts source rows: a split-row hook that fans one row into several table rows still counts one.

docs.title: Reading a run
docs.text:
lm run get <id> shows IN, OUT, SKIPPED and DEAD-LETTERS (always part of SKIPPED). A ten-row orders export where two lines do not match the header:

$ lm run get 8ffcd5ae
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS     IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
8ffcd5ae  orders     default   Completed  10  8    2        2             2026-10-19 01:47  2026-10-19 01:47
⚠ 2 rows quarantined — see: lm dlq list --run 8ffcd5ae-c387-45b9-8a57-091043af6c59

10 = 8 + 2, and both skipped rows are dead letters. --run takes the full id or its first 8 characters.

The run can print three other notes (on stderr):

Note Means ⚠ N cell(s) a hook did not deliver as declared — the rows were still written a lead, not a loss — see the table below • N row(s) removed — the source no longer holds them rows left the table — see below ✖ run failed: … (• run cancelled: … for a cancelled run) the reason the run ended

A cell a hook did not deliver as declared — the row still landed and counts in OUT, and nothing goes to the DLQ:

Shape What happened to the cell emptied a hook could not read the value; the cell was written empty declined a repair hook left the value exactly as it arrived (repairing it would have lost more) replaced a value the source never sent, where the manifest asks for it by name overwritten a value from another column that a rename landed on

Rows removed:

  • csv, one local file: the rows the file no longer holds. The run fails instead, and removes nothing, when it would remove more than 30% of the table (refresh.max_removed), when the file is empty, when it has dead letters, or when the file changed while it was read — see CSV § full refresh.
  • jdbc: the older versions of a key, once — see Upgrading.
$ lm run get a569be52
ID        CONNECTOR  ENDPOINT  STATUS  IN  OUT  SKIPPED  DEAD-LETTERS  STARTED           ENDED
a569be52  orders     default   Failed  5   5    0        0             2026-10-19 01:47  2026-10-19 01:47
✖ run failed: 3 of 8 rows would be removed: the file holds 5 where the table held 8, more than refresh.max_removed (30%) allows — nothing was removed. If the file really lost them, raise refresh.max_removed (or set it to off) and run again.

docs.title: A run that refuses to finish
docs.text:
When a chunk reads records but the endpoint's stored position does not move, the next chunk would read the same rows for ever. The run stops itself and ends Failed, naming the endpoint:

✖ run failed: endpoint 'order_lines' read 500 records but its stored position did not move — the same window would be re-read for ever

Nothing was lost: the rows read were written, and re-reading them is not a duplicate. Re-running reproduces it, because the position is stored.

docs.title: Seeing why
docs.text:
• lm dlq list --run <id> — every dead letter of the run (reason, attempts, message).
  • lm dlq get <id> — the full reason and the offending payload (the exact row). The 8-character id from the list works; keep the same --run so it resolves against that list.
$ lm dlq list --run 8ffcd5ae-c387-45b9-8a57-091043af6c59
ID        CONNECTOR  RUN       REASON           ATTEMPTS  MESSAGE
e4d33067  orders     8ffcd5ae  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/drop/orders.csv:9 — Index for header 'status' is 2 but …
5b15008d  orders     8ffcd5ae  MalformedSource  1         /tmp/drop/orders.csv:8 — Record has 6 values but only 5 colu…

$ lm dlq get 5b15008d --run 8ffcd5ae-c387-45b9-8a57-091043af6c59
ID:        5b15008d-eec6-404d-b9f4-35f7d75121c9
Connector: orders (ede74f60-6705-4388-9d62-ed4a55d6c0f4)
Run:       8ffcd5ae-c387-45b9-8a57-091043af6c59
Reason:    MalformedSource
Attempts:  1
Message:   /tmp/drop/orders.csv:8 — Record has 6 values but only 5 columns are declared
Detail:    {"file":"/tmp/drop/orders.csv","line":8,"message":"Record has 6 values but only 5 columns are declared"}
Payload:   {"raw":["ORD-1007","C-001","IN_PROGRESS","640.00","","extra"],"file":"/tmp/drop/orders.csv","line":8}

Line 8 carried six values for five columns. The payload keeps every raw value: fix it in the export, then close the entry with lm dlq discard or lm dlq replayed.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
The Prometheus endpoint (/q/metrics) exposes:

  • lumnik_runs_total{status} — runs by terminal status (Completed, Partial, Failed, Cancelled). Partial: the run wrote everything it read, but stopped before reading everything there was.
  • lumnik_dead_letters_total{reason} — quarantined rows by reason.

No dashboards ship with lumnik; wire these into your own monitoring.
